title: Student Body Constitution: Article I The Student Body

sections.heading: Section 1 NAME
sections.text: The name of this organization shall be the Student Body of the Florida State University, hereinafter referred to as the Student Body. The governing entity of the Student Body shall be the Student Government Association of the Florida State University, hereinafter referred to as the Student Government Association.

sections.heading: Section 2 JURISDICTION
sections.text:
The Student Government Association derives its authority from the Florida State Legislature under Florida Statutes 1004.26 and 1009.24.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 3 MISSION STATEMENT
sections.text:
The mission of the Student Government Association (SGA), is to provide FSU students with representation, services and advocacy within the university structure. The Student Government Association provides quality leadership for, and accountability to its constituency by recognizing that strength arises from diversity, engagement, and dialogue.

History: Revised by Constitutional Amendment 6, 56th Student Senate, Spring Elections 2004

sections.heading: Section 4 FRANCHISE
sections.text:
All students by virtue of their registration in the Florida State University, hereinafter referred to as the University, shall be members of the Student Body, shall be entitled to vote in the student body elections, and shall be subject to this Constitution, the Student Body Statutes, and to all University Rules and Regulations.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 5 PURPOSE
sections.text:
The purpose of this organization shall be:

To ensure the greatest participation by students in the immediate governance of and policy development for the Florida State University at all levels.

To manage all Activity and Service Fees in a fiscally accountable manner.

To organize events for students.

To receive complaints from students, investigate the problems of students and participate in academic policy making decisions concerning students.

To take action on behalf of the student body in general, and to specifically work for:

The expansion of student power in all aspects of student and university governance.

The recognitions of access to education as a basic human right.

The enforcement of civil rights guarantees in all aspects of university life and policy.

The ability of students, staff, and faculty to function without undue financial stress.

The protection of public education.

The defense of the right of faculty, students and campus workers to organize in their interest.

The protection of full student autonomy over student life, services, and interests.

To provide an official voice through which the opinions of the student body may be expressed.

To develop SGA policies in a fair and open manner.

To inform all students of SGA activities and encourage participation in them.

History: Revised by Amendment 10, 57th Senate. Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA58-001 on 2/26/2006

sections.heading: Section 6 STUDENTS RIGHTS
sections.text:
Each student shall be subject to the rules of the courts and the University but these rules shall at no time and in no way abridge the student's rights as citizen under the United States Constitution or the Constitution of the State of Florida.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Ii The Legislature

sections.heading: Section 1 LEGISLATIVE VESTING
sections.text:
The Legislative Powers of the Student Body shall be vested in the Student Senate, hereinafter referred to as the Senate.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 2 COMPOSITION
sections.text:
There shall be an elected group of student representatives known as Senators.

From this body the Senate shall select a Senate President and President Pro Tempore in the Fall Semester, and they shall be elected for a one (1) year term during which their seats shall not come up for election, even if they were initially elected in the Spring.

Method for the selection of Senate officers shall be by statute.

The exact number of Senate seats shall be determined by statute, but at no time shall this number exceed eighty (80).
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-001 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 3 ELECTIONS (Reserved)
sections.text:
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Repealed by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 4 SENATE SESSION
sections.text:
The session of the Senate shall begin on the second week of classes and terminate on the week prior to the final week of classes, pursuant to the academic calendar for each semester.
There shall be an organizational meeting to elect the incoming Senate’s President and President Pro Tempore, at a date determined by the sitting Senate President,  between the day of the Fall election and prior to the corresponding inauguration, but no later than eight (8) school days before inauguration. The results of the organizational meeting shall be ratified by motion of the Senate at their first official meeting. The rules for such election shall be laid out in the Senate’s Rules of Procedure.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 5 POWERS AND DUTIES
sections.text:
Senate shall:

Enact its own Rules of Procedure, which shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote.

Propose, by a two-thirds (2/3)	vote, Constitutional amendments.

Provide for the compilation and publication of legislation.

Consider appointments of the Student Body President by a two-thirds (2/3) vote for appointments to fill vacated elected offices, and by a majority vote for other appointments. Confirmation of a Supreme Court Justice shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote under any circumstances.

Impeach Student Body officers, both elected and appointed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote, as shall be determined by statute.

Take final action of the proposed Activity Fee Budget.

Establish its own meeting times and rules of procedure.

Issue subpoenas upon majority vote of a standing committee, as shall be prescribed by Student Body Statutes.

Require the registration of student organizations with the Senate as provided by Statute.

Any veto by the Student Body President may be overridden by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of not less than a quorum of the Senate.

Present to the Student Body President all bills passed by Senate, within three schools days.

Have the power to write legislation.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-008 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 6 LIMITATION OF POWERS
sections.text:
Legislation of the Senate shall be subject to review:

Only by such officials authorized to do so by the Rules and Regulations of the University, the Board of Trustees, or by the President of the University.

By the Student Supreme Court in cases where it has jurisdiction.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Iii The Executive

sections.heading: Section 1 EXECUTIVE POWERS
sections.text:
All executive powers of the Student Body shall be vested in a President of the Student Body, assisted by the Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, and such administrative officers as the President shall appoint in accordance with this Article, and by Statute. The Student Body President shall hereinafter be referred to as the President, and the Student Body Vice President as the Vice President.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004

sections.heading: Section 2 ELECTION OF EXECUTIVE POWERS
sections.text:
The President shall be elected by a plurality of those voting in the Student Body elections.

The Vice President shall be the President's running mate.

The Student Body Treasurer who shall be elected by plurality of those voting in the student body elections.

History: Revised by Amendment 10, 57th Student Senate. Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-005 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA73-002 on 10/13/2021

sections.heading: Section 3 DUTIES AND POWERS OF THE PRESIDENT
sections.text:
The President shall:

Administer and enforce all laws of the Student Body.

Appoint Cabinet members as specified in the Statutes. Such appointments shall require a majority vote of Senate to be approved.

Have the power to veto or sign acts of the Senate, provided that they exercise such power within five (5) school days of presentation to the Student Body President. A veto may be overridden by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of not less than a quorum of the Senate.

Call and preside over meetings of the Student Body.

Make recommendations for legislation to the Student Senate.

Address the Senate at the beginning of each semester and at other times upon invitation by the Senate.

Instruct and require reports from Cabinet members and approve all policies made from them.

Remove, at their discretion, any officer whom they have appointed to a position in the Executive Branch.

Have the power to call for a referendum subject to two-thirds majority Senate concurrence.

History: Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA73-002 on 10/13/2021

sections.heading: Section 4 DUTIES OF OTHER EXECUTIVE OFFICERS
sections.text:
The Vice President shall assume the duties of the President in their absence or upon their request.

The Vice President shall coordinate the efforts of the Cabinet and shall serve as coordinator for the formulation and completion of Cabinet projects.

The Office of the Vice President shall direct grievances and ideas to the proper functionary and see that they are acted upon.

The Student Body Treasurer shall have all the appropriate powers and duties granted to them by statute.

History: Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA73-002 on 10/13/2021

sections.heading: Section 5 PRESIDENT'S CABINET
sections.text: There shall be a Cabinet to assist and advise the President, the membership of which shall be determined by Statutes.

sections.heading: Section 6 LIMITATIONS OF POWERS
sections.text: Policies adopted by officers and committees of the Executive Branch shall be subject to review in the same manner as legislation.

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Iv Judiciary

sections.heading: Section 1 JUDICIAL VESTING
sections.text: The Judicial power of the Student Body shall be vested in a Supreme Court and such other courts as the Senate may form from time to time ordain and establish.

sections.heading: Section 2 ADMINISTRATION: PRACTICE AND PROCEDURE
sections.text:
The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court as chief administrative officer of the Judicial System, shall be vested with, and shall exercise in accordance with rules adopted by the court the authority to:

Assign cases and duties among the Justices of the Court.

Supervise the administration of all courts.

Inform the Legislature during the Spring Academic term of the condition of the Judicial System and recommend measures for the improvement of the administration of justice.

The Supreme Court shall adopt rules governing the practice and procedures in all courts.

All courts shall conduct open hearings.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-003 on 1/1/2004

sections.heading: Section 3 SUPREME COURT
sections.text:
Composition: The Supreme Court shall consist of:

A Chief Justice who shall be a law student of at least second year standing.

Four (4) Associate Justices who shall be law students of at least second year standing.

A Clerk of at least second semester freshman standing; and such deputy clerks as the Chief Justice deems necessary. A deputy clerk shall serve as acting clerk in the absence of the Clerk.

If there is a vacancy on the Supreme Court as the result of a recusal of a sitting Justice, the Chief Justice shall appoint a Temporary Justice to sit by designation. The Temporary Justice shall be a law student of at least a second year standing.

Procedures:

Concurrence of a majority of Justices shall be necessary to render effective a decision of the Supreme Court.

The Chief Justice shall preside over sessions of the Supreme Court. If the Chief Justice, in their absences, fails to designate an Acting Chief Justice, then the Student Body President shall designate an Associate Justice to be acting Chief Justice.

The Clerk shall keep records of the Court, shall cause all decision except privileged matter to be made available to members of the Student Body, and shall deliver into the hands of their successor all permanent records of the Court.

The Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction:

Over cases and controversies involving questions of the constitutionality of actions by student governing groups, organizations and their representatives.

Over violations of the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.

Over conflicts between student groups.

To issue writs of mandamus, prohibition, and quo warranto when a Student Body officer is named as a respondent, or such other writs necessary and proper to the complete exercise of its jurisdiction.

To issue advisory opinions concerning student rights under the Student Body Constitution upon request of the Student Body President or any Senator. 

History: Revised by Constitutional Amendment 1, Spring 2002 SGA Runoff Elections. Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA74-002 on 10/19/2022
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 4 STUDENT CONDUCT (Reserved)
sections.text:
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Repealed by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 5 SELECTION AND VACANCIES
sections.text:
Justices shall be appointed by the Student Body President confirmed by Student Senate as follows:

Once confirmed by the Senate, Justices shall serve until they graduate, resign, or are impeached, unless the Supreme Court fail to remove them from office. Within six weeks after a vacancy on the Court occurs, the Student Body President shall select a nominee for each vacant position and present these names to the Senate. The Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court shall be responsible for notifying the Student Body President of any vacancy on the Court.

Before choosing a nominee, the Student Body President shall submit the candidate’s application forms to the Student Bar Association at the College of Law. The Student Bar Association shall then interview each candidate and submit a written opinion on the fitness and qualifications of each candidate to serve on the Court to the Student Body President. The Student Body President shall then forward one of the candidates to the Student Senate for confirmation.

Confirmation shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.

No person shall sit on the Supreme Court who is not a student at the Florida State University College of Law of second or third year standing.

The Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court must have completed the Evidence courses at the College of Law before taking office.

History: Revised by Amendment 1, 67th Student Senate Spring 2015. (Article IV Section 5 (1)(e)). Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-002 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA74-002 on 10/19/2022

sections.heading: Section 6 SUBPOENA
sections.text:
The Supreme Court shall have the power of subpoena over all students having interest of effect in matters before the Court.

Failure to obey a subpoena shall be contempt, punishable as provided in Article IV, Section 7.

sections.heading: Section 7 CONTEMPT
sections.text:
The Supreme Court shall have the power to cite the defendant’s counsel, the opposing counsel, all parties at interest, a witness or spectator for contempt of court and shall have the power to try them for this offense and issue punishment thereof. This punishment shall be defined as a reasonable penalty that the Supreme Court deems appropriate for the particular case.

History: Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004

sections.heading: Section 8 ADMINISTRATION OF ELECTIONS
sections.text:
The power to administer elections shall be vested in a Supervisor of Elections, who shall be assisted by Deputy Supervisors and other officers as the Senate may establish by statute, and an Elections Commission, subject to the election statutes passed by the Student Senate.
The Supervisor of Elections shall be appointed by the Chief Justice of the Supreme  Court, confirmed by two-thirds vote of the Student Senate, and shall serve a term  of two years.
The Deputy Supervisors of Elections shall be appointed by the Supervisor of  Elections and confirmed by two-thirds vote of the Student Senate.
The Elections Commission shall be made up of six (6) law students, appointed by  the Chief Justice, and shall be chaired by the Supervisor of Elections, who shall only vote in cases of a tie.
The Senate may, by statute, place additional requirements on appointees under this section.
The Supervisor, their deputies, and the Elections Commissioners shall maintain neutrality in all acts, on pain of impeachment.
The Supervisor shall be empowered to determine whether a violation of election-related statutes occurred, subject to the regulations made by statutes, when the Supervisor is presented with or discovers evidence of such violations.
Decisions of the Supervisor shall be appealable to Elections Commission, who shall review the alleged violation de novo, whose procedures shall be set by:
Statutes, and
Rules of Procedure, agreed to by a majority of the Elections Commission.
Decisions of the Elections Commission shall be appealable to the Supreme Court, who shall review the Commission’s decision:
De novo for questions of law, and
By a clearly erroneous standard for questions of fact.
The Supervisor shall be empowered to issue memoranda setting out the Supervisor’s interpretation of election statutes.
Such memoranda must be published on the SGA website and are merely advisory. The memoranda shall have no binding authority.
At least twenty-four hours prior to the promulgation of any such memorandum, the Supervisor shall provide a copy of the memorandum to all Student Senators, all  COGS Representatives, and the Student Body President.
Within twenty-four hours of such promulgation, any student may petition the Elections Commission for review of the memorandum. Any such review shall be de novo and the Commission shall meet within forty-eight (48) hours of the petition to determine whether to approve or reject the memorandum
HISTORY
Adopted by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

title: Student Body Constitution: Article V Elections And Qualifications

sections.heading: ARTICLE V ELECTIONS AND QUALIFICATIONS
sections.text: History: Revised by Constitutional Amendment 2: Spring 1999 SGA Elections. Revised by Constitutional Amendment 10, 56th Senate.

sections.heading: Section 1 TIME OF ELECTION
sections.text:
Senate and Campus Recreation Board elections will be held in the Fall academic term as provided by Statute.

Student Body President, Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, Union Board, Senior Class Council officers, all elected Agency, Bureau and Affiliated Projects Officers, and Senate elections will be held in the Spring academic term as provided by Statute.

Referendum and Constitutional amendment elections will be held as provided by Statute.

Recall elections will be held as provided in Article VII of the Student Body Constitution and by Statute.

Elections for the Representatives in the Congress of Graduate Students shall be held as provided for in the Student Body Statutes and the COGS Code.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-005 on 1/1/2004

sections.heading: Section 2 ELECTION CONFLICTS
sections.text:
In the case of a holiday, campus closure, or school function conflict with any of the above dates in the regular session, the Supervisor of Elections shall designate another date.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 3 ACADEMIC QUALIFICATIONS
sections.text:
All students holding a major Student Government office as defined in the Student Body Statutes shall be in good academic standing.

HISTORY
Revised by Bill B42-069 on 3/14/1990
Revised by Other CA56-004 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 4 RESTRICTIONS ON CANDIDACY
sections.text:
No student shall hold two major offices of the Student Government concurrently. The list of major offices shall be determined by Statute, but shall always include the Student Body President, Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, Student Senators, Justices of the Student Supreme Court, Congress of Graduate Representatives, and Supervisor of Elections.

No candidate for offices shall exceed campaign expenses limits.

Any student found guilty by the Student Government Association Supreme Court of two or more violations of the Florida State University Constitution and/or Statutes, or found guilty of any violation of the University Student Code of Conduct or Academic Honor Code, will not hold any office in the Florida State University Student Government Association until the required sanctions are completed.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-009 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA57-001 on 1/1/2005
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 5 PROCEDURE FOR ESTABLISHING CANDIDACY
sections.text:
Any qualified student may be placed on the Official Ballot by submitting a delcaration of candidacy.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 6 TERM OF OFFICE
sections.text:
All officers of the Student Body shall take office at the time of installation, to be specified by Statute. Their term shall cease upon the installation of their successors.

History: Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004

sections.heading: Section 7 VACANCIES
sections.text:
In the event of a vacancy in the Office of the President, the Vice President shall assume that office for the remainder of the Presidential term. If the office of Vice President should happen to be vacant at the same time as that of the President, the Senate President shall assume the Office of the President for the remainder of the Presidential term, followed by the Student Senate President Pro Tempore, and the Student Body Treasurer, in that order. The individual, who has become acting President for the remainder of the Presidential term, shall then appoint a new Vice President from within the ranks of the student body. This appointment shall be subject to confirmation by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate. If there is a vacancy in the Office of the Student Body Treasurer, and no Deputy Treasurer is available to fill the vacancy, then the President shall have the power to appoint a new Student Body Treasurer for the remainder of the Presidential term, subject to confirmation by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

All other vacancies created in elected Student Body offices, except for those in the Union and Recreation Boards, the Congress of Graduate Students, in Agencies, Bureaus, and Affiliated Projects with campus-wide elected officers, as well as in the Senior Class Council, shall be filled by appointment by the Student Body President, with confirmation by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate, provided all succeeding officers have the same constitutional qualifications as the originally elected officers. Vacancies in the above listed offices shall be filled as provided for in the Student Body Statutes, except that if no pertinent statute exists then the Student Body President shall have the power of appointment by default.

Offices vacated pursuant to a leave of absence as defined by the Student Body Statutes shall be filled for the duration of the absence in accordance with the provisions of this Article.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-009 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Vi Amendment Process And Referendum Elections

sections.heading: Section 1 CONSTITUTIONAL AMENDMENTS
sections.text:
Amendments to this Constitution may be proposed by three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Student Senate, by petition of 1,500 members of the Student Body, or by recommendation from the Constitutional Review Commission, and shall become part of this Constitution upon ratification by two-thirds (2/3) of the votes cast in an election of the Student Body.
Statutes shall adopt procedures by which notice is given when a constitutional amendment is introduced in the Senate for consideration and at least one week prior to the election where the amendment is to be voted on.
Each amendment shall be accompanied by a Statement of Intent, as shall be further defined by statute, that explains the text of the amendment.
If an amendment is proposed by the Senate or Constitutional Review Commission, the Senate President shall deliver the amendment unto the Supervisor of Elections within forty-eight (48) hours of the Senate or Commission proposing the amendment, who shall then place the amendment on the ballot and ensure the amendment’s compliance with the requirements of this article. Failure of either officer to carry out such duties constitutes nonfeasance and, additionally, the Supreme Court may compel the officer(s) to carry out such duties by writ of mandamus.
The Senate may, by statute, provide the form for petitions to amend this Constitution.
Procedures for timely review of proposed constitutional amendments by the Student Supreme Court may be made by statute, provided that such review may not invalidate a proposed amendment unless there is a finding that the proposed amendment violates state or federal law. 
Except as provided for in this Article, no further requirements may be placed on the amending process by statute.
Notwithstanding the provisions of subsection (a) above, any amendment to Article IX shall require approval by two-thirds of graduate and professional students voting on the proposed amendment, in addition to all other requirements provided in this Article.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA73-002 on 10/13/2021
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 2 REFERENDUM
sections.text:
The Student Body may demand a referendum election upon the properly signed petition of at least five hundred (500) students. The result of the election shall serve as a mandate for the Student Body Government provided that ten percent (10%) of the Student Body shall have participated in the election. At no time shall a referendum election demand any result that would violate the provisions of the Student Body Constitution or any result contrary to federal, state, local or university law.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Art VI Section 3 (Reserved)
sections.text:
HISTORY
Repealed by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 4 OPINION QUESTIONS
sections.text:
There shall be a commission that shall have the authority to place opinion questions regarding issues of the university on the SGA ballot. The composition and procedures of this commission shall be further defined by statute.
Students may petition the commission to consider adding a question to the ballot after receiving the signature of two hundred (200) students on a petition. The Senate may prescribe the form of the petition by statute.
The Senate may place opinion questions on the ballot by majority vote.
Opinion questions shall not be binding on the Student Government.
HISTORY
Repealed & Replaced by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 5 GENDER NEUTRALITY
sections.text:
Amendments to this Constitution, either through the Student Senate or petition, must use gender neutral language.

Gender neutral language shall be defined as the pronouns “they, them, and their(s).”

History: Added by Constitutional Amendment 2, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 6 CONSTITUTIONAL REVIEW COMMISSION
sections.text:
There shall be a Constitutional Review Commission to review the Student Body Constitution and present amendments for ratification by the Student Body.

The Commission shall have the authority to propose amendments to the Student Body Constitution.

The Commission shall meet every three years and submit all proposed amendments before the following Spring Election.

The Commission shall consist of the following 10 members:

The Student Body President shall appoint 3 members.

The Student Senate President shall appoint 3 members from the Student Senate and shall serve as a member.

The Chief Justice of the Supreme Court shall appoint 3 members.

All members of the commission must be enrolled students at Florida State University.

The Commission shall be organized as follows:

The Senate President shall serve as the Commission's chair, and shall be a non-voting member except in the event of a tie.

The Commission shall elect a Vice Chair by majority vote.

Any proposals to be forwarded for ratification by the Student Body must pass the commission by majority vote.

The Commission shall adopt a rules of procedure at their first convening by majority vote.
HISTORY
Adopted by Other CA73-004 on 10/13/2021

meta.subBook: ARTICLE VI AMENDMENT PROCESS AND REFERENDUM ELECTIONS

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Vii Recall Of Student Body Officials

sections.heading: Section 1 METHOD OF RECALL
sections.text:
Every elected and appointed official of the Florida State University Student Body is subject, as herein provided, to recall by the legal voters of the Florida State University Student Body. The person or persons demanding recall shall set forth in a petition the reasons for the demand of recall. If the elected official in question offers their resignation it shall be accepted and take effect on the day it is offered, and the vacancy shall be filled as provided by law. If they do not resign within thirty days an election will be held to determine whether the people will recall the officer. On the sample ballot at the election shall be printed in not more than two hundred (200) words the reasons for demanding recall and in not more than two hundred (200) words the officers justification of their course in office. They shall continue to perform the duties of their office until the results of their official election shall be officially declared. The recall petition shall be filed with the officer with whom the petition for nomination to such office should be filed, and the same officer shall order the special election when it is required. No such petition shall be circulated against any officer until they have actually held office for three months. After one such petition and special election, no further recall shall be filed against the same officer during the term for which they were elected.

History: Revised by Amendment 1, Spring 2020 election.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 2 NUMBER OF SIGNATURES REQUIRED FOR A PETITION OF RECALL
sections.text:
Pertaining to the recall of campus-wide elected officers (Student Body President, Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, Campus Recreation Board Members, Elected Agency, Bureau, and Affiliated Project personnel, and Union Board Members, or any other campus-wide elected officer as dictated by statute) five percent (5%) of all students or 1,500 signatures, whichever is greater.

Pertaining to the recall of Senators, COGS Representatives and Senior Class Council officers: ten percent (10%) of those enrolled in the division in which the seat in question is located or fifty (50) signatures from that division, whichever is greater. In the event that a particular division has less than fifty (50) students enrolled, then the number of signatures required shall be two-thirds (2/3) of all the students in that division.
Pertaining to the recall of appointed officers: two percent (2%) of all students or 800 signatures, whichever is greater.
HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-010 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA73-001 on 10/13/2021
Revised by Other CRC 2024-25 on 7/21/2025

sections.heading: Section 3 IMPEACHMENT
sections.text: Any elected official of the Student Body or any officer appointed to fill the vacancy of any elected officer or any Supreme Court Justice may be impeached by the Senate, as provided by Statute, on charges of malfeasance, misfeasance or nonfeasance.

sections.heading: Section 4 REMOVAL
sections.text:
Any elected officer of the Student Body or any officer appointed to fill the vacancy of any elected officer or any Supreme Court officer may be removed from office, following impeachment of the Senate, by the Supreme Court as provided by Statute.

Upon impeachment by the Senate of a Supreme Court Justice, the Justice shall be automatically suspended. The Student Body President shall appoint an acting Justice who shall serve only in the impeachment proceedings. The temporary appointee shall have the same qualifications of a Justice, but need not go through the normal nomination process required under Article IV, Section 5, except for being nominated by the Student Body President and confirmed by Senate.

meta.subBook: ARTICLE VII RECALL OF STUDENT BODY OFFICIALS

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Viii Panama City Branch Campus

sections.heading: Article VIII Section 1
sections.text: Students of the FSU Panama City Branch Campus shall have all the rights, privileges, protection, and duties accorded to the students of the Florida State University as defined in the Constitution.

sections.heading: Article VIII Section 2
sections.text: The Florida State University Student Senate shall be empowered to adopt, alter or amend statutes of the FSU student body in order that the members of the Branch Campus be afforded the full and appropriate benefits of FSU Student Body membership.

meta.subBook: ARTICLE VIII PANAMA CITY BRANCH CAMPUS

title: Student Body Constitution: Article Ix Congress Of Graduate Students

sections.heading: Article IX Section 1
sections.text:
There shall be a graduate student organization as part of the Student Government Association (SGA) known as the Congress of Graduate Students (COGS). COGS shall represent certain graduate, special, master, specialist, professional, doctoral and post-baccalaureate students. COGS as well as its Administrative Code shall be subject to all of the provisions of the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-007 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA58-002 on 10/2/2006

sections.heading: Article IX Section 2
sections.text:
Graduate students shall receive fifty percent (50%) of Activities and Services (A&S) Fees paid by students classified by the Registrar as Master’s, Specialist, Doctoral, Juris Doctor, Doctor of Medicine, or otherwise notated as post-baccalaureate and/or graduate students. These fees shall be allocated to COGS by SGA at the start of the annual budget process and shall be administered by the elected representatives in the Congress of Graduate Students. COGS financial administration shall be consistent with and subject to the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA58-002 on 10/2/2006
Revised by Other CA73-010 on 10/13/2021

sections.heading: Article IX Section 3
sections.text:
COGS shall have an elected group of representatives, who shall govern it. Rules controlling COGS’ elections and appointments in the event of a vacancy shall be set down in the COGS Administrative Code, and by the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-007 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA58-002 on 10/2/2006

sections.heading: Article IX Section 4
sections.text:
COGS shall have the authority to make its own internal Administrative Code, rules, and procedures that shall be set down in the COGS Administrative Code. COGS shall control its funds provided to it in Section 2 of this article, and establish its own rules for its expenditures, subject to applicable Federal, State, Local, University and Student Body Statutes laws.

HISTORY
Revised by Other CA56-007 on 1/1/2004
Revised by Other CA58-002 on 10/2/2006

sections.heading: 2024-01 - Section 1: Authority And Purpose
sections.text:
In accordance with the Student Body Constitution, there shall be a cabinet in the Executive Branch to assist the constitutional officers in the execution of their duties. The Constitution delegates the authority to define the positions and their duties to Statutes.

Pursuant to 301.2 of Student Body Statutes, this policy shall outline the cabinet of the Student Body President, including the processes and procedures thereof.

sections.heading: 2024-01 - Section 2: Revision Procedure
sections.text:
Revisions to this document may be initiated by the Student Body President or their designee, and shall be written in the form of a consent resolution sent to Senate to be placed on their consent calendar. Senate shall then have the authority to approve, deny, or amend any changes rendered, if the revision is objected to on the floor. Revisions shall be enacted immediately upon approval by the Senate.

Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day, who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept up-to-date at all times.

sections.heading: 2024-01 - Section 3: Executive Branch Offices And Responsibilities (New Version)
sections.text:
General Provisions
The Executive Branch is structured under the overarching Executive Office of the President, which encompasses the Office of the President, the Office of the Vice President, and the Office of the Treasurer. Each office has distinct responsibilities. The head of each office is responsible for working with the Student Body President or their designee in appointing its members. 

Executive Office of the President
The Executive Office of the President supports the Student Body President and Vice President in executing their constitutional powers and carrying out their administration's programs, projects, and agenda.

Duties of the Executive Office
Assist in executing the plan for the Executive Branch.
Represent segments of the student body in accordance with the structure issued by the Student Body President.
Fulfill the obligations of the job descriptions for each office.
Work for the improved quality of life of the student body.
Meet regularly, no less than once every two weeks during the fall, spring, and summer semesters. Minutes of these meetings will be recorded and kept on record.

Organization and Appointments:
The Student Body President may organize the Executive Office as deemed necessary and proper within the limits imposed by the Student Body Statutes.
If a new position is created, the Student Body President must notify the Student Senate in writing. 
Within two (2) weeks of inauguration, the Student Body President, in consultation with the Student Body Vice President, shall present the plan for the organization of the Executive Office to the Student Senate. This plan must be published on the SGA website.
All members of the Executive Office must be confirmed by the Student Senate as “Cabinet Offices” and major office positions within the Executive Branch.
The Chief of Staff, appointed by the Student Body President and subject to Student Senate confirmation, directs the activities of the Executive Office and is subject to the will of the Student Body President.

Office of the President

The Office of the President is responsible for the overall leadership and direction of the Executive Branch, overseen by the Student Body President.
Positions in the Office of the President
Student Body President: Represents the student body, oversees the execution of SGA policies, and coordinates with university administration and external entities. Has sole power of appointment within the Executive Office and may dismiss any individual serving under them at their discretion.
Chief of Staff: Manages and leads the staff, represents the Student Body President to internal SGA entities, coordinates executive projects, and interviews and recommends applicants for appointed positions within the SGA.
Deputy Chief of Staff: Supports the Chief of Staff, organizes and prepares for board meetings, ensures efficient operation, manages communications with university partners, facilitates collaboration across departments, and oversees special projects.
Sub-Groups within the Office of the President:
Executive Cabinet: The Executive Cabinet advises the President on subjects related to their respective offices and accomplishes work within their positions.
Cabinet Director: Manages the Executive Cabinet, holds weekly meetings, and provides monthly platform updates.
Secretary of Sustainability: Leads projects related to environmental sustainability on campus and within the greater Tallahassee community.
Secretary of Health & Wellness: Leads projects to advance health, safety, and wellness, partnering with various departments on related initiatives.
Secretary of Athletics & Recreation: Fosters relationships with the Athletic Department and advances recreation opportunities for students.
Secretary of Student Services: Coordinates projects for student safety, transportation, and other services, partnering with FSUPD and Transportation and Parking Services.
Secretary of Collegiate Affairs: Assists with Board of Governors and Board of Trustees preparations, establishes relationships with other universities, and spearheads statewide student projects.
Secretary of Diversity, Equity, & Inclusion: Focuses on anti-discrimination initiatives through student programming, development, and policies, collaborating with various departments.
Office of the Attorney General:
The Office of the Attorney General provides legal support and oversight for the Executive Branch.
Attorney General: Represents the Executive Branch in all SGA legal proceedings, conducts statutory revisions, and creates executive memorandums.
Deputy Attorney General(s): Assists the Attorney General in statutory revisions and ensures compliance with SGA and Florida law.
Communications Team:
The Communications Team manages the Executive Branch's internal and external communications.
Press Secretary: Represents the Executive Branch to external outlets, manages media relations, speechwriting, interviewing for articles, and oversees SGA's social media presence.
Director of Media and Content: The Director of Media and Content involves managing the development of multimedia content, overseeing content scheduling, and ensuring that all media output aligns with the Executive Branch's communication strategy.
Director of Communications: Assists the Press Secretary, maintains the SGA website, and contributes to speechwriting and articulating the Executive Branch's vision.
Graphic Design Coordinator: Documents SGA events and supports other branches and projects as needed.
Office of the Vice President
The Office of the Vice President is responsible for supporting and coordinating various executive projects and overseeing Agencies, Bureaus, and Class Councils.

Positions in the Office of the Vice President:

Chief Administrative Officer: Manages the Executive Office of the VicePresident’s staff, represents the Vice-President to internal SGA entities, coordinates executive projects, and ensures proper tracking of files, records, and documents.
Deputy Chief Administrative Officer: Assists in the overall management and coordination of the Vice-President’s staff and supports the Chief Administrative Officer with assigned duties.

Sub-Groups within the Office of the Vice President
Programming Team
The Programming Team handles event planning and student programming initiatives.
Director of Activities & Student Programming: Leads or assists with any programming effort of the Executive Branch, including providing support to student government entities as requested.
Events & Student Programming Coordinators: Assist the Director of Activities & Student Programming with programming efforts and support various SGA entities and projects.

Student Logistics Team:
The Student Logistics Team focuses on student engagement and the overall student experience.

Director of Project Development & Strategic Planning: Performs regular assessments of SGA Executive Projects, oversees risk management, and conducts project research and evaluations.
Director of Student Engagement: Facilitates relationships between SGA Officials, Registered Student Organizations, Direct Support Organizations, and other student life entities, leading student outreach efforts.
Director of Campus Life: Drives innovation in programs, services, and infrastructure, overseeing new initiatives to enhance institutional effectiveness and campus experience.

Office of the Treasurer
The Office of the Treasurer is responsible for managing the financial aspects of the Executive Branch and is headed by the Student Body Treasurer.

Positions in the Office of the Treasurer:
Deputy Treasurer: Advises and assists the Student Body Treasurer in financial actions and supports the Treasurer's roles and responsibilities in their absence.
Internal Budget Analyst: Assists with internal financial projects, provides financial support to the Executive Branch, and serves on financial committees as requested by the Student Body Treasurer.
External Budget Analyst: Assists with external financial projects, provides financial support to the Executive Branch, and serves on financial committees as requested by the Student Body Treasurer.

sections.text:

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 1: Authority And Purpose
sections.text: These rules of procedure shall lay forth the processes and procedures in which the Student Body President and Executive Branch as empowered through the President shall exert their constitutionally-granted power of appointment and dismissal. This document is empowered by the Senate through 304.1 of Student Body Statutes.

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 2: Revision Procedure
sections.text:
Revisions to this document may be initiated by the Student Body President or their designee, and shall be written in the form of a consent resolution sent to Senate to be placed on their consent calendar. Senate shall then have the authority to approve, deny, or amend any changes rendered, if the revision is objected to on the floor. Revisions shall be enacted immediately upon approval by the Senate.

Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day, who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept up-to-date at all times.

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 3: Candidate Search
sections.text:
No position requiring Student Senate confirmation may be filled until the position has been advertised properly.

The Chief of Staff, assisted by one designee from the Executive Branch, will conduct all candidate searches.

This designee from the Executive Branch shall be chosen by the Chief of Staff.
In the absence of a designee, the Chief of Staff retains all responsibility for conducting the work of the Candidate Search Process.
 All positions shall be advertised for at least one week on the SGA Website.

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 4: Candidate Screening Process
sections.text:
Upon the receipt of applications for a vacant position in Student Government Association, a screening process shall be overseen by the Student Body President to determine the most qualified candidate.
The Candidate Screening Process shall take no longer than ten (10) school days from the end of the candidate search period.
The Candidate Screening Process, conducted by the Chief of Staff, or designee as stipulated in Section Three of this document, shall include the following:

The Chief of Staff, or designee as stipulated in Chapter 304.2 shall interview all candidates.
All candidates shall provide the appropriate application as defined in Chapter 307.3, in completed format, demonstrating their qualifications for the position.
The interview shall be conducted in a standardized and professional form for all candidates, and shall draw at least five interview questions from the forwarding interview questions published on the SGA Website.
The interview shall consist of a basic questionnaire outlining the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and goals for the respective position.
After all candidates have been interviewed, the Student Body President shall forward the candidate deemed most qualified to the Student Senate for confirmation.
The Student Body President may forego the candidate screening process with the exception of subsection 4.3, subsection c, in cases where the candidate is forwarded to the Student Body President, with a written notice of a proper interview being conducted, by the Student Government Entity to which the candidate is applying for a position.
It is the responsibility of the Student Body President, the Chief of Staff, or designee to ensure that this process is carried out in a fair and constitutional manner. To that end, any person(s) conducting the interviews shall recuse themselves from the Candidate Screening Process and the processes of determining the most qualified candidate in situations where a candidate for any position has a conflict of interest with the President, Chief of Staff, or designee. They shall select, for that particular set of candidates, a non-biased actor or actors to interview candidates for said office and deem the most qualified of those candidates to then be forwarded by the President.

The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice when any recusal occurs for any selection of Officers, stating that there was a recusal and a signed statement from the non-biased actor(s) of their lack of conflict of interest.

If during the candidate screening process, the Student Body President finds that a candidate is better suited for another position within the same Student Government entity to which the candidate applied, the Student Body President may reserve the right to forward the candidate, with their consent, for another position for which they meet all Constitutional and statutory requirements.
If a candidate is forwarded to the Student Body President by an agency, bureau, or other SGA entity for confirmation pursuant to Section 4.4, any changes to the position for which a candidate is being forwarded to Senate shall also require the consent of the head of the respective SGA entity.
Agency, Bureau, and SGA entity heads may also reserve the right to change the position that a candidate is being forwarded for with the consent of the applicant before forwarding the candidate to the Student Body President pursuant to Section 4.4.
The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice in all cases when candidates are forwarded to the Senate for positions that are different from those which they applied for.

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 5: Executive Office Positions
sections.text:
The Student Body President shall appoint all Executive Cabinet Officers as defined in Section 4.1.
The Chief of Staff shall, upon recommendation by the appropriate Executive Cabinet Director, appoint all Deputy Directors and administrative support office staff.
The Student Body President may create any office or position deemed necessary and proper provided that the Student Senate is notified of the action in writing.
Any individual appointed to a Cabinet position as indicated in the Student Body Statutes shall require confirmation by the Student Senate.
The Student Body President may appoint an Acting Executive Cabinet Officer who shall serve in the role, but shall not receive compensation, until a nominee can be forwarded to the Student Senate.
No individual may serve as an Acting Executive Cabinet Director for longer than six (6) weeks.
The Student Body President-elect, as defined in Chapter 704, shall have the power to designate and forward to the Student Senate for confirmation, the Cabinet nominees for their administration after all appeals and violations have been exhausted or ruled on.
The nominees must be confirmed by a majority vote of the Student Senate.
The confirmed nominee shall be referred to as the "designee" (i.e. Chief of Staff designee).
Upon installation of the Student Body President-elect, all Cabinet Officer designees shall assume the positions for which they were confirmed and all duties, responsibilities, rights, and compensation vested with their position.
The terms of all Executive Office appointees shall end when they are dismissed, impeached, or upon installation of their successors.
The Student Body President may dismiss any appointee to the Executive Office at their discretion.

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 6: Executive Bureau And Agency Positions
sections.text:
The selection process for Executive Bureau Directors shall occur as follows:
The Student Body President shall conduct a candidate search as outlined in Section Four beginning the first week of the new administration.
The Chief of Staff shall conduct a screening process as defined in Section 4.
The outgoing Director shall submit a written recommendation to the Student Body President on the replacement Director.
The Student Body President shall choose a Director and submit the name to the Student Senate for confirmation.
A majority vote of the Student Senate, with a quorum being present, is necessary for confirmation.
The terms of all Executive Bureau Directors shall end when they are dismissed, impeached, or upon installation of their successor.
Should a directorship become vacant, the Student Body President may appoint an Acting Director, who shall not receive compensation, to serve in the position until a nominee can be forwarded to the Senate.
No individual may serve as Acting Director for longer than six (6) weeks.
If the Student Body President wishes the existing Director to remain in office, the individual must be forwarded to the Student Senate for reconfirmation.
In accordance with the Article III, Section 3 (H), of the Student Body Constitution, the Student Body President may remove the Director at President’s discretion.

The selection process for Executive Bureau Assistant Directors shall occur as follows:
The Director shall conduct a candidate search.
The Director shall interview the applicants and make a recommendation to the Student Body President.
The Student Body President may choose to either reject the nominee or forward the name to the Student Senate for confirmation.
Student Senate confirmation requires a majority vote of the Student Senate with a quorum being present.
If the Student Body President rejects the nominee, then the Director must submit another name.
The term of the Assistant Director shall be the same as the Director of that Bureau. This term length shall not be affected by the early dismissal, resignation, or impeachment of said Director.
In accordance with Article III, Section 3 (I) of the Student Body Constitution, the Student Body President may remove the Assistant Director from office at President’s discretion.

The selection process for other Executive Bureau personnel shall occur as follows:
The selection process and appointment of all Bureau personnel below the Assistant Director shall be delineated by their individual Chapters in Title XI of Student Body Statutes.
The selection process for Executive Agency Directors shall occur in accordance with Section Four unless otherwise stipulated in their individual rules of procedure, as outlined in Title X of Student Body Statutes.
For all non-elected Agency Director positions, the outgoing Executive Board of Directors of each respective agency may shall choose one (1) nomination by a majority vote for Agency Director and forward said applicant to the Student Body President. The Student Body President will then choose a candidate from the applications forwarded from the Agency Executive Board of Directors and forward said candidate to the Student Senate within ten (10) school days for confirmation.
In the event that the Student Body President feels that any of the candidates are unqualified, an additional candidate search period may be conducted.
Within two (2) weeks of the Director's confirmation, that Director will appoint any non-elected Assistant Director. This appointment shall be ratified by majority vote of the Board and then forwarded to the Student Senate.
In the event that the Agency Directorship is vacated, the Assistant Director shall assume the Directorship and proceed with filling the Assistant Directorship as outlined in Chapter 304.6.
Agency Directors and Assistant Directors who are appointed shall remain in office until they are dismissed, impeached, or upon the installation of their successors.
The selection process for Executive Agency Assistant Directors shall occur as follows:
The Assistant Directors shall be chosen in the same manner as Executive Agency Directors.
The Student Body President may dismiss the Assistant Director. The dismissal may be appealed through the same process as the agency director's termination.
The selection process for Executive Agency personnel shall occur as follows:
Staff appointments shall be made in the manner mandated by the agency's individual Rules of Procedure statute.
The Student Body President may not dismiss any agency staff person below the Assistant Directors that the President have not directly appointed.
The selection process for all other Executive Agency’s Board of Directors shall occur as follows:
Members of the Executive Board of Directors, not including the treasurer and secretary, shall be appointed following the process outlined in each agency’s respective Rules of Procedure statutes.
The terms of all Executive Board members shall last one (1) year.
In accordance with Article III, Section 3 (H) of the Student Body Constitution, the Student Body President may dismiss any Agency Executive Board member, at the President’s discretion, that the President directly appointed.

sections.heading: 2024-02 - Section 7: Vacancies In Elected Positions
sections.text: Vacancies in Elected Positions shall be filled as other positions are, but shall require 2/3 of a Senate quorum for confirmation.

sections.heading: Section 1: Authority And Purpose
sections.text:
A. In accordance with the Student Body Constitution, there shall be a cabinet in the Executive Branch to assist the constitutional officers in the execution of their duties. The Constitution delegates the authority to define the positions and their duties to the Student Body Statutes. 

B. Pursuant to § 301.2, this policy shall outline the cabinet of the Student Body President, including the processes and procedures thereof. The Senate shall adopt this Executive Policy pursuant to Title IV, § 421, upon which this Executive Policy document shall become effective as the governing document of the  Branch.

sections.heading: Section 2: Executive Departments And Positions
sections.text:
A. Pursuant to Title III, § 304, the Student Body President, in the execution of their authority to appoint and dismiss appointed offices of the Student Body, shall have the authority to create a policy pursuant to Title IV, § 421 to regulate specific processes regarding appointment and dismissal. 

B. Department of Academic Affairs
    a. The Department of Academic Affairs ensures student access to high-quality education, research opportunities, and academic resources that enhance student success and career readiness.

    b. Secretary of Academic Affairs

        Director of Grants

        Director of Communications

        Director of Publications

C. Department of Administrative Affairs
    a. The Department of Administrative Affairs ensures the internal organization, structure, and communication of the Executive Branch by facilitating executive appointments, maintaining institutional records, and overseeing the creation of new positions within the administration. 

     b. Secretary of Administrative Affairs
         i. Executive Leadership Program Director

D. Department of Athletics
    a. The Department of Athletics facilitates collaboration between the FSU Athletics Department, student organizations, and student-athletes to promote engagement, enhance school spirit, and ensure strong support for campus athletics. By working closely with key stakeholders, this department seeks to create a unified student-athlete and fan experience while strengthening the relationship between SGA and athletics.

The Department of Campus Life ensures that students have access to engaging extracurricular opportunities, well-maintained recreational facilities, and active student governance within campus life spaces. It works directly with student leaders, university administrators, and campus departments to expand student involvement, improve campus facilities, and advocate for resources that enhance the student experience.
    b. Secretary of Campus Life

Through partnerships, student-led advocacy, and community-centered programming, it ensures that all students, regardless of background, ability, or identity, have equitable access to resources, representation, and opportunity.

sections.heading: Section 3: Executive Agency Positions
sections.text:
A. Pursuant to Title X, §1000.4(a), the supervision and regulation of the agencies is the responsibility of the Student Body Vice President. The Student Body Vice President shall supervise and regulate all agencies, pursuant to Title X, § 1000.4(a).

B. Pursuant to Title X, § 1000.2(c), each Agency shall adopt its own internal “Rules of Procedure” in compliance with the Student Body Constitution and Statutes to further enumerate its organization, administration, and general operating procedures. Each agency shall, pursuant to Title X, § 1000.2(c), adopt internal Rules of Procedure consistent with the Student Body Constitution and Statutes. These Rules of Procedure shall define the agency’s organization, administration, and general operations, shall carry the force of policy under Chapter 421, and shall not require Senate approval for adoption or revision.

C. Pursuant to Title X, § 1000.5, all agencies shall be governed by an executive board composed of no fewer than five (5) student members. Each agency shall include, at a minimum, the following executive board members, who shall be selected internally and confirmed by the Senate: Director, Assistant Director, and Treasurer.

D. Pursuant to Title III, § 300.4(h), and Title IV, § 405.2(a), all Appointed Agency Officers are subject to removal by the Student Body President. Pursuant to Title X, § 1000.7, all Agency Directors, Assistant Directors, and Treasurers are subject to Senate impeachment. Agency Directors,  Assistant Directors, and Treasurers are further subject to Senate impeachment, pursuant to Title X, § 1000.7.

sections.heading: Section 4: Vacancies And Related Procedures
sections.text:
A. Pursuant to Art. III, § 4(1), the Student Body Vice President shall assume the duties of the Student Body President in their absence or upon their request.

B. Pursuant to Art. V, § 1(d), the Student Body President may, for Vacated Elected Positions that were once operated by an elected person, appoint a new person subject to Senate confirmation by a 2/3 vote.

C. Pursuant to Art. VII, § 2, all other vacancies, except those specifically exempted, shall be filled by the Student Body President pursuant to appointment procedures and subject to Senate confirmation by a 2/3 vote.

D. Pursuant to Title III, Chapter 301(4)(b)(4)(B)-(C), all executive appointees shall serve at the pleasure of the Student Body President, and any Secretary vacancies may be remedied by an appointment by the Student Body President. 

E. Pursuant to Title IV, Chapter 404(4), the Student Body President shall ensure the Senate maintains membership of no less than thirty Senators and may appoint Senators to maintain this required threshold. 

F. Pursuant to Title II, Chapter 201(1), the Student Body President may appoint senators to vacant seats.

G. Pursuant to § 301.2, no position requiring Student Senate confirmation may be filled until the position has been advertised properly.
    a. All positions shall be advertised for a minimum of three days on the SGA Website. 

    b. All candidates shall provide the appropriate application as defined in Chapter 307.3, in completed format, demonstrating their qualifications for the position.
    c. The interview shall be conducted in a standardized form for all candidates. 

    d. After all candidates have been interviewed, the Student Body President shall forward the candidate deemed most qualified to the Student Senate for confirmation.
   e. It is the responsibility of the Student Body President, the Secretary of Appointments, or designee to ensure that this process is carried out fairly and constitutionally. In situations where a candidate for any position has a conflict of interest with the interviewer, the interviewer may recuse themselves from the candidate screening process. 
    f. If, during the candidate screening process, the Student Body President finds that a candidate is better suited for another position within the same Student Government entity to which the candidate applied, the Student Body President may reserve the right to forward the candidate, with their consent, for another position for which they meet all Constitutional and statutory requirements.
    i. The forwarding letter sent to the Senate must include a notice in all cases when candidates are forwarded to the Senate for positions that are different from those for which they applied.

H. Pursuant to § 301.2, the Secretary of Appointments, or the Student Body President’s designee, will conduct all candidate searches for positions within the Executive Departments. I. Pursuant to § 301.2, the Student Body President may create any office or position deemed necessary and proper, provided that the Student Senate is notified of the action in writing. J. Pursuant to § 301.2, the Student Body President may appoint an Acting Executive Cabinet Officer who shall serve in the role, but shall not receive compensation, until a nominee can be forwarded to the Student Senate.

K. The Student Body President-elect, as defined in Chapter 704, shall have the power to designate and forward to the Student Senate for confirmation, the Cabinet nominees for their administration after all appeals and violations have been exhausted or ruled on.
     a. The nominees must be confirmed by a majority vote of the Student Senate. 

     b. The confirmed nominee shall be referred to as the "designee" (i.e. Secretary of  Appointments designee).
     c. Upon installation of the Student Body President-elect, all Cabinet Officer designees shall assume the positions for which they were confirmed and all duties, responsibilities, rights, and compensation vested with their position.
