title: Executive Branch: Class Councils Policies

sections.heading: Policy CC-2024-01: Class Councils
sections.text:
HISTORY
Adopted by Res. R76-047 on 4/10/2024

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 1: Authority And Purpose
sections.text:
These rules of procedure shall lay forth the processes and procedures in which the Florida State University Class Councils shall operate internally, as permitted by 302.4 of Student Body Statutes.

The Class Councils shall work to instill unity in the Florida State University’s Senior, Junior, Sophomore, and Freshman classes to enhance their college experience and encourage active participation in the Florida State University community as both students and alumni.
All programming developed by Class Councils must align with the strategic direction and objectives established by SRCC.
The Senior Class Council (SRCC) shall establish annual programming priorities and initiatives. These initiatives must be determined during the semester preceding their intended implementation to ensure sufficient planning and coordination time for all Class Councils.
SRCC reserves the authority to assign specific initiatives, programs, or projects to designated Class Councils as deemed necessary to support organizational goals and ensure effective distribution of responsibilities.
Class Councils shall be responsible for executing assigned initiatives. Within this responsibility, individual councils are granted discretion to design, develop, and implement programming that aligns with the assigned initiative while addressing the unique needs and interests of their respective class.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 2: Revision Procedure
sections.text:
Revisions to this document may be initiated by any member of the Class Councils, and shall require a majority vote of all officers of the Class Councils to be enacted. Revisions shall be adopted immediately upon passage.

Any revisions made shall be sent to the Webmaster within one business day, who shall then post these revisions on the website. This document must be kept up-to-date at all times.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 3: Membership
sections.text:
Under the single identity of The Class Councils, there shall be four Class Councils: the Freshman Class Council (FCC), the Sophomore Class Council (SoCC), the Junior Class Council (JCC), and the Senior Class Council (SrCC), and will be led by the executive board of the Senior Class Council with the guidance of Student Government's Executive Cabinet. 

Membership of the Senior Class Council shall be as follows:

The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the Senior Class Council shall be officers of the SrCC.
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the SrCC shall have at least seventy-two (72) semester credit hours by the semester in which they run for office.
The President, Vice Preaident, Treasurer, and Secretary of the SrCC shall be elected in the Spring Student Government Association elections as stipulated in Chapter 706.8 of the FSU Student Body Statutes.
All officers of the SrCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.

The Members At-Large of the Senior Class shall be representatives of the SrCC.
The Members At-Large of the SrCC shall have at least seventy-two (72) semester credit hours by the semester in which they apply for office.
The Members At-Large of the SrCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Section 4 following the Spring Student Government Association elections.
All representatives of the SrCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.

There shall be no fewer than five (5) and no more than ten (10) Members At-Large of the SrCC.
The SrCC President may establish and assign roles and titles under the Member At-Large position to perform tasks in line with the Class Council's needs, as determined appropriate.
 Membership of the Junior Class Council shall be as follows:
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the Junior Class shall be officers of the JCC.
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the JCC shall have at least forty-two (42) semester credit hours by the semester in which they run for office.
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the JCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Chapter 302.4 following the Spring Student Government Association elections.
All officers of the JCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.

The Members At-Large of the Junior Class shall be representatives of the JCC.

The Members At-Large of the JCC shall have at least forty-two (42) semester credit hours by the semester in which they apply for office.
The Members At-Large of the JCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Section Four following the Spring Student Government Association elections.
All representatives of the JCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.
There shall be no more than ten (10) Members At-Large of the JCC.
The JCC President may establish and assign roles and titles under the Member At-Large position to perform tasks in line with the Class Council's needs, as determined appropriate.
Membership of the Sophomore Class Council shall be as follows:
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the Sophomore Class shall be officers of the SoCC.
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the SoCC shall have at least forty-two (12) semester credit hours by the semester in which they run for office.
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the SoCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Chapter 302.4 following the Spring Student Government Association elections.
All officers of the SoCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.
The Members At-Large of the Senior Class shall be representatives of the SoCC.
The Members At-Large of the SoCC shall have at least twelve (12) semester credit hours by the semester in which they apply for office.
The Members At-Large of the SoCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Section Four following the Spring Student Government Association elections.
All representatives of the SoCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.
There shall be no more than ten (10) Members At-Large of the SoCC.
The SoCC President may establish and assign roles and titles under the Member At-Large position to perform tasks in line with the Class Council's needs, as determined appropriate.
Membership of the Freshman Class Council shall be as follows:
The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the Freshman Class shall be officers of the FCC.

The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the FCC shall be students enrolled in undergraduate studies, who have not completed any collegiate level schooling between their graduation of high school and their enrollment at Florida State University.

The President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary of the FCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Chapter 302.4.
All officers of the FCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.
The Members At-Large of the Freshman Class shall be representatives of the FCC.
The Members At-Large of the FCC shall be students enrolled in undergraduate studies, who have not completed any collegiate level schooling between their graduation of high school and their enrollment at Florida State University.
The Members At-Large of the FCC shall be appointed through the application process as stated in Section Four following the Spring Student Government Association elections.
All representatives of the FCC are to be enrolled as undergraduate students at Florida State University for the entire designated term of service.
There shall be no more than ten (10) Members At-Large of the FCC.
The FCC President may establish and assign roles and titles under the Member At-Large position to perform tasks in line with the Class Council's needs, as determined appropriate.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 4: Selection
sections.text:
The Senior Class Council shall be selected as follows:
All applications to run for the SrCC will follow the deadlines pursuant to Student Body Statutes Chapter 706.3.
Representatives of the SrCC shall be selected by the President of the SrCC with approval by the majority of the remaining officers of the SrCC. At least five (5) representatives of the SrCC shall be approved by the beginning of the Fall Semester.
The Junior Class Council shall be selected as follows: 
All applications for the JCC must be publicly released within thirty (30) days after the Spring Student Government inauguration. The deadline for applications may be postponed, for up to two (2) week under extreme circumstances.
Once the incoming Senior Class has been elected they may, with the Student Body Vice President-elect, begin conducting interviews for the officer positions of the JCC.
Once the incoming SrCC has been inaugurated, the President of the SrCC must, within twenty-one (21) business days, submit nominations for all officer positions of the JCC to the Student Body President and Chief of Staff for appointment, with confirmation by the Student Senate.
Representatives of the JCC shall be selected by the President of the JCC with approval by the majority of the remaining officers of the JCC. Representatives of the JCC shall not be selected or approved until all officers of the JCC have been confirmed.
The Sophomore Class Council shall be selected as follows: 
All applications for the SoCC must be publicly released within thirty (30) days after the Spring Student Government inauguration. The deadline for applications may be postponed, for up to two (2) week under extreme circumstances.
Once the incoming Senior Class has been elected they may, with the Student Body Vice President-elect, begin conducting interviews for the officer positions of the SoCC.
Once the incoming SrCC has been inaugurated, the President of the SrCC must, within twenty-one (21) business days, submit nominations for all officer positions of the SoCC to the Student Body President and Chief of Staff for appointment, with confirmation by the Student Senate.
Representatives of the SoCC shall be selected by the President of the SoCC with approval by the majority of the remaining officers of the SoCC. Representatives of the SoCC shall not be selected or approved until all officers of the SoCC have been appointed.
The Freshman Class Council shall be selected as follows:
All applications for the FCC must be publicly released no later than seven (7) business days before the start of Fall semester classes. Completed applications must be received by the SrCC no later than 5 p.m., thirty (30) business days after the first day of Fall semester classes. The deadline may be postponed for up to one (1) week under extreme circumstances.
The SrCC may begin conducting interviews for the officer positions of the FCC upon the completion of thirty (30) business days into the Fall semester of classes.
Fourteen (14) business days following the close of applications, the SrCC must submit nominations for all officer positions of the FCC to the Student Body President and Chief of Staff for appointment, with confirmation by the Student Senate.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 5: Term Of Office
sections.text:
The officers and representatives of the SrCC shall hold office starting with their inauguration, or their appointment, and ending with the end of the Spring Semester following their inauguration, or the inauguration of a new SrCC, whichever comes first. The officers and representatives of the SrCC shall fundraise and represent the respective graduating classes.
The officers and representatives of the JCC shall hold office starting with their confirmation by the Student Senate, or their appointment, and ending with the end of the Spring Semester following the inauguration of the reigning SrCC, or the confirmation of a new President or Vice President of the JCC, whichever comes first. The officers and representatives of the JCC shall fundraise and represent the respective upcoming graduating classes.
The officers and representatives of the SoCC shall hold office starting with their confirmation by the Student Senate, or their appointment, and ending with the end of the Spring Semester following the inauguration of the reigning SrCC, or the confirmation of a new President or Vice President of the Sophomore Class, whichever comes first. The officers and representatives of the SoCC shall fundraise and represent the respective upcoming graduating classes.
The officers and representatives of the FCC shall hold office starting with their confirmation by the Student Senate, or their appointment, and ending with the end of the Spring Semester following the inauguration of the reigning SrCC, or the confirmation of a new President or Vice President of the Freshman Class, whichever comes first. The officers and representatives of the FCC shall fundraise and represent the respective upcoming graduating classes.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 6: Duties And Responsibilities
sections.text:
The duties and responsibilities of the Senior Class Council shall be as follows:
The SrCC shall strive to keep all Seniors informed and apprised of all graduation requirements and deadlines.
The SrCC shall raise funds for the Senior Class gift.
The SrCC shall provide programming to build community and pride for graduating year and/or benefit of the members of the Senior Class.
The SrCC shall meet at least twice a month.
The SrCC shall provide guidance and information to the Junior, Sophomore, and Freshman Class Councils and students of the university who are interested in being a part of the entity.
The SrCC shall send one of their officers or representatives to give monthly updates to the Student Senate about the current projects and upcoming goals of the FCC, SoCC, JCC, and SrCC.
The duties and responsibilities of the Junior Class Council shall be as follows:
The JCC shall meet with FSU administration to research selection options for their respective gift to the university, which will be a dedication from their class.
The JCC shall raise funds for their upcoming Senior Class gift.
The JCC shall strive to keep all Juniors informed of all upcoming deadlines and requirements, including Graduation Checks.
The JCC shall provide programming to build community and pride for graduation year and/or benefit of the members of the Junior Class.
The JCC shall meet at least twice a month.
The JCC shall provide guidance and information to FSU students who are interested in being a part of the entity.
The duties and responsibilities of the Sophomore Class Council shall be as follows:
The SoCC shall raise funds for their upcoming Senior Class gift.
The SoCC shall provide programming to build community and pride for graduation year and/or benefit of the members of the Sophomore Class.
The SoCC shall meet at least twice a month.
The SoCC shall provide guidance and information to students of the university who are interested in being a part of the entity.
The duties and responsibilities of the Freshman Class Council shall be as follows:
The FCC shall raise funds for their upcoming Senior Class gift
The FCC shall provide programming to build community and pride for their graduation year and/or benefit of the members of the Freshman Class.
The FCC shall meet at least twice a month.
The FCC shall provide guidance and information to students of the university who are interested in being a part of the entity.
The FCC shall ensure a meaningful transition of the new Freshman class into FSU's student body.
The FCC shall not have discretionary spending of A&S monies, and all purchases must be approved by the SrCC Treasurer.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 7: Positional Duties And Responsibilities
sections.text:
The officers of the Senior Class Council shall have the following Duties and Responsibilities:
The President shall:
Preside over and call all meetings of the SrCC.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of all officers and members of the SrCC.
Act as a spokesperson of the Florida State University Senior Class.
Hold a meeting between all the Presidents at least once a month.
The Vice President shall:
Assist the President.
Oversee the progress of the Junior, Sophomore, and Freshman Class Councils.
Assume the duties and responsibilities of the President upon the President’s inability to discharge the duties of office.
The Treasurer shall:
Oversee all fundraising for the SrCC.
Act as the chief financial officer of the SrCC.
Oversee all purchase requests from the FCC Treasurer.
The Secretary shall:
Coordinate all correspondence of the SrCC.
Ensure that accurate minutes are recorded for all meetings and publicized on the SGA Website. The Secretary shall also compile a record documenting the activities of the SrCC for the benefit of future administrations.
Ensure that accurate minutes are recorded by all other Class Council Secretaries, and manage the process of compiling a record for each class’s activities.
The Members-at-Large shall:
Represent the Senior Class in council meetings and at events.
Regularly attend both Senior Class-specific and full Class Council meetings.
Actively support the council's initiatives and participate in school-wide events.
Undertake additional roles or responsibilities as delegated by the Senior Class Council President.
The officers of the Junior Class Council shall have the following Duties and Responsibilities:
The President shall:
Preside over and call all meetings of the JCC.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of all officers and members of the JCC.
Act as a spokesperson of the Florida State University Junior Class.
Work closely and report to the SrCC Vice President with their progress.
The Vice President shall:
Assist the President.
Assume the duties and responsibilities of the President upon the President’s inability to discharge the duties of this office.
The Treasurer shall:
Oversee all fundraising for the JCC.
Act as the chief financial officer of the JCC.
The Secretary shall:
Coordinate all correspondence of the JCC.
Ensure that accurate minutes are recorded for all meetings and publicized on the SGA Website. The Secretary shall also complete a record documenting the activities of the JCC for the benefit of future administrations.
The Members-at-Large shall:
Represent the Junior Class in council meetings and at events.
Regularly attend both Junior Class-specific and full Class Council meetings.
Actively support the council's initiatives and participate in school-wide events.
Undertake additional roles or responsibilities as delegated by the Junior Class Council President.
The officers of the Sophomore Class Council shall have the following Duties and Responsibilities:
The President shall:
Preside over and call all meetings of the SoCC.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of all officers and members of the SoCC.
Act as a spokesperson of the Florida State University Sophomore Class.
Work closely and report to the SrCC Vice President with their progress.
The Vice President shall:
Assist the President.
Assume the duties and responsibilities of the President upon the President’s inability to discharge the duties of this office.
The Treasurer shall:
Oversee all fundraising for the SoCC.
Act as the chief financial officer of the SoCC.
The Secretary shall:
Coordinate all correspondence of the SoCC.
Ensure that accurate minutes are recorded for all meetings and publicized on the SGA Website. The Secretary shall also complete a record documenting the activities of the SoCC for the benefit of future administrations.
The Members-at-Large shall:
Represent the Sophomore Class in council meetings and at events.
Regularly attend both Sophomore Class-specific and full Class Council meetings.
Actively support the council's initiatives and participate in school-wide events.
Undertake additional roles or responsibilities as delegated by the Sophomore Class Council President.
The officers of the Freshman Class Council shall have the following Duties and Responsibilities:
The President shall:
Preside over and call all meetings of the FCC.
Supervise and coordinate the activities of all officers and members of the FCC.
Act as a spokesperson of the Florida State University Freshman Class.
Work closely and report to the SrCC Vice President with their progress.
The Vice President shall:
Assist the President.
Assume the duties and responsibilities of the President upon the President’s inability to discharge the duties of this office.
The Treasurer shall:
Oversee all fundraising for the FCC.
Act as the chief financial officer of the FCC.
Submit purchase requests to the Treasurer of the SrCC.
The Secretary shall:
Coordinate all correspondence of the FCC.
Ensure that accurate minutes are recorded for all meetings and publicized on the SGA Website. The Secretary shall also complete a record documenting the activities of the FCC for the benefit of future administrations.
The Members-at-Large shall:
Represent the Freshman Class in council meetings and at events.
Regularly attend both Freshman Class-specific and full Class Council meetings.
Actively support the council's initiatives and participate in school-wide events.
Undertake additional roles or responsibilities as delegated by the Freshman Class Council President.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 8: Resignations
sections.text:
In order for an officer or representatives of the Class Councils to resign, the resigning person must submit a resignation to the President of their respective council at least two (2) weeks in advance, along with any relevant information in the form of a letter. If the resigning member is the President of the JCC, SoCC, or FCC, they shall submit their resignation to the President of the SrCC. If the resigning member is the President of the SrCC, they shall submit their resignation to the Student Body President.
One (1) week prior to the officer’s final day, the officer shall submit all documents pertaining to the position and shall facilitate a proper transition for the new officer.

sections.heading: 2024-03 - Section 9: Vacancies And Leaves Of Absence
sections.text:
In the event a seat on the SrCC becomes vacant the replacement procedure for said seat will be done in accordance to Chapter 304.
In the event a seat on the JCC, SoCC, or FCC becomes vacant the replacement procedure will be done as follows:
Replacements for a President or Vice President position shall be done as follows:
Applications must open within five (5) school days of an officer renouncing the position.
The application must be advertised for a minimum of ten (10) school days.
Upon the receipt of applications for a vacant position, the interviews will be conducted by the Senior Class Council President, and the remaining members of the respective Class Council, before being forwarded to the Chief of Staff.
After being forwarded by the Chief of Staff, the applicant will be confirmed through Internal Affairs Committee of the Student Senate, with final confirmation on the Senate floor.
Replacements for a Treasurer or Secretary position shall be done as follows:
Applications must open within five (5) school days of an officer renouncing a position.
The application must be advertised for a minimum of ten (10) school days.
After the interviews for said positions have been concluded and a candidate has been chosen by the respective Class Council that person will be appointed by the President of that Class Council at their earliest convenience.
Leaves of absence in the Class Councils shall take place in accordance with the following procedure:
If a member of the Class Councils needs to take a leave of absence in excess of two (2) weeks, a request must be submitted to the Class Council’s Advisor a minimum of five (5) business days before the start of the leave.
If a member of the Class Councils needs to take a leave of absence for less than two (2) weeks, a request must be submitted to the Class Council’s Advisor a minimum of two (2) business days before the start of the leave.”

title: Executive Branch: Agency Rules Of Procedure

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 1 - Creation And Purpose
sections.text:
Creation

This act shall create an agency of the Student Government Association known as the Asian American Student Union (AASU).

Purpose

The AASU shall represent the Asian American community at the Florida State University and promote the spread of awareness pertaining to Asian American heritage and culture. AASU will serve to encourage and promote the civic engagement of the Asian and Asian American community, as well as the student body at the Florida State University. It shall function as an educational and cultural learning instrument for the FSU community, by providing cultural programs and materials, which promote awareness of and appreciation for the various and distinct Asian cultures. AASU shall serve as the nucleus of a network to improve the opportunities and living conditions of the Asian community. To this end, AASU shall represent all registered Asian and Asian American student organizations on campus, coordinate available resources, and serve as a catalyst in protecting the rights and representation of the Asian and Asian American student body.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 2 - Membership
sections.text:
Anti-Discrimintation
No hazing or discrimination will be used as a condition of membership in this organization. Membership shall include all students interested in preserving the rights of Asians; furthering the cultural and ethnic experience within the Asian and Asian American community; and participating in the activities of AASU. This organization agrees to adhere to the University non-discrimination statement: “No University student may be denied membership on the basis of race, creed, color, sex, religion, national origin, age, disability, veteran status, marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or any other protected group status.”
Affiliate Membership
Qualifications
Affiliate Membership is available to all Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) that promote and have an interest in contributing to the Asian Pacific Islander American (APIA) community on campus. RSO’s seeking Affiliate Membership must meet the following requirements: 
Contact the Director with all necessary information outlined in Title X, Section 1000.10 of Student Body Statutes.
A representative must set up an interview with the Director and Assistant Director.
After deliberation from the Director and Assistant Director, the potential new affiliate’s representative(s) will hold a meeting with a majority of all existing Affiliate Member Presidents, in which they present their case for membership and are subject to questioning.
Approval 
Once a RSO applicant is approved by a majority vote of the Executive Board and a majority of all existing Affiliate Member Presidents, the applicant will become an Affiliate Member subject to membership requirements.

Denial 
If a RSO applicant is denied Affiliate membership, the applicant shall wait a full semester before re-applying. Basis for denial constitutes failure of a majority vote at any stage in the Affiliate Membership process detailed above.

Membership Requirements 
Approved Affiliate member organizations are subject to the following requirements: 

Presidents must attend all Affiliate President meetings (see #8), conducted once every month on a date to be set a week in advance by the Assistant Director. 
The Affiliate must send at least two representatives to each semester’s Affiliate Summit.
A representative of the affiliate must communicate intent for membership renewal to the Director and Assistant Director in April of each year, before the appointment of a new administration.
Abide by the semesterly affiliate calendar when scheduling events.

Revoked Membership 
Revoked membership constitutes any Affiliate Member who is no longer in good standing and has failed to comply with the AASU Affiliated requirements stated prior (see #4). A three-strike system will be implemented with the following course of action. 
After the first infraction: Verbal warning with internal AASU documentation. 
After the second infraction: Written notice and meeting with AASU Director and Assistant director. 
After the third infraction: Meeting with the AASU Director, Assistant Director, AASU Advisor, Affiliate President and Affiliate Advisor. If another infraction is committed, the organization will be revoked of its Affiliate membership. 

Resignation 
The Affiliate Member no longer wishing to be affiliated with AASU must submit a letter to the Assistant Director with any relevant information as well as schedule an Exit Interview with the Director, Assistant Director, and the AASU Advisor. 

Meetings 
Meetings will be held on a monthly basis with the Assistant Director and the President of each Affiliate organization. If the President is unable to attend, this individual may appoint an officer with their organization to attend in their absence.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 3 - Executive Board
sections.text:
Membership

The Executive Board of AASU, hereinafter referred to as the “Board,” shall consist of at least nine (9) student members and shall include the Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, Secretary, Public Relations Coordinator, Programming Coordinator, Education Coordinator, Historian, and Outreach Coordinator. All members of the Board shall be voting members, with the exception of the Director. 
There shall be a staff or administrative advisor of AASU. The advisor shall be a non-voting ex-officio member of the Board.
Selection and Term of Office
Selection 
Each year, the new Director and Assistant Director shall be selected by a voting committee composed of that year’s Board members who are not applying for either position. The outgoing Director will not have a vote, but will participate in interviews and deliberation.

Once confirmed, the new Director shall forward nominees for Treasurer and Secretary for Student Senate confirmation. 

Term of Office

The Director and Assistant Director shall each serve a one year term, with the option of the summer session. The Director’s term of office shall take effect one week after appointment, and end one week after confirmation of the new Director the following year, notwithstanding extensions as may be required by the Student Body Constitution. 

The Director may be re-nominated at the end of the term of office by the Board and may be reappointed by the Student Body President for a second term of office. The Director shall serve a maximum limit of two terms of office. 

The term of office for the Board members shall be one year. Board members, including the Assistant Director, shall not be limited to the number of terms they may serve. After their year term, to be reappointed, they must go through the initial procedures.

Powers and Duties of the Executive Board
The Executive Board shall approve decisions on policy, procedure and activities as suggested by the Director.
In the absence of the Director, the Assistant Director shall preside over the Executive Board.
Responsibilities
The responsibilities of each respective officer shall include, but not be limited to the following:
The Director shall:
Represent the interest of AASU on the campus of Florida State University in accordance with the Statement of Purpose. 
Be responsible for the agency's daily operation. 
Be the Executive head of all functions, meetings, or any related activities concerning the AASU, with the approval of the Board. 
Create ad hoc and standing committees as needed to deal with specific needs. 
Make and execute decisions on policy, procedure, programs and activities with the advice of the Board. 
Preside over all Board, informational and general membership meetings and shall have the authority to call such meetings. 
Have the authority to appoint and remove staff members. 
Execute and be responsible for submitting in a timely manner, all budget requests and other forms, documents and reports as required. 
Reserve the right to delegate responsibilities to other Board members, within their respective positions, necessary for the growth of the AASU. 
Shall serve as an ex-officio member of the Office of Governmental Affairs Agency Advisory Committee or appoint a designee. 
The Assistant Director shall:

Exercise the authority and duties of the Director in the absence of the Director. 
Oversee all ad hoc and standing committees. 

Assist the Director with the agency's daily operation. 

Update the Board with any new information and changes concerning AASU related activities, functions and meetings. 

Sign official documents along with the Director as required in their respective capacity. 

Work with affiliate leadership and conduct monthly meetings set at least a week in advance.

Act as a liaison between all of the affiliates of AASU, and set up internal affairs meetings as needed.
The Secretary shall:

Write all the minutes for all AASU meetings.

Maintain a collective set of minutes for AASU meetings to be turned in to the new Secretary following the eleciton of officers.

Maintain a membership roll and record of the attendance at Board Meetings as well as the membership roll of each active AASU affiliate.

Call for correspondence of the AASU except when otherwise delegated.
Oversee the organization of AASU's internal calendar.

Excercise the authority and duties of the Director in the absence of the Director and Assistant Director.

The Treasurer shall:
Maintain and submit all necessary requests regarding the funds of the AASU. 
Monitor and report the financial status of the AASU to the Executive Board and the Student Government Association. 
Conduct inventory of the AASU office space, located in the Student Union, at the beginning of each new administration in collaboration with AASU’s affiliates.
The Public Relations Coordinator shall:

Be responsible for all agency communication
Advertise and promote all AASU-related activities including but not limited to emails, tabling and any other form that they deem needed.
Keep a visual record documenting all AASU-related meetings, functions, and activities including, but not limited to, documentaries, videos, scrapbooks, and any other means of documentation demonstrating creativity and uniqueness to AASU.
Update as needed the AASU webpage and social media accounts as needed with details of upcoming events and a review of past AASU sponsored activities.
The Programming Coordinator(s) shall:
Plan all AASU-related activities, with the assistance of executive board members.
Oversee the Event Planning committee in the planning of AASU-related activities (events with which the committee might assist may include, but are not limited to: Homecoming, Lunar Banquet, Halloween Social, etc.).
Make recommendations to the public relations officer concerning the betterment of advertisement and promotion.
The Education Coordinator shall:
Gather local, state, and Student Government issues which concern the Asian and Asian American community.
Develop educational General Body Meetings at least once per semester.
Oversee the Social Advocacy committee in any endeavors for the year.
The Historian shall:
Assist the Public Relations Coordinator in the execution of their duties.
Initiate all video projects.
Maintain AASU social media presence.
Maintain information for AASU archives.
Oversee the Multimedia committee.
The Outreach Coordinator shall:
Plan all external events and co-sponsorships with other RSOs, agencies, and bureaus.
Maintain relationships with all agencies.
Work closely with the Programming Coordinator(s) on collaborative projects.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 4 - Removal From Office
sections.text:
Executive Board
All Board members are subject to removal at any time by two thirds (2/3) vote of all Board members.
Director
The Board may, by two-thirds (2/3) vote of its members, recommend the removal of the Director to the Student Body President after consultation with the Advisor. Only then will the Student Body President decide upon the dismissal of the Director.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 5 - Vacancies
sections.text:
Executive Board

Any position made vacant shall be advertised for three (3) days. The applicants shall be interviewed by the remaining Board members and selected by a majority vote. If there should be a tie, the Director shall break the tie by voting, and appoint the individual to the vacant position. Should the Board fall below quorum, the Board may meet only for the purpose of selecting new members.
Director

Upon vacancy of the Director’s position, the Assistant Director shall assume the office and appoint a new Assistant Director.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 6 - Meetings
sections.text:
Board Meetings

Board meetings shall be held weekly or biweekly, at the discretion of the Director and Assistant Director.
Meetings of the Board shall be called by the Director or upon written request of at least a majority of the Board members. 
Notification of all regularly scheduled AASU Board meetings shall be given at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the designated meeting time.
The Board may take no official action unless a quorum is present.
Regular Information and General Membership Meetings 
Regular meetings shall be held once a month. The time and date shall be publicly advertised.
Meetings are to be open to the general public and shall be publicly advertised.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 7 - Finances
sections.text:
Spending

For the protection of the organization and its officers it is required that two authorized signatures sign all purchase requests. Only the Director, Assistant Director, and Treasurer can be signers on the organization’s account. Organizational funds may be spent on items such as office supplies, events/activities, publicity, travel expenses, conference fees, etc., but will not be used for anything illegal under University, local, state, and federal laws.

Certification
The Director, Assistant Director, and Treasurer must be financially certified through the Student Government Association.

sections.heading: Policy AASU: Section 8 - Publications
sections.text:
Comliance
All advertisements of the organization must comply with the University Posting Policy (http://posting.fsu.edu).
Approval
The Director and Assistant Director must approve all publications, shirts, flyers, etc. prior to duplication and distribution.

sections.heading: Policy JSU: Section 1 - Mission Statement
sections.text: The Jewish Student Union (JSU) is a Student Government Agency belonging to Florida State University. The Jewish Student Union at Florida State University is committed to creating an environment for students to learn, embrace, and celebrate Jewish culture. The Jewish Student Union shall serve the Jewish community as a unifying organization through its Advisory Council, which is made up of other Registered Student Organizations. The JSU will represent the Jewish community to the Student Government Association, Administration, and Tallahassee community. We aspire to foster an inclusive community to engage the student body in meaningful programming. Through educational initiatives, cultural celebrations, and social events, the JSU strives to cultivate a vibrant space that empowers individuals to deepen their understanding of Judaism.

sections.heading: Policy JSU: Section 2 - Executive Board
sections.text:
Membership
The Executive Board of Directors shall consist of an Executive Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, Secretary, Director of Outreach, Director of Programming, & Director of Marketing.

There shall be a staff or administrative advisor of JSU. The advisor shall be a non-voting ex-officio member of the Executive Board.
Qualifications. The qualifications are as follows:

Students in good standing at FSU with a minimum 2.0 GPA.

Have an interest in promoting and contributing to the Jewish culture and community on campus.
Any other qualifications listed either within the Jewish Student Union Rules of  Procedure or indicated in Student Body Statues.
Selection. The selection process is as follows:

After the Student Government Spring Election, the current Advisory Council of the Jewish Student Union will open applications for the Executive Board of the Jewish Student Union. This includes the positions of: Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, Secretary, Director of Outreach, Director of Programming, & Director of Marketing. After reviewing applications, conducting interviews, and any other selection process that the Advisory Council deems fit, the Advisory Council will vote to select the next Jewish Student Union Board of Directors. The candidate who recieves the majority of the vote of the Advisory Council shall be appointed to their respective positions.

If a current Advisory Council Member is running for the Board of Directors on the following year’s Board, that individual may not be present at any interviews, shall not participate in any selection processes, and shall not cast a vote. Such persons shall not count towards quorum.
For the positions of Executive Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, Secretary, and any other positions subject to forwarding by the Student Body President and confirmation by the Student Senate, their selection shall be considered as an official recommendation to the Student Body President for forwarding.
Following the confirmation of the Executive Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, and Secretary, applications will open for any other board positions deemed necessary by a majority vote of the Advisory Council.
Potential board positions include Greek Life Coordinator, Market Wednesday Coordinator, Market Wednesday Coordinator, Public Relations Coordinator, and Jewish Heritage Month Coordinator. These positions report to their respective member on the Board of Directors. 

Powers and Duties of the Executive Board
The Executive Board shall work towards identifying, developing, and monitoring programs and initiatives that address the needs of the Jewish community, thereby increasing the awareness of and sensitivity to issues among non-Jewish and Jewish students in accordance with but not limited to the Statement of Purpose as stated in 100.1 of this Rules of Procedure.

The Executive Director shall:
Serve as the Chief Executive of all functions, meeting and any related activities concerning the JSU.
Assist the Treasurer in financial activities as needed.
Have the power to implement ad-hoc committees.
Oversee the appointment of all chairpersons and assign organizational duties as necessary.
Be in constant communication with the Executive Branch and Legislative Branch of the Student Government Association.
Act as an official representative of JSU to the campus community.
Serve as the Chair of the Advisory Council.
Be financially certified by SGA.
Serve as an ex officio member of the Office of Governmental Affairs Agency Advisory Committee or appoint a designee.
Attend Council of President’s Meetings. 
The Assistant Director shall:
Support the Executive Director as needed.
Oversee educational programs and initiatives.
Become acting Executive Director in situations where the Executive Director is unable to serve.
Be financially certified by SGA.
The Treasurer shall:
Document and allocate money, keep accounts, deposit funds, and make expenditures.
Oversee petty cash distributions and authorize disbursement of funds.
Make regular budget reports at executive board an general body meetings.
Represent the JSU to the SGA in all budget and funding concerns, allocations, or presentations.
Oversee the budget of the Jewish Student Union.
Be financially certified via SGA.
The Secretary shall:
Record all meeting minutes and distribute them as needed. This may include but is not limited to: Executive Board meetings, Advisory Council meetings, General Body meetings, and more.
Coordinate the transition of Jewish Student Union Executive Board and Advisory Council appointments and elections.
Maintain and updated JSU active member roster.
Track projects being completed by Executive Board members.
The Director of Outreach shall:
Serves as the point of contact between JSU and external organizations.
Responsible for sharing our events with students.
Must maintain the JSU roster on NoleCentral.
Works with the Director of Marketing to share all communications.
Manage respective Coordinators.
The Director of Programming shall:
Responsible for planning and executing all programs
Create calendar of events for the year alongside Secretary
Creates social, educational and cultural programs for JSU
Manage respective Coordinators
The Director of Marketing shall:
Coordinates social media, merchandize, and promotional graphics for the organization
Maintain a strong social media presence and promote events
Oversee all external Marketing material including but not limited to: 
Graphics
Presentations
Posters 
Promotional materials
Videos 
Manage respective coordinators
Board Meetings
Board meetings shall be held at least twice a month.
Board Meetings shall be called by the Executive Director or upon the written request by a majority of the Board. 
Notification of all board meetings shall be given at least 48 hours in advance of the designated meeting time.
The Board may take no official action unless quorum is met.
Vacancies
Any position made vacant shall be advertised for at least ten (10) business days. The applicants shall be interviewed in accordance with Statute 1008.5 (c).

sections.heading: Policy JSU: Section 3 - Committees
sections.text:
Membership

Committees shall be open to all Jewish Student Union members. The committees shall be formed at the discretion of the Jewish Student Union Executive Board, with Chairs appointed to lead a committee through an application process.
Committees may include:
The Cultural and Spiritual Experiences Committee
The Service Committee
The Social Committee
The Education Committee
The Outreach Committee
Greek Committee Ad Hoc Committees created as needed
Committee Chairs
Qualifications
All Committee Chairs must be currently enrolled students at the Florida State University.
No member of the executive board may be Chairperson of a Committee.
Powers and Duties
Preside over committee meetings.
Create a typed agenda for every committee meeting.
Turn in a monthly report to the Secretary of JSU regarding all activities the committee discussed or participated in during the past month.
Notify committee members at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the designated meeting time.
Take minutes and attendance of all meetings and turn in a copy of both the agenda and minutes to the Secretary of JSU within forty-eight (48) hours following the meeting.
Selection and Term of Office
Chairpersons shall be selected by the Executive Board at the beginning of the fall and spring semesters or as needed.	
Meeting
Individual committees shall meet at least once a month. A record of attendance and committee business shall be kept at all committee meetings.
Powers and Duties of Committees
Ad Hoc Committees
Shall be formed as needed to advance the purpose of the JSU as stated in Statute 1008.1, Section (b).

sections.heading: Policy JSU: Section 4 - The Advisory Council
sections.text:
Purpose
The Advisory Council’s purpose is to ensure the success of and foster collaboration among all Jewish student organizations.

Composition:
The Advisory Council shall consist of all the Executive Board members of the Jewish Student Union and representatitves from any RSO that are approved for affiliate membership.
Representatives from RSOs may not be JSU Board members.
The Executive Director of the JSU shall serve as the chair of the Advisory Council.

Any Recognized Student Organization (RSO) that has an interest in contributing to the Jewish culture and community on campus may submit a written request to the Executive Director to become a member of the Advisory Council.
Approval: RSO applicants shall be approved by a majority (50% plus one) of all existing Advisory Council representatives. Upon approval, one member from the approved RSO will be appointed to the Advisory Council.
Denial: Denied RSO applicants shall wait a full semester before re-applying.
Membership Term Length
Members of the Advisory Council shall serve from when they are admitted on the Council to the end of the current JSU Executive Board’s term, after which they can apply to renew their membership.

Membership Requirements
A representative of the member RSO must attend all Advisory Council meetings. If they are unable to attend, they should notify the Chair of the Advisory Council 24 hours in advance.
At each Advisory Council, all member RSOs and the JSU Executive Director will give a report about the RSO's status.
Membership Renewal, Revocation, and Resignation

Renewal
In order to maintain their seat on the Advisory Council, each RSO member must email the Executive Director of the JSU within four weeks of the start of their term with their intent to remain a member of the Advisory Council.
Revocation
Any Advisory Council member who does not participate in Advisory Council proceedings may be removed by a 2/3 vote of the Advisory Council. Member RSOs may also be removed by a 2/3 vote for committing egregious acts.
Resignation
Any RSO no longer wishing to be a member of the Advisory Council must submit a letter to the Executive Director of the JSU with any relevant information.

Reinstatement
If an RSO has resigned or had their membership revoked from the Advisory Council and wishes to be reinstated, the RSO may be reinstated per Statute 1008.5 (b) no less than one semester after leaving the Council.
Meetings
The Advisory Council shall meet at least once each semester on a date to be set at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance.

sections.heading: Policy JSU: Section 5 - Removal From Office
sections.text:
Non-Confirmed Executive Board Member
All Executive Board members not confirmed by the Student Senate are subject to removal at any time by a 2/3 vote of the Executive Board.
Confirmed Executive Board Members
The Advisory Council may, by a 2/3 vote of its members, recommend the removal of the Executive Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, Secretary, and any other confirmed member of the Executive Board to the Student Body President.
The recommendation provided to the Student Body President for removal must be in writing and include reasons for the removal.

sections.heading: Policy JSU: Section 6 - Rules Of Procedure
sections.text:
Beginning of the Executive Board Term
At the beginning of each Executive Board Term, the current JSU Executive Board will vote to adopt the Rules of Procedure. This must be done with a majority vote, regardless of if there are revisions.
No official actions may be taken by the JSU Executive Board or Advisory Council until a Rules of Procedure are adopted.
The JSU Advisory Council will operate under the previous Executive Board's Rules of Procedure through the board selection process.
If any revisions are deemed necessary, the JSU Executive Director will call a meeting of the Executive Board, or 1/2 of the membership of the Executive Board can petition for a meeting. These edits must be read at this meeting and followed with pro/con debate. The edits will be adopted by a majority vote.

sections.heading: Policy WSU: Section 1 - Mission Statement
sections.text: The purpose of the Women Student Union (WSU) shall serve to develop a greater awareness in the Florida State University community of women’s rights and issues and their relationship to the economic, social, and political nature of society. The Women Student Union of the Florida State University values struggles of the past, asserts rights in the present, and celebrates aspirations for the future. The Women Student Union fosters the growth of women personally, professionally, and politically. The WSU will celebrate the power existing within every woman to promote self-autonomy, denounce all limitations, educate on systems of oppression and advocate inclusivity within a diverse community. WSU facilitates a network among organizations, departments, and services to embrace, engage and empower. The Women Student Union shall be limited neither to the aforementioned objectives nor to the Florida State University in scope. It shall serve to promote a positive approach towards women’s concerns in the Florida State University community. The Women Student Union will develop programs, services, and activities that will reach out to women and will connect students to administration, faculty, and staff to create a feeling of strength and solidarity within the Florida State University community. It shall empower women in the Florida State University community by actively confronting sexual discrimination, teaching leadership skills, encouraging involvement and promoting advocacy. The agency will function as an educational and cultural learning instrument for students, administration, faculty and staff. It shall serve as a nucleus for a network with other women-centered organizations to improve the opportunities and conditions of women on campus and in the community. The agency shall provide a centralized coordination of resources and services for women. It shall be open and accessible to everyone, and will strengthen the connection between Florida State University and the Tallahassee Community.

Creating and advertising applications, selecting the committee, training the committee, coordinating meeting times, overseeing projects and delegating tasks, and responsible for the overall function and output of the committee
Organize monthly community service events and develop relationships with service organizations in the Tallahassee community
Organize donation drives for the WSU
Ex. Menstrual product drive, clothing drive, food drive
Must have 1 per term
Engage in the greater Tallahassee community by establishing connections with women owned businesses, women leaders, and women centered organizations and programs within the community
Coordinate with the Secretary to keep a record of volunteers and their hours
The Term of the External Affairs Coordinator will begin when they send their acceptance of the position and will expire when applications for the executive board are posted

Political Education Coordinator
Maintain a high level of understanding regarding current US and FSU events, especially those pertaining to womxn
Provide a weekly update on current politics at e-board meetings
Coordinate with other agencies and RSOs to educate about civic engagement
Publicize civic involvement opportunities for students’ participation like voter registration events
Hold events that pertain to, and advocate for, women’s concerns
Attend SGA/senate meetings on behalf of WSU or coordinate with the Senate Liaison to provide an update of any policy that could potentially impact women on campus or the WSU and our function or purpose
The Term of the Political Education Coordinator will begin when they send their acceptance of the position and will expire when applications for the executive board are posted

Women's History Month Coordinator(s)
Responsible for developing the overall Women’s History Month Programming Calendar
With the support of the executive board, manage all details of events and programs for the month of March
Select a committee and serve as the chair of the Women’s History Month Committee, including
Creating and advertising applications, selecting the committee, training the committee, coordinating meeting times, overseeing projects and delegating tasks, and responsible for the overall function and output of the committee
Collaborate with the External Affairs and OWL Coordinators to find co-sponsorships for programming events with women-centered organizations, departments, and registered student organizations
Serve on campus committees and attend various events or meetings of other women’s centered organizations and campus departments to develop relationships
The Term of the Women’s History Month Coordinator will begin when they send their acceptance of the position and will expire when applications for the executive board are posted

Design Coordinator
Design posts in a timely manner, and create a social media aesthetic
Coordinate with the PR Coordinator for the posting
Design and create merchandise for the Women Student Union and oversee the process of getting funding for, ordering, and obtaining merchandise
Both general merchandise and merchandise for Women’s History Month
Coordinate with the Finance Coordinator/Treasurer to finance merchandise
Plan events or smaller marketing campaigns for social media content and highlighting women in the community and members of the WSU
Create promotional content to be used on WSU social media
Take pictures at events and market wednesdays highlighting our organization, affiliates, and our mission
Responsibility is shared with the PR Coordinator and Historian

Membership Coordinator

Maintain a current membership roster on Nole Central
Must plan at least 2 events per semester (not including co sponsorships or tablings)
Responsible for all Market Wednesday tabling, including weekly registration, coordinating schedules with executive board, and membership committee
Coordinate with the Design Coordinator to issue the monthly newsletter, The Voice, via email that details WSU’s and OWL affiliate’s events and programming for the month
Plan social events each semester for members and students at FSU
Coordinate with the Programming Coordinators and External Affairs
Manage WSU outreach functions that grow our membership and presence on campus
Includes Market Wednesdays and Involvement Fairs
Collaborate with External Affairs and Programming Coordinators to do so
Select a committee and serve as the chair of the Membership Committee
Creating and advertising applications, selecting the committee, training the committee, coordinating meeting times, overseeing projects and delegating tasks, and responsible for the overall function and output of the committee
Take attendance at events
This is a shared responsibility with Secretary or whoever is heading that specific event

Historian/HerVoice Coordinator

Document all WSU events and take pictures at Market Wednesdays, volunteering events, GBMs, and more with the support of the executive board
Create a scrapbook throughout the year to be released at the end of the Administration’s term, which documents the progress throughout the year
Collaborate with the Public Relations Coordinator and the Design Coordinator as needed
Create the Her Voice Magazine (released at the end-of-year banquet)

Coordinate with Student Pubs
Coordinate with Student Pubs to put together the Magazine and get it printed
Student Pubs is also available for photography services
Select a committee and serve as the chair of the HerVoice Committee, including
Creating and advertising applications, selecting the committee, training the committee, coordinating meeting times, overseeing projects and delegating tasks, and responsible for the overall function and output of the committee
Collaborate with PR Coordinator to plan and execute an e-board photoshoot/headshot op for the SGA website and other social medias
The Term of the HerVoice Coordinator will begin when they send their acceptance of the position and will expire when applications for the executive board are posted

sections.heading: Policy WSU: Section 3 - General Rules Of Procedure
sections.text:
Be respectful to all executive board members
If someone asks you to do something, do it in a timely manner
Requests made by the Director or Assistant Director should be completed within 3 business days unless otherwise specified
Attend weekly executive board meetings
All Executive Board members must attend a great majority (70%) of Executive Board meetings
No official action may be taken at these meetings unless a quorum is present
Executive Board members are expected to submit their notes to the Secretary to be included in the agenda 24 hours prior to the Executive Board Meeting.
If a board member is going to be late, they shall notify the Director, Assistant Director, or Secretary know beforehand
If 20 minutes pass in the meeting, is will be considered an unexcused absence
If you are going to be absent, let the Director, Assistant Director, or Secretary know at least 24 hours in advance
Must provide a valid reason for absence that is approved (this is at the discretion of the Director, Assistant Director, and Secretary)
Respect the WSU office space by cleaning up after any mess made in the office, refraining from using WSU possessions for personal use, being productive during office hours, etc.
Attendance is expected for all events (GBMs, Let’s Talk Events, Volunteering with WSU, Tablings, etc.)
An excuse must be provided 48 hours or more before an event and must be approved by the Secretary, Director, and Assistant Director before the event.
Secretary will keep track of attendance at all events, including executive board attendance to make sure this requirement is being fulfilled.
Each Executive Board member must host at least 1 event per semester

This can be a GBM, Let’s Talk, Event, Social Hour, or a Co-sponsorship with heavy WSU involvement
Exceptions must be approved by the Director or Assistant Director
Event delegation for Women’s History Month may count towards individual event requirements for non-event centered roles
Only Programming Coordinators, External Affairs, and Membership Coordinator will be expected to have their own events outside of WHM in the spring semester weekly executive board meetings
Everyone else on the board is good for their semester event with a WHM event as long as the WHM Coordinators approve after that adequate work was done
It is the responsibility of the Membership Coordinator and Programming Coordinators to make sure that WSU is holding at least 1 GBM per month
Preferably 2 or more programming events per month (at least 1 or more non-co-sponsored events)

Check-ins

 Every Executive Board member will be expected to have a training meeting with the Director, Assistant Director and the Advisor (2⁄3 must be present) to be trained for their position and ask any questions
This is a good time to pitch any event ideas or goals for the position
1 on 1 check-ins with the Director or 2 on 1 check-ins with the Director and Assistant Director should be completed 2x a semester to give a general report, receive a performance review, address questions or concerns, receive feedback or advice, and discuss new projects

Executive Board members are expected to serve 2 Office Hours weekly, which should be dedicated to working on WSU projects, collaborations, keeping the office space welcoming and tidy, or preparing for physical events if necessary. These office hours must be served in the office unless otherwise specified (by contacting the Director, Secretary, and Advisor; and these hours will be expected to be made up within the next two weeks)
Some positions will be more demanding, especially if that position has a committee they need to manage or extra duties. These hours will count toward office hour time, but some people may expect to be physically in the office more than others may need to be
Executive board members are not limited to two hours per week, and can spend time in the office outside of office hours, BUT each executive board must have two hours worth of work to show for the week
Secretary will keep track of board’s scheduled office hours and attendance
Resignation
If at any point an Executive Board member feels they do not wish to be on the Executive Board any longer, an Exit Interview with the Director and Advisor must be arranged and a 2 week written notice shall be provided

sections.heading: Policy WSU: Section 4 - Officer Selection
sections.text:
The entire executive board will be involved in the selection of the Executive Director, this process is outlined in 304.6.A of the Uniform Agency Act
Executive Director applications will be posted February 15 or the closest business day and will be open for 14 days per SGA regulations
Current Executive Director and Assistant Director will take 1-2 weeks of deliberation and decide on a candidate to be forwarded
The current Director, Assistant Director, and Upcoming Director (after they have been confirmed) will collaborate in the decision for the candidate of Assistant Director
After the Executive Director is confirmed, they have 14 days to decide on an Assistant Director and forward them
Applications will be posted for 2 or more weeks on the SGA website, we will advertise for application openings at or before the date they are opened
Interviews will be granted to everyone who applied for a position on the board and will be conducted by the Director and Assistant Director, with the Faculty Advisor assisting in the process as needed
The same questions will be asked to all candidates, with one question that differs depending on whether or not the applicant has held a position on the board before or not
If an applicant is a ‘no-show’ or cancels within 12 hours of their interview two times, they will not be granted a third interview opportunity and will be removed from consideration
After every interview, the interviewer(s) will write down notes about the interview overall and judge whether or not they would be a good candidate for their preferred positions, and then whether or not they would be a good candidate for other positions on the board
The Director and Assistant Director will meet to deliberate about the board and unanimously decide on a board with the Advisor’s guidance
Candidates will be emailed with the position they are being offered and given a deadline of more than 48 hours to respond and confirm their acceptance
All rejected candidates will receive a notice after the board has confirmed their positions that they will not be offered a position
In this email, an interest form regarding Committees or Womxn’s Initiative will be sent out to ensure candidates have another opportunity for involvement and leadership within the agency

sections.heading: Policy WSU: Section 5 - Officer Removal
sections.text:
All executive board members are subject to removal by a ⅔ vote, with the exception of the Director and Assistant Director who must be impeached through the senate or by the Student Body President
Removal is defined as an executive board member being relieved of their position, they will no longer be part of the Executive Board and applications for the position that was previously held will be opened again
If the Director and Assistant Director unanimously agree that a board member should be removed, a meeting must be held with the party subject to removal where options are outlined (resignation, senate vote or executive vote)
A 2-week notice shall be given to the Director and Assistant Director if the board member is requesting removal or resigning from the board
An exit interview shall be conducted with at least two of the following positions: Director, Assistant Director, and Faculty Advisor
Confirmed positions must be removed through a ⅔ vote by the Executive Board and then removed by the Student Body President
Vacancies due to removal will be filled the same way as the regular Executive Board selection process, but only that specific position will be opened
A “Three Strike” policy will be in effect
Two Infractions are equal to 1 Strike
Major issues will be considered 1 Strike
Director and Assistant Director will keep track of Infractions and Strikes
This will be recorded for members to see and keep track of their status, but it will not be disclosed to Executive Board members other than the offender
Any party who has been issued a Strike or Infraction will be notified immediately after a decision is made
There will be an opportunity for a meeting with the Director or Assistant Director to discuss the consequences of a Strike or Infraction as well as why it was received, as well as to create a plan of action moving forward

Distribution of Infractions and Strikes
Both the Director and Assistant Director shall decide together whether or not an incident is worthy of an Infraction but the overseer is the deciding vote
Director oversees Secretary, Treasurer, Membership Coordinator, Programming Coordinators, Women’s History Month Coordinators
Assistant Director oversees Historian, Design Coordinator, PR Coordinator, Political Education Coordinator, OWL Coordinator, and External Affairs Coordinator
Director and Assistant Director must unanimously decide if an offense is worthy of an entire Strike
An Infraction may be
Not notifying the Director, Assistant Director, or Secretary of an absence 24 hours
before an executive board meeting
Not attending 3 WSU events per semester
Not holding your pre-ordained number of events per semester
Not scheduling or attending check-ins 2x a semester
Not completing a specific task by a certain deadline or in a timely manner (asked 2x and it is still not done)
This will not be an Infraction if it is out of your control (ex. not being able to get something scheduled due to a delayed response by the other party)
Being uncooperative and an unwilling participant on the board
Being disrespectful of someone's time
Disrespecting someone’s boundaries more than once
Scoring below a 50% on a check-in with the Director
Anything else within the discretion of the Director and Assistant Director

A Strike may be
Not showing up to your own event and giving no notice
Saying that you will go to something on behalf of WSU and not showing up
Missing a major deadline
Any excessive problems or delegation of tasks that are your position
Being outright disrespectful to another executive board member or staff member
Forgetting to show up to a committee meeting that you are supposed to be leading
Scoring below a 25% on a check-in with the director
Anything else within the discretion of the Director and Assistant Director

FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY

STUDENT GOVERNMENT ASSOCIATION

STUDENT BODY STATUTES

sections.heading: Chapter 100
sections.text:
NOTE: Student Senate Bill #78-043 made revisions to this Chapter which will become effective on December 1, 2026.

There will be eleven titles, each dealing with related and similar topics, and each composed of a number of numerically designated chapters, as follows:

TITLE I
	(100-199)
	Statutory Framework and Compliance
TITLE II
	(200-299)
	Membership, Powers, and Duties

TITLE III
	(300-399)
	The Executive Branch

TITLE IV
	(400-499)
	The Legislative Branch

TITLE V
	(500-599)
	The Judicial Branch

TITLE VI
	(600-699)
	Organizations and Extra Curricular Activities

TITLE VII
	(700-799)
	The Election Code

TITLE VIII	(800-899)	The Finance Code
TITLE IX
	(900-999)
	The Executive Agencies

TITLE X
	(1000-1099)
	The Affiliated Projects

Statutory Formatting:
Each Chapter may be subdivided by means of a decimal arrangement. For instance, Chapter 100 may be divided into sections 100.1, 100.2, 100.3, etc. Each section may, in turn, be subdivided in the following order, so that as many subsections are obtained as necessary. Paragraphs shall be designated by lowercase letters followed by a period, as this paragraph is.
Subparagraphs shall be designated by Arabic numerals in parentheses, as this subparagraph is.
Sub-subparagraphs shall be designated by uppercase letters in parentheses, as this sub-subparagraph is.
Sub-sub-subparagraphs shall be designated by lowercase letters in parentheses, as this sub-sub-subparagraph is.
Each section or subsection in the statutes shall have printed a history giving the Senate and Bill numbers in which it was amended. Further history of these and previously repealed chapters may be found in the Archive Book on Municode.
All Student Body officers must comply with the Student Body Statutes. Willful and deliberate disregard of these Statutes and/or section thereof shall be grounds of impeachment in accordance with Article VII, Section 3 of the Student Body Constitution.
Major Offices:
Definitions:
Director - The chief executive of an entity.
Assistant Director - The individual who would assume the role of the chief executive of an entity in the absence of the chief executive.
Treasurer - The individual in charge of monitoring the finances of an entity.

The definitions listed in this statute shall include any positions which fit the criteria of the definition.
Within the Student Body the following elected or appointed offices shall be considered major offices:
Student Body President
Student Body Vice President
Student Body Treasurer
Student Body Attorney General
Members of the Executive Office of the President
Members of the Office of the Vice President
Members of the Office of the Treasurer
The Executive Cabinet

Executive Department Directors
Executive Branch Coordinators and Operational Staff
Directors, Assistant Directors, and Treasurers of Agencies
Student Senators
Congress of Graduate Students Representatives
Office of the Student Body Attorney General

Union Board Members
Campus Recreation Board Members
Justices of the Student Supreme Court
SGA General Counsels
Clerk of the Court
Supervisor of Elections
Deputy Supervisors of Elections
President and Vice President of each Class Council, and Treasurer and Secretary of the Senior Class Council
Homecoming Director, Assistant Director, and Homecoming Live Director
Directors of the Executive Institutes
Elected RSO Allocation Committee Members

Any elected or appointed office which receives OPS Wages from Student Government.
Any position or office requiring confirmation by the Student Senate.

Major offices may only be held by FSU students registered for at least six (6) hours in both the fall and spring semesters, respectively, and at least three (3) hours during the summer session.
The registration requirement during the summer session may be waived if the student fits the above requirements for the previous Spring semester, shows that they will be enrolled in the required number of hours in the Fall semester, and receives joint approval from the Program Director for Student Governance & Advocacy and the Program Director for Student Organizations & Involvement.

To be considered a student for purposes of holding OPS positions, an individual must be registered for one semester hour.
Student Government Association officers may take a leave of absence in the summer term according to the procedures outlined in the applicable chapter of statutes. At other times they must have approval of the Student Body President (for the Executive Branch) or the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court (for the Judicial Branch). All other officers of the Student Government Association may take a leave of absence during the summer session or at other times by notifying the Student Body President of their intentions in writing before they take a leave of absence, unless otherwise prohibited by Statute, or by individual bylaws.
Throughout the Student Body Statutes, as well as the Senate Rules of Procedure, persons designated as ex-officio members of any committees or entities, shall be voting members of the committees or entities unless they are specifically designated in the Statutes or Rules of Procedure as not having that privilege. Ex-officio members shall count toward or against quorum unless they are specifically designated as not having voting privileges on that committee or entity. Ex-officio members shall not be entitled to proffer motions unless they have been granted the right to vote.
The Student Body Constitution, Student Body Statutes, and any policies adopted pursuant to Chapter 416, shall be updated, and published by the Student Government Association staff at an interval not to exceed six (6) months. It shall be reprinted in physical form at an interval not to exceed twelve (12) months.

sections.heading: Chapter 200 Powers
sections.text:
Student Political Power: The enumeration of certain rights in these Statutes shall not be construed to impair or deny those rights already granted by state or federal law.
Student Government Association materials and offices may not be used for campus partisan political purposes. This shall include, but is not limited to, display of campus political materials in offices. This section shall not apply to materials posted in the personal offices (excluding doors) of elected and appointed Student Government Association officials, staff and advisors.
