sections.heading: Chapter 201 Student Body Presidential Appointments
sections.text:
Vote Required: Appointments of the Student Body President, in accordance with Chapter 304.3, shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate for appointments to vacated elected offices, and a majority vote for all other appointments except for Supreme Court Justices, who shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote for confirmation by the Senate, under any circumstances.
Interim Period for Non-elective Offices - Description of Duties: During the interim period between appointment and confirmation, the outgoing office holder shall describe the duties and responsibilities to the newly designated officeholder.
In all cases where an individual applies, or is forwarded for a Student Government position, the Student Body President shall act in accordance with Section 304(3) of the Student Body Statutes. In addition, the Student Body President shall have ten (10) school days, upon the completion of the candidate search process, to forward a candidate to the Student Senate for confirmation. In cases in which the Student Body President is not in compliance with Section 304(3), or when the aforementioned ten (10) day period, has been exceeded, the Student Body President shall attend (or submit in writing) by the next Student Senate meeting an explanation as to why a qualified candidate could not be found. The Student Body President may request an additional candidate search period. At their discretion, the Senate may grant an extended search period by a majority vote of the body. (If the Student Body President requests a second additional amount of time, the Student Senate may vote to extend by a two-thirds (2/3) vote. The screening process must be completed by the next regularly scheduled Student Senate meeting at the end of the ten (10) school days. If the Student Senate declines to extend the search period, the Student Body President shall forward an appointment (by the next regularly scheduled Student Senate meeting) for confirmation.
Suggested Qualifications for Appointed Positions:

"Interview" shall be defined as a live meeting between a designee of the Office of the Student Body President and the applicant, either conducted in person or over a video conferencing software.

The Student Body President, via executive policy, shall have the authority to create a list of suggested qualifications for each position appointed by the executive branch, 

Nothing in this paragraph shall be construed as to prevent any student from submitting an application for any position regardless of qualifications,

This list shall not include any qualifications for vacant Senate seats.

This list shall be presented to the Senate within the annual policy on the organization of the executive branch, defined in Chapter 300.4,

Following the approval of the list of suggested qualifications, those qualifications shall be listed on any applicable SGA application prior to the acceptance of any completed application.

The Student Body President, or designee thereof, shall have the authority to discard applications that do not align with the minimum qualifications, so long as the Student Body President has submitted these suggested qualifications in writing as defined in this Chapter.

Such designee shall be required to keep a document of all candidates that are disqualified. This document shall include specific information on why the candidate was disqualified, including a citation to the specific qualification not met as outlined in Executive Policy.

This document shall be accessible and shared with the Senate President and the Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee,

Regardless of the designee of the Student Body President, the Department of Administrative Affairs or successor Office and the Department of Student Governance and Advocacy shall be responsible for the facilitation of said document in line with Chapter 210 (The SGA External Transparency and Digital Records Act of 2025),
When a candidate is disqualified per this paragraph, the Student Body President, or designee thereof, shall be responsible for communicating such disqualification to the applicant in question in a timely manner. This communication shall include an explanation of the qualifications for which the candidate did not meet.
All suggested qualifications shall be objective in nature, including but not limited to:

Current academic year,

Objective measurements of experience, such as years within a given field or previous background,

Leadership positions, if appropriate,

No suggested qualifications shall include limitations of race, color, religion, sex, pregnancy, national origin, age, handicap, or marital status as pursuant to Florida Statue 760.01.

Applications that meet the suggested qualifications, or that are not discarded in line with this chapter, shall require an interview as defined in Chapter 304,

All Senate applications shall be considered, regardless of their qualifications, 

Any allegation of the Executive Branch improperly discarding candidates shall be submitted via resolution and heard by the Internal Affairs committee. If the committee finds a preponderance of the evidence presented, the complaint shall be forwarded to the full Senate for consideration.

sections.heading: Chapter 202 Student Senate Confirmation, Inauguration, And The Oath Of Office
sections.text:
Committee Accountability During the Confirmation Process:
Once candidates for appointed Student Body Offices have been forwarded to the Student Senate for confirmation, the rules set forth in the Student Body Statutes, as well as in the Student Senate Rules of Procedure, shall apply. During the confirmation process, the Student Senate, by a majority vote, may request a report from the chair of the committee that interviewed the candidate. The report shall disclose the committee's findings and criteria the committee used to recommend the approval or disapproval of the candidate.
The Student Senate President or presiding officer shall allow the candidate adequate time to answer questions as well as to address the Student Senate on issues pertinent to the candidate’s confirmation when the candidate is called on the Senate floor for confirmation.

Student Senate Action Required: The Student Senate shall act upon appointments within three regular Senate meetings after submission by the appropriate officer.
Candidate Action Required: After the Student Senate President confirms the committee(s) the candidate is required to pass through, the applicable Committee Chair(s) shall inform the candidate henceforth of the dates and times for their committee hearing or work with the candidate on finding an applicable schedule. Upon failure to communicate at least 12 hours in advance and failure to arrive to a Committee meeting for their hearing, the Committee Chair shall notify the candidate that they have one remaining absence left before their candidacy shall be deemed null and void.

Upon communication from the candidate regarding extenuating circumstances, after being declared null and void, the Senate President may rescind the null and void declaration and allow the candidate to continue through the confirmation process.
If found null and void, the candidate may reapply to the position in question after one academic semester has passed, and the appropriate appointing officer shall be required to find a new candidate for that position.

Compensation Limitations: No compensation shall be authorized for any officeholder whose appointment requires Student Senate confirmation until the officeholder has been confirmed.
Assumption of Duties: Duties, rights, and responsibilities, shall vest upon confirmation by the Student Senate and upon taking the oath of office. The Student Senate President, Pro-Tempore or Senator acting in this role shall be responsible for administering the oath of office to all nominees who have been confirmed by the Student Senate.
Selection of Oaths: All Student Government Association Officers shall take the same oath in Section 202.7, except for the Student Body President, Student Senate President, Student Senate President Pro Tempore, Justices of the Student Supreme Court, and the officers of the Congress of Graduate Students, who shall take the oaths prescribed in Sections 202(8), 202(9), 202(10), 202(11), and the COGS Code, respectively.
Candidates for Student Body offices may choose to replace the words “so help me God” with “on pain of impeachment,” when taking the oath of office. The person administering the oath shall inform the candidate of the option to change the ending of the oath prior to the administration of the oath.
The oath for all non-Presidential and Judicial offices shall be as follows: 

I, (officer's name), promise to support and defend the Constitution of the United States of America, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body. And I shall perform my duties to the best of my ability, so help me God. (On pain of impeachment).
The Presidential Oath of Office shall be as follows: 

I, (officer’s name), do solemnly swear that I will faithfully execute the Office of President of the Student Body, and will to the best of my ability preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States of America, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body, so help me God. (On pain of impeachment).
The Senate President Oath of Office shall be as follows:

I, (officer’s name), do solemnly swear to faithfully discharge the duties of my office and preside over the Senate without favour or prejudice, upholding its integrity, fairness, and transparency in service to the Student Body, and that I will preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body. So help me God. (On pain of impeachment).
The Senate President Pro Tempore Oath of Office shall be as follows:

I, (officer’s name), do solemnly swear to faithfully discharge the duties of my office and serve, alongside the Senate President, in presiding over the Senate without favour or prejudice, upholding its integrity, fairness, and transparency in service to the Student Body, and that I will preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body. So help me God. (On pain of impeachment).
The Judicial Oath of Office shall be as follows: 

I, (officer’s name), do solemnly swear that I will administer justice and render judicial interpretation without respect to persons or parties, do equal right to all members of the Student Body, and that I will faithfully and impartially discharge and perform all the duties incumbent upon me as a Justice of the Student Supreme Court under the Constitution and laws of the United States of America, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body, so help me God. (On pain of impeachment).
There shall be two inauguration ceremonies held per year, following the Fall and Spring Student Government Association elections, on the dates specified in the Student Body Election Code. The oath of office will be administered to all students who have been duly elected to office by the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court. If the Chief Justice is unavailable, then an Associate Justice may be appointed to administer the oath. If no Justice to the Student Supreme Court is available, then the Supervisor of Elections shall choose any judge or justice who is currently serving on the bench in the State of Florida. The candidates for the offices of Student Body President, Student Body Vice President, and Student Body Treasurer must be administered the oath individually. All duties, rights, privileges, and responsibilities of office shall vest upon taking the prescribed oath of office.

sections.heading: Chapter 203 The SGA Sunshine Act
sections.text:
This Act is to be entitled the “Florida State University Student Government Association in the Sunshine Act of 2021”, referred to hereafter as the “Sunshine Act.”
Definitions: The following definitions shall be fully applicable for the purpose of this act.
“The Public” shall be defined as any member of the Student Body who is neither an officer nor candidate for office in the Student Government Association, as well as University faculty and staff unaffiliated with Student Government, as well as any person not affiliated with the Florida State University or the Student Government Association.
“Student Government Association Affiliates” shall be defined as all officers and candidates for office in the Student Government Association, as well as all staff members of the same.
“Official Acts” shall be defined as:
Formal actions taken by an SGA body or its members. This includes, but is not limited to:
Legislative acts;
Allocation of funds;
Passage of resolutions;
Passage of executive orders;
Presidential vetoes;
Presidential appointments;
Presidential dismissals;
Adoption of rules; and
Execution of projects funded by SGA.
Deliberations around the taking of formal actions by either an SGA body or its members.
All meetings held under the auspices of Student Government Association, except as otherwise provided in the Constitution, at which official acts are to be taken, are declared open to the public at all times. No resolution, rule, or formal action shall be considered binding, except if enacted at such a meeting.
Student Government Association Affiliates shall be entitled to attend all meetings held under the auspices of the Student Government Association except as provided for in these statutes, the Constitution, or any policies pursuant to Chapter 415, regardless of whether official acts are being taken.
There shall be no less than two (2) minutes per person reserved at the beginning of any meeting held under the auspices of Student Government Association, in which official acts take place, for members of the public and all Student Government Association affiliates to address those assembled.
In cases where the assembled body deems necessary, the body may vote to place a time restriction of no less than two minutes on members of the public and all Student Government Association affiliates who wish to address those assembled. This motion shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote.
Each body shall provide, in advance of the meeting, a form through which members of the public may submit comments virtually and request to attend the meeting remotely for the purpose of providing public comment. Submissions shall include the commenter’s name and affiliation.
Public comment must be provided before final action is taken on any proposition.

The minutes and records of any meeting held under the auspices of the Student Government Administration, regardless of whether official acts are taken, shall be recorded at the time of the meeting and such records shall be open to the public and to Student Government Affiliates and be uploaded to CivicPlus for publication within two (2) business days following the meeting. The Student Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to issue injunctions to enforce the purposes of this chapter upon application by any member of the Student Body.
Minutes shall be written to reflect any and all business conducted within a meeting. This includes any discussions, deliberations, and decisions made.
Deliberations shall, at the very least, include a summary of the reasoning behind all decisions.

Failure to publish minutes, notices, or related records in accordance with Chapter 208 (The SGA External Transparency and Digital Records Act of 2025) shall constitute a violation of this Act.

Any person may be requested to leave any meeting held under the auspices of Student Government Association; however the person must be explicitly informed of their access rights granted under the Sunshine Act.
No provision within this Act shall be construed so as to prohibit the chair of a meeting from maintaining decorum necessary to the facilitation of business, nor to waive any officer’s right to call upon law enforcement officials in the event of a criminal disturbance.
Any meeting in which official acts are to take place held without twenty-four (24) hours prior public notice shall be considered in violation of the provisions of this chapter.
Major bodies such as the full Senate, Cabinet, Congress of Graduate Students, and Supreme Court hearings require at least thirty-six (36) hours’ notice. Public notice of a meeting of these bodies does not prohibit their committees or sub-entities from convening while such notice is active.

Public notice shall consist of an announcement on FSU-SGA CivicPlus platform of the meeting time, place, purpose, and agenda. Social media posts shall not serve as official public announcements.

No card or written notice of intent to comment may be required in any meeting (Executive, Senate committee, etc.) to speak, except regular Senate meetings, unless the presiding officer wishes to do so and gives adequate notification to those wishing to speak. Presence at the beginning of a non-Senate meeting (including Senate’s Committees) can indicate intent to comment. Nothing here shall prohibit the presiding officer of a meeting from maintaining order or facilitate the allowing of student comments in an organized system.
Any actions taken at meetings found in violation of this act are to be declared null and void.
Adherence to the provisions of this Act shall be considered a fundamental duty of all Student Government Association officers, officials, and appointees. Compliance with these transparency standards is a requirement for holding office.
Violations of the SGA Sunshine Act shall be referred to the Student Body Attorney General for correction.
Upon receipt of a submission, the Office shall confirm receipt of the initial request within twenty-four (24) hours. The Attorney General shall determine whether a violation occurred and issue a written response of findings within. All responses to submissions and the corresponding findings shall be published to Municode pursuant to Chapter 208 within five (5) business days of issuance.
The Office shall have the authority to enforce this Act by requesting any corrective or remedial action necessary under its provisions, including the cancellation of meetings, the voiding of actions taken in violation, or the publication of withheld records. Upon refusal of compliance by the relevant parties, the Office shall be required to seek judicial action to compel enforcement.
Nothing in this section shall limit or restrict the right of any student to directly petition the judicial branch or appropriate authority to seek enforcement or remedy for violations of this Act.

sections.heading: Chapter 204 The SGA Public Records Act Of 1988
sections.text:
Scope:
"Reasonable time" means during scheduled office hours, if hours are scheduled and within no more than twenty-four (24) hours. The Student Supreme Court may grant an extension of time.
"Reasonable cost" shall be no more than the actual cost of duplication.
"Public Records" means all documents, papers, letters, maps, books, tapes, photographs, film, sound recordings, or other material, regardless of physical form or characteristics, made or received pursuant to the Constitution or Statutes or in connection with any transaction or business.
This chapter is applicable to any Florida State University Student Government official, employee, organization, or any entity or any individual funded or regulated by the Student Government Association.
Every person who has custody of a public record shall permit the record to be inspected and examined by any person desiring to do so, at any reasonable time, under reasonable conditions, and under the supervision of the custodian of the public record or a designee.
Every person who has custody of a public record shall ensure that a legible photocopy or other legible copy of the record be provided upon request within a reasonable time subject to payment of reasonable costs.
Any application of this chapter that conflicts with Federal or Florida Law is null and void in that individual circumstance.
Information obtained through the application of this chapter may not be used for any unlawful purpose or any purpose that is a violation of other FSU Student Body Statutes or the Constitution.
The Student Supreme Court shall have jurisdiction to issue injunctions to enforce the purposes of this chapter upon application of any individual.

sections.heading: Chapter 205 Code Of Ethics
sections.text:
This act shall be entitled "the Student Government Association Code of Ethics." The intent of this code is to strengthen the faith and confidence of the Student Body in the Student Government Association.
Legislative Intent and Declaration of Policy:
It is essential to the proper conduct and operation of the Student Body that its officials be independent and impartial, and that public office not be used for private gain. Student Body officers and employees hold their position for the benefit of the Student Body. Such officers and employees are bound to observe in their official acts the highest standards of ethics consistent with this code, recognizing that promoting the public interest and maintaining the respect of the student body in their Student Government must be the foremost concern.
It is the intent of this act to protect the integrity of Student Government by prescribing conflicts of interest and unethical practices. It shall serve as the basis of discipline for those who violate its provisions.
Any student that feels a violation of the Code of Ethics has occurred, has the right to file a complaint with the Student Supreme Court.
Any organization has the right to establish additional ethical criteria or penalties in its constitution and bylaws.
Standards of Conduct:
To preserve the integrity of the Florida State University Student Government Association, its officers and employees must disclose all potential or actual conflicts of interests.
Conflict of Interest means any business or professional activity or direct or indirect financial interest that would place a person in a position where there is an opportunity to disregard the public interests of the student body for an individual’s private interests.
No officer or employee will judge or vote on any matter that would affect private gain. No Executive Board member of an SGA funded organization may vote within a funding committee of Senate on an allocation to the organization in which that member serves as an Executive Board member which requires Student Senate confirmation. This restriction will not apply to that members’ vote on the final annual budget.
No officer or employee will induce or coerce another officer or employee with favor or retribution, either directly or through implication, to vote, render a decision, or to utilize the powers of their office to act in a prescribed manner.
Any vote, action, or judgment performed by an officer or employee who has a conflict of interest may be appealed with the Student Supreme Court. This must be done in a written, signed complaint submitted no later than three (3) days after the vote, act, or judgment in which the conflict occurs.
In the Student Senate, a written and signed complaint shall be filed with the chair of Rules of Calendar, who will investigate that matter within 48 hours of receipt of the complaint. Upon cause, the Chair shall forward the complaint, findings, and a recommendation for penalties to the Student Supreme Court. The Student Supreme Court shall assign penalties for any Senator or officer of Senate who acts, judges, or votes with a conflict of interest.
Misuse of Student Government Association Property: No officer or employee will use or attempt to use Student Government Association property, facilities, resources, or personnel to secure a gift, reward, privilege, benefit, or exemption for anyone.
No officer or employee will disclose information not available to the general public for personal gain or for the personal gain of any other person or organization.
Unlawful Compensation: No officer or employee shall solicit, accept, provide or attempt to provide any material items of value in cases that would influence, or appear to influence any vote, action, or judgment.
Inducing to Act: No officer or employee shall knowingly aid, advise, encourage, or threaten another officer or employee of Student Government Association or student to act in violation of this chapter, Federal, State and local laws, the Florida State University Student Body Constitution and Statutes, the Student Code of Conduct or Academic Honor code.
Fraud in the Student Government Association:
No officer or employee will willfully misrepresent themselves while acting in an official capacity.
To this end, no Senator may vote with a voting device that is assigned to a different Senator.
No officer or employee will withhold information or documentation when mandated or provide false or misleading information or documentation.
No officer or employee will bring false charges or provide false or misleading evidence against another officer, employee, or student.
No officer or employee will practice any discrimination as defined in the Student Government Association Anti-Discrimination Policy.
No officer or employee will deny any student rights guaranteed by the Federal and State Constitution, or the Florida State University Student Body Constitution and Statutes.
No officer or employee will deny any student the right to due process or the right to an impartial hearing or trial.
No officer or employee of Student Government will dismiss, discipline or take adverse action against a Student Government officer or employee for disclosing information pursuant to the provisions of this section.
Disclosure protected under this rule shall be defined as:
Any violation or suspected violation of any federal, state, or local laws, the Florida State University Student Body Constitution and Statutes, the Florida State University Student Code of Conduct or Academic Honor Code.
Any act or suspected act of misfeasance, malfeasance, or nonfeasance as defined by Student Government Association Constitution and Statutes.
Procedures:
Enforcement of the SGA Ethics Code shall be the jurisdiction of the Student Supreme Court. All ethics complaints shall be heard by the Student Supreme Court.
Upon receipt of a written signed complaint of any student, the Student Supreme Court shall hear the complaint within 48 hours of receipt.
The court may issue any writs necessary.
Penalties:
Upon finding a violation(s) of the SGA Ethics Code, the Student Supreme Court shall assign penalties. Such penalties shall consist of, at the Court’s discretion, suspension, or recommendation to begin impeachment proceedings, or recommendation to the Student Senate to freeze an organization’s funding, or dismissal from employment.
Violation(s) of the Ethics Code does not preclude prosecution under the Student Conduct code or Academic Honor Code.
Any person found guilty of violating two (2) or more provisions of this Code shall not be allowed to hold a Student Government Association office in the future.
Appeal: Both plaintiff and defendant have the right to appeal the decision of the Student Supreme Court to the Vice President for Student Affairs. Appeals must be submitted within three (3) days of the decision of the Student Supreme Court.
Under the laws of the State of Florida, any elected or appointed officer of the Student Body, who has been convicted of a felony matriculated or enrolled as a student at Florida State University, shall be immediately dismissed from Student Body office, and shall be prohibited from ever holding a Student Body office again, unless the conviction is vacated in a court of law, or upon pardon by the Governor of the State of Florida or the President of the United States of America. Individuals with a prior criminal conviction who have been reviewed and admitted to the University through the Judicial Review Committee shall be eligible to serve as a Student Government officer despite their status as a convicted felon. No student official may be subject to removal for conviction of a felony if said conviction antedated the official’s matriculation to Florida State University or the passage of § 240.236, Fla. Stat. (2002). Applicants who have not disclosed prior criminal convictions to the University during the admissions process will remain ineligible to serve as a Student Government officer.
All members of the Student Government Association are expected, at all times, to distinguish between when they speak, act, or communicate in their personal capacity and when they speak or act on behalf of the Student body’s or Student Government’s interests. Reference to affiliation with the Student Government Association must be made only as an aid to identify the individual making the contact. It must be made clear the contact is not being made on the behalf of the Student Government Association.
No individual shall willfully misrepresent themself or their office for personal, political, or professional gain. Willfully lying or otherwise being untruthful in any official capacity shall be considered malfeasance and a violation of this code. Candidates for Student Government office shall not intentionally misrepresent themselves nor their plans in their application, interview, or confirmation hearing. Willfully misleading the Legislative or Executive Branch in pursuit of any office shall be considered perjury and a violation of this code.

sections.heading: Chapter 206 Anti-Discrimination Policy
sections.text:
No Student Government Association officer, employee, branch, agency, affiliated project, recognized student organization, or any entity which receives any Student Government Association funding will practice discrimination. Discrimination will be defined as the differential treatment of a student based on, but not limited to race, creed, color, religion, sex, age, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, national origin, marital status, parental status, disability, socio-economic status, inability to pay dues, political orientation, class standing (freshman, sophomore, etc., unless allowed by Statute) or any combination thereof. Student Government Officers shall not be penalized if they choose to observe a Holy Day. As per Florida Statutes, anti-Semitism and any other form of religious discrimination shall be considered when a grievance regarding religion is submitted. Discrimination will be further defined as the denial of due process or the infringement of the substantive rights of any student guaranteed by the Florida State University Student Government Association Constitution and Statutes, or organization bylaws, University Rights and Responsibilities, and State and Federal Constitutions.
Students with grievances will submit a written complaint to the Student Supreme Court. Upon finding a violation of 206.1, the Court will recommend penalties to be carried out by the executive and legislative branches such as:
The Senate Finance Committee freezing already allocated Student Government Association funds in the guilty party’s university recognized bank account, or
The Student Body President may issue an executive order which recommends the suspension or permanent removal of the entity’s Student Government Association status should they fall within the purview of the executive branch, or
The Senate may permanently remove any Student Government Association funding from the entity by a resolution, or
The Senate Judiciary Committee may initiate impeachment proceedings against any Student Government officers, members, or employees of the entity found in violation of Section 206(1), or
This chapter shall not preclude the Student Supreme Court from making other recommendations they deem appropriate for the corresponding severity of the violation.
Nothing in this chapter may preclude the Court from pursuing all types of relief allowable under university policies, state law, and federal law.
Any Student Government Association Officer, employee, branch, agency, affiliated projects, recognized student organization or any entity that receives Student Government Association funding may appeal sanctions imposed by Student Senate to the Vice President for Student Affairs.
All funds that have been frozen by the Senate shall remain as such until a proof of correction is provided to the Student Senate with a deadline that was voted upon by the Student Senate as a whole.
The aforementioned “proof of correction” must be provided by a designee or representative of the entity found guilty of the violation. The proof must be physically presented in a form of writing and in person to the Student Senate with all required amends made as well as proof that relief for the discrimination was made to the afflicted victim.

sections.heading: Chapter 207 The Student Government Training Act
sections.text:
The purpose of this legislation is to ensure that all officials of the Florida State University Student Government Association have received adequate training in the areas of fiscal and ethical responsibility in the allocation and expenditure of state funds collected through the Activity and Service Fee, and all other statutory responsibilities and duties of their position.
For purposes of furthering the interest of this Student Government Association, SGA entities shall conduct an appropriate training program suitable to the needs of the members of their respective organizations within a reasonable timeframe once assuming office or confirmation by the Student Senate.

The following positions shall be responsible for conducting such training.

Student Body President.

Student Body Treasurer.

Student Senate President. 

Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court.

Supervisor of Elections.

Chair of the Union Board.

Chair of Campus Recreation Board.

Senior Class Council President. 

Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students.

Directors of all Executive Agencies.

Executive Department Secretaries. 

Directors of Affiliated Projects.

Funding Board Chairs.

The content of such training programs shall be at the discretion of the officers listed at the beginning of this section, but should include:

Information on the SGA Constitution and Statutes.

Procedures that are pertinent to the operation of their respective organizations.
Transfer of Power

To facilitate a smooth transition of power, officeholders shall keep a physical copy of pertinent information contained within their offices needed to complete the duties of their position.

The officeholders subject to this paragraph shall include:

All offices mentioned in paragraph 2(a) of this chapter.

Student Body Vice President. 

Student Body Attorney General.

Senate Stating Committee Leadership.

Senate College Delegation Leadership.

Executive Institute Directors.

Homecoming Director.

All other Class Council Presidents not previously listed.

This shall include:

Administrative access information consistent with Chapter 208 (SGA External Transparency and Digital Records Act of 2025).

Suggested timeline of responsibilities, including weekly, monthly, and yearly requirements.

Contact information for relevant offices and stakeholders needed to successfully execute the official duties required. 

Any other information deemed helpful or necessary by the previous officeholder;

Major officeholders shall make reasonable efforts to include all information that could be needed by a successor, regardless of its inclusion in this statute.

After the certification of a new election in which the officeholder has changed, in compliance with Chapter 714, Student Body Statutes, the outgoing officers shall transfer the above documents to the Office of Student Governance and Advocacy.

The Office of Student Governance and Advocacy shall be responsible for facilitating, and keeping receipt of, the transfer of documents to incoming officers once the office is assumed.

In the event of resignation, removal, or other mid-term vacancy, the outgoing officer shall transfer the above documents within fourteen (14) days of the vacancy. 

Outgoing leadership defined in this paragraph are encouraged to arrange a meeting with their successor. 

This meeting shall not be interpreted as a replacement for the transition documents defined in this paragraph. Instead, this optional meeting shall encourage a working relationship between both parties.
New Senator Orientation:
New Senator Orientation shall serve as a means to bring about a more efficient transition into Student Senate for new Senators.
The current Student Senate President, in conjunction with Student Senate President Pro Tempore, shall be required to conduct New Senator Orientation in the week prior to the Student Government Inaugurations; additional New Senator Orientations shall be conducted at the discretion of the Student Senate President. In the case of a contested election, or special circumstances, New Senator Orientation may be moved to the week after the Inaugurations.
New Senator Orientation shall consist of teaching new Senators how to compose and submit legislation for first reading, properly follow Robert’s Rules of Order during a Senate meeting, properly follow Student Senate Rules of Procedure, and anything deemed necessary by Senate President or Student Senate President Pro Tempore. In addition, new Senators should have a basic understanding of the Student Body Constitution, the Student Body Statutes and the SGA Financial Manual.
At New Senator Orientation, the new Senators shall take part in a mock Senate meeting in which the Student Senate President, in conjunction with the Student Senate President Pro Tempore, shall teach the new Senators all relevant information about the procedure of a Senate meeting.
After New Senator Orientation:
New Senators shall be encouraged to attend a scheduled meeting with the Student Senate President, in which the new Senators’ committee appointment shall be discussed in addition to any relevant questions the Senator might have. Successful completion of New Senator Orientation shall be determined by the Student Senate President or Student Senate President Pro Tempore.
A voluntary survey to ascertain the efficiency of the program will be conducted by the Student Senate President Pro Tempore at the last meeting of each Senate term.
Committee Leadership and College Delegation Leadership Training:

Conducted by the Senate President and the Senate President Pro Tempore, all elected or appointed Chairs and Vice Chairs of standing or ad-hoc committees shall be required to attend a Committee Leadership Training to ensure competency with all skills that are expected of them. This training shall be performed before the first convened meeting of any standing committee of the semester in which they were elected.

This training shall consist of the following content:

Presiding Officer training in line with all pertinent Rules of Procedure and Robert's Rules of Order,
CivicPlus Training, including all technical skills needed to record votes and take meeting minutes. This should be primarily overseen by the Senate President Pro Tempore.
Information on committee-specific Rules of Procedure, attendance tracking policies, and any other content deemed necessary by the Senate President and/or Senate President Pro Tempore.

Also conducted by the Senate President and the Senate President Pro Tempore, all elected Chairs and Vice-Chairs of College Delegations shall be required to attend a training session. This training shall be performed before any meeting of any College Delegation of the semester in which they were elected. 

This training shall consist of the following content:

Effective constituent outreach,

Reporting procedures,

Time management strategies,

Information on stakeholders, such as the administrative staff and Deans of each college,

Or any other content deemed necessary by the Senate President Pro Tempore. 

At the discretion of the responsible officers, nothing in this statute shall prevent the training of Committee Leadership and College Delegation Leader from being conducted concurrently.

Professional Development:
All SGA officeholders shall be encouraged to participate in on and off-campus personal and professional development opportunities to strengthen the leadership of the Student Government Association.

The Student Body President shall designate, by executive order, a member of their office responsible for maintaining a working list of opportunities for professional and leadership development.

This shall include on-campus, local, state, and national opportunities that are pertinent to campus leaders.

This list shall be published on the SGA website and periodically updated, pursuant to Chapter 208(a)(1)(A).
