sections.heading: Chapter 208 The SGA External Transparency And Digital Records Act Of 2025
sections.text:
Purpose and Scope:

Title: 
This Chapter shall be established as the “SGA Digital Records Act of 2025,” and shall serve as the comprehensive statutory framework governing all digital platforms, publications, and records maintained or authorized by the FSU-SGA.
Purpose: 
The purpose of this Act is to: 
Codify uniform standards for the publication, preservation, and administration of digital records produced or maintained by any component of the SGA; 
Promote government transparency through timely, consistent, and public-facing digital communications; 
Ensure compliance with applicable statutes, including the Florida Sunshine Act (Chapter 203), the SGA Public Records Act (Chapter 204), and any related mandates of the Student Body Constitution; 
Protect the institutional memory and archival integrity of the SGA through the use of designated publishing and records platforms. 
Scope and Applicability: 
This Act shall apply to any and all officers, entities, and governing instruments operating under, funded by, or deriving authority from the Student Government Association, including all bodies, offices, programs, or subdivisions: 
Established by the Student Body Constitution or its amendments; 
Created or empowered by statute or enrolled legislation of the Student Senate; 
Formed or governed pursuant to any formally adopted directive, order, policy, regulation, or governing document authorized under SGA, including but not limited to administrative rules, executive policies, branch directives, procedural rules, or internal regulations; 
Instituted or directed by a valid Executive Order of the Student Body President or other action authorized by an officer vested with statutory or constitutional authority; 
Receiving funding in whole or in part from Activity and Service Fees as appropriated by the Student Senate, the Congress of Graduate Students, or any affiliated budgeting authority. 
The provisions of this Chapter shall extend to all digital communications, recordkeeping responsibilities, and public-facing documentation conducted or maintained by the aforementioned entities, and shall apply equally to any future office, department, or subdivision not explicitly exempted by this statute. 
Digital Records Infrastructure: 
This Chapter shall govern the establishment, use, and legal status of the following platforms as official instruments of record for the SGA: 
The SGA Website, hosted at https://sga.fsu.edu or its successor domain; 
CivicPlus, as the official platform for meeting notices, agendas, calendars, and related public disclosures; 
Municode, as the official legislative and archival codification platform for any enrolled legislation and other binding governance materials. 
Official Social Media and Online Communications Platforms, defined as any digital platform, including social media accounts, third-party engagement platforms, or content distribution systems, which have accounts created, authorized, or maintained by the Student Government Association or any of its subordinate entities for the purpose of disseminating official information, updates, outreach materials, or policy notices to the Student Body or general public. Such platforms shall be subject to the same publication, content integrity, and compliance standards as other official digital instruments of the SGA; 
Any other digital platform, service, software, or infrastructure, whether existing at the time of enactment or adopted in the future, that is utilized by the Student Government Association or its agents for the publication, archiving, transmission, or communication of information that constitutes, or is intended to serve as, an official governmental record or public notice, shall be deemed subject to this Chapter and all legal obligations herein, irrespective of its naming, hosting structure, or administrative origin. 
Amendment of this Statute: 
In the event of any conflict between this Chapter and any other Chapter of the Student Body Statutes, internal procedure, directive, policy memorandum, executive issuance, or other administrative action issued by any officer, agency, branch, or body of the Student Government Association, the provisions of this Chapter shall be deemed controlling and shall supersede any conflicting authority. 
This Chapter shall not be amended, repealed, or suspended in whole or in part except by a bill of the Student Senate passed in accordance with the legislative process set forth in Title IV of the Student Body Statutes and subject to the following conditions: 
Any bill amending any provision of this Chapter shall require the affirmative vote of three-fourths (3/4) of Senators present and voting, provided that no such vote shall be taken unless two-thirds (2/3) of all Senators are present and voting on the floor at the time of the vote. 
No such bill shall be eligible for placement on the Senate Calendar or considered on the floor unless it has been referred to, heard in, and reported favorably from no fewer than three (3) standing committees of the Senate. At least one of these committees must be the Senate Rules Committee or its functional successor by whatever name it may be designated in the future. 
Each assigned committee shall consider the bill in its original committee form. No suspension of this requirement shall be permitted by motion or waiver, and no committee may be bypassed, discharged, or removed from the referral chain prior to the bill's consideration on the Senate floor. 
Any proposed amendment to this Chapter which alters, expands, or otherwise reinterprets its legislative intent or declared purpose must appear on Second Reading on the Senate Calendar for a minimum of ten (10) school days following its final committee referral. No motion to expedite, waive, or suspend the calendar requirements herein shall be in order. 
Definitions
Purpose: For the purposes of this Chapter, the following terms shall be defined as follows. 
“Digital Platform” shall mean any web-based, cloud-based, or otherwise internet-accessible service, application, software, or content management system (CMS) used to host, transmit, publish, or store any content produced or disseminated by the Student Government Association. 
“Official Record” shall mean any document, file, post, directive, order, policy, notice, transcript, recording, or other material—regardless of format—that has been created, adopted, enacted, published, or archived by any SGA officer, branch, board, or entity in furtherance of their official duties and which is intended to serve as a matter of public record or internal institutional record. 
“SGA Website” shall refer to the official website hosted at https://sga.fsu.edu, or its successor domain, as maintained by the Student Government Association and operated under the oversight of Department of Student Engagement. The Website shall serve as the primary portal for publishing contact information, event listings, application forms, executive and legislative notices, and other content intended for general student body access. 
“CivicPlus” shall refer to the digital platform licensed or utilized by Florida State University, and managed in coordination with the SGA, for the purpose of posting meeting agendas, public notices, meeting minutes, event calendars, and other transparency-related items. CivicPlus shall constitute the official vehicle for fulfilling public notice and meeting transparency obligations under Chapter 203 and related statutes. 
“Municode” shall refer to the official legislative codification and archival platform authorized for use by the Student Government Association for the exclusive purpose of publishing, preserving, and displaying all binding, historical, or otherwise authoritative documents and materials adopted, enacted, issued, or maintained by any component of the SGA. No other platform, service, or storage system shall be deemed sufficient to fulfill any statutory requirement for the publication, long-term preservation, or legal accessibility of the above categories unless expressly exempted by an act of the Student Senate or by provision of this Chapter. Such documents shall include, but are not limited to: 
All enrolled legislation,
The Student Body Statutes and Constitution (including all amendments, repeals, and historical versions), 
All policies, procedural rules, executive orders, judicial opinions, and binding administrative directives, 
Any other record that is or was binding on any branch or affiliate entity of the Student Government Association, or intended to have legal, administrative, or historical effect,
A formal and continuously updated roster of all current and former Student Government officers who have held “major positions,” as defined in Chapter 100, including dates of service and the office(s) held, 
All official records of SGA elections, including but not limited to: 
Candidate filings, campaign finance disclosures, and violation reports; 
Final certified results, referenda, and recount records; 
Advisory opinions, contested case documentation, judicial rulings, or administrative actions related to any election or referendum held under Title VII of Student Body Statutes. 

“Social Media Platform” shall mean any digital communication channel or application, including but not limited to Instagram, X (formerly Twitter), Facebook, LinkedIn, YouTube, TikTok, or similar services, that is created, owned, operated, or authorized by the SGA or any of its subdivisions for the purpose of disseminating official communications, updates, promotional content, or public engagement efforts. 
“Webmaster” shall mean the individual or office designated by Department of Student Engagement with primary responsibility for maintaining and updating the SGA Website. The Webmaster shall act as the publishing authority for purposes of this Chapter and may coordinate with branch designees to ensure compliance. The Webmaster shall retain no right to make decisions outside of the scope of requests from the Student Government Association’s officers. 
“Publishing Authority” shall refer to the individual or office designated by each branch or entity of the SGA responsible for transmitting records and ensuring timely publication of required materials to the appropriate digital platform, including but not limited to Student Governance and Advocacy staff, or other designated official(s). A Publishing Authority shall at no point retain independent decision rights or decision-making authority. 
“Affiliate Entity” shall refer to any agency, board, institute, program, office, or other body established pursuant to the Student Body Constitution, Statutes, or Executive Order and operating with funding from A&S Fees or under the functional jurisdiction of the SGA, excluding student organizations recognized by the Office of Student Organizations & Involvement unless specifically incorporated into an SGA structure. 
“Successor Platform” shall mean any platform, software, or service that replaces, updates, or supersedes an existing platform referenced in this Chapter, including those not yet developed or adopted, provided the new platform serves the same core function as that which it replaces. 
“Visual Asset” shall mean any graphical or design element created for the purpose of representing, identifying, or promoting a branch, entity, program, or official initiative of the Student Government Association. This shall include, but not be limited to: logos, seals, wordmarks, sub-brand marks, emblems, stylized text, graphic packages, icons, digital headers, templates, social media profile images, or any other image or design used for official SGA representation in print, digital, or merchandise form. 
"Rebrand" shall mean any substantial alteration to the thematic presentation, visual identity, or public-facing designation of any Student Government Association entity, including but not limited to: 
A change in the official name, handle, or display name of any social media account, website, or digital profile; 
A modification of the entity's official logo, seal, wordmark, graphic identity, or visual branding package, whether in color, design, typography, or overall style; 
A significant change in the descriptive language, mission statement, or thematic content presented through the entity's public-facing channels that materially alters the manner in which the entity is recognized, promoted, or perceived by the Student Body or general public. 
Platform Specific Content and Functional Requirements 
Purpose: The purpose of this Section is to establish the minimum content, operational functionality, and publication requirements for each digital platform utilized by the Student Government Association. Each platform shall serve a distinct legal and procedural function, and their contents shall be maintained in accordance with the responsibilities prescribed herein. 
The SGA Website:
The Student Government Association Website, hosted at https://sga.fsu.edu or its successor domain, shall serve as the primary digital access point for the Student Body and the general public regarding current operations of the SGA. 
The following content shall be maintained on the SGA Website at all times: 
Contact information for each branch of government, including SGA entity leadership and key staff; 
A current calendar of events and meetings, embedded or otherwise directly accessible through CivicPlus or its successor platform; 
Application portals or procedures for students seeking positions any SGA position or office; 
A directory of all SGA entities, including links to individual pages or profiles; 
Public-facing announcements or statements issued by any officer or body of the SGA; 
A direct and accessible link to the Student Government Association’s Municode archive, through which all governing documents shall be accessible to the public; 
Information on requesting funding for Registered Student Organizations (RSOs); 
Resources for student involvement, including open SGA positions and application procedures; 
A comprehensive roster of all officers who have held major positions as defined by Chapter 100, including their office and term of service, as information availability allows. 
The Webmaster shall ensure that all content listed above is updated no less than once every fifteen (15) business days, or within five (5) business days of a change in leadership, policy, or schedule. 
CivicPlus:
CivicPlus shall be the exclusive platform for the publication of public notices, agendas, event calendars, and post-meeting documentation related to official business of the SGA. 
The following content shall be required on CivicPlus: 
Agendas and official notices for all meetings of the Senate, Congress of Graduate Students, Executive Cabinet, Judicial Branch, and any other body meeting pursuant to Chapter 203 of the Student Body Statutes; 
Approved meeting minutes or summaries, posted no later than two (2) business days following the meeting; 
Attendance records, voting records, and any roll call data from public meetings. 
All notices published on CivicPlus shall fulfill the public notice requirements pursuant to Chapter 203, and shall be considered the controlling public record of such notice. 

Municode:

Municode shall serve as the exclusive codification and archival platform of the Student Government Association. 
The following content shall be uploaded to and maintained on Municode: 
The current and all prior versions of the Student Body Statutes and Constitution; 
All enrolled legislation passed by the Senate or Congress of Graduate Students; 
All executive orders, judicial opinions, binding rulings, and governance documents referenced in statute; 
A comprehensive roster of all officers who have held major positions as defined by Chapter 100, including their office and term of service, as information availability allows; 
All official election records, including filings, results, violations, rulings, and decisions. 
All documents listed under this subsection shall be uploaded no later than five (5) business days after their adoption, certification, signature, or issuance. 
Social Media and Online Communications Platforms:
All social media accounts operated by any entity of the Student Government Association shall be subject to the following governance and operational requirements.
Minimum identifiable standards and requirements shall include: 
For all social media accounts affiliated with the Executive Branch or any of its constituent entities: 
The account logo shall be designed in consultation with, and formally created by, Student Publications, and must receive approval from the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications. 
The account biography or description shall include a statement indicating that the account is an official communications channel "Established by the FSU Student Government Association" or "@FSUSGA", or equivalent language as appropriate to the platform’s formatting. 
The handle or username of the account shall, where possible, reflect the agency or entity’s formal name and affiliation with FSU SGA. 
The branding and graphic identity of each account must remain consistent with SGA visual standards, and shall not deviate from institutional style guides without written authorization from the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications. 
For all social media accounts operated by entities not falling under the Executive Branch, including the Student Senate, Congress of Graduate Students, Judicial Branch, Union Board, Campus Recreation Board, and any other statutorily independent entity: 
The account logo shall be created in consultation with Student Publications and approved by the entity’s presiding officer, including but not limited to the Senate President, COGS Speaker, Chief Justice, or respective board chair. 
The account biography or description shall include language identifying the account as an official entity of the Florida State University Student Government Association. 
All visual identifiers, logos, or branded elements must align with university and SGA visual identity guidelines and may not use informal or unauthorized imagery. 
The account must not use any unauthorized adaptation of the FSU seal, the institutional wordmark, or similar protected university marks. 
In all cases: 
No account may imply personal ownership, partisanship, or represent unofficial student groups. 
Upon the conclusion of an administration or turnover of presiding officers, all visual and biographical content must be reviewed for compliance with current thematic standards and updated as necessary within ten (10) business days. 
Minimum operational standards and requirements shall include: 
Each official SGA social media account shall be registered using a shared, SGA-managed email address maintained by Department of Student Engagement, which shall serve as the recovery and administrative address; 
Login credentials for each account shall be known only to the designated communications officer of the respective branch or affiliate entity, the head of the entity, and professional staff within Department of Student Engagement; 
A formal record of account credentials, recovery email addresses, and authorized users shall be securely maintained by Department of Student Engagement and reviewed at the beginning and end of each administration; 
No social media account shall be registered to or maintained via a personal email address, nor shall any account be managed solely by an individual student. 
No social media account shall be authorized to make statements on behalf of the Student Government Association or on behalf of their respective entity, with exception granted to the following instances: 
The SGA account managed by the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications, publishing official statements from the Student Government Association authorized by the Senate via legislation or the Student Body President. 
The Student Senate account publishing official statements from the Student Senate or Student Government Association authorized by the Senate President, or the Senate at large via legislation. 
The COGS account publishing official statements from the Congress of Graduate Students authorized by the COGS Speaker or COGS, at-large, via resolution. 
Any SGA entities’ respective account shall be authorized to share or collaborate any published statement with any of aforementioned accounts. 
All social media posts shall utilize available accessibility features to ensure that the content may be accessed by students who are visually or audibly impaired.

The following minimum content shall be published through official SGA social media accounts at regular intervals: 
Announcements of meetings, events, and application periods; 
Policy updates, student engagement campaigns, and relevant student resources; 
Any information required to be posted to social media platforms pursuant to statute or Executive Order for Executive Branch entities. 
Executive Branch Communication Oversight: 
The Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications by the Student Body President through Executive Order shall at all times retain the ability to request access to all social media accounts, websites, or other online platforms operated by any agency, department, or affiliate entity established under the Executive Branch by statute. 
This officer shall exercise this access on behalf of, and at the direction of, the Student Body President, and may take action necessary to: 
Ensure compliance with visual and thematic standards as provided in this Chapter; 
Prevent unauthorized posting or misrepresentation of Executive Branch policy or branding; 
Execute a transition of access and platform control between administrations;.
Each Executive Branch entity shall coordinate with the Department of Student Engagement and the designated communications officer to ensure access credentials are current, securely stored, and transferred appropriately at the beginning and end of each term of service. 
Failure by any Executive Branch entity to provide or maintain shared administrative access in accordance with this subsection shall constitute a statutory violation and may be referred to the Student Body Attorney General and/or the Senate Judiciary Committee for disciplinary review. 
Violations of this subsection shall be referred to the Student Body Attorney General for correction, and repeated or deliberate violations may result in temporary suspension of platform authorization or formal disciplinary referral as provided by statute. 
Branch and Entity-Specific Posting Requirements:
Executive Branch: 
The Executive Branch of the Student Government Association, including all entities established by statute or executive order, including the Union Board and the Campus Recreation Board shall be required to publish the following information: 
On the SGA Website: 
A list of all current Executive Cabinet members, directors, and appointed officers, including publicly available contact information and the agency, office, or department to which they are assigned; 
Public application materials for all open positions within any Executive Branch entity, including deadlines and methods of submission; 
A summary of current initiatives, programs, and public-facing services administered by each Executive entity. 
On CivicPlus: 
Agendas and minutes for all Executive Branch meetings or meetings of any statutorily established entity under the Executive Branch, that require public notice pursuant to Chapter 203; 
Attendance and voting records for such meetings, where quorum or policy decisions are made. 
On Municode: 
All Acts of the Student Body President, including but not limited to: 
All Executive Orders, including directives, policy statements, and administrative instructions issued under constitutional or statutory authority; 
All official Appointments to statutory or constitutional officers, boards, agencies, university advisory committees, and/or any position requiring Senate confirmation or internal Executive assignment; 
All Dismissals or removals from office of any appointed Student Government Association officer; 
All Veto messages issued in response to legislation passed by the Student Senate; 
Any Memorandum, Directive, or Communication issued by the President or Executive Office and intended to bind internal Executive operations, policies, or procedures; 
Annual or term-based Executive reports, plans, or strategic initiatives, if published or submitted to the Student Senate or Student Body; 
Any emergency declarations, executive suspensions of services, or official responses to crises or campus-wide issues. 
All communications or instruments issued by an Executive Branch agency, department, or entity that contain binding policy, procedural rules, or administrative actions adopted under statutory authority or Executive delegation. 
A comprehensive chronological register of all Executive actions, indexed by date, subject matter, and office of origin, to be maintained in perpetuity as part of the official Executive archive. This register shall include, but not be limited to: 
All Executive Orders issued by the Student Body President; 
All official memoranda, directives, or statements issued by or on behalf of the Executive Branch that carry administrative effect or directive authority; 
All regulations promulgated in accordance with Executive Policy, including regulations issued by the Executive Branch and any entity established under Executive Branch. 
Legislative Branch:
The Legislative Branch, including the Student Senate and Congress of Graduate Students (COGS), shall ensure publication of the following: 
On the SGA Website: 
A full and current roster of all Senators and COGS Representatives, including office held, college represented, committee assignments, and contact information via university issued email; 
Legislative calendars for the year, including all planned meetings for the legislative session, committee schedules, and application procedures for vacant seats; 
Any special order adopted by the Senate or COGS that changes the operations or procedure of a standard meeting. 
On CivicPlus: 
All notices and agendas for meetings of the full Senate, COGS Assembly, and all standing or ad hoc committees; 
Minutes and attendance records within two (2) business days following such meetings; 
A copy of the official Senate Journal including the agenda prior to and minutes after each regularly scheduled Senate meeting, which shall constitute compliance with statutory posting requirements under Chapter 208 and Chapter 204. 
Any written public comment, testimony, or third-party document submitted for the purpose of inclusion in a public meeting shall be uploaded to CivicPlus as a public record prior to the meeting. 
On Municode: 
All enrolled legislation passed by the Senate or COGS, including all forms of enrolled legislation, amendments, and allocations; 
All committee and officer reports adopted by vote or submitted for the record by motion and majority vote of the committee or body. 
All binding memoranda issued by the presiding officer or authorized leadership of the Senate or Congress of Graduate Students, which shall include, but not be limited to: 
Memos that confirm the legislative body's approval or confirmation of any officer, appointee, or designee under the requirements of statute; 
Memos that serve as formal notification to the Supervisor of Elections of the passage of any constitutional amendment, referendum item, or election-related legislation requiring administrative action or ballot placement; 
Memos that assign, delegate, or transmit direction, duties, or obligations to the Executive Branch or any other entity as a result of legislation duly passed by the Senate or Congress of Graduate Students. 
Such memoranda shall be indexed by date, subject, issuing officer, and legislative file reference, and shall carry the same legal weight as enrolled legislation for the purposes of statutory compliance, archival, and reference. 
The Senate Clerk and the COGS Deputy Speaker for Communications shall be responsible for ensuring all required information is transmitted and published following each meeting or legislative action. 
Judicial Branch:

The Judicial Branch, shall publish: 
On the SGA Website: 
A roster of current Justices, Election Commissioners, the Office of the Supervisor of Elections, and any other current officer of the Judicial Branch, with contact information and term expiration; 
A description of court jurisdiction, procedure, and submission forms for requests for advisory opinion, appeals, original jurisdiction complaints, original jurisdiction responses, and request for counsel, or any other form required by statute or judicial policy. 
On CivicPlus: 
Dockets or public notices for all scheduled court hearings, including elections-related hearings; 
Attendance records and public minutes, if applicable, from court or elections-related public proceedings. 
On Municode: 
All majority, concurring, and dissenting opinions issued by the Judicial Branch; 
All rulings, orders, or opinions related to elections, including candidate qualification rulings and infraction decisions;
All records and final rulings related to contested elections, candidate qualifications, and campaign violations; 
All certified election results, referenda outcomes, campaign finance summaries, infraction reports, and formal documentation produced or received by the Supervisor of Elections in the course of administering any Student Government election, including but not limited to General Elections, Special Elections, Referenda, and Constitutional Amendment votes; 
All official records of the Elections Office, including candidate filings, disqualification notices, advisory opinions, and elections administration manuals. 
For the purposes of this Chapter, all statutorily established affiliate entities, including the Union Board and Campus Recreation Board, shall be administratively categorized under the Executive Branch. As such, they shall be subject to the same publication, content, and transmission standards as all other Executive entities unless explicitly exempted by law. An exception shall be granted to an entity if it is funded annually 50% or more by another type of revenue source other than Activity and Service (A&S) fees. 
Branding and Visual Identity Standards:
Purpose:
This section shall govern the creation, approval, and authorized use of all visual branding, logos, graphic elements, and stylistic identifiers used on digital platforms, print materials, merchandise, and communications issued by the Student Government Association or any of its affiliated entities. 
Creation and Approval of Visual Assets: 
All official logos, seals, graphic marks, or branding packages representing an SGA entity shall be designed in consultation with and created by Student Publications, unless otherwise exempted by this statute. 
Approval for Visual Assets shall be granted as follows: 
For Executive Branch entities, approval shall be issued by the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications by the Student Body President. 
For Legislative Branch entities, including the Student Senate and Congress of Graduate Students, approval shall be issued by the Senate President and COGS Speaker, respectively. 
For Judicial Branch and the Supervisor of Elections, approval shall be issued by the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court and the Supervisor of Elections, respectively. 
For all other entities not specifically named above, approval shall be granted by the presiding officer of the respective body or board, subject to notification of the Student Body President or designee. 
Mandatory Branding Content: 
All official social media accounts, websites, print publications, and public-facing communications issued by any SGA entity shall display the following elements, as appropriate to the medium: 
Each communication must include a logo or visual identifier that has been formally approved in accordance with subsection 208.5(b)(2). For graphics, this must include either the entity’s logo or the full entity name clearly spelled out. 
For photographs, a logo is not required. However, the entities’ name must be clearly indicated within the caption or accompanying text. If the communication is only partially composed of photographs, a logo is required. 
The account’s public description, bio, or about section must include language identifying the entity as part of the Florida State University Student Government Association (FSU SGA). Acceptable phrasing includes: 
“An Entity of @FSUSGA”;
“Established by the Florida State University Student Government Association (@FSUSGA)”;
“A (BLANK) of @FSUSGA”, options include: Identity Based Agency, Department, Affiliated Project 
All phrasing must include the appropriate mention of the official Student Government Association account on the platform that is being used, as applicable. 
A visual style and graphic identity consistent with the University’s visual standards and those established by Student Publications or the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications by the Student Body President. 
Restrictions on Use: 
The following restrictions shall apply to all visual materials issued by or on behalf of an SGA entity: 
No entity may adopt or use the official seal of Florida State University, the University’s institutional wordmark, or any other protected visual mark without formal approval from the University; 
No visual materials may incorporate political campaign branding, endorse partisan political content, or unofficial imagery inconsistent with the University’s regulations or SGA’s statutes; 
No personal or individually branded logos may be used on official social media or publications in a manner that suggests institutional endorsement, authorship, or ownership; 
All graphic content must comply with applicable accessibility and digital formatting standards established by the University. 
Review of Transition of Branding: 
All official visual branding shall be reviewed at the start and conclusion of each administration to ensure compliance with this Chapter, by the outgoing Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications, in partnership with the incoming Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications. 
Outgoing officers shall provide to their successors and to Department of Student Engagement any editable branding files, access to design platforms, and historical materials necessary to continue the consistent visual identity of the entity. 
No rebranding of an SGA entity may occur during an officer’s term of service without justification of programmatic need and written authorization from the designated approving officer listed in subsection 208.5(b)(2). 
SGA Funding Attribution and Required Marking: 
Any item, material, publication, apparel, promotional product, or digital content that is produced, distributed, or made available using Activity and Service (A&S) Fees appropriated by the Student Government Association and issued by any external organization, registered student organization, or University-affiliated entity not established under the constitutional or statutory authority of the SGA, shall be required to include a funding attribution mark in accordance with the following standards: 
The attribution mark shall include the phrase “Paid for by the Florida State University Student Government Association”, or such substantially similar language as approved by Student Publications; 
The attribution shall be accompanied by a different version of the SGA logo or wordmark specifically designed for this purpose by Student Publications and approved by the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications and the Student Senate via resolution. 
If the item is funded by the Congress of Graduate Students, the attribution mark must include the phrase “Paid for by the Congress of Graduate Students”, further standards may be defined by COGS Code. 
The mark shall be legible, clearly visible, and placed in a location appropriate to the medium, product, or digital format in which it appears. 
Additional standards may be provided by statute or policy to further define the requirements of funding attribution, such standards shall not interfere or supersede the aforementioned standards. 
This subsection shall apply to, but not be limited to: 
Printed or digital promotional materials produced by Registered Student Organizations or University departments receiving SGA Activity and Service fee funding through the Executive Projects Account or Senate discretionary allocations; 
Free design and printing services offered by Student Publications to Registered Student Organizations through any SGA-funded program; 
Promotional items or goods distributed on campus using A&S-funded appropriations, regardless of quantity or value; 
Websites, flyers, videos, or other outreach efforts conducted on behalf of a non-SGA entity using SGA appropriated funds. 
For materials produced by SGA entities the following rules shall apply: 
All such materials shall display the standard SGA logo or alternatively the entities’ approved logo as provided and maintained by the Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications or other designated approving officer for the entity; 
No external attribution mark shall be required unless the materials are co-branded or jointly funded with an outside organization; 
Logos shall not be modified or substituted without express written approval by the Executive Branch communications officer and Student Senate, in consultation with Student Publications. 
The use of unapproved branding, omission of required attribution, or misrepresentation of funding source shall constitute a violation of this Chapter shall result in the funding being cancelled or revoked, content removed, and referral to the Senate Finance Committee for disciplinary consideration. Violations related to COGS funding shall be referred to the COGS Internal Affairs Committee for disciplinary consideration. This section shall be enforced by the Student Body Treasurer and/or Student Body Attorney General. 
Credential Access and Transition Protocols:
Custodianship of Access Credentials:
Each branch of the Student Government Association, and every entity thereof, shall be required to maintain secure and up-to-date administrative access credentials for all digital platforms, including but not limited to websites, email-based accounts, social media profiles, scheduling tools, and document repositories. 
Administrative access shall be retained by both: 
The officer or staff member directly responsible for content or operational control of the platform and head of the respective entity; and 
The Department of Student Engagement office or the designated Executive Branch communications officer, who shall serve as the institutional custodian. 
No official SGA digital platform shall be registered, operated, or administered solely through a personal email address, private device, or individual login without dual access also granted to the designated custodial office. 
Credential Documentation and Storage: 
Each entity shall maintain a record of the following information, to be submitted to Department of Student Engagement at the start of each term of office and updated as necessary: 
Platform or account name and direct URL; 
Account handle or display name; 
Recovery email address and phone number, if applicable; 
Names and titles of all individuals currently authorized to access or manage the account. 
This record shall be stored securely by Department of Student Engagement and may only be accessed by authorized personnel for oversight, transition, or compliance purposes. 
Transition Between Administrations: 
Upon the conclusion of each administration or the replacement of any officer responsible for account management, all access credentials and account information shall be formally transferred to the succeeding officer or designee within five (5) business days of the transition. 
No outgoing officer or staff member may delete, repurpose, privatize, or transfer ownership of any SGA-affiliated digital platform without prior approval from the Senate in consultation with the Department of Student Engagement office. 
Failure to complete a timely and accurate credential transition shall constitute a violation of this Chapter and may result in referral to the Senate Judiciary Committee or administrative intervention by the Executive Branch via the Student Body President or designee. 
Emergency Recovery and Administrative Intervention: 
In the event that an official account becomes inaccessible, is compromised, or is being misused in violation of this Chapter or any other provision of the Student Body Statutes, the Department of Student Engagement office, in consultation with the Executive Branch communications officer, and Senate leadership shall have the authority to: 
Initiate password recovery or administrative override procedures; 
Lock or suspend platform usage until access can be reestablished or re-secured; 
Transfer control to an appropriate successor officer or institutional administrator. 
All such interventions shall be documented in writing and reported to the appropriate presiding officer of the branch or entity involved. Such interventions shall be appealed and halted by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate. 
Enforcement and Judicial Remedies:

Violations of This Chapter:
The following acts shall constitute a violation of the Student Government Digital Records Act of 2025: 
Failure to publish or transmit required records or content to the appropriate platform in the timeframe required by this Chapter; 
Unauthorized deletion, concealment, or alteration of official records, digital content, or access credentials; 
Refusal to provide access to or transition credentials of a digital platform during a lawful change in administration or office; 
Use of official SGA platforms or branding to mislead, impersonate, or disseminate unofficial, false, or personal content; 
Use of personal accounts, unapproved branding, or private infrastructure to conduct official business in circumvention of this Chapter; 
Repeated failure to comply with visual identity, social media access, or record-keeping standards as prescribed herein. 
Administrative Investigation and Enforcement: 
The Student Body Attorney General shall serve as the initial point of intake for reported or suspected violations of this Chapter and shall investigate or coordinate corrective actions in cooperation with the relevant branch head or designee. 
Upon determination that a violation has occurred, the following actions may be taken, following a period to allow voluntary compliance relief not to exceed a period of two (2) school days: 
Issuance of a written order to correct or republish missing content within a specified timeframe; 
Suspension of access to digital platforms or removal of noncompliant content; 
Referral to the Senate Judiciary Committee or Student Body President for consideration of disciplinary proceedings, including censure, removal from office, or ineligibility for future appointment. 
Referral to University Conduct Authorities:
In the event that any student officer or appointee is found to have committed: 
Unauthorized access or theft of SGA digital accounts; 
Deliberate destruction, defacement, or removal of institutional records; 
Obstruction of lawful transition of digital assets; 
The Executive Branch officer designated to oversee communications, in coordination with Department of Student Engagement, shall be required to submit a formal referral to the Florida State University Office of Student Conduct and Community Standards. 
This referral shall be accompanied by a written summary of findings and supporting documentation to assist in adjudication under the University’s Student Conduct Code. 
Judicial Authority of the Student Supreme Court: 
The Student Supreme Court shall retain original jurisdiction over all alleged violations of this Chapter and may, upon petition by any member of the Student Body, issue: 
Injunctive relief compelling publication or access; 
Writs of mandamus requiring compliance with content or transition obligations; 
Declaratory judgments clarifying the obligations of officers or branches under this Chapter; 
Other remedies authorized under Article IV of the Student Body Constitution and applicable provisions of Chapter 600 of the Student Body Statutes. 
The Clerk of the Court shall ensure all judgments or orders arising from such cases are published in accordance with the requirements of Section 208.4(c). 

Non-Retaliation and Whistleblower Protection:
No student, officer, or employee shall be subject to retaliation, discipline, or adverse action for reporting a violation of this Chapter or participating in an investigation or judicial proceeding related thereto.

sections.heading: Chapter 209 The SGA Land Acknowledgement Statement
sections.text:
Purpose and Scope of This Act: The Student Government Association of the Florida State University shall:
Adopt this Statement as the official position of the Student Body.
Post this Statement on the official Student Government website in a place of prominence.
Strongly encourage the reading aloud of this Statement, in its entirety, by the:
Student Body President following their taking of the Oath of Office as outlined in SBS Section 202(8), during the Fall Inauguration Ceremony, at the introduction of the State of the Student Body Address as outlined in SBS Chapter 306, and at any and all other events or meetings wherein they are present in their official capacity as Student Body President.
Student Senate President at any and all meetings of the Student Senate and at any and all other events or meetings wherein they are present in their official capacity as Student Senate President.
Furthermore, the Senate and its committees are empowered to include the Student Government Association Land Acknowledgment Statement as a listed Calendar item pursuant to Senate and Senate Committee Rules of Procedure.
Chair or Presiding Officer of any Student Government meeting held pursuant to SBS Chapter 203, prior to public comment.
Furthermore, if any SGA Officer or FSU Student present at such an SGA meeting requests to read the Student Government Association Land Acknowledgment Statement, the Chair must recognize that Officer or Student for the time to read the Statement in its entirety at the beginning of the meeting prior to Public Comment.
Such a reading shall not be counted as a Public Comment.
In the case of multiple requests at one meeting, the Chair shall select one requesting individual to read the Statement at their discretion.
In the event that the Chair does not permit an Officer or Student the right to read the Student Government Association Land Acknowledgment Statement after a formal request, that Chairperson shall be found in Violation of SBS Section 205(3)(f)(1).
Strongly encourage the reading aloud of this Statement, in its entirety, by any other SGA Officers and at any and all other events or meetings wherein they are present in their official capacity as an SGA Officer.
Strongly encourage the reading aloud of this Statement, with appropriate alterations to the Collective Nouns of the Statement, by any and all FSU students and organizations at RSO and other private events in their capacity as individual persons or organizations.
The Student Govenment Association Land Acknowledgment Statement shall be as follows:

The Florida State University Student Government Association acknowledges that FSU's Florida campuses are located on the ancestral and traditional homelands of the Seminole Tribe of Florida, the Miccosukee Tribe of Indians of Florida, the Apalachee, Seminole, and Muscogee Creek Nations, the ancient Calusa, Uzita and Tocobaga, and others. We pay respect to the resiliency of their tribal members, past and present, and to all Indigenous peoples. The University honors its unique and collaborative friendship with the Seminole Tribe of Florida, together paying tribute to the Tribe's great history and rich culture. We encourage all to learn about the significance of the Indigenous peoples in this region and throughout the nation. With a collective knowledge of the past, we are inspired to teach, live, and support a future that empowers all individuals.

sections.heading: Chapter 300 The Executive Branch
sections.text:
Purpose and Scope
Purpose: The purpose of this legislation is to define and outline the structure of the Executive Branch within the Student Government Association.
Scope: This act provides the framework and body within which the entities of the Executive Branch operate. It encompasses all entities in Title III, Title IX, and Title X and its provisions are considered fully binding to the aforementioned entities.
Composition of the Executive Branch:
The Executive Branch shall be composed of:
The Executive Departments (Chapter 301)
The Class Councils (Chapter 302)
The Executive Institutes (Chapter 303)
The Presidential Appointments and Dismissal Powers (Chapter 304)
Presidential Addresses (Chapter 306)
The Student Government Association Open Positions and Application Act (Chapter 307)
Leaves of Absences During the Summer Session for Members of the Executive Branch (Chapter 308)
The Executive Projects Account (Chapter 309)
The Student Body President, assisted by the Student Body Vice President, shall serve as head of the Executive Branch.
The "Executive Cabinet" shall be defined as the chief advising body to the Student Body President and shall include the Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, Chief of Staff, Chief of Staff to the Vice President, Deputy Student Body Treasurer, Student Body Attorney General, Cabinet Director and Executive Department Secretaries, as specified in §301.4, Student Body Statutes, or subsequent governing statutory language regarding Executive Departments, pursuant to Article III, Section 5 of the Student Body Constitution. 
The “Executive Branch” shall be defined as the collective of the Executive Branch Cabinet, Directors, Coordinators, and any other entity designated as being under the authority of the Student Body President. All members of an Executive Department shall serve in the Executive Branch. Officers serving within Agencies, Class Councils, Institutes, and Affiliated Projects that do not require Senate confirmation shall not be considered to hold a “major position” for purposes of restrictions on dual office-holding as provided in Chapter 100, Student Body Statutes.
Authority of the Executive Branch
The power of entities within the Executive Branch is derived from the Student Body President's constitutional investiture of the executive powers of the Student Government Association.
The Executive Branch shall be the administrative arm of the Student Government Association.
The Executive Branch shall be responsible for the enforcement and execution of the Student Body Statutes.
The Executive Branch shall be responsible for the planning and execution of programs, projects, and services provided to the students through the Student Government Association.
The Executive Branch shall be responsible for researching and developing programs to enhance the health, education, safety, or welfare of the Student Body of Florida State University.
Annual Policy on the Organization of the Executive Branch
The Executive Branch shall propose a policy, pursuant to Chapter 416, each academic year, before the last Senate meeting of the Summer Senate, to reflect the membership and positions of the Executive Branch. Such policy shall be updated as necessary to reflect the positions within the Executive Branch, within the scope of this Chapter’s structure.
The Student Body President designee who is announced as the winner of the election for Student Body President may propose a draft policy.
The Chiefs of Staff
The Student Body President, or President-elect by policy adopted pursuant to §301.11(b), Student Body Statutes, may establish the office of Chief of Staff to the Student Body President. The Chief of Staff shall have such duties assigned to them by the President, but these duties shall not duplicate any duties of any Secretary.
The Student Body President, or President-elect by policy adopted pursuant to §301.11(b), Student Body Statutes, may establish the office of Chief of Staff to the Student Body Vice President. The Chief of Staff shall have such duties assigned to them by the President, in consultation with the Vice President, but these duties shall not duplicate any duties of any Secretary or the President’s Chief of Staff.
Cabinet Director
The Student Body President or President-elect may, by policy adopted pursuant to §301.11(b), Student Body Statutes, establish the office of Cabinet Director.
The Cabinet Director shall be responsible for liaising between the Executive Departments and assisting the Executive Departments in carrying out the policies of the Executive Branch.
The Cabinet Director shall be the custodian of records for the Cabinet. Should there not be a Cabinet Director, the Student Body President shall designate a Secretary to serve as custodian of records for the Cabinet.
Independent Executive Officers
All executive powers of the Student Body shall be vested in the President of the Student Body, assisted by the Student Body Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, and such administrative officers as the President shall appoint in accordance with the Constitution of the Student Body and by Statute. 
The Student Body President shall hereinafter be referred to as the President, the Student Body Vice President as the Vice President, and the Student Body Treasurer as the Treasurer. 
The President shall:
Administer and enforce all laws of the Student Body.
Appoint Cabinet members as specified in the Statutes. Such appointments shall require a majority vote of the Student Senate to be approved.
Have the power to veto or sign acts of the Student Senate, provided that such power is exercised, within five (5) school days of its presentation to the Student Body President. A veto may be overridden by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of not less than a quorum of the Student Senate.
Call and preside over meetings of the Student Body.
Recommend legislation to the Student Senate.
Address the Student Senate at the beginning of each semester and at other times upon invitation by the Student Senate.
Instruct and require reports from Cabinet members and approve all policies made from them.
Remove any officer who has been appointed to a position in the Executive Branch.
Have the power to call for a referendum subject to two-thirds (2/3) majority Student Senate concurrence.
Represent the Student Body on the FSU Board of Trustees.
Prepare the budget of the Executive Branch with the assistance of the Treasurer.
Provide strategic oversight to the Executive Cabinet through the coordination of the Vice President.
The Vice President shall:
Assume the duties of the President in the absence of the President or upon that individual’s request.
Coordinate the efforts of the Cabinet and serve as coordinator for the formulation and completion of Cabinet projects.
Coordinate with the Student Body President, Student Body Treasurer, and Executive Cabinet to accomplish executive projects.
Direct grievances and ideas to the proper functionary and see that the grievances and ideas are acted upon.
Meet at least once a month with the directors of executive agencies, affiliated projects, and class councils to review performance, address questions and/or concerns, receive feedback and/or advice on the functioning of the Executive Branch, and discuss possibilities of new projects.
Serve as the vehicle throughout the Executive Branch to support programming events and accomplish agency, and council projects.
The Treasurer shall:
Provide information and support to any organization, executive agency, and funding board.
Meet monthly with the director or financial officer of executive agencies, affiliated projects, and funding boards individually to turn in monthly expenditure statements for review, address questions and/or concerns, and discuss upcoming funding opportunities.
Review all A&S expenditures made by executive agencies, student organizations (with the exception of COGS) and funding boards before the expenditures are submitted to the SGA Business Manager of SGA Accounting.
Have forty-eight (48) hours to approve or reject any expenditure. After forty-eight (48) hours, the expenditure may be considered without approval of the Student Body Treasurer.
Reject any expenditure; must have the approval and signature of the Student Body President.
Assist all entities within the Executive Branch in the development of effective resource management techniques.
Assist all entities within the Executive Branch with the correction of financial problems, and developing techniques to avoid further financial problems.
Assist the President in preparing the budget of the Executive Branch ensuring accuracy, transparency, and alignment with the goals and priorities of the student body.
Defend the Executive Branch budget in meetings or discussions with relevant stakeholders, including university administration, funding boards, and external entities.
Review the financial manual periodically and provide official recommendations for any necessary reforms or updates to ensure compliance with applicable regulations, enhance financial management practices, and promote transparency and accountability within the Executive Branch.
Review the finance code in student body statutes and provide official recommendations to the student body Senate for any necessary reforms.
Represent the Executive Branch in financial discussions, meetings, or negotiations with external entities, such as RSOs. This includes advocating for the financial interests and needs of the student body, seeking additional funding opportunities, and collaborating with external organizations or institutions on matters related to the financial well-being of the Executive Branch.
The Deputy Student Body Treasurer shall be subject to dismissal as articulated in Section 301(4). This person shall advise and assist the Student Body Treasurer. 
The Deputy Treasurer shall work with the Executive Branch and Student Senate Press Secretary to post on the FSU SGA Instagram account when any SGA funding board opportunities become available. This post should include a brief description of the opportunity, a link to the relevant pages or information on the SGA website, and links to the applications.
 In the absence of the Student Body Treasurer, the Deputy Treasurer shall assume all responsibilities outlined for the Treasurer.
Office of the Attorney General
The Student Body Attorney General shall hereinafter be referred to as the Attorney General.
The Office of the Attorney General is responsible for the enforcement of Student Body Statutes, the Constitution of the Student Body, any policies adopted pursuant to Chapter 416, Student Body Statutes, and any other rules and procedures that govern a student or organization, provided such provisions fall within the jurisdiction of the SGA.
The Attorney General shall be the head of the Office of the Attorney General.
The Attorney General shall serve at the pleasure of the Student Body President.
The Student Body President may assign other duties and responsibilities to the Office of the Attorney General, so long as these do not violate the Student Body Statutes or the Constitution of the Student Body.
When the position of Attorney General is vacated, the most senior deputy Attorney General shall assume the position of Acting Attorney General. In such instances, the acting Attorney General shall serve as the Attorney General until a new Attorney General is confirmed.
The Office of the Attorney General shall be responsible for and empowered to:
Investigate and/or initiate proceedings against any SGA funded RSO, Agency, Affiliated Project, funding board, member/entity of the executive branch, or student, for violations of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, the Constitution of the Student Body, any policies adopted pursuant to Chapter 416, Student Body Statutes, and any other rules or procedures governing the student or organization as it relates to SGA.
Launch an investigation into possible violations of these provisions.
Only initiate proceedings regarding a possible violation following an approved investigation by either the Director of Student Governance and Advocacy or The Student Body President.
If necessary, petition the Student Supreme Court to obtain records as may pertain to any investigation, subject to applicable public records exemptions.
Recommend to the Senate potential changes to Statutes and the Constitution of the Student Body.
Work with the Student Body President and their Cabinet to follow the proceedings of both the Judicial and Legislative Branch, in order to keep the Student Body President and their Cabinet knowledgeable on what is occurring in the other Branches and any actions they may wish to take.
Provide counsel and represent the Executive Branch and members/entities of the Executive Branch in all SGA legal proceedings heard before FSU authorities.
Any member/entity of the Executive Branch may choose to waive this counsel and representation if they so desire.
If this counsel and representation is waived then, the member/entity may choose to have other individuals or groups to counsel and represent them.
Appoint a designee to represent the Executive Branch on behalf of the Office of the Attorney General when so desired, with prior notice to the appropriate parties.
Work with the Student Body President to appoint at least one, but no more than two, Deputy Attorneys General.
Assist in the creation and/or filing of executive orders at the request and approval of the Student Body President.
Assist Executive Branch officers in understanding their roles, duties, and responsibilities.
Create internal Rules and Procedures as a policy pursuant to Chapter 416, Student Body Statutes, to help execute the duties and responsibilities of the Office of the Attorney General, including, but not limited to, the parameters for investigations and prosecutions. These Rules and Procedures shall be made available to the public, but adoption and amendments shall not require Senate approval.
Render public memorandums on the activities of the Office of the Attorney General including, but not limited to, investigations and/or proceedings made on behalf of the Executive Branch.
Execute any other duties and responsibilities delegated to them as enumerated in the Student Body Statutes.
