sections.heading: Chapter 301 The Executive Departments
sections.text:
Purpose and Scope: This act shall be called the "Student Government Association Executive Department Act of 2025," hereinafter referred to as the "Executive Department Act." The amendments to this act, as it relates to the creation of executive departments requiring tangible outcomes, shall be called “The Cabinet Overhaul for Responsibility and Efficiency Act," hereinafter referred to as “The CORE Act.”
Creation
Executive Departments are created in bill form, as additions to the Student Body Statutes under Title III “Executive Branch.”
The bill shall contain information of the Department's title, purpose, internal organizational structure, and a clear outline of what the Department's service or function is for the student body. Upon creation, Executive Departments shall be incorporated into the organizational structure of the Student Government Association Executive Branch.
Definitions
An Executive Department is an administrative division of the Executive Branch, established to implement student-facing services, initiatives, or advocacy efforts in designated areas of policy, programming, or student interest. Each department shall be led by a Secretary and shall operate under the supervision of the Student Body President. Executive Departments are responsible for delivering tangible outcomes, defined as real resources, opportunities, and value for the Student Body as a whole.
Operation
Student Government Association Executive Departments are required to be in compliance with the Student Body Constitution and Statutes, Florida State University policies and regulations, the State of Florida Statutes, the State of Florida Constitution, the United States Statutes and the United States Constitution at all times while in operation. Noncompliance with these provisions shall call for remedial action, which will be a review conducted by the Student Senate Internal Affairs committee. The Student Body President shall be authorized to take whatever action is deemed necessary and proper as defined by the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.
Each Executive Department shall be structured as follows:
Secretary: Serves as the chief administrative officer of the Department, providing leadership, implementing policy, and representing the Department within the Executive Branch while supervising all department personnel.
Director: Oversees broader functional areas within the Department (Offices), supervises the work of Coordinators or other personnel, and provides strategic guidance to advance departmental goals and initiatives.
Coordinator: Manages specific programs, initiatives, or logistical functions within the Department, operating under the direction of a Director or a Secretary. They also may be a liaison to an FSU SGA or campus entity.
Appointment, Term, and Vacancies:
Secretaries shall be appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by a majority vote of the Student Senate. Directors and Coordinators shall be appointed by the Secretary with the approval of the Student Body President.
All appointees shall serve at the pleasure of the Student Body President for a term not to exceed the appointing President’s tenure, unless reappointed by a succeeding President.
In the event of a vacancy, the Student Body President (for Secretaries) or the Secretary and Student Body President (for Directors and Coordinators) may designate an acting officer, who may serve for no more than six (6) weeks without Senate confirmation. Such designations of acting officers shall be made in the form of Executive Orders issued by the Student Body President, which shall specify the effective date and termination date of such appointments.
Dismissal of acting officers shall also be made in the form of Executive Orders issued by the Student Body President, which shall specify the effective date of the termination.
The Secretaries shall act within the restrictions stated in Section 5 to execute the statutory responsibilities of the department.
The guidance, administration, and regulation of the departments are the responsibility of the Student Body President. The Secretaries shall report directly to the Student Body President, but any action taken by a Secretary may be countermanded by the Student Body President if the President feels it is in the best interest of the student body.
Pursuant to the Activities and Service Fee Guidelines, the Student Senate shall be the allocation and revisionary authority in all budgetary matters pertaining to departments.
All Secretaries may be dismissed at the discretion of the Student Body President or be impeached by the Senate pursuant to the Student Body Constitution.
The Student Body Treasurer shall be responsible for the financial responsibility of departments. All expenditures of departments must be approved and submitted by the Secretary in the form of a purchase request via the University-designated student organization management platform. Once submitted, all purchase requests shall be reviewed by the Student Body Treasurer for approval or rejection. The SGA Accounting Office will finalize and process all purchase requests approved by the Student Body Treasurer in accordance with the University's purchasing policy.”
In the event that the Secretary of a department should take temporary leave of ten (10) consecutive business days or more from the FSU environment, and thus be unable to directly contribute to, or oversee the department, it shall be their responsibility to notify in writing the Student Body President and the Secretary of Administrative Affairs no less than ten (10) consecutive business days prior to such leave.
Said letter must include an officer of the department appointed by the Secretary who will serve as chief contact, liaison, and administrator of the department, and who is duly authorized to serve in such capacity during such time as the Secretary may be absent.
Failure to submit said letter will result in mandatory audit or management and fiscal controls of the department.
An extension of up to ten (10) school days can be permitted for good cause by proof of extenuating circumstances received by the Student Body President including, but not limited to, death of an immediate family member, medical reasons, or religious observance.
Leaves of absences do not include university recognized holidays including but not limited to Spring Break or other regularly scheduled campus-wide holidays.
Responsibilities and Reporting
The Secretary shall:
Manage and oversee all Department operations, staff, and programming.
Appoint and supervise Directors, Coordinators, and any other designated roles.
Maintain communication with the Executive Branch and other departments as needed.
Submit written reports, upon request, to the Student Body President and the Student Senate detailing operations, expenditures, initiatives, and outcomes.
Appear before the Student Senate or relevant Senate committees when requested.
Serve in the Executive Cabinet.

Directors shall report directly to the Secretary, oversee all operations of their respective department branch, and fulfill duties assigned by the Secretary in line with the Department’s mission.
Coordinators shall report directly to the Secretary and fulfill duties assigned by the Secretary in line with the Department’s mission.
All executive department regulations shall be posted in Municode.
Student Senate Oversight
The Student Senate shall receive notice of all proposed regulations within Executive Departments.
Upon findings of possible violations of Student Body Statutes and the Student Body Constitution regarding Executive appointments and staffing, the Senate Internal Affairs Committee, or an Investigative Board set up under Chapter 406, Student Body Statutes, shall be the proper venue.

The Executive Departments:
Department of Academic Affairs
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Academic Affairs
The Secretary of Academic Affairs shall:
Supervise all efforts related to Research Grants facilitated through the executive branch.
Supervise all efforts related to The Owl facilitated through the executive branch.
The Department shall liaison with the College Leadership Council Chairs, University Libraries, University Provost’s office, and the Student Senate President’s appointees to the Academic Honor Policy Committee.
Department of Administrative Affairs

This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Administrative Affairs, who shall:
Administer all appointments for vacated major and minor positions in the executive branch, except those appointments in the agencies and affiliated projects, and vacated senate seats.

Assist in the administration of the Executive Branch to the extent determined by the Student Body President.

Department of Athletics
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Athletics
The Secretary of Athletics shall:
Serve as the liasion between the Student-Athelete Advisory Council and the executive branch. 
Serve as the liasion between the Student Seminole Boosters and the executive branch.
Department of Campus Life
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Campus Life.
The Secretary of Campus Life shall assign student issues to be prioritized by the executive branch.
This Department shall oversee and support the following affiliated projects:
Inter Residence Hall Council
Union Board
Campus Recreation Board
Department of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion.

This Department shall collaborate with and support:
The Diversity and Inclusion Institute
The Executive Agencies

Department of Health, Wellness, and Safety
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Health, Wellness, and Safety.

Department of Sustainability
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Sustainability.

Department of Legal Affairs
This department shall be supervised by the Attorney General.
The Attorney General shall:
Carry out the duties assigned in Chapter 300, Student Body Statutes.
Maintain executive compliance.

This department shall, at minimum, be composed of:
The Deputy Attorney(s) General

The Solicitor General
The Legislative Affairs Director

The Legislative Affairs Coordinator(s)
The Department of Governmental Affairs

The Department of Governmental Affairs (DGA) is the official advocate for advancing student interests in local, state, and federal government. The office promotes civic engagement and public policy participation through initiatives such as voter registration drives, student advocacy, testimony before legislative bodies, and policy education. DGA provides training in advocacy skills, supports student involvement in government internships, and works closely with the FSU Office of Governmental Relations to coordinate events like FSU Day at the Capitol. Additionally, DGA partners with student organizations to mobilize students around key legislative and policy issues relevant to the student body.
DGA shall contain, at a minimum, a Secretary and Deputy Secretary of Governmental Affairs.
The Secretary of Governmental Affairs shall manage student government advocacy and policy initiatives by coordinating lobbying efforts and serving as the primary liaison with institutional and governmental bodies at the local, state, and federal levels.
The Deputy Secretary of Governmental Affairs shall have the rank of Director and shall assist the Secretary in the operations of the Department.
DGA shall operate a program entitled Noles Engaged in Politics.
The Noles Engaged in Politics (NEP) Program is a professional development initiative under DGA. Its primary purpose is to engage and educate students on political systems, current issues affecting the state of Florida and higher education, and to provide leadership and mentorship opportunities in preparation for FSU Day at the Capitol.
Participation in the NEP Program is open to all FSU students who demonstrate a commitment to civic engagement and public service. The selection process shall be conducted by DGA leadership.
Students participating in NEP are not officers of SGA and represent SGA only insofar as it is consistent with the Legislative Agenda.

DGA shall have the authority to create and advocate for a legislative agenda representing the interests of the FSU student body at the local, state, and federal levels. This includes developing policy proposals and legislative stances aligned with student needs and the current administration’s goals.
Policy Proposals Approval Process:
DGA may draft and submit policy proposals for consideration by legislative bodies. To inform priorities, DGA should engage in outreach to solicit student input. While student feedback should be considered, it is not binding.
The DGA Board may present a draft proposal to the Student Senate for feedback. A finalized version must be submitted for Senate approval before advocacy begins. A majority vote in the Senate authorizes lobbying efforts on the proposal, but preparatory work with stakeholders may be conducted prior to Senate approval.
If the Senate is not in session for more than three (3) weeks in the two (2) months prior to the start of a session of the Florida Legislature, the Student Body President may provide provisional approval of the policy proposal(s).
Should provisional approval be necessary, DGA must present the proposal(s) to the Senate at the earliest opportunity possible. DGA must cease all lobbying efforts on proposal(s) not adopted by the Senate immediately upon the Senate informing the Secretary of the proposal(s) failing.
If the Agenda fails to pass the Student Senate, DGA must revise the proposal and/or conduct additional consultation with Senators before resubmitting. The revised proposal should include a summary of changes made or feedback addressed. Advocacy efforts on unapproved proposals shall not proceed until approval is granted.
Legislative Stances Approval Process
DGA may also adopt positions on external legislation relevant to students. These stances shall be compiled into a resolution and submitted to the Student Senate for approval. If passed, DGA may choose to advocate for those positions. Additional stances can be added through future resolutions.
If the Senate is not in session for more than three (3) weeks in the two (2) months prior to the start of a session of the Florida Legislature, the Student Body President may provide provisional approval of the legislative stance(s).
Should provisional approval be necessary, DGA must present the legislative stance(s) to the Senate at the earliest opportunity possible. DGA must cease all lobbying efforts on legislative stance (s) not adopted by the Senate immediately upon the Senate informing the Secretary of the legislative stance(s) failing.
If the Legislative Stances fails to pass the Student Senate, DGA must revise it and/or conduct additional consultation with Senators before resubmitting. The revised stances should include a summary of changes made or feedback addressed. Advocacy efforts on unapproved stances shall not proceed until approval is granted.
Following lobbying efforts, the Secretary shall deliver a report to the Senate summarizing the Department’s activities and outcomes. The Senate should also be notified of any proposals that result in legislative action.
The Department of Communications
The Department shall manage SGA's outward-facing communications. This includes media outreach, digital engagement, branding, and messaging efforts that communicate SGA’s initiatives, impact, and services to the FSU community and beyond.
The Department shall, at a minimum, consist of a Press Secretary, who shall be Secretary for the Department. The Press Secretary shall be SGA’s primary spokesperson, overseeing media outreach, crafting clear messaging, and promoting SGA’s initiatives to the FSU community and beyond.
The Office of the Treasurer
The Office shall:
Serve as the administrative housing for the operations of the Student Body Treasurer.
Be the office in charge of all financial matters in relation to the Executive Branch.
Provide assistance to all SGA entities on financial matters.
Be authorized to undertake all actions and exercise all powers granted to the Student Body Treasurer.
Engage in routine reviews of spending in Student Government. 
Undertake all duties assigned to it by the Student Body Treasurer.
The office shall be an independent executive office led by the Student Body Treasurer.

The office shall include a Deputy Student Body Treasurer, as created by §300.5, SBS, who shall, for the purpose of organizational structure, have the powers of a Secretary.
The Deputy Student Body Treasurer shall solely report to the Student Body Treasurer.
The Deputy Student Body Treasurer shall serve at the pleasure of the Student Body Treasurer, in addition to the constitutional removal authority of the Student Body President.

Department of Programming
This Department shall be supervised by the Secretary of Programming.
This department shall support and oversee:
Golden Torch Lecture Series
The Homecoming Council

The Class Councils

Any SGA entity, department, or affiliated project in the effectuation of student body programming funded by A&S fees.
Confirmed Officer Reserved Power
The following powers and functions are reserved exclusively to confirmed officers and may not be delegated to non-confirmed members of the Executive Branch:
Approval of expenditures from any Student Government fund or account held by the department, or any official communication on behalf of FSU SGA to any: university entity, external organization, or local, state, federal government entity and/or official;
Submission of hiring recommendations to the Student Body President for positions requiring Senate confirmation; 
Issuance of official departmental policy statements or orders having the effect of binding departmental personnel to a course of action;
Any official communication on behalf of FSU-SGA to any university entity; external organization; or local, state, federal government entity and/or official.
Any action taken in violation of this section by a non-confirmed individual shall be voidable at the discretion of the Student Body President or, upon a formal recommendation of the Senate Internal Affairs Committee and majority vote of the Student Senate. Violations may also be reported to the Attorney General for enforcement.
Coordinator and Operational Staff Positions
The Student Body President and/or Cabinet Secretaries may create Coordinator and Operational Staff positions within Executive Departments to support the programmatic and administrative functions of the Executive Branch. Such positions shall not require Senate confirmation.
The Secretary and/or Student Body President shall issue a formal “Intent to Hire” for any additional internal department roles or operational staff positions. This document shall serve as written public notice and must contain a comprehensive justification for the role’s creation, a detailed list of duties, the specific reporting structure, defined organizational goals, and all reporting responsibilities.
These roles shall be publicly noticed for applications on the official Student Government Association website for no less than one (1) week, and all candidates must be interviewed prior to the position being filled. The recruitment and posting process shall proceed according to the following sequence:
The Intent to Hire shall be provided to the Student Senate President and Internal Affairs Chair who shall transmit said notice to the Senate and Internal Affairs Committee. 
Following these transmissions, the position may be posted to the website and recruitment may commence. 
Upon the selection of an appointee, their application and interview notes shall be transmitted to the Student Senate.
Individuals serving in Coordinator or Operational Staff positions shall be limited to operational support, program coordination, and functions assigned by their supervising confirmed officer. 
The Student Body President shall maintain a live public roster of all active Coordinator and Operational Staff positions, including position title, department, and name of the individual serving, on the SGA Website. The roster shall be updated within seven (7) calendar days of any change in personnel.
Each confirmed officer shall be accountable for the actions and the conduct of Coordinator and Operational Staff personnel under their direct supervision. Any violation of this section by non-confirmed staff shall be attributed to the supervising confirmed officer, for purposes of Senate oversight.
Substantiated instances of misfeasance, malfeasance, or nonfeasance by Coordinator or operational staff personnel may be reported by the supervising confirmed officer to the Student Body President within five (5) business days of substantiation. Failure to report or take appropriate corrective action may constitute grounds for the supervising officer's own impeachment for nonfeasance.
Special Advisor Appointments
The Student Body President may appoint Special Advisors to provide counsel on designated subject areas. Special Advisors shall not hold voting authority, operational authority, or a position within any established Executive Department, but shall be considered a major position pursuant to Chapter 100.5.
A Special Advisor appointment shall have an initial term of no more than eight (8) weeks from the date of appointment. A Special Advisor appointment may be extended for one additional period not to exceed eight (8) weeks upon adoption of a consent resolution by the Student Senate. No further extensions shall be permitted. Total continuous service as a Special Advisor shall not exceed sixteen (16) weeks.
Upon the initial appointment of any Special Advisor, the Student Body President shall provide written notice via Executive Order to the Student Senate President and Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee within three (3) calendar days, identifying the advisor by name, describing the subject area of advisory responsibility, and stating the initial term start and end dates.
The Student Body President shall include all active Special Advisor appointments in the public roster maintained pursuant to § 301.9(c), Student Body Statutes.  
Transitional Appointments and Confirmations
To allow for the efficient transition of power each Spring, the candidate who is declared the winner of the election for Student Body President each year (the “President-designate”) shall be authorized to, under the same rules which apply to a sitting Student Body President, appoint officials as designates for the role they are being appointed to (an “officer-designate”).
The President-designate shall, prior to appointing any persons as an officer-designate, propose a draft policy setting forth the structure of their Executive Branch, pursuant to Chapter 421, Student Body Statutes.
The Senate shall be authorized to hear and vote on candidates appointed to be officers-designate if the role they are being designated for requires Senate confirmation. Candidates to be officers-designate which require Senate confirmation shall not become an officer-designate until they receive Senate confirmation.
Officers-designate shall take office upon the swearing-in of the President730 designate.

sections.heading: Chapter 302 The Class Councils
sections.text:
The Class Councils at Florida State University shall instill unity in each class of the Florida State University, in order to enhance their college experience and encourage active participation in the Florida State University community as both students and alumni.
The Class Councils shall exist of four independent entities: the Freshman Class Council, the Sophomore Class Council, the Junior Class Council, and the Senior Class Council.
Each one of the Class Councils shall have a President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary. Each of these positions in the Senior Class Council shall be elected in the SGA Spring General Election, pursuant to Chapter 706.8 of Student Body Statutes. All other positions shall be appointed in line with the policy permitted by 302.4. 
The Class Councils may adopt internal Rules of Procedure to regulate their activities, which shall be treated as a policy pursuant to Chapter 416. These Rules of Procedure may be adopted and amended in a manner as determined by the Senior Class Council.

sections.heading: Chapter 303 The Executive Institutes
sections.text:
Creation and Purpose:
Purpose: The purpose of this chapter is to define and delineate the nature of the Institutes placed under the auspices of the Executive Branch of the Student Government Association.
Definition: An Institute is an annual Executive Project that is administered under the auspices and supervision of the Executive Branch through changing administrations.
Executive Authority Over Institutes: The Student Body Vice President shall have the responsibility over the supervision and regulation of the Executive Institutes. The Student Body President shall have the discretion to dismiss Institute Directors and Assistant Directors.
Leadership Structure:
All Institutes shall have a Director and Assistant Director who shall be interviewed and selected by the outgoing Director and Assistant Director, unless otherwise specified in the individual Institute’s statutes. The Director and Assistant Director shall be sent as recommendation to the Student Body President and may be forwarded to the Student Senate pursuant to Section 304(3)(d).
The newly confirmed Institute Directors shall be responsible for the appointment and supervision of all other Institute personnel deemed necessary. An executive board member from each Institute shall be designated as a financial officer to administer the finances of each respective Institute.
Policy: Each Institute shall have the right to adopt internal policy and procedures pursuant to Chapter 421 governing attendance, structure, or what is deemed necessary by the Director and Assistant Director in consultation with the Institute's advisor.
Such policy shall be sent to the Senate via a resolution placed on the Consent Calendar sponsored by the Institute's liaison or Senate leadership.

Monetary Allocations: The Student Body Treasurer shall be responsible for the financial responsibility of Executive Institutes. Monetary allocations required by Institutes to fulfill their outlined purposes shall be budgeted from the Executive Projects account. 
The Institutes: The following is a list of the Executive Institutes and corresponding section numbers that appear in Chapter 303:
Freshman Leadership Institute (Section 303(2))
Transfer Leadership Institute (Section 303(3))
Diversity and Inclusion Institute (Section 303(4))
Executive Leadership Institute (Section 303(5))

Freshman Leadership Institute:
Purpose: The Freshman Leadership Institute (FLI) is a 10-week program aimed at providing first-year students with the tools to become active student leaders while providing support as students adjust to the Florida State University campus and culture.
Program:
Participant Selection:
The application will be made available to incoming first-year Freshman at least two (2) weeks before the start of the Fall Semester and will close the first Friday of the Fall Semester.
Meetings:
The Freshman Leadership Institute shall meet once a week for the duration of the program during the Fall Semester.
Additional meetings may be held at the discretion of the Director of FLI to fulfill the purpose stated in Section 309(1)(a).
Leadership Team Selection:
Director:
The Director of the Freshman Leadership Institute shall be selected by the outgoing Leadership Team.
The Leadership Team is defined as any officer positions, including the Director, that has been appointed by the Executive Branch to fulfill the stated purpose in Section 303(2)(a).
The Leadership Team shall consider participatory or leadership experience of the Institute during recruitment for this position.

The application for the Director of the Freshman Leadership Institute shall be made available on the Student Government Association Website on the 1st week of the Spring Semester and close no later than the third week.
Once selected by the outgoing Leadership Team, the candidate will then be forwarded to the Executive Branch for confirmation.
Responsibilities: The responsibilities of the Director shall include, but not be limited to the following:
Represent the interests of the Freshman Leadership Institute on the campus of Florida State University in accordance to the stated purpose.
Be responsible for the operation of the Freshman Leadership Institute.
Make and execute decisions on program structure, Freshman Leadership Institute affiliated events, finances, and other activities with the advice of the Leadership Team, Student Body Vice President, and Student Program Coordinator.
Recommend officer positions, to the Executive Branch, that are needed, in order to fulfill the stated purpose in Section 303(2)(a).
Operations: 
Transition of Office

The outgoing Leadership Team shall transfer all pertinent information to the incoming Leadership Team pursuant to Chapter 207.

General Rules and Requirements

Attendance and Participation

Participants shall be expected to attend and actively participate in all scheduled meetings, events, and opportunities associated with the Freshman Leadership Institute.

Participants who accumulate more than three (3) unexcused absences during the duration of the program may be removed from the Institute under the discretion of the Director. 
Excused absences may include obligations, medical emergencies, family emergencies, university-sponsored activities, and other responsibilities as stated in Florida State's "University Attendance Policy".

Removal from Office:
If the Director fails to fulfill the stated purpose, it will be up to the discretion of the Student Program Coordinator or Student Body Vice President to determine whether the Director shall be removed from office.
Vacancies:
If any vacancy occurs during the duration of the Freshman Leadership Institute that is under the Director, the Executive Branch shall appoint a person at the recommendation of the Director to fulfill the duties of said position.
If the Director position becomes vacant, the Assistant Director shall fill in as the Acting Director until a new Director is selected.
The application for the Director of the Freshman Leadership Institute shall be made available on the Student Government Association Website within five (5) school days of the Director renouncing the position and shall remain open for no less than ten (10) school days.
The Executive Branch will then interview and confirm a new Director from the applicant pool for the remainder of the Freshman Leadership Institute.
Transfer Leadership Institute:
Purpose: The purpose of the Transfer Leadership Institute (TLI) is to provide personal, professional, and leadership growth opportunities for ambitious transfer students through networking, programming, and educational experiences that impact the Florida State University student body and its surrounding community.
Program:
Participant Selection:
The application will be made available to incoming transfer students at least two weeks before the start of the Fall semester and will close no later than the first week of the Fall semester.
Meetings:
The Transfer Leadership Institute shall meet once a week for the duration of the program during the Fall Semester.
Additional meetings may be held at the discretion of the Director in order to fulfill the stated purpose in Section 303(3)(a).
Leadership Team Selection:
Director:
The Director of the Transfer Leadership Institute shall be selected by the outgoing Leadership Team.
The Leadership Team is defined as any officer positions, including the Director, that have been appointed by the Executive Branch to fulfill the stated purpose in Section 303(3)(a).
The application for the Director of the Transfer Leadership Institute shall be made available on the Student Government Association Website the first week of the Spring Semester and close no later than the third week of the Spring Semester.
Once selected by the outgoing Leadership Team, the candidate will then be forwarded to the Executive Branch for confirmation.
Responsibilities: The Responsibilities of the Director shall include, but not be limited to, the following:
Represent the interest of the Transfer Leadership Institute on the campus of Florida State University in accordance to the stated purpose.
Be responsible for the operation of the Transfer Leadership Institute.
Make and execute decisions on program structure of the Transfer Leadership Institute affiliated events, finance, and other activities with the advice of the Leadership Team, Student Body Vice President, and Student Government Advisor.
Recommend needed officer positions to the Executive Branch, in order to fulfill the stated purpose.
Removal from Office:
If the Director fails to fulfill the stated purpose, it will be up to the discretion of the Student Program Coordinator or Student Body Vice President to determine whether the Director shall be removed from office.
Vacancies:
If any vacancy occurs during the duration of the Transfer Leadership Institute that is under the Director, the Executive Branch shall appoint a person at the recommendation of the Director to fulfill the duties of said position.
If the Director position becomes vacant, then the Assistant Director shall fill in as the Acting Director until a new Director is selected.
The application for the Director of the Transfer Leadership Institute shall be made available within five (5) school days of the Director renouncing the position and shall remain open for no less than ten (10) school days.
The Executive Branch will then interview confirm a new Director from the applicant pool for the remainder of the Transfer Leadership Institute.
Diversity and Inclusion Institute:
Purpose: The Diversity and Inclusion (D&I) Institute is an 8-week program held in the Spring semester dedicated to providing a space for students to fully understand the range of diversity and multiculturalism, including but not limited to ability, socioeconomic, age, rural/urban, veterans, sexual orientation, ethnicity, race, gender identity & expression, religion, and faith structures through workshops that are focused on awareness, discussion and collaborative learning activities.
Program:
Participant Selection:
The application will be made available to prospective participants at least three (3) weeks before the end of the Fall Semester and will close on the last day of the Fall Semester.
The selection of the participants shall be conducted at the discretion of the Executive Board.
Meetings:
The D&I Institute shall meet once a week for the duration of the program during the Spring Semester.
Additional meetings may be held at the discretion of the Director of the D&I Institute to fulfill the purpose stated in Section 303(4)(a).
Leadership Team Selection:
Director:
The Director of the D&I Institute shall be selected by the outgoing Leadership Team.
The Leadership Team is defined as any officer positions, including the Director, that has been appointed by the Executive Branch to fulfill the stated purpose in Section 303(4)(a).
The application for the Director of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute shall be made available on the Student Government Association Website on the 1st Friday after Spring Break and close two (2) weeks thereafter.
Once selected by the outgoing Leadership Team, the candidate will then be forwarded to the Executive Branch for Student Senate confirmation.
Responsibilities: The responsibilities of the Director shall include, but not be limited to the following:
Represent the interests of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute on the campus of Florida State University in accordance to the stated purpose.
Be responsible for the effective operations of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute.
Make and execute decisions on program structure, D&I Institute affiliated events, finances, and other activities with the advice of the Leadership Team, Student Body Vice President, and Student Program Coordinator.
Be financially certified for the fiscal year.
Recommend officer positions, to the Executive Branch, that are needed, in order to fulfill the stated purpose in Section 303(4)(a).
Removal from Office:
If the Director fails to fulfill the stated purpose, it will be up to the discretion of the Student Program Coordinator or Student Body Vice President to determine whether the Director shall be removed from office.
Vacancies:
If any vacancy occurs during the duration of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute that is under the Director, the Executive Branch shall appoint a person at the recommendation of the Director to fulfill the duties of said position.
If the Director position becomes vacant, the Student Body Vice President shall fill in as the presiding Director until a new Director is selected.
The application for the Director of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute shall be made available on the Student Government Association Website within five (5) school days of the Director renouncing the position and shall remain open for no less than ten (10) school days.
The Executive Branch will then interview and confirm a new Director from the applicant pool for the remainder of the Diversity & Inclusion Institute.
Executive Leadership Institute

Purpose
The Executive Leadership Institute (ELI) provides FSU students with practical experience in the operations of the Executive Branch to enhance leadership skills and promote continuity. Students shall be provided the opportunity to make tangible change under the supervision of a member of the Executive Branch.
Program

Selection

The application will be made available to FSU students for two (2) weeks before the start of the Fall semester.

Selection of students will be conducted under the supervision of the Student Body Vice President or designee.

The number of students selected is left to the discretion of the Student Body Vice President or designee.

Participants in the Executive Leadership Institute shall not be considered as major offices as per statutes section 100.5.

Meetings

The Executive Leadership Institute shall, at minimum, meet once a month for the duration of the program during the Fall and Spring semesters.

Additional meetings may be held at the discretion of the Student Body Vice President, or designee, to fulfill the stated purpose in 303.5 Section A.

Leadership

The Institute shall be maintained and run by the Student Body President or designee within the Executive Branch.

sections.heading: Chapter 304 Presidential Appointment And Dismissal Powers
sections.text:
The Student Body President, in the execution of their authority to appoint and dismiss appointed offices of the Student Body, shall have the authority to create a policy pursuant to Chapter 416 to regulate specific processes regarding appointment and dismissal.
The adoption and revision of this policy shall be subject to approval by Senate, and shall be placed on the consent calendar. In the case of an objection, a majority vote of Senate shall be needed for the adoption or revision to pass.

Minimum Positions Requiring Confirmation
The following positions within the Executive Branch shall require appointment by the Student Body President and confirmation by a majority vote of the Student Senate prior to assuming official duties with independent authority: 
Executive Department Secretaries
Executive Department Directors
Student Body Attorney General
Deputy Attorney(s) General
Solicitor General
Deputy Solicitor(s) General, should such position(s) be created by the Student Body President
Deputy Director(s) of the Department of Government Affairs
Deputy Student Body Treasurer
Chief of Staff, Cabinet Director and Chief of Staff to the Vice President, upon the creation of such position(s) by the Student Body President.
Any additional position requiring Senate confirmation defined by statute.
Confirmation obtained for one position shall not satisfy the confirmation requirement for any other position. Any individual moving from one confirmable position to another confirmable position, whether by promotion, reassignment, or reclassification, shall be required to obtain new Senate confirmation for the new position prior to exercising independent authority in that role. 
The Student Senate may, by statutory amendments, add positions to the list in subsection (a) upon a finding that a position exercises policy-level authority, independent decision-making, or represents the Student Body externally.
The Student Body President shall maintain a current public roster of all confirmed officers on the SGA Website, updated within seven (7) calendar days of any change in status.

sections.heading: Chapter 305 Presidential Addresses
sections.text:
The Student Body President shall have the authority to address the Student Body on any matter, given public notice no less than twenty-four (24) hours in advance of the address.
Opening Address:
At the Spring Inauguration, the incoming Student Body President shall deliver an opening address.
The incoming Student Body President shall collaborate with the organizers of Inauguration to ensure that the opening address follows the applicable parameters of the event and venue.
If a Student Body President vacates office, their successor shall schedule the first opportunity possible to deliver an opening address.
The Student Body Vice President and Treasurer may also be given time to give an opening address if the Student Body President deems it appropriate.
Closing Address:
At the Spring Inauguration, the outgoing Student Body President shall deliver a closing address.
The outgoing Student Body President shall collaborate with the organizers of Inauguration to ensure that the closing address follows the applicable parameters of the event and venue.
If a Student Body President resigns, is impeached, or otherwise vacates office, they shall have the opportunity to give a closing address.
If a Student Body President is elected for a second term, at the Spring Inauguration which would mark the beginning of their second term, the opening and closing addresses may be combined for the sake of time.
The Student Body Vice President and Treasurer may also be given time to give a closing address if the Student Body President deems it appropriate.
State of the Student Body Address:
The Student Body President shall address the Student Body in an address known as the “State of the Student Body Address” no later than five (5) weeks into the Fall Semester. The State of the Student Body Address shall be designed to inform the Student Body of goals, comments on the student experience, and any other appropriate topics.
In the event of severe extenuating circumstances, the State of the Student Body Address may be postponed past the five (5) week mark in the Fall Semester, prior to fall elections. This should only be done when there is a genuine concern which would make it unfeasible to hold the address in the timeframe as laid out here.
The State of the Student Body Address must be open and advertised to the entire Student Body. However, the following individuals must be in attendance, unless there is a genuine conflict as confirmed by the SGA Program Director:
Justices of the Student Supreme Court
The Executive Chief of Staff
The Student Body Attorney General
The Executive Cabinet and Executive Office of the President
The Directors of all Agencies, Institutes, and Affiliated Projects
The Chair of the Union Board
The Chair of the Campus Recreation Board
The Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students
The Student Body Vice President
The Student Body Treasurer
Senior Class Council Officers
All Student Senators
The Student Body President may invite any other individuals they deem appropriate for this address, and the University President and Vice President for Student Affairs must receive an invitation.
The address may be structured at the discretion of the Student Body President, so long as it follows the criteria as laid out in this statute and does not unnecessarily restrict any individuals from attending.
The Student Body President must attend the first Senate meeting following their inauguration and detail the plan for their term. This must include a presentation on the structure of the Cabinet.
The funds for all Presidential Addresses, not including the opening and closing addresses, must come out of the Executive Projects account, unless additional funding is provided by a third-party entity.

sections.heading: Chapter 306 The SGA Open Positions And Application Act
sections.text:
The purpose of the Student Government Association Open Positions and Application Act is to clearly define Student Government Open Positions and Student Government Association Applications.
The Student Government Association Open Positions:
It shall be the duty of the SGA Webmaster to update and publish all open/vacant positions within the Student Government Association with the original date of publications included next to the position title. These positions shall fall under but shall not be limited to:
Executive Branch - All current cabinet positions, agencies, and institutes.
Legislative Branch - Senate
Judicial Branch
Other SGA entities
The Student Government Association Applications:
The Student Senate Internal Affairs Committee shall determine the format for the Student Government Association application. Once a format has been originally selected, the Internal Affairs Committee may propose any changes it deems necessary, which must pass the committee as well as the Student Senate by a two-thirds (2/3) vote to be formally adopted.
Any changes to the existing Student Government Association application shall be done in the period following the Fall Inauguration until Spring Inauguration. 
Applications must be consistent with all rules and regulations of the Student Government Association, as well as those of the Florida State University, state, and federal government.
In changing or creating forms, the Internal Affairs committee shall seek the advice of the Attorney General, the Student Body Chief of Staff, and the Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy. 
In order for candidates to be interviewed before the next Student Senate meeting, the forwarding letter must be sent to the Senate President, no later than three (3) business days before the regular Senate meeting so it may be assigned to the appropriate Standing Committee. If the forwarding letter is sent after this deadline but before the Senate meeting, all candidates on the letter shall not be considered by the Senate or any Standing Committee until the following week, while still abiding by Statute Section 202(2).
The Forwarding Letter must include the number of applicants to each position being forwarded, copies of each candidate's application, and any minutes or relevant documents from the interviewing party of the forwarded candidate.

sections.heading: Chapter 307 Leaves Of Absences During The Summer Session For Members Of The Executive Branch
sections.text:
Purpose:
The purpose of this chapter shall be to allow for certain members of the Executive Branch to take a leave of absence during the summer session and to set forth the procedures to select their temporary replacements during that term.
Applicability and Scope:
The Student Body Treasurer
The Executive Chief of Staff
The Student Body Attorney General
The Executive Cabinet MembersThe provisions of this chapter shall apply to the following officers of the Executive Branch:
All Executive Institute Directors
All Affiliated Project Directors
Individual Executive Agencies, Executive Institutes, and Affiliated Projects may make their own rules regarding summer leaves of absences for their officers, including restricting their Directors from taking a summer leave of absence. If no such rule exists, then the procedure outlined in this chapter shall apply.
The Student Body President and Student Body Vice President shall not be permitted to take a leave of absence during the summer session.
Procedure:
All eligible officers shall notify the Student Body President in writing on or before the last day of spring final examinations at the university of their intention to take a leave of absence during one or more summer academic sessions.
At the conclusion of spring final examinations at the University, the Student Body President shall appoint temporary officers to fill all or some of these vacated seats at their discretion. These temporary officers must meet all of the qualifications for the office to which they are being appointed as if they were appointed in the normal, permanent manner. All temporary officers appointed to positions requiring Student Senate confirmation must be confirmed by a majority vote of Senate. These nominations by the Student Body President shall go directly to the floor at the earliest possible summer session of the Senate.
All appointees to the Executive Branch during the summer session shall be on notice that their appointments are of a temporary nature. Their term of office shall terminate on the last day of final examination for the summer academic term(s) that they are serving for, subject to Subsection (3)(g) below.
All temporary executive officers are subject to impeachment by the Student Senate and dismissal by the Student Body President according to the appropriate statutes.
All temporary officers of the Executive Branch who are entitled to compensation shall be compensated for the summer term(s) in question as if they were permanent officers. This compensation shall cease at the close of the summer academic term(s) that they are serving for, or should they resign from office, whichever comes first.
All of the permanent officers of the Executive Branch who take a leave of absence for the summer term(s) shall receive no compensation for any summer term that they are not enrolled. Such compensation shall only resume when they assume their permanent offices at the opening of classes in the fall semester, or if and when they begin attending classes for a subsequent summer session.
All temporary Executive officers are entitled to serve throughout the summer session for which that person have been appointed, although they shall immediately vacate their office if and when their permanent counterpart begins attending classes for a subsequent summer session in the same academic year.

sections.heading: Chapter 308 The Executive Projects Account
sections.text:
Purpose: The purpose of the Executive Projects account is to create an account of the Executive Branch of the student body from which initiatives of said branch may be funded.
Guidelines:
The Executive Projects account should be used to fund new projects that would further the image of Student Government Association to the Florida State University student body, provide new services or opportunities to students, or fulfill an observed need on campus.
The funds in the account shall not be expended for the following purposes without the approval of the Student Senate via resolution:
Expenditures consisting solely of increasing funds in other budget categories of the executive branch, or any other A&S Fee recipient, through the transfer of funds or of augmenting a pre-existing and re-occurring expense.
Membership of the student government or student body in any organization.
Travel to conferences
Office Supplies
Telephones
OPS Wages
Personalized Awards
Postage
Maintenance, Repair, or Gasoline Charges
Insurance
Other Capital Outlay
Funding: The account may be replenished by the annual budget or by transfer from any other account.

sections.heading: Chapter 400 Organization Of The Senate
sections.text:
Senate Session:
Fall, Spring, and Summer Meetings: The fall, spring, and summer meetings of the Student Senate shall begin on the second Wednesday in the respective semester and shall terminate on the Wednesday prior to finals week of the three semesters.
Each Student Senate shall adopt its own Rules of Procedure as a policy pursuant to Chapter 416, at the first meeting of the Senate after Fall Inauguration in accordance with the Student Body Constitution and Statutes. Any changes to this policy must be approved in the form of resolution by a 2/3 vote of the Senate, with any other requirements adhering to SBS 401.1.

Office of the Senate President: The Office of the Senate President shall consist of the Senate President, Senate President Pro-Tempore and the Officers of the Senate, hence referred to as Senate Officers. The Student Senate President shall be responsible for the duties of all vacant Senate Officers.
There shall be a President of the Student Senate who shall be elected by majority vote of the Fall Senators-elect and returning Spring Senators from among their membership during the Organizational Session of the Student Senate, as prescribed in Section 400.8 of the Student Body Statutes. The Student Senate President shall be the chief legislative officer of the Student Body and shall perform duties as provided by law and Student Senate Rules of Procedure.
There shall be a Student Senate President Pro-Tempore who shall be elected by majority vote of the Fall Senators-elect and returning Spring Senators from among their membership during the Organizational Session of the Student Senate, as prescribed in Section 400.8 of the Student Body Statutes. The Senate President Pro Tempore shall assist the President of the Senate and perform duties as provided by law and by Senate Rules of Procedure.
The Student Senate President and President Pro-Tempore’s seats shall not come up for election during their respective terms as President and Pro-Tempore. Upon the resignation, removal, or conclusion of term of the Student Senate President or President Pro-Tempore, they shall immediately vacate their Senate seat, if the term to which they were elected or appointed has expired.
There shall be a Senate Parliamentarian, who shall be appointed by the Student Senate President, subject to confirmation by the Student Senate, from outside the membership of the Senate and who shall serve at Student Senate President’s discretion. The Parliamentarian shall attend the Student Senate meetings and upon request, give advice on parliamentary procedure and any applicable law(s). This individual shall maintain order under the direction of the Student Senate President or Presiding Officer. The Parliamentarian shall endorse strictly the rules relating to the privileges of the chamber.
There shall be a Senate Clerk, who shall be appointed by the Student Senate President, subject by the confirmation of the Student Senate, from outside the members of the Senate and who shall serve at the Student Senate President’s discretion. The Senate Clerk shall attend the Student Senate meetings and mainly be responsible for distributing legislation, ballots, messages and other literature to Student Senators within the Chamber. The Clerk shall also perform any other duties that the Student Senate President or President Pro-Tempore shall determine to be necessary for these purposes.
There shall be a Senate Historian, who shall be appointed by the Student Senate President, subject to confirmation by the Student Senate, from outside the members of the Senate and who shall serve at the Student Senate President’s discretion. The Historian shall be responsible for taking Senate Chamber minutes. The Historian, along with the Senate Public Affairs Officer, shall have the responsibility of publishing a Senate newsletter to document Senate legislative actions and updates. The Historian shall also perform any other duties that the Student Senate President or President Pro-Tempore shall determine to be necessary for these purposes;
There shall be a Senate Public Affairs Officer, who shall be appointed by the Student Senate President, subject to confirmation by the Student Senate, from outside the members of the Senate and who shall serve at the Student Senate President’s discretion. The Senate Public Affairs Officer shall be responsible for maintaining the Senate social media presence and outreach and create a weekly calendar of Student Senate funded or related events. The Senate Public Affairs Officer shall work with committee chairs to help inform the student body on committee meeting information. The Senate Public Affairs Officer, along with the Senate Historian, shall have the responsibility of publishing a Senate newsletter to document Senate legislative actions and updates. The Senate Public Affairs Officer shall also perform any other duties that the Student Senate President or President Pro-Tempore shall determine to be necessary for these purposes.
The Senate Public Affairs Officer Shall attend a training session with the SGA Webmaster to ensure that postings are within the Florida State University communications guidelines. This shall ensure that the social media properly represents the Student Senate.Office of the Senate President: The Office of the Senate President shall consist of the Senate President, Senate President Pro-Tempore and the Officers of the Senate, hence referred to as Senate Officers. The Student Senate President shall be responsible for the duties of all vacant Senate Officers.
During the summer meetings of the Senate, the Student Senate President may select a temporary replacement for any appointed officer, if that individual is absent during the session.
Upon the receipt of applications for a vacant appointed position as defined by statutes Sections 400(2)(c),(d), and (e) in the Office of the Senate President, a screening process shall be overseen by the Senate President to determine the most qualified candidate. The process shall be defined by the following:
All candidates must receive an interview.
The interview shall be conducted in a standardized and professional form for all candidates.
The interview shall consist of a basic questionnaire outlining the candidate’s experience, qualifications, and goals for the respective position.
No officer position shall be filled until it has been advertised properly in accordance with Section 403(2).
All positions shall be advertised for at least one week on the SGA Website in accordance with Section 403(2).
After all candidates have been interviewed, the Senate President may appoint and forward a candidate, who they deem most qualified, to the floor of the Student Senate for confirmation.
Calling of Senate Meetings:
The Student Senate President of the Senate shall be empowered to call Senate meetings, and shall call a meeting if petitioned by a majority of the members of Senate holding office at the time the petition is presented, or if requested by a majority vote of the Senate. 

The Student Senate President may call a special session of the Senate at their discretion.
If a special session is called by the Student Senate President, an excused absence shall not negatively affect a Senator’s attendance record.
Quorum: A majority of the members shall constitute quorum for Senate and committee meetings.
"Majority" and "Two-Thirds" Votes: A majority vote shall be more than half of the votes cast, excluding abstentions, at any properly called meeting at which a quorum is present. A two-thirds (2/3) vote shall be at least two-thirds of the votes cast, excluding abstentions, at any properly called meeting at which a quorum is present.
In the case that a piece of legislation is on the floor for Second Reading where a vote requires either a majority or two-thirds vote of votes cast, but a majority or two-thirds vote is not met of all Senators present, and 25% or more Senators present have abstained, a revote is necessary. After two (2) additional votes, if no decision is made, the legislation shall be sent to a committee as though it were on first reading.
Financial Certification:
All Senators must be financially certified by the SGA Accounting Office within fifteen (15) school days following a Senator taking the Oath of Office, and at the start of each new fiscal year.
If a Senator is not financially certified within fifteen (15) school days of taking office, the Senator shall be considered suspended until they are financially certified. The Senator shall still accrue absences while on such suspension.
It shall be the responsibility of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore to inform Senators of their current financial certification status at the beginning of the first three (3) Senate meetings following their Oath of Office.
Senate Committee:

Standing committee Chairs and Vice Chairs shall be elected by a majority vote of the committee on which they serve. Elections shall occur the first meeting after the allocation of committee assignments following fall and spring inaugurations, and upon the resignation, impeachment, or departure of a sitting Chair and/or Vice Chair.
A Chair or Vice Chair may be removed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the committee they serve on; only those who have served on the committee for a minimum of one (1) calendar month shall be eligible to vote on this motion. At least five (5) committee members eligible to vote on the matter must be present to vote.
The Rules Committee is exempt from Section 400(7)(a).
No Senator may serve on more than one standing committee, at the same time, except that they may serve on Rules in addition to being a Chair or Vice Chair of their committee. 
Organizational Session:
The Organizational Session of the Student Senate shall serve to elect the incoming Senate’s President and President Pro Tempore, facilitate leadership transition, and prepare the Senate for its forthcoming session, pursuant to Article II, Section 4 of the Student Body Constitution.
The Organizational Session shall occur between the certification of the fall general election and prior to inauguration. The sitting Senate President shall determine the date and time of the session and shall provide public notice in accordance with Chapter 407 of the Student Body Statutes.
The election of the Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore shall be conducted in accordance with the Senate Rules of Procedure. A majority vote (over fifty percent) of the members of the upcoming Senate, consisting of all continuing Spring and newly elected Fall Senators, shall be required to elect either officer. Balloting shall be by secret ballot, and successive rounds shall occur until a majority is achieved.
Only duly certified Fall Senators-elect and Spring Senators may be nominated for the offices of Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore.
No individual may be elected to serve as Senate President or Senate President Pro Tempore for more than two terms in either office.
The results of the Organizational Session shall be certified by the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore and Clerk of the Senate and recorded in the minutes by the Senate Historian. The Clerk shall transmit the certified results to the Student Body President, Student Body Vice President, and the SG&A Program Director within one (1) school day of the session.
The Oath of Office for the Senate President and the Senate President Pro Tempore, as prescribed in 202.9 and 202.10 of the Student Body Statutes, shall be administered by the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore at the conclusion of the Organizational Session. The Clerk of the Senate shall record the administration of each oath in the Journal of the Senate.
Outgoing officers shall provide written transition reports to their successors and shall use the period between the Organizational Session and the first meeting of the new Senate to assist, onboard, and support the newly elected leadership in assuming their duties and establishing operations for the upcoming term.
At the first official meeting of the newly inaugurated Senate, the incoming Senate shall ratify the results by motion. The ratification motion shall confirm the validity of the elections of the Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore and shall be entered into the Journal of the Senate.

sections.heading: Chapter 401 Forms Of Legislation
sections.text:
Resolutions: 
Resolutions shall be formal instruments for:
Amendments to any official Student Government Association policies and procedures, pursuant to Chapter 416, and the Senate Rules of Procedure. 

Stating a formal policy decision of the Senate on matters relevant to the Student Body.
Agreeing to changes in Senate policy and ratifying agreements to which the Senate is a party.
Resolutions shall not be used for the purpose of commending or condemning individuals, organizations, or events.
Resolutions shall require a majority vote of the Senate for adoption and shall take effect immediately upon passage unless otherwise specified. 

Amendments to the Senate Rules of Procedure shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate for adoption.

The enacting clause for all resolutions shall read: "Be it resolved by the Student Senate at the Florida State University that:"
Allocation Resolutions
Allocation Resolutions shall be formal instruments for:
Approving and allocating funding recommendations originating from Student Government Association funding boards or committees established in Student Body Statutes.
Allocating or transferring Student Government funds to student organizations through processes expressly authorized by statute.
Allocation Resolutions shall only be used for the purpose of disbursing, allocating, or approving funding as recommended by a duly constituted SGA funding board or committee.
Allocation Resolutions originating from the Registered Student Organization Allocation Committee shall be sponsored exclusively by the Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee and co-sponsored by the Chair and Vice Chair of the Student Senate Finance Committee.
Allocation Resolutions originating from a College Leadership Council Funding Committee shall be sponsored by the Senators serving on that respective College Leadership Council Funding Committee.
Allocation Resolutions shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate for adoption.
The enacting clause for all Allocation Resolutions shall read: “Be it resolved by the Student Senate at the Florida State University that:”

Proclamations:

Proclamations shall serve as formal public declarations or official announcements issued by the Senate to recognize a specific individual, group, event, or cause, including:
Commending or condemning individuals, organizations, or events.
Articulating non-binding statements of position on matters relevant to the Student Body, such as:
Expressing formal recognition of national, cultural, or other holiday or event. 

Proclamations condemning or stating opposition to individuals, organizations, or events shall require:
A majority approval from the Rules Committee prior to being considered by the Senate.
A two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate for adoption.
Proclamations not condemning or stating opposition to a topic shall require a majority vote of the Senate for adoption.
The enacting clause for all proclamations shall read: "Be it proclaimed by the Student Senate at the Florida State University that:"

Bills:

Bills shall serve as legislative instruments to:
Appropriate the annual Activity and Service Fee (A&S) budget and/or transfer funds as provided by statute.
Amend or revise the Student Body Statutes.
Adopt budget amendments or revisions via a Budget Amendment Bill pursuant to Chapter 413.6.
Bills shall include a brief title expressing their subject and purpose.
Bills shall require a majority vote unless otherwise specified. 

The enacting clause for all bills shall read: "Be it enacted by the Student Senate at the Florida State University that:"

Constitutional Amendments

Constitutional Amendments shall serve to change, delete, or add to the Student Body Constitution. The process for consideration shall be carried out pursuant to Article VI Section 1.

General Provisions for Legislation:

Submission Deadlines: All forms of legislation must be submitted through a Qualtrics form hosted by the SGA Webmaster no later than Friday at midnight before the upcoming Senate meeting. A direct copy of each submission shall be sent to the Student Senate President, Student Senate President Pro Tempore, Student Senate Clerk, Student Senate Historian, Student Senate Parliamentarian, and the Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy. Additionally, a copy of the submission shall be sent back to the sponsor (submitter).
Each piece of legislation shall have a minimum of one (1) and a maximum of two (2) primary sponsors. Additional co-sponsors may be added at the discretion of the primary sponsor(s).
Each piece of legislation shall be numbered by the iteration of the Senate, followed by the number of sequential order that legislation falls within, example: #77-010.
Withdrawal of Legislation: Once submitted, legislation may only be withdrawn by the sponsor(s).
Amendments and Strike-throughs: Legislation amending the Statutes, Constitution, or Rules of Procedure shall strike out any text proposed for deletion.
Omnibus Bills:
Legislation addressing three or more statutory titles or providing funding for multiple organizations shall be considered an Omnibus Bill.
Omnibus Bills shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote for passage, except for the Annual Budget or RSO Budget bills.
Effect of Legislation: All bills shall take effect upon signature by the Vice President for Student Affairs unless otherwise specified in the original text.

Enrolled Copies:
Each enrolled copy of legislation must be formatted to include: 
A cover sheet (first attachment) including:
A short title;
 Summary of legislation;
Background information, including a summary of discussion held with stakeholders affected by the legislation such as students, other University departments and offices, and entities of the FSU Student Government Association;
The effect of proposed legislation; and 
Any attachments that may be relevant to the legislation.
The second attachment of legislation shall include the title, date of introduction, committee referrals, names of all sponsors. 
All financial transfers approved via legislation shall include a financial transfer sheet outlining the details of the transfer. 
Each enrolled copy of proclamations shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Student Senate: 
The Student Senate President, who shall sign in a ministerial capacity to signify the Senate’s approval of the proclamation.
Each enrolled copy of resolutions shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Student Senate:
The Student Senate President, who shall sign in a ministerial capacity, within two (2) school days of passage, to signify the Senate’s approval of the resolution. 
Each enrolled copy of resolutions signifying the completion and final report of a Departmental Review or Affiliated Project Review shall be signed, within two (2) school days of passage, in a ceremonial capacity by the Chair of the Committee of jurisdiction.

Each enrolled copy of allocation resolutions shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Student Senate:
The Student Senate President, who shall sign in a ministerial capacity, within two (2) school days of passage, to signify the Senate’s approval of the allocation resolution.
Each enrolled copy of bills shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Student Senate: 
The Student Senate President, who shall sign in a ministerial capacity to signify the Senate’s approval of the bill. 
The Program Director of Student Governance & Advocacy, who shall sign, in a ministerial capacity, within two (2) school days of receipt to signify receipt by the SG&A Advising Office.
The Student Body President, who has five (5) school days from receipt to sign or veto the bill. Should the bill not be acted upon within the aforementioned time limit, the bill shall be sent to the Vice President for Student Affairs.
The Vice President for Student Affairs, who has ten (10) school days from receipt to sign or veto said legislation. Should the bill not be acted upon within the aforementioned time limit, the bill shall be determined as approved and enrolled. Pursuant to Chapter 402.2 (c), the Vice President for Student Affairs retains the authority to request additional time to review the legislation.

Each enrolled copy of the Annual Budget Bill, ceremonially numbered "#1851" shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Student Senate:

The Student Senate President, who shall sign in a ministerial capacity to signify the Senate’s approval of the bill. 
The Student Senate Budget Committee Chair, who shall sign in a ceremonial capacity to signify the completion of the Annual Budget process. 
The Student Body Treasurer, who shall sign in a ministerial capacity to signify the Office of the Student Body Treasurer’s commitment to uphold the Annual Budget Bill’s proviso language.
The Student Body President, who has ten (10) school days from receipt to sign or veto the bill. Should the bill not be acted upon within the aforementioned time limit, the bill shall be sent to the Vice President for Student Affairs.
The Vice President for Student Affairs, who has ten (10) school days from the receipt to sign or veto said legislation. Should the bill not be acted upon within the aforementioned time limit, the bill shall be determined as approved and enrolled. Pursuant to Chapter 402.2(c) the Vice President for Student Affairs retains the authority to request additional time to review the legislation. 

Record Keeping and Online Posting:
The Department of Student Governance & Advocacy shall maintain a record of all passed legislation and post it on the Student Government Association Municode dashboard within 24 hours of passage.
The Municode posting shall constitute official publication.

Authority to Correct Minor Errors
The Program Director of Student Governance & Advocacy and the Senate Judiciary Committee may correct errors such as spelling, formatting, or grammar in enrolled legislation, provided the substantive intent is preserved.

Corrections to statutory references that no longer indicate the correct title, chapter, section, or subsection may also be made under this provision.
Gender Neutrality
All legislation shall be written in a gender-neutral manner.
The Program Director of Student Governance & Advocacy is authorized to amend legislation to ensure compliance with this requirement.
Notification of Changes: All changes made pursuant to Sections 401.9 and 401.10 shall be documented and distributed to the Senate at the next meeting.

sections.heading: Chapter 402 Procedure For Approval Of Bills
sections.text:
Submission of Bills:

The Senate President or a designee shall transmit an enrolled copy of all bills passed by the Student Senate to the Student Body President for consideration by the end of the second day following the previous Senate meeting.

Legislation shall be sent to the designated officers through DocuSign and all signing deadlines shall begin upon receipt via email.

An enrolled copy of a proposed constitutional amendment shall be submitted directly to the Attorney General and the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court.

If the Office of the Attorney General is vacant, an enrolled copy of a proposed constitutional amendment shall be submitted directly to the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court.

Bill Veto and Reconsideration Process:

Upon presentation of a bill, the Student Body President shall have five (5) school days to approve or veto the legislation. If no action is taken within the five (5) day limit, then the bill shall be treated as approved by the Student Body President. If approved, bill shall be sent to the Vice President for Student Affairs for consideration, pursuant to Florida State University Regulation 3.001 (4). 

The Student Body President must submit written justification/reasoning to the Student Senate, within the five (5) day limit, to sustain any veto of legislation. The Student Body President or a designee must also deliver an oral justification to the Student Senate for the reason for the veto(es) within two (2) Senate meetings. The copy of the President’s justification/reasoning for the veto(es) must be e-mailed from the Student Body President to the Senate President so that the Senate President may distribute it to all Senators at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to the President’s oral justification to the Senate. The Senate President must send the originally vetoed bill to all Senators. If the Vice President for Student Affairs vetoes a bill, it is suggested that they send an email notification/reasoning of the veto to the Senate President. If this occurs, a copy of the emailed justification/reasoning must be distributed to all Senators.

Bills not acted upon within ten (10) school days after being received by the Vice President for Student Affairs shall be treated as approved unless the Student Body President, Senate President and Student Body Attorney General are notified by the Vice President for Student Affairs within the ten (10) day limit as to why the bill will not be acted upon within that limit and when action will be taken. 

If a vetoed bill from either the Student Body President or Vice President for Student Affairs is amended on the floor of the Senate during the reconsideration of the bill, that bill will be considered new legislation and be resubmitted to the Student Body President and Vice President for Student Affairs for approval or veto, all preceding statutes on time constraints to bill consideration applying.

If a presidential veto is overridden, that bill shall then go directly to the desk of the Vice President for Student Affairs for consideration as soon as possible; the preceding statutes on time constraints to the bill consideration applying again upon presentation.
