sections.heading: Chapter 404 Terms Of Office
sections.text:
Senate members shall take office upon inauguration.

Senators shall terminate office when one of the following circumstances occurs:

At the inauguration of their successors.

If occupying an upper-division seat, and changing their major, or field of study, would change their division classification.

Upon their graduation, be it at either the undergraduate or graduate classification.

An exception to this applies when the Senator graduating with their undergraduate degree will be enrolled as a graduate student in the same academic division, and will be permitted a “Leave of Absence” for any Summer or Winter break between their graduation as an undergraduate and enrollment as a graduate student.

If they are no longer an enrolled student at Florida State University, unless they are taking a summer leave of absence, pursuant to Section 405(6).

Installation of Senators shall occur at the inauguration ceremony for the term for which they are elected. Any Senators not formally sworn in at inauguration shall be sworn in at the next available Senate meeting. Should a senator not be sworn in by the third Senate meeting after inauguration, not including meetings of the Summer Senate session if the Senator is not serving within that session, the seat shall become vacant and available for appointment.

An exception to this applies if a Senator has a valid excuse deemed acceptable by the Office of Student Governance and Advocacy. The advisor shall notify the Senate President and Pro-Tempore if this exception is to be applied.

The number of Senators available to serve during any term shall at no point fall below thirty (30). Should occasion arise wherein there are fewer than thirty available serving Senators, the Student Body President shall make appointments to maintain a total of thirty (30) Senators. In this case Senate and its committees may meet for the sole purpose of voting on new Senators even if there are less than 5 voting members in each standing committee.

Senators, by virtue of their office and the public trust, may not apply to be appointed to any vacated Seat within the Student Senate. Additionally, upon resignation or removal from their Seat, no former Senator may apply to be appointed to any vacated Seat within the Student Senate apportioned for the opposite semester from the seat which they originally held until after the said opposite semesters elections are completed and certified, but shall always be permitted to run in said election.

sections.heading: Chapter 405 Impeachment And Removal From Office
sections.text:
Elected Officers:

The following shall be designated as elected officers of the Student Body:

Senators
Student Members of the Union Board
Student Body President
Student Body Vice President 
Student Body Treasurer
Student Members of the Campus Recreation Board 
Congress of Graduate Students Representatives

Appointed Officers:

The following shall be designated as appointed officers of the Student Body:

Executive Chief of Staff 
Executive Cabinet Officers
Student Senate Officers
Supervisor of Elections 
Supreme Court Chief Justice
Supreme Court Associate Justices 
SGA General Counsel
Deputy Supervisors of Elections 
Election Commission Members
Election Commission Secretary 
Student Body Attorney General
All Agency, Executive Institute, and Affiliated Projects personnel who require confirmation by the Senate.

Provisions for Impeachment:

The Judiciary Committee of the Senate, by a majority vote, shall be responsible for initiating the impeachment proceedings against any elected or appointed officer of the Student Body once the Chair of the Judiciary Committee has been given the formal charges from the Senate Program Assistant.

All such charges must be in writing, and include the specific grounds for impeachment, citing pertinent constitutional rule, statutes, policy as adopted pursuant to Chapter 416, or state or federal law that have been violated. All such charges must also include the date, place, and approximate time(s) when the offense(s) are alleged to have occurred.

Any member of the Student Body may file formal charges against any elected or appointed officer of the student body with the Senate Program Assistant at any time, as long as the charges are in compliance with Subsection (3)(a) of this section.

Elected or appointed officers of the student body may only be impeached on charges of misfeasance, malfeasance or nonfeasance, as defined by Black’s Law Dictionary. The Senate Judiciary Committee shall not forward charges to the full Senate that do not meet these specific criteria, except for Senators who have accumulated excessive absences in accordance with the Senate Rules of Procedure.

Impeachment Proceedings:

Impeachment of a student body officer shall require a majority vote of the Student Senate Judiciary Committee followed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the full Senate.

Before the Senate Judiciary Committee votes to initiate impeachment proceedings, the committee must notify the accused officer via the official’s FSU email address, at least one week prior to the impeachment hearing. Such notification shall also include the time, date, and place of the Judiciary Committee hearing pertaining to the impeachment proceedings. The accused shall have the right to speak in their defense at the hearing, to refuse to appear, to remain silent, and to refer to counsel at any time. At the conclusion of the hearing the committee shall openly deliberate and then vote by open ballot on whether or not to recommend impeachment to the full Senate.

If the Judiciary Committee votes to recommend impeachment, the impeachment charge shall be brought before the Student Senate at the next scheduled Senate session and presented for a vote at that session.

The officer considered for impeachment shall have five (5) minutes to speak in their defense. This time may be split between an opening statement and a closing statement. Following the opening statement of the accused, the Senate shall openly deliberate until a motion is made to vote on the candidate for impeachment. The accused will then have the option to make a closing statement, only if there is time yielded from the opening statement. The Senate will then vote by open ballot on whether or not to formally impeach the accused officer.

Removal from Office:
Upon impeachment of a Student Body Officer, the President of the Senate shall deliver to the Chief Justice of the Supreme Court, within three (3) days, the Articles of Impeachment.

The Senate Judiciary Committee shall elect a Senator by majority vote to act as Special Prosecutor to present the Student Senate’s case to the Supreme Court. This Senator must be a member of the Judiciary Committee, as they are the most involved in the impeachment proceedings, and can therefore present the most informed case for impeachment to the Supreme Court.

The Special Prosecutor may appoint, at their discretion, Assistant Special Prosecutors to serve at the pleasure of the Special Prosecutor through the duration of the impeachment proceedings. Any member of the Florida State University Student Body who is in good academic standing and without any active conduct sanctions may be appointed as an Assistant Special Prosecutor.

The Student Supreme Court shall have sole jurisdiction over cases involving removal of any officer of the Student Body impeached by the Student Senate. In the case of Supreme Court Justices being impeached, temporary justices shall be appointed pursuant to Article VII, Section 4(2), of the Student Body Constitution.

Any officer who is impeached by the Senate shall be suspended from office until a decision is reached by the Student Supreme Court. Suspension is defined as the temporary loss of all rights and privileges of office.

The impeached officer shall be removed upon conviction by a majority vote of the justices. If the Student Supreme Court fails to convict the impeached officer, this individual shall be declared not guilty and shall be reinstated to office immediately.

The President of the Student Body may remove, at their discretion, any officer who has been appointed to a position in the Executive Branch.

Any officer of the Student Body may resign at any time. Such resignations must be in writing and delivered to the head of the officer’s respective branch.

Any elected or appointed Student Government Officer who has been disciplined, suspended, or removed from office shall have the right to directly appeal such decision to the Vice President of Student Affairs or another senior university administrator designated to hear such appeals, pursuant to Florida Statute 1004.26(4)(d). The exercise of such right and its resulting decision shall not be construed as to condition precedent on any student panel.

Leaves of Absence:
Senators, under certain circumstances, may take a Leave of Absence, during which time any absences will not count toward their record.

There shall be two different kinds of Leaves of Absence: a Special Leave of Absence and a Summer Leave of Absence.

A Special Leave of Absence is a Leave of Absence given special extenuating circumstances that may rise on a case-by-case basis. In order to take a Special Leave of Absence, a Senator must provide notice to the Pro Tempore and at the next Rules and Calendar committee meeting, the committee shall vote, by two-thirds (2/3), to approve the Leave of Absence.

A Special Leave of Absence shall not extend for a period of more than three (3) months and shall last at least one (1) month. A temporary Senator may be appointed to fill the seat for the period of the leave of absence. These temporary Senators shall be appointed in the same manner as summer Senators.

No Special Leaves of Absence shall extend beyond the end of the Spring Semester. If a Senator is on a Leave of Absence until the end of the Spring Semester, and wants to serve during the summer session, they must undergo the process in the same manner as any Senators not on a leave of absence. Senators temporarily filling the spot of another senator on a Leave of Absence are not permitted to fill out a notice of intent to serve during the summer session.

A Summer Leave of Absence may occur during the summer session, with specific circumstances listed below. During a Summer Leave of Absence, a Senator’s seat may be temporarily reassigned for the extent of that Senator’s Summer Leave of Absence.

During the summer session, Senators may take a leave of absence. In order to serve, Senators must file a notice of intent with the SGA Advisor two (2) weeks prior to the last Student Senate meeting of the Spring Semester. At the discretion of the SGA Advisor or by a majority vote of Senate, the Senate may accept a late notice of intent. If this notice of intent is not submitted, the Senator shall go on a Summer Leave of Absence for the Summer Session, and will return to office upon the first day of the Fall Semester.

When a Senator is on a Leave of Absence, their presence will not be counted towards nor against quorum of Senate or any committees.

sections.heading: Chapter 406 Investigative Rights Of The Senate
sections.text:
The Student Senate shall have the right to initiate and conduct an investigation in order to examine any impropriety or to question any action of any Student Government Association officer, appointed official, or Student Government Association funded organization, agency, institute, affiliated project, or funding board.

An investigative Board may only be initiated by:

A 2/3 vote by the Student Senate in the form of a resolution, or

Whenever a standing or ad hoc committee deems necessary by 2/3 vote, and

The Student Senate President.

An Investigative Board will consist of the Judiciary Committee unless otherwise deemed by a Student Senate resolution.

All conclusions of any Investigative Board will be reported to the Student Senate in the form of a resolution.

An Investigative Board may make a recommendation for action to the Student Senate in the form of a resolution.

If the Investigative Board produces a resolution containing the results of the investigation or any recommendation for action, upon passage by the senate, the resolution shall be published in the Senate minutes.

In order to carry out its duties, an Investigative Board or standing committee shall have be empowered with the right and authority to issue a legislative subpoena upon an SGA officer for any private records related to the investigation, unless prohibited by the Student Body Constitution, state law, or federal law (such as FERPA or HIPPA), provided that: 

The text of the subpoena includes:

The name of the SGA Officer upon whom the subpoena is to be served;

The names of all acting Senators on the Investigative Board or standing committee which has authorized the issuance of the subpoena by majority vote;

The date and time wherein the Investigative Board or standing committee authorized the issuance of the subpoena by majority vote;

The date and time wherein the Student Senate President authorized the issuance of the subpoena;

The nature of the specific evidence sought by issuance of the subpoena;

A legitimate investigative purpose for the evidence sought within the context of the investigation;

Sufficient reason as to why the evidence sought is not unreasonably burdensome to produce; and

A designated time and place, at least fifteen (15) days after the Investigative Board or standing committee’s majority vote to authorize the subpoena’s issuance, wherein the information compelled for disclosure may be inspected and examined by the Investigative Board or standing committee under the direct supervision of an impartial custodian of the public record.

The subpoena is approved using the following timeline:

The investigative board or standing committee approves the text of the legislative subpoena by a majority vote, the Chair of the Investigative Board or standing committee authorizes the subpoena by signature, and sends the subpoena to the Student Senate President for further authorization;

The legislative subpoena is subsequently authorized by the Senate President by signature and sent by the Student Senate President to the Chair of the Investigative Board or standing committee within eight (8) business days of the Investigative Board or standing committee’s majority vote;

Upon the decision to deny a legislative subpoena for issuance, the Student Senate President shall, within twenty-four (24) hours of the subpoena’s denial, provide the Chair of the Investigative Board or standing committee with the full and unrelenting rationale as to why the legislative subpoena was denied so that the Investigative Board or standing committee may attempt to cure those deficiencies by drafting and authorizing a revised subpoena, or alternatively, appeal the Student Senate President’s decision to the Student Supreme Court pursuant to Article IV, section 3(3)(a) of the Student Body Constitution.

The Chair of the Investigative Board or standing committee shall present the subpoena to the Senate via a resolution which must be heard on the Senate floor and affirmed by a majority vote of the Senate at that meeting.

sections.heading: Chapter 407 "Senate In The Sunshine"
sections.text:
Notice of all meetings of any nature wherein official Student Senate business is to be conducted must be posted on the Student Government Association Website at least 24 hours in advance of such meetings. The time, place, and agenda of such meetings shall be incorporated in the notice. Copies of such notices shall be furnished to any FSU student so requesting. Copies must always be made available to any newspaper or newsletter or general student circulation so requesting.

All legislation titles, with a short descriptive phrase, to be referred to committee, must be advertised in a widely published forum prior to their debate on the Senate floor. Upon acceptance by the Student Senate, the aforementioned legislative documents shall be archived in the Student Government Association Website, if available.

Individualized voting results from every Student Senate meetings and Student Senate standing committee meetings shall be published and archived on the Student Government Association website within ten (10) school days of the meeting.

At the request of twenty-five (25) percent of the Senators, a short summary of any debated measure must be advertised in a widely published forum.

The Student Senate shall sponsor an information and suggestion table, on campus, at appropriate times as determined by the Senate. This service shall be advertised in a widely published forum at least one (1) week prior thereto.

sections.heading: Chapter 408 Student Participation In Senate Act Of 1994
sections.text:
This act shall be called the "Student Participation in Senate Act of 1994," hereinafter referred to as the "Student Participation in Senate Act."

The purpose of this act is to provide an effective procedure for the inclusion of the student voice in the Student Senate and its various committees.

This legislation shall become fully binding upon its enactment on the Student Senate and all standing, ad hoc, and special committees or subcommittees of the Legislative Branch of the Student Government Association.

The Student Voice in the Senate:

The Student Senate shall promulgate the necessary rules and procedures to permit members of the student body to address the Senate or one of its standing, ad hoc, special committees, or subcommittees on Calendar items as part of the regular order of Senate or committee business, except for the first meeting of the regular session.

Student Comments shall be included in the Senate Calendar, Journal and any other agenda.

For the purpose of this act, a student does not require a majority vote of the Senate or committee to comment on a calendar item, but shall make comments adhering to the rules and procedure promulgated by the Senate. However, individual students may have time restrictions placed upon their comments.

The Student Senate shall advertise the opportunity for Student Comments on the Student Government Association Website or on social media.

Rules and Procedure: The Student Senate shall promulgate and amend the Rules of Procedure to conform, but not conflict, with the provisions of this act.

sections.heading: Chapter 409 Senator's Committee Rights
sections.text:
At the first meeting following the taking of the oath of office, Senators shall submit their committee preferences. The Student Senate President shall assign committees and at no time shall any committee fall below five (5) voting members.

Once committee membership has been initially decided upon committee members may only be switched to another committee by the Senate President with permission of the Senator to be moved.

Neither Section 409(1) nor (2) applies to the Rules, Sweepings, or Supplemental Funding.

Committee members will be allowed three (3) unexcused absences, after which point, the chair must call for a motion to remove the Senator from the committee. Such a motion will require a majority-vote of the committee that they served on. Only those who have served on the committee for a minimum of one (1) calendar month shall be eligible to vote on this motion. At least five (5) committee members eligible to vote on the matter must be present to vote. If the motion passes the Student Senate President must be immediately notified at the conclusion of the meeting where the motion takes place.

For an absence to be excused, the committee member must email the vice chair at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to the meeting or, in the event of an unforeseen circumstance on the day of the meeting, twenty-four (24) hours after the meeting, providing information as to why they were not present. The request shall be approved by a majority vote of the committee at the next meeting. All excused absences must comply with the Florida State University policy.

Two (2) tardies shall count as an unexcused absence.

Once a Senator has been notified of removal from an assigned committee the Senator will have two (2) business days to submit their availability and request for a new committee assignment to the Student Senate President.

The Student Senate shall have the following standing committees:
Judiciary Committee
Internal Affairs Committee
Student Life Committee
Finance Committee
Rules Committee

All members of the Finance and Budget Committees shall be required to attend a workshop held by the Student Government Association Accounting Office.

sections.heading: Chapter 410 Sweepings Regulations Act Of 1995
sections.text:
Sweepings Allocation Process:

All A&S fee-funded accounts shall be swept at the end of the fiscal year to be rolled over into the Student Government Association discretionary account to be re-allocated during the Annual Budget process by the Budget Committee.

There shall be an annual report detailing the amount of money swept from every A&S fee-funded account created by the Student Body Treasurer in coordination with the SGA Business Manager of SGA Accounting. The annual report shall be presented to the Student Senate Budget Committee at the start of the annual budget process.

sections.heading: Chapter 411 Senate Awards
sections.text:
Purpose and Creation: This act is established to govern the creation and administration of Senate Awards. All Senate awards shall be created by statute.

Senator of the Month:
The Student Senate shall, by majority vote, select a “Senator of the Month” for the previous month, on the first regular Senate meeting of each month.

If the legislative session ends prior to the following month, a vote for Senator of the Month shall occur at the last meeting of the respective month.

The nomination and voting process shall be conducted in a manner that the Senate President shall determine.

The Senate Press Secretary shall publish an announcement with the winner of the award on the SGA website and applicable social media.

After winning the award, that Senator shall not be eligible for nomination again until 180 days has passed.

The Student Senate President and Student Senate Pro Tempore shall not be eligible for this award.

The FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence:

Each Senator may nominate one FSU student, faculty/staff member, or campus entity that they directly represent in the Senate for an FSU Senate Award for Excellence per year, though a maximum of five (5) such awards shall be given each year. The FSU Senate Award for Excellence is to be granted for distinguished service to the Florida State University or to the community, or for outstanding performance in representing this university.

A Senator wishing to nominate an individual or entity for the Student Senate Award for Excellence must do so by submitting a proclamation for referral to the Student Life Committee containing the nominee’s name and a description of why they are deserving of the award. Upon approval by the Student Senate, the award shall be presented to the recipient in any fashion deemed fit. The FSU Student Senate Award for Excellence shall be a certificate or other memento designed and provided by the Student Senate President.

When nominating proclamations are debated on the Senate Floor, two rounds of pro may be given, but no rounds of con will be permitted. If the resolution is approved by the Senate by two-thirds (2/3) vote, the nominated individual or entity will be considered a recipient of the Student Senate Award for Excellence.

The provisions in this section shall not preclude the Student Senate President from immediately placing a nominating proclamation on the calendar for second reading if that right is granted to them by the Senate Rules of Procedure.
Special Awards: Every academic year, the Student Senate shall vote on the following Special Awards. These awards honor individuals whose legacy and service to Florida State University and the Student Government Association continue to inspire future Senators. Senate neither establishes nor funds these awards but shall determine their recipients in accordance with the foundations and traditions tied to each honor.
The Robert A. Brandewie Awards: These awards are named in honor of Robert A. “Bob” Brandewie, for whom the Brandewie Senate Chamber in the Oglesby Union was dedicated on September 28, 1988. Brandewie worked for Florida State University for nineteen years, thirteen of which he served as liaison to the Student Government Association. His experience and knowledge of student affairs made him an unparalleled resource for student leaders, and his legacy continues through the Brandewie Foundation’s support of student leadership and engagement. The Brandewie Awards are presented annually through the generosity of the Brandewie Foundation, which continues to allow the Student Senate to determine the recipients of these honors. These awards shall be presented during the Spring Inauguration Ceremony.
Robert A. Brandewie Student Life Award: Granted to the Senator who has made the most impact on the student life of Florida State University. All Senators except the Student Senate President and Student Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senators who receive OPS wages for being Senators, are eligible for this award.
Robert A. Brandewie Freshman of the Year Award: Granted to the Senator who has made the most impact in Senate during their brief time as a student at Florida State University. Only Senators who possess fewer than sixty (60) credit hours, or who are in their first year at Florida State University, and are currently serving their first Senate term are eligible.
Mattie Durham Senator of the Year: This award is named in honor of Mattie “Ms. Mattie” Durham, who served as the Senate Program Assistant for thirty-four years and was beloved for her unwavering commitment to the Student Senate and its members. Her dedication, compassion, and guidance shaped generations of student leaders and embodied the values of service, integrity, and excellence that define the Florida State University community. The Mattie Durham Senator of the Year Award shall be presented to the Senator who best reflects Ms. Mattie’s legacy, demonstrating exceptional service to students, distinguished leadership within the Student Senate, and a meaningful impact on the broader university community during their term. This award shall be presented during the Fall Inauguration Ceremony.
Russell Hellein Award for Exemplary Dedication and Service to Student Government: This award is named in honor of Russell Hellein, President of the 50th Student Senate and the inaugural inductee into the Student Senate Hall of Fame. A model of integrity, perseverance, and leadership, Hellein’s legacy reflects an enduring commitment to public service and the advancement of the Student Government Association. The Russell Hellein Award is the highest honor a sitting Senator can receive within the Student Senate. It shall be presented to a Senator who has served two full consecutive terms in the Student Senate and whose record of service exemplifies sustained dedication, institutional stewardship, and the highest ideals of student leadership. This award recognizes those whose consistent contributions have strengthened Student Government and left a lasting mark on the Senate’s mission and traditions. This award shall be presented during the Fall Inauguration Ceremony.
Fall Awards: Every fall semester, the Student Senate shall vote on the following four awards. These awards shall be presented during the Fall Inauguration ceremony to the Senator receiving the most votes for each award. Only Senators may be permitted to nominate individuals for these awards:
The Vires Award (New Senator of the Year): The best Senator who is serving their first term in Senate (not necessarily a Freshman). The Senator who exhibits strength (“Vires”) through their first term by continuing to persevere in their learning and striving to make a difference.
The Artes Award (Chair of the Year): The best Chair of a standing Senate committee (other than Rules). The Senator awarded the Artes Award demonstrates exceptional skill and dedication working with their committee, resulting in outstanding service to the student body.
The Mores Award (Vice Chair of the Year): The best Vice Chair of a standing Senate committee (other than Rules). The Senator awarded the Mores Award demonstrates strong character, integrity, and respect for the traditions and values of the Senate.
The Flame Award (Senate Officer of the Year): The best Senate Officer team member who has shown exceptional commitment to advancing the mission and operations of the Student Senate. Selected jointly by the Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore, the recipient embodies reliability, initiative, and a steady devotion to keeping the Senate’s institutional flame burning.
Spring Awards: Every spring semester, the Student Senate shall vote on the following two awards. These awards shall be presented during the Spring Inauguration ceremony to the Senator receiving the most votes for each award. Only Senators may be permitted to nominate individuals for these awards:
The Bridge Builder Award: Awarded to the Senator who has demonstrated outstanding commitment to collaboration and partnership within the Student Senate and across the university community. The recipient of the Bridge Builder Award exemplifies unity, diplomacy, and service by fostering connections that strengthen the Student Senate and advance the collective interests of the student body.
The Advocate Award: Awarded to the Senator who has most effectively championed the voices and needs of Florida State University students. The recipient of the Advocate Award demonstrates persistence, empathy, and leadership in representing student interests and translating their concerns into meaningful action.
The Senate Hall of Fame: Membership in the Senate Hall of Fame is the highest honor a student Senator can achieve. This honor shall be bestowed upon any Senator who has performed their duty as a member of the Senate with the highest standard of excellence, beyond that normally expected of a Senator at the Florida State University.
Prospective candidates for this award shall be nominated by the Student Senate in Resolution format. Included in the Resolution should be the name of the Senator to be nominated, the Senate(s) in which the individual served and reasons why the Senator is deserving of this honor. When this resolution is debated on the Senate Floor, two rounds of pro may be given, but no rounds of con will be permitted. If the Resolution is approved by the Senate, by two-thirds (2/3) vote, the Senator will be automatically considered a member of the Senate Hall of Fame.

The Senate shall determine the criterion for selecting the recipients of the award. The following exceptions to this apply:

Only the Senator’s accomplishments in the Student Senate shall apply.

Holding a position of Senate leadership shall not be the sole basis for determining if a nominee is qualified.

Only senators who have served two calendar years or two full terms of office or more in the Student Senate may be considered.

The length of the Senator's term beyond this threshold shall not count for or against the nominee.

Time served shall count time served in Senate Officer positions such as Senate Clerk, Senate Press Secretary, and Senate Parliamentarian.

This stipulation may be overruled by a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the senate before opening statements occur in situations where the senate determines a nominee’s work is exceptional (emphasis added) in a shorter amount of time. 

Excluding the original members of the Senate Hall of Fame, no person shall be considered for membership following their graduation from Florida State University.

No more than four (4) Senators shall be inducted in the Hall of Fame per year.

Once a nominee has been selected to be a member of the Senate Hall of Fame, they will be notified in a timely manner as to the award. The Senators placed in the Senate Hall of Fame shall have their names placed on a plaque that will be permanently displayed in the hall outside of the Senate Chamber. 
Legislative Certification Program (LCP) Excellence Award:
This award recognizes participants in the Legislative Certification Program (LCP) who demonstrate exceptional involvement, leadership, and dedication throughout the program. This award shall be given out at the Inauguration Ceremony following the completion of the given semester’s LCP.
Each senator may nominate one LCP participant for the award. Nominations may be accompanied by one optional letter of recommendation. The Student Senate President Pro Tempore, in consultation with the Student Senate President, shall review all nominations and select between one (1) and five (5) award recipients.

sections.heading: Chapter 412 Senate Legislative Certification Program
sections.text:
Purpose: This act is to establish a program administered by the Student Senate Pro Tempore for students who are neither currently nor former members of the FSU Student Senate who are interested in gaining knowledge of how the Senate operates through first-hand experiences.

Name: The name of this program shall be “The Senate Legislative Certification Program.”

Administration of Program: The Senate Pro Tempore shall create an application and make it available to students on the SGA website each semester the program is offered. The Senate Pro Tempore shall have discretion over which applicants are to be admitted to the program. The Senate Pro Tempore shall be responsible for holding an orientation session for admitted applicants to explain the program and answer questions they may have.

Certification Requirements:
Each candidate enrolled in the Student Senate Certificate Program shall complete the following requirements:

Attend three (3) Student Senate meetings and take notes about each meeting.

Attend three (3) committee meetings and take notes about each meeting.

A candidate must attend the meeting of at least two (2) different committees, to include no less than one standing committee meeting.

Participate in writing a piece of legislation.

Meet with a Senate liaison to discuss their role as a liaison and how they serve the campus entity they are a liaison to.

Meet with the Senate Pro Tempore after all other requirements have been completed to discuss the experiences had through this program.

Verification of a Candidate’s Completed Requirements:

Each candidate shall notify the Senate Pro Tempore upon their completion of all requirements of the program, and the Pro Tempore shall verify that all requirements have been completed.

If the Pro Tempore finds that a candidate has not successfully completed all requirements by the end of the semester that candidate is enrolled in this program, that candidate shall not receive a certificate of completion as outlined in Student Body Statute Section 412(5)(b).

Upon the Pro Tempore’s verification, the candidate shall be awarded a certificate of completion of The Student Senate Certification Program at the next student government inauguration.
Legislative Certification Program participants shall be able to receive the Legislative Certification Program Excellence Award pursuant to Section 411.8.

sections.heading: Chapter 413 Annual Budget Procedures Act Of 2016 (Updated)
sections.text:
Purpose: This act is to establish a procedure by which the annual Activity and Service Fee (A&S) Budget of the Student Senate is produced and passed.

Scope: The Annual A&S Fee Budget hereby referred to as the Budget shall be passed in compliance with the provisions of this act and all applicable provisions within the State of Florida Administrative Code. No exceptions are authorized other than those specified within. Amendments to Chapter 413 shall require a three-fourth (3/4) vote of the Student Senate.

Procedures for Passage of the Budget:

The Budget shall not be approved by the Student Senate in a Summer Session.

The Budget Committee shall be convened once per fiscal year as a special committee of the Senate for the purpose of preparing the Student Government Association’s Annual Budget. Its membership shall consist of:
One (1) designee of the Chair of the Campus Recreation Board;
One (1) designee of the Chair of the Union Board;
One (1) designee of the Student Body President;
Two (2) ex-officio designees from the Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students;
Eight (8) Senators selected jointly by the Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore;
The Vice Chair of the Senate Finance Committee;
The Chair of the Senate Internal Affairs Committee;

The Speaker of the Congress of Graduate Students;
The Student Body Treasurer, serving as Vice Chair of the Committee;
The Chair of the Senate Finance Committee, serving as Chair of the Committee.
The Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore may sit as ex-officio voting members of the Budget Committee.

An estimated amount of the Budget shall be used to submit to the Senate President for First Reading by the Chair of the Budget Committee. After which, hearings shall be held and operated at the discretion of the Chair of the Budget Committee.

Each prospective recipient of monies from the Budget shall make a budget request. The Budget Committee shall hold hearings during which budget requests are defended. Each prospective recipient of the Budget shall have a separate hearing.

The hearings shall be administered by the Chair of the Budget Committee and shall require a minimum of seven (7) members of the Committee, at least three (4) of whom shall be Student Senators.

The Budget Committee shall have the authority to deliberate monies to requesting and non-requesting prospective recipients. The Budget Committee shall also be authorized to deliberate more or less than the amount requested.

When the Budget has been deliberated and approved in whole by the Budget Committee it will be heard on Second Reading. All Senators shall be presented copies of the proposed allocations. The Budget shall be on the calendar for second reading for a minimum of five (5) business days with proposed allocations before passage. The annual budget and proviso must properly be advertised on the Student Government website while on Second Reading.

The Budget shall be approved by the Senate before the beginning of the fiscal year of which it affects. The Chair of the Budget Committee shall make a good-faith effort to confirm the membership of the Committee no later than the last week of the Fall Semester and shall further make a good-faith effort to complete the Budget no later than February 28 of each year.

The Budget and Proviso language cannot be approved separately. Changes to the Proviso language may be made via resolution at any point before the Budget is signed by the Vice President for Student Affairs. This resolution shall be passed with a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.

Amendments to the Budget, on the Senate floor, must follow a majority vote to unlock a specific line item and category of the Budget or a line of the Proviso language. Any amendment that affects the allocation amount in any line of any recipient shall require a three-fourth (3/4) vote of the Senate.

Amendments may only be made to a specific category of one recipient.

The Budget Committee, as a special committee of the Senate, shall meet only for the purposes of fulfilling its duties under this Chapter. Hearings, deliberations, and meetings of the Budget Committee are public and shall be advertised in the Senate. The Chair of the Budget Committee shall not exclude any student from witnessing the hearings or deliberations in accordance with Chapter 407 of the Student Body Statutes.

The Budget shall be passed by a roll-call vote. A simple majority is required for passage.

Only Senators who are financially certified by the Senate session in which the bill is voted on may cast a vote on the Budget.

If the Budget fails in the Senate or is vetoed in its entirety, the Budget Committee shall be reconvened, or if it is not practicable to reconvene, the Senate Finance Committee shall assume responsibility for producing a new Budget consistent with this Chapter.

The University President or their designee shall retain line-item veto power over the budget bill and have fifteen (15) school days from the date of presentation of the budget to act on the allocation and expenditure recommendations, which shall be deemed approved if no action is taken within the 15 school day limit.

If any line item or portion within the budget is vetoed by the University President or their designee, the Student Senate shall, within fifteen (15) school days, make new budget recommendations for expenditure of the vetoed portion of the bill. These new recommendations shall be made in the form of a new bill, which shall be deliberated by the Budget committee without the need for new budget request hearings.

If the University President or their designee, vetoes any line item or portion thereof within the new budget revisions, the University President, or their designee, may reallocate by line item that vetoed portion to bond obligations guaranteed by Activity and Service fees pursuant to F.S.1010.62.

The University President or their designee, may also veto the budget bill in its entirety, in which case the Budget Committee shall create a new budget in due time, following the guidelines in these statutes.

Unexpended funds and undisbursed funds remaining at the end of a fiscal year shall be carried over and remain in the student activity and service fund and be available for allocation and expenditure during the next fiscal year.
Procedure for Amending the Adopted Budget:
Amendments to the adopted budget must be submitted in the form of a Budget Amendment Bill pursuant to §401.4. The Budget Amendment Bill shall contain the following required items in listed
order, with an official format provided by the Student Senate President or designee:
The bill cover page and standard template; and 
A Budget Amendment Summary detailing all additional revenues, expenditures, and miscellaneous changes, along with a clear purpose and justification for such amendment; and
If a line item is created or deleted, an updated version of the adopted Annual A&S Fee Budget, incorporating the amendments detailed in the Budget Amendment Summary.
A Budget Amendment Bill shall be submitted by a member of the Senate Finance Committee.
Budget amendments under $500 shall be exempt from the process detailed in §413.4; these may be approved as a budget transfer administratively without Senate approval through the Department of Student Engagement, with a limit of two such transfers per semester.
Budget Amendment Bills shall be referred to, at minimum, the Senate Finance Committee. Budget Amendment Bills are prohibited from being moved to 2nd reading outside of the standard legislative process.
The Finance Committee must pass the Budget Amendment Bill by a two-thirds (2/3) vote.

A Budget Amendment Bill must be passed by a roll-call vote with a simple majority required for passage. Only Senators who are financially certified in the session in which the bill is voted on may cast a vote.
Amendments to a Budget Amendment Bill, on the Senate floor, that affects the allocation amount in any line of any recipient shall require a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Senate.

All budget amendments approved under this subsection must receive the approval and signature of the Student Body Treasurer.

sections.heading: Chapter 414 The Senate Projects Account
sections.text:
Purpose:

The purpose of the Senate projects account is to create an account of the Senate of the student body from which initiatives of said branch may be funded.

Guidelines:

The Senate Projects account should be used to fund projects that would further the image of Student Government Association to the Florida State University student body, provide services or opportunities to students, or to fulfill an observed need on campus.

Process:

Funds from the Senate Projects Account shall be allocated via a transfer bill.

Senate Projects bills shall be subject to the following process: 

Such bills shall be referred to the Student Life Committee, the Finance Committee, and the Internal Affairs Committee.
The Student Life Committee shall determine whether the bill will have a positive impact on student life.
The Finance Committee shall determine whether the bill is fiscally responsible and financially well planned.
The Internal Affairs Committee shall determine whether the bill fills a necessary gap in services already provided by the Student Government Association.
Each committee shall consider the bill independently in its original committee form. The Senate shall not convene as a committee of the whole for the purpose of considering such bills, nor may such bills be moved to Second Reading prior to full committee consideration.
Final passage of any Senate Projects bill shall require a two-thirds (2/3) roll-call vote of the Senate and shall not pass by unanimous consent. 

If the transfer bill request is over $5,000, it will require a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Student Senate.

Funding:

The account may be replenished by the annual budget or by transfer from any other account. 

At the final Senate meeting of the summer semester, the Senate Projects account shall be reimbursed by the appropriate funds distribution committee for funds allocated. These transfer bills shall be drafted by the Chair of the Finance Committee and shall not exceed $2,000 per committee.

sections.heading: Chapter 415 Major Legislation
sections.text:
Definition of Major Legislation: Major legislation shall include the Budget Bill, the RSO Budget Fund Bill, and the Legislative Agenda Resolution. The Senate President has the authority to determine if any other piece of legislation shall be deemed major legislation.

Scheduling of Major Legislation: If the Senate session that major legislation is scheduled to be voted on coincides with a Holy Day, any member of the Florida State University Student Body whom it affects may express their concerns to the Student Senate President. The Student President, with the consultation of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore, may then ensure that the major legislation is scheduled to be voted on during a senate session that does not conflict with that Holy Day. The Student Senate President has the discretion to change the voting date for major legislation before a concern is made.

sections.heading: Chapter 416 Policies
sections.text:
Policies
Senate may may permit SGA entities to adopt a “policy” which shall be treated as a governing document for said entity.

Policy Restrictions

No policy adopted by any SGA entity shall contradict the Student Body Constitution or Statutes. In the case of contradiction or inconsistency between any adopted policy and the Constitution or Statutes, the Constitution or Statutes shall take precedence.
Policy Adoption & Revision

Through statutory requirement, the Student Senate may or may not require Senate approval of any adoption or revision of policies. In the case that no approval is required, the entity adopting or revising their policy may adopt or revise their policy at their own discretion.

Policy Amendment

The Student Senate shall reserve the right to amend any adopted policy established within these statutes. This shall be formatted as a Student Senate resolution to revise said established policy.

sections.heading: Chapter 417 The Campus Advancement And Development Fund
sections.text:
Establishment
The establishment of a fund to facilitate substantial infrastructure improvements and long-term projects that advance the Student Government Association's mission and enrich the collegiate experience for the entire student body. 

Funding and Contributions
The fund shall receive a minimum allocation equivalent to 0.30 percent (0.30%) of the yearly budget collected from A&S fees.
A line item must be included in the yearly budget that shall be explicitly be allocated to this fund titled "CAD Fund."
Purpose
The Fund is established to provide financial backing for large-scale projects and initiatives that benefit the student body and enhance the capabilities of the Student Government Association.
The Fund may also act as a strategic resource for mitigating minor budgetary shortfalls, by empowering the Student Government Association to effectively manage its finances without needing to access the Central Reserves account.

Usage of Funds
Expenditure from the fund shall be approved through the following process:
A bill proposing the use of funds shall be presented to the Senate.
The Finance Committee shall determine whether the bill is fiscally responsible by a three-fourths (3/4) majority vote.
The Student Life Committee shall determine whether the bill shall provide substantial improvement or enrichment to the student body.
If the bill is being used to mitigate a minor budgetary shortfall the Finance Committee shall objectively verify if this fund is needed to address the budgetary constraint by a four-fifths (4/5) majority vote.
Following passage by the required standing committees, the bill shall require a two-thirds (2/3) majority vote of the Senate.
Each committee shall consider the bill independently in its original form. The Senate shall not convene as a committee of the whole for the purpose of considering such bills, nor may such bills be moved to Second Reading prior to full committee consideration.

Following approval from the Senate, the Student Body President and Student Body Treasurer must approve the bill by signature.
This fund shall be a non-sweepable account. All monies allocated to the fund shall be held in the fund for at least two (2) fiscal years prior to being transferred or used. This provision can be waived by a three-fourths (3/4) majority vote of the Senate.
The Congress of Graduate Students shall be given the opportunity to contribute to this fund, should COGS contribute to this fund, COGS shall have voting representation on the Finance Committee during the usage of these funds.

Fund Administration and Oversight

The Student Body Treasurer shall be responsible for the management, investment, and oversight of the fund, ensuring its compliance with this chapter and other relevant statutes.
An annual report detailing the inflows, outflows, and project funding from the fund shall be submitted to the Senate and made available to the entire student body via the SGA website. 

Project Proposal Form Requirement
Mandatory Proposal Form
All bills requesting expenditures from the Campus Advancement and Development (CAD) Fund shall be accompanied by a completed “CAD Fund Project Proposal Form.”
The Senate shall maintain the standardized form, which shall be made available on the Senate Canvas page.
No CAD Fund bill shall be placed on the Senate Calendar without an accompanying form that is complete and compliant with this Chapter.
The Project Proposal Form shall be divided into the following sections, each of which must be completed in full by the bill sponsor(s):
Section I: General Information
Project Title
Sponsoring Senator(s), Organization(s), or Agency(ies)
Contact Information for External Project Lead(s)
Date of Submission
Section II: Project Description and Purpose
A clear description of the project or initiative
Statement of purpose, including how the project aligns with the mission of the Student Government Association
Identification of unmet need or gap in services currently provided by the SGA
Section III: Student Impact Statement
Estimated number of students directly and indirectly impacted
Student populations expected to benefit (e.g., undergraduate, graduate, international, marginalized groups)
Anticipated long-term benefits to the student body
Section IV: Financial Plan
Itemized project costs
Potential funding partners or cost-sharing opportunities
Long-term financial obligations, including maintenance costs
Explanation of financial sustainability without recurring dependence on the CAD Fund or SGA at-large
Section V: Implementation Plan
Timeline of key milestones
Responsible individuals, offices, or organizations for implementation
Coordination with relevant university offices, if applicable
Section VI: Accessibility and Inclusion Plan
Explanation of how the project will be accessible to all students, including those with disabilities, if applicable in the scope of the project
Section VII: Community and Stakeholder Input
Evidence of consultation (forums, surveys, or organizational endorsements)
Letters of support from relevant university departments or stakeholders, where applicable
Section VIII: Risk Assessment (Completed by the Student Body Treasurer’s Office)
Identification of potential financial, legal, or logistical risks
Mitigation strategies to address such risks
Section IX: Evaluation Metrics
Criteria for measuring the project’s success
Reporting obligations following implementation
Review and Compliance
Committees reviewing CAD Fund bills shall verify that each section of the Project Proposal Form has been completed prior to consideration.
The Senate shall not advance any CAD Fund bill to Second Reading unless a completed Project Proposal Form is attached and properly vetted by the Student Body Treasurer’s Office.

sections.heading: Chapter 500 Power Of The Court
sections.text:
Notice to Appear: The Court shall have the power to compel all enrolled students to appear before the Court, pursuant to Article IV, Section 6, of the Student Body Constitution.

Contempt: Failure to obey the notice to appear, without good cause being shown, shall constitute contempt of court.

Jurisdiction of the Court:

The Student Supreme Court shall be an appellate court for cases tried in other bodies at FSU that recognize the Supreme Court’s appellate jurisdiction. The Supreme Court shall also have original jurisdiction over such matters as defined in Article IV, Section 3 of the Student Body Constitution. Supreme Court Justices shall be selected through the procedures outlined in the Student Body Constitution, although the Chief Justice shall have the power to appoint the Clerk and Deputy Clerks of the Court, in addition to any other powers granted to the Chief Justice by the Student Body Constitution.
The Chief Justice shall appoint FSU law students to the University Defender Program to assist FSU students accused of violations of the Student Conduct Code, Academic Honor Policy, University Housing Code, Student Government Statutes, Student Body Constitution, or any other established University Policy.

Removal of Student Body Officers: The Student Supreme Court may only remove elected or appointed officers of the Student Body from office when the Court is holding an impeachment trial after receiving approved articles of impeachment from the Student Senate, and only after the Court has found the impeached officer guilty of the charges set forth in the articles of impeachment.

sections.heading: Chapter 503 Review Of Constitutional Amendments
sections.text:
Title and Purpose:

This act shall be called the "Student Supreme Court Constitutional Amendment and Referendum Review Act of 2017," hereinafter referred to as the "Court Review Act".

The purpose of this act is to provide for an effective procedure for the review of all constitutional amendments and referenda, collectively referred to as "provisions" for the purpose of this chapter, before the provisions are placed on the ballot as a means to ensure that all provisions voted on by students are fair and not deceptive in terms of the provision's language, and do not violate the Student Body Statutes, the Student Body Constitution, the Board of Governors Regulations, University Policy or Regulation, or any local, state, or federal law.

All proposed provisions shall be reviewed by the Student Supreme Court for vagueness and inconsistency with Federal and State laws and regulations, within seven (7) days of being submitted through the methods outlined in the Student Body Constitution, Article VI as well as any other relevant statues, laws, or rules.

The decision of the Court shall be advisory in regards to the clarity and leader of the provision. This advisory opinion shall be made available to the public and published on the Student Government Website. If a bill or constitutional amendment is amended after an opinion has been rendered, said bill must be resubmitted for a new opinion. In no case may the Supreme Court prevent the student body from voting on a proposed constitutional amendment from the ballot unless such amendment is found to clearly violate federal, state, or local law, including the Student Body Constitution and Statutes. Nor has it the authority to overturn the passage of a constitutional amendment, except in the aforementioned circumstance.

All Statements of Intent and language regarding proposed provisions shall be reviewed by the Student Supreme Court to ensure that the language of the statement adequately and fairly reflects the intent of the ballot proposal.

No proposed provision shall be placed on the ballot until the adequacy and fairness of the language is approved.

In the event that the Student Supreme Court does not offer an opinion within seven (7) days of receipt of the provision, the statement and its accompanying proposed constitutional amendment or referendum shall be immediately certified for placement on the ballot with the following disclaimer statement: “This ballot has been reviewed by the Student Supreme Court to determine the clarity of the language or legality."

If a provision does not satisfy the requirements enumerated in Section 503(1)(b) and/or any other relevant statute, law, or rule, as determined by the Student Supreme Court, the sponsors shall have an opportunity to correct the deficiencies and resubmit the provision to the Student Supreme Court. The Student Supreme Court shall submit a written opinion detailing the findings of its review.

If the Student Supreme Court rules that a provision is inconsistent with any relevant statute, law, or rule, it shall include in its opinion exactly which relevant statute, law, or rule the provision is alleged to be inconsistent with, as well as cite any relevant precedents if the application of said law is not immediately obvious.

The Student Supreme Court shall also include in its advisory opinion recommended changes to the language that would place it in compliance.

For the purpose of this provision, an election shall not be postponed if the Student Supreme Court has not reviewed a provision before the election.

In the event that the Student Supreme Court cannot review a provision a written explanation of the reason why shall be submitted to the Senate President and the Student Body President, and the provision shall be reviewed under this chapter by the Election Commission.

sections.text:

Represent parties requesting assistance in the drafting and execution of all motions before the court.

The SGA General Counsel shall serve until resignation or graduation unless removed by a majority vote of the Student Supreme Court or by the Student Senate. Additionally, the General Counsel shall be subject to impeachment by the Student Senate in the ordinary manner.

sections.heading: Chapter 505 Leaves Of Absences During The Summer Session For Members Of The Judicial Branch
sections.text:
Purpose:

The purpose of this chapter shall be to allow for certain members of the Judicial Branch to take a leave of absence during the summer session, and to set forth the procedures to select their temporary replacements during that term.

Applicability and Scope:

The provisions of this chapter shall apply to the following officers of the Judicial Branch.

Associate Justices of the Supreme Court
SGA General Counsel

Clerk of the Court

Deputy Clerks of the Court

The Chief Justice shall not be permitted to take a leave of absence during the summer session.

Procedure:

All eligible officers shall notify the Chief Justice in writing on or before the last day of final examination at the College of Law of their intention to take a leave of absence during the summer session.

At the conclusion of final examinations at the College of Law, the Chief Justice shall appoint temporary officers to fill all or some of the vacated seats at their discretion. These temporary officers must meet all of the qualifications for the office to which they are being appointed as if they were being appointed in the normal, permanent manner. In keeping with Article IV of the Student Body Constitution, the Student Body President and the Student Bar Association do not need to be contacted for temporary appointments. However, all temporary summer appointees to the Judicial Branch must be confirmed by a majority vote of the Student Senate. These nominations by the Chief Justice shall go directly to the floor at the earliest summer session of the Student Senate.

All appointees to the Judicial Branch during the summer session shall be on notice that their appointments are of a temporary nature. Their term of office shall terminate on the last day of final examinations for the summer academic term.

All temporary officers of the Judicial Branch who are entitled to compensation shall be compensated for the summer term as if they were permanent officers. This compensation shall cease at the close of the summer academic term or should they resign from office, whichever comes first.

All of the permanent officers of the Judicial Branch, who take a leave of absence for the summer term, shall receive no compensation for the summer term. Such compensation shall only resume when they assume their permanent offices at the opening of classes in the fall semester.

All temporary judicial officers are entitled to serve throughout the summer session, even if their permanent counterparts come back from the summer early. Permanent members only resume their offices at the opening of classes during the fall semester.

All temporary judicial officers are subject to impeachment by the Student Senate during the summer session according to the procedures listed in Chapter 405 of the Student Body Statutes.
