sections.heading: Chapter 702 The Office Of The Supervisor Of Elections
sections.text:
Selection Process:

Supervisor of Elections: The Supervisor of Elections shall be appointed by the Supreme Court Chief Justice and confirmed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

A Supervisor of Elections must be appointed no later than the last week of the Spring semester and confirmed no later than the first Student Senate meeting of the fall semester.

If the Supervisor of Elections leaves office within three (3) weeks of an election, a Deputy Supervisor of Elections must be appointed by the Supreme Court Chief Justice and shall immediately be subject to Senate confirmation.

The Senate Judiciary Committee shall create an exam on the elections code. The exam shall be revised by the Senate Judiciary Committee at their next meeting following any revision of the election code to reflect the current statute. This exam shall be taken by candidates for Supervisor of Elections, Deputy Supervisors of Elections, and Elections Assistants. The Student Senate shall administer the exam.

The candidates above must pass the exam within two (2) attempts per semester, with at least eighty (80) percent or more of the questions answered correctly.

No Supervisor of Elections shall be a candidate for any Student Government Association office or be affiliated with any SGA political party.

Deputy Supervisors of Elections:
Deputy Supervisors of Elections shall be appointed by the Supervisor of Elections, in accordance with the Student Body Constitution, and are subject to confirmation pursuant to Chapter 304.
Deputy Supervisors of Elections shall serve their terms concurrently with the Supervisor of Elections who appoints them.

No Deputy Supervisor of Elections shall be a candidate for any Student Government Association office or be affiliated with any SGA political party.

Duties and Powers of the Supervisor of Elections: The Supervisor of Elections shall perform the following duties:

Ensure that SGA political parties follow the Student Body election code.

Ensure that all candidates meet the qualifications of the office they are running for within three academic days following the filing deadline.

Employ no more than three (3) impartial Deputy Supervisors to serve an election and assist the Office of Elections.

Hire, train, assign duties to, and supervise any Deputy Supervisors of Elections.

Dismiss any Deputy Supervisors due to malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance.
Deputy Supervisors of Election who are dismissed have the right to formally appeal their dismissal through the same processes outlined in Section 405.5 in Student Statute.

Create and implement marketing strategies to improve voter turnout for all SGA elections.

At least four (4) weeks prior to the Elections, the Supervisor of  Elections shall advertise the available seats up for election.

Enforce the Election Code subject to the approval of the Elections Commission, when appropriate.

Verify the fair market value of each campaign expense, discount, or donation through various means including but not limited to job quotes and receipts.

Verify the Final Expense Statements for all candidates and political parties.

Refer questions of interpretation of the Election Code to the Student Supreme Court. The Student Supreme Court must render a written advisory opinion within forty-eight (48) hours of any submission of a request for an interpretation of the Election Code.

Notify all candidates via e-mail within twenty-four (24) hours of the decision to hold a Special Election. At this time, the Supervisor of Elections will inform the candidates of the date, time, and circumstances of the election.

Publish all offices up for election at least one (1) week prior to the filing deadline on the SGA website.

Ensure the publication of the election date, time, and appropriate procedures for voting on the SGA website.

Ensure the publication of the official ballot, referenda, and constitutional amendments one (1) week following the candidacy filing deadline, on the SGA Website.

Ensure the publication of the unofficial elections results no later than forty-eight (48) hours after the close of polls on the SGA website.

Ensure the publication of the dates and times of the deadlines for the declaration of candidacy for an elected office one (1) week prior to the opening of candidacy declaration on the SGA Website.

Enforce all campaign rules.

Host one SGA sponsored debate every Spring semester. The Spring debate shall be between all Student Body President, Vice President, and Treasurer candidates. Any other debates may be held at the discretion of the Supervisor of Elections. The debates must take place during the nine (9) day campaign period excluding voting days.

The Supervisor shall ensure that questions not selected for inclusion from student submissions are excluded because they do not address matters specific to the positions the candidates are running for, or are not relevant to the Florida State University Student Government Association.

The Supervisor shall notify all candidates for office of the event details including the time, date, and venue, no less than five (5) school days prior to the event, as well as request their attendance and participation at the event. Known questions selected by the Supervisor prior to the debate shall be made available no less than three (3) days prior to the debate

The Supervisor shall advertise the event to the student body no less than five (5) school days prior to the event. The debate advertisement must include the date, time, and place of the debate.

The Supervisor shall allot a portion of all debates for questions directed to the candidates. All questions asked at any debate held under this section shall originate from students; the Supervisor of Elections shall not author, draft, or contribute questions for use at any debate. This procedure applies to the Spring debate, the Executive Question and Answer segment of the Spring debate, and any other debates held at the discretion of the Supervisor. 
Seven (7) days prior to all debates, the Supervisor shall open a form for students to submit questions. The general audience question portion shall consist of no fewer than three (3) questions submitted in advance by students through this form, and no fewer than three (3) questions asked live by students in attendance at the given debate.

Within any form opened by the Supervisor of Elections for student-submitted questions, there shall be an option to include a student's email for identification. If a student provides their email and their comment is excluded, the student shall be notified by the Supervisor of Elections before the debate or event takes place. If the student does not provide their student email, they shall remain anonymous, and the Supervisor of Elections shall not be required to notify them if their question is excluded. 

A submitted question may be excluded only if it contains true threats, incitement to imminent lawless action, is considered vulgar or obscene, is not in the form of a question, or is duplicative in substance of another submitted question. The Supervisor may not exclude a question based on its political content, viewpoint, or the identity of the questioner. Explanation shall be given to the student who submitted an excluded question if they have provided a contact email.

Questions removed for containing true threats, incitement to imminent lawless action, or language considered vulgar or obscene shall not be published on the SGA website. Explanation shall be given to the student who submitted an excluded question upon request to the Supervisor of Elections.

If fewer than three (3) eligible questions are received by twenty-four (24) hours before an event, the Supervisor of Elections shall pull applicable questions for each candidate from the Forwarding Interview Questions created by the Student Senate Internal Affairs Committee on the SGA website. The Supervisor of Elections shall not have the authority to author questions should there not be enough student submissions.

When the number of advance-submitted questions exceeds the number of slots available, the Supervisor of Elections shall select questions by random lottery alongside the Deputy Supervisor(s) of Elections. Questions that meet the criteria of exclusion shall be removed. If enough questions are excluded to leave additional slots remaining, additional questions shall be selected by random lottery until all slots have been filled by eligible questions. 

For the Spring debate, an Executive Question and Answer Event shall be held in which candidates are given the opportunity to address position-specific questions. The Supervisor shall select no more than six (6) position-specific questions from eligible advance submissions for this segment, subject to the same fallback provisions set forth for debates. In addition, the Supervisor shall allot time for no fewer than three (3) position-specific questions asked live by students in attendance. Candidates shall receive questioning in order of positions.
For all live audience questions, students in attendance shall be recognized by the Supervisor in the order they indicate a desire to speak. The Supervisor shall briefly review each live questions before it is posed to confirm it meets the requirements for a submitted question, and shall be granted the authority to remove any that do not. 

No candidate or candidate representative shall have the right to approve, reject, or be consulted on any question before it is asked.
The Supervisor of Elections shall publish the recording of the debate and/or the Question and Answer Event on the SGA website within forty-eight (48) hours following the conclusion of the debate and event.

The Supervisor shall maintain decorum among candidates and the public at events hosted by the Elections office. Anyone who fails to maintain decorum may be asked to leave by the Supervisor.

Declare candidates or voting blocks of any election to be elected by acclamation if an election is uncontested upon the deadline of declaration of candidacy filing, pending the resolution of any candidacy controversies to be resolved by the Elections Commission, Supervisor of Elections, or other pertinent authority.

Invalidate illegally cast ballots.

The Supervisor of Elections shall not hold the capability to change legally cast votes.

Maintain, as public record, the final result and ballots of all elections.

Declare results valid and certify elections.

Change the Declared Seat Number for Candidates to the Student Senate, Congress of Graduate Students, Union Board, and Campus Recreation Board no earlier than three (3) days following filing deadline and no later than twenty-four (24) hours prior to the opening of polls if all of the following criteria is met:

The number of candidates who filed for that division is equal to or less than the number of seats allocated for that semester’s election.

All filed candidates for that division have been properly contacted about the change by the Supervisor.

No candidates show disapproval to themselves of being moved to a different seat number than they originally filed for.

There remain no outstanding appeals for qualifications of candidates in that division as outlined in Chapter 704.
Employ no more than five (5) impartial Elections Assistants to volunteer in the Office of Elections. Election Assistants shall be tasked with facilitating projects that enable voter turnout, voter education, and voter  engagement.

Hire, train, assign duties to, and supervise any Elections Assistants.

Dismiss any Elections Assistants due to malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance.

No Elections Assistants shall be a candidate for any Student Government Association office or be affiliated with any SGA political party.

Hours of Operation:
The Office of Elections shall be open for a minimum of fifteen (15) hours during the five (5) week election period. During the operation weeks prior to and after this five (5) week period, the office shall be open a minimum of ten (10) hours and a maximum of fifteen (15) hours.

Two weeks prior to election day the Office of Elections shall be open for at least two (2) hours per business day.

Two weeks prior to the filing deadlines, the Supervisor of Elections shall inform all candidates and political parties of their office hours.

The Supervisor of Elections shall work no more than twenty (20) hours a week during the five (5) week election period. During the operational weeks prior to and after this five (5) week period, the Supervisor of Elections shall work no more than ten (10) hours a week. 

Role in the Election Commission: The Supervisor of Elections shall have the following responsibilities and duties in the Election Commission:
Serve as chair of the Elections Commission.

Convene the Elections Commission and assist in setting the agenda for its meetings.

Publish meeting times at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to the commencement of Elections Commission meetings. The Elections Commission shall notify candidates or political parties who are charged with alleged violations at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance of the meeting by phone or email. 

Receive and review complaints which allege violations of the Elections Code per Chapter 710 of the Student Body Statutes. 

Upon receipt of a complaint alleging a violation of the Elections Code, notify the accused of the alleged violation within twenty-four (24) hours of receipt of the violation. The Supervisor of Elections shall have the authority to dismiss alleged violations which have insufficient evidence, lack clarity, cite the improper respondent, or do not cite the proper statute. If the Supervisor of Elections dismisses a violation, the Supervisor of Elections shall notify the petitioner(s) and respondent(s) of the complaint’s dismissal within twenty-four (24) hours of the receipt of the initial complaint and provide the reasoning of dismissal. If the petitioner(s) resubmit the same violation within twenty-four (24) hours of the dismissal or there is no dismissal, the Supervisor of Elections shall forward the complaint to the Elections Commission. Every receipt of a complaint, dismissal by the Supervisor, or forward to the Elections Commission must be documented and made publicly available within twenty-four (24) hours of the receipt, dismissal or forward.

sections.heading: Chapter 703 The Elections Commission
sections.text:
Composition of the Elections Commission:

The Elections Commission shall be composed of the Supervisor of Elections and six (6) FSU students selected by the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court. Alternate(s) shall be selected by the Supreme Court Chief Justice to fill absences. The SGA Advisor and one Deputy Supervisor of Elections, as chosen by the Supervisor of Elections, shall serve as ex-officio non-voting members. Quorum for meetings shall be constituted as a majority of voting members.

The Supervisor of Elections shall serve as the chair of the Elections Commission. The Commission shall elect a vice chair, who shall be a voting member of the Elections Commission, by a majority vote of no less than quorum. A Deputy Supervisor of Elections shall serve as the secretary of the Elections Commission by a majority vote of no less than quorum. The Supervisor of Elections shall be responsible for convening this meeting. Any vacancies shall be filled by the Commission as the first order of business of the next Commission meeting 

The Elections Commission must convene for the first time no later than three (3) weeks prior to the Fall Election to elect a vice-chair and secretary. The Elections Commission must convene no later than two (2) weeks following any election in order to review alleged violations referred by the Supervisor of Elections. The Elections Commission must meet no later than two (2) weeks following the inauguration of certified candidates elected during the Spring Election in order to review the contents of the current Elections Code and make recommendations to the Student Senate. All other Commission meetings will be held at the discretion of the Supervisor of Elections.

No member of the Elections Commission shall be a candidate for an elected office within SGA, nor shall they be affiliated with an SGA political party.

In a written and signed request to the SGA Attorney General, any student running for an elected office or associated with a political party shall have the right to request a recusal of any member of the Elections Commission. The SGA Attorney General shall investigate the complaint and upon finding merit, that member must recuse themselves.

The Elections Commission shall serve as an administrative review board of original jurisdiction and will hear only those cases which are forwarded by the Supervisor of Elections pursuant to Section 702(4)(e) of the Student Body Statutes. The burden of proof to be met by an entity alleging a violation in order to prove that violation shall be by “clear and convincing evidence.”

All voting members of the Election Commission shall take the Election Code Exam upon their appointment, and shall retake the Exam prior to the beginning of the Fall Election Cycle every year.

All voting members and candidates for the Election Commission must pass the exam within two (2) attempts per academic year prior to installation, with at least eight (80) percent or more of the questions answered correctly.

The Election Code Exam will be administered and graded by the Student Senate President or Student Senate President Pro Tempore.

Only the questions answered incorrectly may be revealed, but not the answer choices.

The test questions and scores may be made available upon demand to the Student Body President, Vice President, Chief of Staff, Supervisor of Elections, Senate President, Senate Pro Tempore, Senators, COGS Speaker of the House and the SGA Advisor. 

Powers and Duties of the Elections Commission: The Elections Commission shall have the following Powers and Duties: 
All actions of the Elections Commission shall require the approval by a majority present of voting members.

The Supervisor of Elections shall preside over Elections Commission hearings as chair and must abstain from voting unless to break a tie. In the event that the Supervisor of Elections recuses themselves or is otherwise unavailable, the Vice Chair of the Elections Commission will chair the hearing, in which case the Vice Chair must abstain from voting unless to break a tie.

Submit recommendations regarding the Elections Code to the Student Senate.

Appoint a Secretary selected by majority vote of the Elections Commission, who shall record the minutes of the Elections Commission.

Decide and validate the agenda of the Elections Commission.

Upon the receipt of a complaint from the Supervisor of Elections pursuant to Section 702(e)(2), the Elections Commission will schedule a hearing to take place within five (5) business days. The Rules of Procedure for Elections Commission hearings for appeals or alleged violations shall be the following:

The Elections Commission shall notify all concerned entities involved at least 24 hours prior to a scheduled hearing.

The meeting time shall not conflict with any meeting of the Student Senate. If a conflict of schedule exists, the affected candidate or party has until five (5) hours prior to the Elections Commission meeting to notify the Supervisor of Elections. Candidates shall provide the Supervisor of Elections with documentation regarding the scheduling conflict and any excuse granted shall be in accordance with University Policy. If no such excuse is provided to the Supervisor of Elections, the alleged violation shall move to default judgment. If such an excuse is provided, a second Elections Commission meeting pertaining to the particular violation shall be scheduled to directly accommodate the candidate and occur no later than one (1) week from the original hearing.

Once convened the presiding officer of the Elections Commission shall then read aloud each appeal or alleged violation that the Commission will hear during the meeting.

The Elections Commission shall hear each appeal or alleged violation in the order that it was received.
The Election Commission is authorized to dismiss any violations it determines to be frivolous or defective. Violations dismissed under this clause shall require an opinion explaining the rationale of the frivolous or defective finding and shall be published publicly within 48 hours. This clause shall not prohibit any dismissed cases from being further appealed to the Supreme Court.

Beginning with the entity who alleged an Elections Code violation, the Elections Commission shall hear each entity’s opening oral arguments for a maximum of five (5) minutes. During this time, the entity accused of a violation may plead guilt as a substitute for an opening oral argument. The Elections Commission may move to closing arguments if a guilty plea is entered.

Once opening oral arguments are concluded, the Elections Commission shall direct each concerned entity, beginning with the entity who alleged a violation of the Elections Code, to present their cases in chief by way of oral arguments not exceeding ten (10) minutes.

After the first three (3) minutes of an entity’s case in chief have expired, any currently empaneled member of the Elections Commission is entitled to ask questions of the entity making oral arguments. Questioning shall not penalize any entity’s respective time limit.

Following the presentation of each entity’s case in chief, each shall be entitled to a five (5) minute closing, beginning with the entity who alleged an Elections Code violation. 

After closing arguments have commenced, the Elections Commission shall adjourn to deliberate for no more than one (1) hour per violation, at which time a final majority vote must be taken to determine if the alleged violation shall be sustained, and the respondent found responsible for violating the Elections Code.

The Elections Commission shall immediately notify all relevant entities of the case’s disposition and shall submit to the SGA Webmaster for posting to the SGA website, including any concurring or dissenting opinions, within five (5) business days of the final vote in any given case. The majority shall write at least one opinion as to the reasoning of the disposition of the case.

Investigate, note, and make findings of fact of violations of the Election Code.

Decisions of the Elections Commission may be appealed to the Student Supreme Court. The Elections Commission must rule on a matter before it can be appealed to the Supreme Court. Under no circumstances may the Elections Commission defer ruling on a matter to a higher body without rendering a decision.

Any decision made by the Elections Commission may be appealed by a concerned entity to the hearing to the Student Supreme Court no later than thirty-six (36) hours after said decision and all accompanying opinions have posted to the SGA website pursuant to Section 703(2)(f)(10) of the Student Body Statutes. No appeals of decisions made by the Elections Commission shall be accepted after this thirty-six (36) hour period.

Any appeal of a decision by the Elections Commission to the Supreme Court cannot be remanded or sent back to the Elections Commission by the Supreme Court to rule on a case.

sections.heading: Chapter 704 Qualifying For Office
sections.text:
Qualifications:

All candidates must qualify for the office as defined by the Student Body Constitution and Statutes. 

All candidates for Student Senate must be enrolled, by filing deadline, in the College that they seek to represent. Senators who file in divisions in which they are not registered shall be removed from the ballot.

If a candidate has been admitted into one or more Colleges, that individual may represent any College that they are admitted to. 

After submission of candidacy, students cannot change the division in which they run under in that given election, unless a special election is called in which candidates must resubmit declarations of candidacy. 

Candidates for the Senior Class Council must be enrolled such that they will at least have seventy-two (72) academic credits at the end of the semester that they run. 

Declaration of Candidacy:

All candidates for election to Student Body Office must submit a declaration of candidacy form. No student may declare candidacy for more than one office at a time. Submission of a declaration of candidacy form shall indicate an understanding and acceptance of all filing procedures, campaign restrictions, and the elections code and ethics code. 

A political party may remove affiliation with any candidate for any reason until twenty-four (24) hours prior to the starting time of any scheduled election. 

A candidate may withdraw their candidacy or remove their party affiliaition until twenty-four (24) hours prior to the starting time of any scheduled election. 

There shall be Mandatory Candidate Seminars on the Monday and Tuesday after the deadline of the declaration of candidacy organized by the Supervisor of Elections that will inform candidates about rules and procedures. All Candidates, Campaign Managers, and Campaign Treasurers are required to attend one of the mandatory candidate seminars. Political Parties must send all of their candidates along with their Campaign Manager and Treasurer who falls under Section 709(3)(a) of the Student Body Statues. The Supervisor of Elections shall have the sole discretion to hold additional seminars. Candidates or parties who fail to attend one of the seminars held by the Supervisor of Elections shall lose their eligibility for office unless they show proof of class conflict or illness.  
If the Supervisor of Elections, in collaboration with the SGA Advisor or University Administrator, finds that any candidate does not qualify for office, the Supervisor of Elections shall remove the candidate from the ballot and notify the candidate within twenty-four (24) hours. 

Political Parties:

Any group of students may organize as a student political party and nominate candidates. 

The Supervisor of Elections shall officially recognize a political party no later than one (1) day prior to the filing deadline of an election when the party does all of the following: 

Files with the Supervisor of Elections an accurate copy of its Constitution and an up-to-date list of Officers.

Nominates at least one candidate for office per year. 

Files a party name, acronym, or logo that does not duplicate or blatantly resemble the name, acronym, or logo of any other existing FSU campus political party, nor utilizes the copyrighted image or symbol not authorized for use by the individual using the image or symbol, or any individual without their consent. Party names may not contain the following:
Obscene material as defined by Florida Statute §847.001.
Content otherwise prohibited by the FSU RSO Handbook. 

The acceptance of names shall be at the discretion of the Supervisor of Elections, who shall inform the individual(s) who filed for the political party with the discarded name within forty-eight (48) hours of receiving the filing. If a political party would like to appeal the decision of the Supervisor of Elections, they may file an appeal to the Elections Commission within three (3) business days of being informed of the decision. 

Is a Registered Student Organization with Student Organizations and Involvement. 

Has not been disqualified in a past election within the previous four (4) years due to violations of the Election Code. 

Ballot Provisions: All questions of opinions, compulsory referenda, constitutional amendments, and other ballot provisions must be submitted to the Supervisor of Elections from the Student Senate President stating the Senate’s approval, or with all petitions signed from the sponsor of the proposed ballot provision by the filing deadline for an election. Should the ballot provision achieve all requirements, it shall go on the ballot for the next election. The Senate may withdraw its approval by the same margin needed to propose to ballot. The sponsor of a petition may withdraw a petition for a ballot provision, or individual petitioners may withdraw their signature for a ballot provision. The Supervisor of Elections shall post online all provisions (both wording and statements of intent/understanding), their source (Senate or petition), and the number of remaining signatures needed, if applicable. The Supervisor of Elections shall have the discretion to choose whether or not a petition follows the following guidelines. If the Supervisor ascertains that a petition is not valid, they must inform the sponsor of the petition within three (3) business days of receipt of the petition, with an explanation why. The following rules on petitions shall be enforced: 

All ballot provision petition forms must include identification information for the student in the form of: Full Name, FSU ID, date signed, and signature. 

An E-Signature shall suffice, and may be constituted by an additional text-box for a name on an online form. 

Petitions must follow the below provisions: 

For opinions questions, the following wording must appear: “This is a petition to add an Opinion Question to the FSU Student Body Election ballot. It has no legal force or action other than to ascertain the opinion of the Student Body on a particular issue. It needs two hundred (200) signatures to reach the ballot and a majority to become the unofficial opinion of the FSU Student Body.”

For referendum elections, the following wording must appear: “This is a petition to add a referendum election to the FSU Student Body Election ballot. It has legal force to require SGA to take the actions required therein assuming the majority of the electorate voting on the referendum vote yes, it needs five hundred (500) signatures to reach the ballot.”

For constitutional amendments, the following wording must appear: “This is a petition to add an amendment to the Student Body Constitution to the FSU Student Body Election ballot. It shall become a legally binding part of the Constitution upon ratification by two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Body. It needs fifteen hundred (1,500) signatures to reach the ballot.”

All petition forms must have the full text of the proposed provision and must begin their official ballot text with the statement “I, the undersigned, as a legally registered FSU student, aware that submitting false and/or duplicate information is a punishable offense, do hereby petition the Student Body Supervisor of Elections to add the following ballot provision to the Student Body election ballot.”

sections.heading: Chapter 705 Election Procedures
sections.text:
General Elections:

All candidates in a general election shall declare their candidacy with the Supervisor of Elections no later than 4 p.m. Eastern Time on Monday, three (3) weeks before election day. 

General Elections shall take place on the eighth Monday and Tuesday of the semester in which they take place. In the case of a conflict or a religious holiday, the Supervisor of Elections shall determine the date of election day to be on a Monday and Tuesday between the sixth and eighth week of the semester. The Supervisor of Elections shall announce the date of election day no later than the third Wednesday of the semester. 

The Supervisor of Elections shall notify the Student Body President, Vice President, Chief of Staff, Senate President, Senate Pro Tempore, COGS Speaker of the House and the SGA Advisor of the date and calendar of each General Election, no later than twenty-four (24) hours after deciding the date of any General Election. 

For the Fall General Election, the Supervisor of Elections shall notify the Student Body President, Student Senate President, COGS Speaker, the Chair of the Campus Recreation Board, and the SGA Advising Office of the date and seats up for election no later than twenty-four (24) hours after deciding the date of the Fall General Election. 

For the Spring General Election, the Supervisor of Elections shall notify the Student Body President, the Student Senate President, the Senior Class President, the Chair of the Union Board, and the SGA Advising Office of the date and seats up for election no later than twenty-four (24) hours after deciding the date of the Spring General Election. 

Once the date of the election is determined, the Supervisor of Elections shall send the elections calendar to the SGA Webmaster to be published on the SGA website no later than twenty-four (24) hours after deciding the date of any General Election. 

Nothing in this section shall be construed to prohibit any student from engaging in political speech, including the solicitation of support for or against any candidate, political party, or ballot item, at any time.  

Special Elections: Any Special Election shall follow the same procedure for the General Election of the semester in which the Special Election falls in. The Senate shall provide the funds for conducting a special election by a majority vote. The date and timeline of any Special election shall be determined at the discretion of the Supervisor of Elections within a three (3) week period.
The Supervisor of Elections shall call a Special Election for any race or seat in which one or multiple of the following have occurred: 

The winning candidate is disqualified in an election. 

A campus political party is disqualified in an election where they have won seats. 

The results for an individual and/or an entire election are declared invalid by the Supervisor of Elections.
In the event of a tie between two or more candidates.

Referendum Elections: The Supervisor of Elections shall conduct Constitutional Amendment and referenda elections during the fall or spring General Elections. The admission of referenda shall be placed on the ballot in accordance with Article VI of the Student Body Constitution, unless a special election is called for in accordance with Chapter of the Student Body Statutes.
The official ballot for a referendum or proposed Constitutional amendment shall give a brief statement regarding the proposed changes prepared by the author. Voters shall be given the opportunity to vote "YES" or "NO" for the proposed changes. 

Campus Pulse Commission
The Supervisor of Elections shall form the Campus Pulse Commission (CPC) to develop and refine ballot questions that capture student opinions on key campus issues, i.e. the “pulse” of Campus. The CPC ensures these questions are impartial and representative, facilitating informed decision-making within the Student Government Association and university administration.
At the beginning of each Fall and Spring semester, the Campus Pulse Commission shall have an appointed set of members responsible for the operation of the Commission. The Commission shall be composed of the following members:

Three (3) designees of the Student Senate

Three (3) designees of the SGA Executive Branch

A designee of the Office of Governmental Affairs

The Supervisor of Elections, as Chair of the CPC

Up to six (6) designees from any other relevant entity that may provde beneficial to the mission of the Commission, shall be chosen by the Student Body President, Supervisor of Elections, and Student Senate President, and SGA Advisor prior to the opening of the Commission.

The Commission is tasked with the creation, solicitation, and refinement of questions intended for the ballot; this should be completed no later than one week prior to the filing deadline. The Commission shall meet no fewer than two times and must discuss any matters that may warrant surveying the Student Body by drafting impartial opinion questions to include on the ballot for that semester’s election.

The final selection of questions must be approved by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Commission members and then submitted via the designees of the Student Senate to be placed on the consent calendar. In the case of an objection in the Student Senate, these questions require a simple majority vote of the Senate to pass. If ratified, the Supervisor of Elections will incorporate the selected set of questions into the ballot.

In addition to the questions put forth by the Commission or submitted pursuant to SBS 704.4, the following opinion question shall be on the ballot by default, with “Yes” and “No” being the two responses.

Do you approve of the work done by the Student Government Association?

Recall Elections: The Supervisor of Elections shall conduct recall elections in accordance with Article VII of the Student Body Constitution.
The official ballot shall state the name of the office of the official in question, and two hundred (200) words or less, the reasons for demanding recall of the officer(s) as set forth in the recall petition(s), and in no more than two hundred (200) words of the officer's defense. The ballot must include the statement: “Shall the following officers retain their seats.” Voters shall vote "YES" or "NO" on the recall. A sample ballot shall be available at each polling site in accordance with Article VII of the Constitution.

If a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the students voting elect to recall the official, the official’s term of office shall cease upon certification of the election results by the Elections Commission. The vacancy created shall be filled as provided by the Student Body Constitution and the Student Body Statutes and may not be filled by the recalled officer. 

The Supervisor of Elections shall publish the election date and time of the recall election on the SGA website one (1) week prior to the recall election. 

Senate Apportionment Process:
Each Division shall be entitled to at least one (1) representative in the Student Senate. 

The number of seats allocated to the Student Senate shall be eighty (80). Each elected member shall serve until their resignation or the same-semester inauguration one year following their installation. 

Using the Student Database, the seats shall be apportioned each fall based on the percentages of students classified by their division and will be eligible to vote and run for seats in their respective divisions. All Special and Graduate Studies Students shall be eligible to be candidates for, as well as vote for, all seats in the Special Students division which shall be apportioned seats based on the number of students enrolled in the Graduate Studies and Special Student divisions. 

For the purposes of Senate apportionment, graduate and professional students will be considered members of the collegiate division that offers their course of study and not the Graduate School. Seats apportioned to any division aside from undergraduate studies shall be apportioned to reflect the percentage of the student body engaged in an upper-division undergraduate, graduate, or professional course of study in that college.

Colleges that do not have students enrolled in undergraduate courses of study shall be apportioned seats in the same way as any other normal division. 

Undergraduate Senators serving in an upper division seat when they graduate shall be allowed to retain their seat so long as they are enrolled in graduate courses in the same college that their seat represents the first semester following their graduation. 
Undergraduate Senators who graduate in the Spring shall be allowed to take a leave of absence through the summer semester as defined in Section 100(6). 
The Supervisor of Elections shall, after consultation with the SGA Advising Office, establish which seats shall be designated as Fall and Spring Seats by the third Wednesday of the Fall Academic Semester. New seat apportionments shall be released in the form of an official memorandum signed and published by the Supervisor of Elections on the SGA Website. 

Apportionments shall be released by the Supervisor of Elections at least one (1) week prior to the opening of the Candidacy Declaration form. 

No division shall have a difference in allocated seats greater than one (1) between the Fall and Spring semester of a given academic year.

In the event that a division contains an odd number of seats, the greater number of seats shall be up for election in the Fall Elections. 

Fall Seats shall be designated with odd numbers, Spring seats shall be designated with even numbers. 

Loss of Senate Office Due to Reapportionment: 

Once a Senate Seat has been eliminated from a specific division because of yearly apportionment, it shall dissolve upon the inauguration in the semester (fall or spring) that the seat was originally apportioned to. 

If a Spring seat has been eliminated due to the yearly apportionment, and that seat is held by the Senate President or Senate President Pro-Tempore, that individual may stay in their seat until the individual’s term as President or President Pro-Tempore expires.

If at any time during this period the Senator in question should resign or otherwise be removed from their seat, then the seat shall dissolve immediately.

sections.heading: Chapter 706 Fall Elections
sections.text:
The Fall Election cycle shall include the races for odd-numbered Senate seats, the Campus Recreation Board, the Congress of Graduate Students, elected members of the RSO Allocation Committee, and shall include any applicable constitutional amendments, referenda items, and opinion questions. 

Campus Recreation Board:

There shall be eight (8) elected Campus Recreation Board Seats. Each seat on the Board shall be elected individually. 

The electorate of the Campus Recreation Board shall be limited to students enrolled at the Tallahassee campus. 

Beyond the provisions listed here, elections shall proceed pursuant to Section 1006(4).

The Congress of Graduate Students:

The electorate shall be limited to graduate, post-baccalaureate special and professional students. 

Elections shall be held pursuant to Chapter 603 of the Student Body Statutes and COGS Code Chapter 111.

sections.heading: Chapter 707 Spring Elections
sections.text:
The Spring Election cycle shall include the races for even-numbered Senate seats, the Student Union Board, Student Body President and Vice President, Student Body Treasurer, Senior Class Council President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary, and shall include any applicable constitutional amendments, referenda items, and opinion questions. 

If the current Senate President or Senate President Pro Tempore is holding a Spring seat, that seat shall not be up for election during the Spring elections. Instead, it shall be advertised as a vacant seat in the fall at the end of the officer’s term, or upon resignation of the official from either President or Pro Tempore.

Senior Class Council:

There shall be four elected positions in the Senior Class Council, which shall be elected individually as the Senior Class Council President, Vice President, Treasurer, and Secretary. 

Union Board:

There shall be twelve (12) elected Union Board Seats. Each Union Board seat shall be elected individually.

The electorate of the Union Board is limited to those students enrolled at the Tallahassee campus.

Elections shall be carried out subject to the provisions of Chapter 1008.

Students employed by the Student Union shall be allowed to run for a seat on the Board.

sections.heading: Chapter 708 Campaigning Rules And Campaign Materials
sections.text:
Regulation of Campaign Material and Other Activities:

Any posting or placement of campaign materials must be consistent with applicable University regulations, which can be found at http://posting.fsu.edu or its successor website.
Any campaign materials posted within an election period must be removed by the Friday following the designated election days, as per FSU Policy 4-OP-B-9, Section A Provision 3. Any campaign materials from preceding non-election periods must also be removed by this deadline.

Campaigning in university academic buildings is subject to the same content-neutral time, place, and manner restrictions that apply to all other forms of student expression in those buildings, including applicable noise, posting, and space-reservation policies administered by the university. Campaigning in university resident hall common areas, including lobbies, community rooms, and shared social spaces, is subject to the same rules that govern all other forms of solicitation and student expression in those spaces, and is not permitted during posted quiet hours. Unsolicited door-to-door canvassing of individual residence hall rooms is prohibited during posted quiet hours. No restriction on campaigning in resident halls shall be applied in a manner that grants access to any university entity, student organization, or governing body while denying equivalent access to candidates or political parties. 

Campaign communications sent through the university email system are subject to the same acceptable-use policies that govern all other student use of university email, including any university policies prohibiting mass unsolicited electronic communications. Acceptable-use policies that govern student use of university email can be found at https://policies.vpfa.fsu.edu/policies-and-procedures/technology/electronic-mail-policy or its successor website. No student shall be prohibited from sending campaign-related communications to individual recipients or to recipients who have opted to receive such communications solely because the content of the communication constitutes campaigning.  
Campaigning inside university-owned libraries is subject to the same noise and conduct policies that apply to all other activities in those facilities, which may be found at https://www.lib.fsu.edu/about/community-standards or its successor website. Campaigning in university dining halls and the Student Union is permitted and is subject to the same content-neutral space reservation, tabling, and posting policies that apply to all other student organizations and activities in those facilities. 
Students shall not be prohibited from wearing properly registered campaign clothing materials. 
Within the Student Senate Chambers, candidates and designated party representatives who are formal presenting before the Student Senate shall be expected to not display or distribute campaign materials during their presentations. This restriction does not apply to attendees, observers, or candidates who are not actively presenting before the body, but these individuals are also expected to abide by the dress code, to the extent practicable, while in the Student Senate Chambers.

sections.heading: Chapter 709 Campaigning Finances
sections.text:
Election Expenses:

Election expenses shall be incurred by a party or independent candidate within the election period, which shall be considered the period beginning five (5) weeks before the election days set by the Supervisor of Elections, and ending on the Friday following the identified election days, as stated in Section 700.2 of Student Statutes.
The Supervisor of Elections shall, in consultation with the SGA Advisor and Office of the Student Body Treasurer, rule on all questions of value regarding campaign expenses for both election and non-election periods.

Total election expenses shall not exceed $10,000 for all candidates of a party in any one general or special election. Party expenses shall be attributed to each candidate of the party. 

Election expense limits of independent candidates shall be as follows: 

Student Body President and Vice President Candidates: $3,500 

Student Body Treasurer Candidates: $1,500

Senate Candidates: $250

Union Board or Recreation Board Candidates: $250
RSO Allocation Committee Candidates: $250

Senior Class President: $1,500

Senior Class Vice-President: $1,500

Senior Class Treasurer: $1,000

Senior Class Secretary: $1,000 

All expenditures of any candidate shall be paid by the campaign (party or independent) manager and/or treasurer.

Candidates shall not receive contributions of any kind from Student Government Association organizations. 

Non-Election Expenses:
Non-election expenses shall be all campaign-related expenses outside of the election period, including:

Expenses from the beginning of the Fall or Spring semester until the election period begins.

Expenses after the election period, until the end of the semester. 

Expenses during a semester in which there is no general or special election.

There shall be three (3) non-election periods in a school year.

The first shall begin on the first day of Fall Semester, and will end at the beginning of the Fall Election period.

The second shall begin the day after the Fall election period, and will end at the beginning of the Spring Election period.
The third will begin the day after the Spring election, and will end on the last day of the Summer B semester.

Total non-election expenses shall not exceed $6,000 in a school year, but expenses may be divided into any non-election period as identified in clause (b).

If a party or independent candidate exceeds the non-election period spending cap, they will receive a Schedule 3 violation for the election period immediately following the non-election period in which the excess occurred, as per Section 710.6(e) of Student Statutes.

If a party or independent candidate further exceeds the non-election period spending cap after already receiving a Schedule 3 violation in that school year, they will receive a Schedule 4 violation for the election period immediately following the non-election period in which the further excess occurred.

Final Expense Statements:

Final Expense Statements shall be submitted to the Supervisor of Elections no later than 12:00 p.m. on the Friday following any election and shall include preceding non-election expenses as well as election expenses. 

Final Expense Statements shall be matched to financial records kept by the Supervisor of Elections to verify accuracy. 

Expense statements shall be submitted only on the official forms as prescribed by the Supervisor of Elections. 

If a candidate or political party spends no money on campaigning within any given period, a sworn statement to that effect, made available by the Supervisor of Elections, shall be accepted as an official final expense statement. This documentation must be submitted in the same manner as a traditional final expense statement.
Each political party shall include a Financial Recap Summary of all funds collected throughout the academic year preceding the election. This summary must:
Detail the source, amount, and date of all income received, including but not limited to donations, dues, merchandise sales, and fundraising activities.
Be attached to the Final Expense Statement submission and shall be posted publicly.
Be formatted according to templates issued by the Supervisor of Elections and verified against any previously reported Campaign Contribution Statements.

Failure to submit a complete Final Expense Statement by 12 p.m. the Friday following the elections, will be considered incomplete. Failure to submit a verifiably complete final expense statement by 12 p.m. the Friday following the election will constitute a Schedule I Violation. The Supervisor of Elections must notify by email and publicly post online whether the final expense statement is complete or incomplete by 5 p.m. Friday. 

Upon notice of a final expense statement being incomplete, the political party or independent candidate has until 4 p.m. the following Tuesday to rectify the final expense statement. The Supervisor of Elections must inform political parties or independent candidates within twenty-four (24) hours of receiving an intended rectified final expense statement on whether the statement is complete or incomplete. Failure to rectify a verifiably incomplete financial statement by 4 p.m. the following Tuesday will constitute a Schedule 4 Violation, consistent with Section 710(6)(e). 
Notwithstanding any other provision of this Chapter, alleged violations concerning Chapter 709 may be filed by the Supervisor of Elections after the forty-eight (48) hour deadline applicable to regular violations. Failure to rectify a verifiably incomplete or procedurally compliant but substantively unlawful financial statement by 4 p.m. the following Tuesday will constitute a Schedule 4 Violation, consistent with Section 710(6)(e).

If the Supervisor of Elections fails to notify an individual political party or candidate of an incomplete Final Expense Statement, or incomplete rectified final expense statement, and any such notice of Incompleteness is not posted online, this offense is grounds for impeachment of the Supervisor of Elections as decided by the Student Senate. If a rectified final expense statement is submitted less than twenty-four (24) hours before the Tuesday deadline, the Supervisor of Elections shall be allowed to notify individuals whether it is complete or incomplete after the close of the deadline.

The Supervisor of Elections shall post the Approved Final Expense Statements of the political parties and individuals prior to the certification of elections.

Campaign Treasuries:

All political parties shall have a designated campaign treasurer if money is spent on their campaign. Candidates running independently, without the aid of a political party, are exempt from this rule. 

Campaign treasuries shall be placed in a non-personal bank account; this bank account must be used only for party and campaign treasuries. Independent candidates are exempt from this nonpersonal bank account provision.

The Campaign Contribution Statement and any other financial documents shall be submitted one (1) week prior to the first election day as designated by the Supervisor of Elections, and shall also be included in the independent candidate or political party’s final expense statement. This shall be submitted on a form produced by the Supervisor of Elections. 

Campaign Contributions:

Political parties and candidates must be able to account for all contributions. The contribution shall be a part of the campaign contribution statement and final expense statement and must detail which individual or organization donated the campaign contribution. Registered Student Organizations (RSO), excluding SGA political parties, and SGA entities are prohibited from donating to SGA political parties or candidates in any SGA election.
No SGA entity may expend Activity and Service Fee funds, or funds derived from mandatory student fees, for the purpose of endorsing or opposing any candidate, political party, or ballot item. SGA entities shall be allowed to educate voters in a nonpartisan manner. Individual members, officers, and employees of SGA entities retain the right to engage in campaign financing in their personal capacity, using their personal resources and personal finances, regardless of their SGA affiliation.

Campaign finance obligations, including spending caps, expense reporting requirements, and contribution disclosure requirements, shall apply to expenditures and contributions made on or after 12:00 a.m. Eastern Time on the Monday one week prior to the date of the elections. 

In cases where campaign materials are sold (i.e. shirts, cups, etc.) to raise funds for a political party or candidate, individual records must be kept in accordance with Section 709(4)(a). Regardless of profit or involvement of campaign goods, anytime “Membership” is extended in return for dues or fees, the donating individual or organization must be recorded.

No money may be accepted by a campus political party or candidate from a 501(c)(4) organization as defined by Title 26 of the U.S. Internal Revenue Code. 

The campaign contribution limit of individual or organizational donors to a candidate or party shall be established as $200 per election cycle or per semester not containing a general election. 

Party-candidate membership dues submitted by an individual shall not exceed the campaign expense limits of the position the candidate is running for.

If an individual is donating as a proxy for someone who donated via a money transfer service such as Venmo, Zelle, CashApp, etc., receipts must be provided of the entire exchange.

If an individual is donating as a proxy for an organization, the entirety of the exchange should be documented.

sections.heading: Chapter 710 Violations And Penalties
sections.text:
Scope and Prosecution of Alleged Violations:

All candidates and political party members are bound by and may be prosecuted under this Code.

Conviction of any person for a violation under this Code shall not preclude subsequent prosecution or violation of the Ethics Codes or the Student Conduct Code.

The Attorney General shall represent the Supervisor of Elections in all proceedings of the Elections Commission and Supreme Court.
Any violation found valid that occurs during a non-election period shall accrue points towards the next election period.

Enforcement:

The Supervisor of Elections, Deputy Supervisors, Elections Assistants, and all members of the Elections Commission shall enforce the Election Code. Failure to enforce the Election Code shall be an impeachable offense.

Standing:

Students or political parties who show actual injury shall have standing to contest the results of any election on grounds within or outside the scope of the Election Code until forty-eight (48) hours following the close of the polls. 

Reporting Procedures:

All alleged violations shall be brought to the Supervisor of Elections in accordance with Section 703(2) of the Student Body Election Code, and must include: 

The name of the party or individual alleging the violation; 

The name of the party or individual who allegedly violated the Elections Code; 

The specific statute(s) in the Elections Code which was allegedly violated; 

Any and all evidence to support the claim of an alleged violation; and 

A short and plain statement describing the occurrence of the alleged violation. 

When an alleged violation is filed against an individual candidate, independent candidate, political party, or a member of a political party, the Supervisor of Elections shall notify the recipient(s) and listed witnesses of the alleged violation within twenty-four (24) hours after receiving the alleged violation. 

All students will have the option to present their case directly to the elections commission, choose a third-party to represent them, or be appointed a law student by the Supreme Court to represent their case before the Elections Commission. 

The Supervisor of Elections and Deputy Supervisor(s) shall have the power to receive and review alleged violations. The time, place, and manner of such violations shall be recorded and submitted to the Elections Commission. 

All alleged violations and appeals must be presented to the Supervisor of Elections electronically by the end of two (2) business days from their discovery.

Any complaint that lists an alleged violation after two (2) business days from its original discovery shall be dismissed by the Supervisor of Elections. 

The final deadline for all alleged violations and appeals to be filed by an individual or political party for a particular election is forty-eight (48) hours following the close of polls from an election, unless it alleges a failure to submit a complete or rectified final expense statement.

If an alleged violation is submitted less than twenty-four (24) hours before the deadline to submit alleged violations, the Supervisor of Elections shall be allowed to notify individuals of an alleged violation after the close of the filing deadline.
The final deadline for an alleged violation and appeal to be filed by an individual or political party alleging a failure to submit a complete or rectified final expense statement is the Wednesday following an election by 4 p.m.

Burden of Proof
The burden of proving an alleged violation of the Student Body Election Code shall rest at all times with the petitioner. 

The applicable standard of proof for all alleged Election Code violations shall be a "preponderance of the evidence," meaning that the existence of a fact is more likely true than not true. 

Procedural Protections for Schedule 4 Findings
A finding of responsibility for any Schedule 4 violation shall require the affirmative vote of no fewer than two-thirds (2/3) of the members of the Elections Commission present and voting.

Any disqualification imposed on the basis of a Schedule 4 violation shall be subject to automatic review by the Student Supreme Court, regardless of whether the respondent files an appeal under Chapter 711. 

Failure to satisfy the applicable burden shall result in dismissal of the alleged violation with prejudice for the current election cycle. 
Implementation of Violations:

Each occurrence, event, or time that violates the Election Code shall constitute an alleged Election violation that must be heard by the Elections Commission. Violations do not count against a candidate or political party until ruled upon by the Elections Commission.

In the event that a party found to be responsible by the Elections Commission appeals to the Student Supreme Court, the violation will not be counted until the Supreme Court issues their ruling. 

Disqualification shall occur according to the following provisions: 

Party Disqualification: 

A political party that has either been found guilty of a schedule 4 violation or has accumulated twenty-five (25) or more penalty points during a single election cycle shall be disqualified. A candidate or individual that has either been found guilty of a schedule 4 violation or has accumulated fifteen (15) or more penalty points during a single election cycle shall be disqualified.

In the case that a political party is disqualified, all candidates running in that election with that party shall become disqualified. Any candidate disqualified shall be barred from running for an elected office or being a member of a political party for one (1) election cycle following their disqualification.

The disqualified political party is barred from participating in future elections for a period of four (4) years.

All party officers and members of the party leadership board shall be barred from participating in student government elections as members of political parties or running for office for one (1) election cycle following their disqualification. 

Winning Candidate Disqualification: 

If a candidate who won an election is then disqualified, the Supervisor of Elections shall call a Special Election pursuant to Student Body Statute Section 705(2) for the office won by the disqualified candidate. 

Individual Disqualification: 

In the event of an individual disqualification, the candidate or individual is barred from running in an election or participating in any political party for one (1) election cycle following their disqualification. 

Special Election After Disqualification: 

If there is a special election following disqualification of a candidate or political party, the following rules will be obeyed: 

Inability to use the political party’s name or logo on campaign materials and during campaigning. 

Inability to use the party funds. 

A disqualified political party cannot endorse a candidate or candidates.
When an Election violation is alleged against a party as opposed to an individual, naming the party as the respondent, it must meet one or more of the following standards:
The violation is perpetrated by any person acting as an officer of a party.
The violation involved the collaboration of more than one member of the same party.
The violation is in a series of violations which constitute a systematic attempt by a party to violate the Elections Code.
The violation is part of a clear pattern of violations perpetrated by individuals internal to a party which represent systemic ignorance of the Elections Code.

Violations of the Code:

No violations will contest or come into contradiction with Section 710(4). 

If a candidate or political party is accused of any election violation and does not challenge the validity of the allegation, they may be eligible for a reduced punishment in exchange for an admission of guilt to the Elections Commission.

This section shall not apply if an individual, candidate, or political party is accused of a Schedule 3 Violation or Schedule 4 Violation. 

After admitting guilt to the Elections Commission, a respondent or petitioner cannot appeal the alleged violation to the Supreme Court.
The vice-chair of the Commission shall move to approve reduced punishments by acclimation unless any member of the Elections Commission objects. If an objection is raised, the reduced punishment must be approved by a majority vote of no less than quorum.
An individual, candidate, or political party may have up to three (3) punishments reduced per election cycle. Reduced punishments eliminate all points associated with a violation.

Schedule one (1) Violations of this Code shall be assigned as follows: 

Removing, obscuring, or damaging another candidate’s or political party’s campaign materials within a given space such as a bulletin board or general flyer area. 

Engaging in an action specified in Chapter 709 of Student Statutes to be a Schedule one (1) violation.

Using campaign materials which fail to comply with University regulations, building regulations, or fail to comply with such regulations in academic classrooms. 

Posting campaign materials in a manner that violates applicable university posting policies, including but not limited to policies administered by Campus Event Services, Facilities, or University Housing. 

Failing to remove campaign materials by the Friday following the designated election days, and campaign materials from previous election periods and preceding non-election periods that have failed to be removed. 

Submitting an incomplete Final Expense Statement, consistent with Section 709(2)(f). 

If an allegation of an incomplete final expense statement is made, the recipient shall have until the Tuesday following the election by 4 p.m. Eastern Time to correct any issues with the document. If all issues are not corrected by the following Tuesday at 4 p.m. Eastern Time this violation will turn into a Schedule 4 Violation. 

Schedule two (2) Violations of this Code shall be assigned as follows: 

Bringing false or malicious charges against another candidate, political party, or political member. 

Posting, utilizing, or distributing, either electronically or physically, campaign material containing a provably false statement of fact concerning an identified person, made with knowledge of its falsity or with reckless disregard for whether it was true or false, that causes demonstrable reputational harm. Statements of opinion, political rhetoric, satire, parody, hyperbole, and commentary on candidates' public records and policy positions do not constitute violations of this section. 

This shall apply to political party’s executive board members, candidates, and/or dues-paying members in the current semester. 

Defacing or damaging official election materials created and distributed by the Supervisor or Elections. 

Deliberately fabricating or manipulating evidence, communications, or circumstances with the specific intent to cause another party or candidate to be charged with or found responsible for a violation of this Code that the party or candidate would not otherwise have committed. 

Using the past and/or present SGA logo on campaign items. 

Utilizing any Student Government owned equipment for express endorsement or support for or against any candidate, platform, political party, or ballot item.
Campaigning physically or electronically using the funds or official institutional resources, platforms, or authority of an SGA entity.

Schedule three (3) Violations of this Code shall be assigned as follows: 

Vandalism or any unauthorized marking of university or private property for campaign purposes.

Falsely representing oneself on behalf of the Supervisor of Elections or the SGA Office of Elections.

Engaging in any action against Chapter 709 of the Election Code, unless otherwise specified.
Failing to appear at any elections commission hearing if listed as a petitioner without giving prior notice to the Supervisor of Elections, five (5) hours prior to the Elections Commission hearing, of inability to appear

Schedule four (4) Violations of this Code shall be assigned as follows: 

Submitting a fraudulent final expense statement. This includes parties or individuals failing to submit a complete final expense statement by the Tuesday following the election at 4 p.m. Eastern Time. 

This is an allegation that can only be made by the Supervisor of Elections and/or the Deputy Supervisors of Elections. 

Providing another individual or group with or receiving personal login information (FSU ID and password) in which they use to cast votes for another person. These votes shall be considered fraudulent. 

Any attempt to perpetrate a fraudulent election. This shall include, but is not limited to, providing false information regarding filing or elections procedures, voting more than once, or attempting to vote with another person’s student identification (FSU ID).

Offering money, gift cards, or other forms of payment in exchange for votes in any election.
Offering goods or services in exchange for votes, not including campaign materials as specified in Chapter 701 of the Election Code.

Further exceeding the non-election period spending limit after having already received a Schedule 3 violation.

Tabulation of Election Violations:

Violations shall be adjudicated by the appropriate body as they arise as much as reasonable efficiency will allow, but a decision to expel or disqualify a candidate from the ballot shall not be executed until after the final closing of the polls during a general election. 

Penalty Point System:

Penalty Points shall be assigned with each violation. The Elections Commission shall hold the discretion to reduce penalties. The vice-chair of the Elections Commission shall assign penalty points in full accordance with Chapter 710 when no reduction applies.

A political party that has either been found guilty of a schedule 4 violation or has accumulated twenty-five (25) or more penalty points during a single election cycle shal be disqualified by the Supervisor of Elections and the Elections Commission.
A candidate or individual that has either been found guilty of a schedule 4 violation or has accumulated fifteen (15) or more penalty points during a single election cycle shall be disqualified by the Supervisor of Elections and the Elections Commission.

Schedule One (1) Violation Penalties:

The following penalties shall be levied against those who have been found responsible for committing a Schedule One (1) violation: 

For the first instance of finding a Schedule One (1) Violation pursuant to the Elections Code, a one (1) point penalty shall be levied against an individual or political party.

For the second and any additional findings of a Schedule One (1) Violation, three (3) point penalty shall be levied against an individual or political party. 

Schedule Two (2) Violation Penalties:

The following penalties shall be levied against those who have been found responsible for committing a Schedule Two (2) violation: 

For the first instance of finding a Schedule Two (2) Violation, a three (3) point penalty shall be levied against an individual or political party.

For the second and any additional findings of a Schedule Two (2) Violation, a four (4) point penalty shall be levied against an individual or political party.

Schedule Three (3) Violation Penalties:

For all instances of finding a Schedule Three (3) Violation, a ten (10) point penalty shall be levied against an individual or political party.

Schedule Four (4) Violation Penalties:

Any person or political party found responsible for a Schedule Four (4) Violation shall be disqualified pursuant to Student Body Statute Section 710(5)(b). 

Additional Prosecution:

Conviction of any person for violations under this Code shall not preclude subsequent persecution of that person for violation of the Ethics Code, the Student Honor Code, or the Student Conduct Code.

sections.heading: Chapter 711 The Official Ballot
sections.text:
Ballot Form:
An electronic ballot shall be defined as the official format chosen by the Supervisor of Elections that shall include the official rules, instructions, candidates and other information pertinent to elections.
The official ballot contains the list of all offices to be elected, referendum questions, and constitutional amendments.
No colors shall be used to designate or accentuate any choices on the official ballot, including, but not limited to candidates for office, political party affiliation or lack thereof, referendum questions, and constitutional amendments.
Candidates shall be listed by seat in alphabetical order of their last names and the name shall be printed in the same form as requested at the time of filing. Each candidate’s last name shall appear on the ballot, and the name must be the same as it appears on the candidate’s my FSU account.
Candidates can request to have a different preferred first name on the ballot and can request to change their name up until twenty-four (24) hours before the election.
For the election of the Student Body President and Vice President, the names of the candidates for President and Vice President within the same party (if applicable) must appear on the ballot as one voting bloc.
For elections to office, the ballot of a general or special election shall only contain the names of candidate who:
Properly filed a Declaration of Candidacy with the Supervisor or Elections in accordance with Section 704(2) of the Student Body Statutes.
Are qualified to hold the office they seek as specified in Section 704(3) of the Student Body Statutes.
Candidates omitted from the ballot may petition to be reinstated by the Elections Commission and may be reinstated following an Elections Commission hearing no later than (3) business days prior to any election.
Party designation for candidates of recognized political parties who run in an election shall be placed on the official ballot.
The ballot may not be changed or altered within the twenty-four (24) hours preceding any election.
Statement of Intent:
All ballot questions proposing constitutional amendments and referenda shall display a “Statement of Intent” to be placed above the amendment or referenda text.
The Statement of Intent shall be no longer than one hundred (100) words.
The Statement of Intent shall be written by the primary sponsor of the produced constitutional amendment and/or the sponsor’s designee.
The Statement of Intent shall be presented to the Student Senate when the amendment is put up for Student Senate approval. The Statement of Intent shall be considered part of the piece of legislation being voted on for approval by the Senate and shall pass or fail jointly with its accompanying legislation.
The provisions of Section 711(2) apply to both measures proposed by the Senate and by the petition process as enumerated in Article VI of the Student Body Constitution.
The provisions of Section 711(2) shall not apply to any proposed constitutional amendment pending the ballot at the time of its enactment.
Counting of Ballots and Vote Tabulation:
The method of counting shall be done electronically. 
The Supervisor of Elections shall announce the complete "unofficial" results between 8pm and 11pm on the night of the election, in the Student Union, upon completion of tabulation.
In the event of an extended election as a result of an electronic failure, the Student Senate President may call a special Senate meeting the day of the extended election.

sections.heading: Chapter 712 Polls
sections.text:
Voting Process:
Voting shall take place entirely on an electronic poll accessible to the student body through the Student Government Elections Website on election day, which shall be a Monday and Tuesday of election week. The link to the poll shall be sent in an email to the entire student body the first and second day of the election when polls open at 8 a.m. Eastern Time.

In the event of any electronic failures or delays—whether as a single occurrence or the cumulative effect of multiple disruptions—that exceed two (2) hours in total during the designated voting period, the following provisions shall apply:

The Supervisor of Elections shall extend the election time from 9 a.m. to 2:30p.m. on an additional day (the next available business day). The Student Senate shall appropriate the necessary funds on the election day in question.

Notification of the extension shall be issued to the student body no later than 9:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the second day of the original election period (Tuesday).

Election results shall be announced no later than 11:00 p.m. Eastern Time on Thursday, marking the official end of the election period.

The Supervisor of Elections shall post a written memorandum on the Student Government Association website detailing the cause and nature of the failure or delay. This memorandum must be published within six (6) hours of the occurrence of the disruption.

Recall Elections:
An online electronic poll shall be open in the event of a recall election of the following officials: 

Student Body President

Student Body Vice President 

Student Body Treasurer 

Student Union Board Members 

Campus Recreation Board Members 

Senior Class Council Officers 

Student Senators
Registered Student Organization Allocation Committee Members 

Hours:
Online polls shall be open from 8:00 a.m. Eastern Time to 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time each day of the election.
The results of the election shall be announced by the Supervisor of Elections prior to 11:00PM on the second day of elections.

The method of announcement shall be up to the Supervisor of Elections’ discretion.
Results of the election shall be announced within twenty-four (24) hours of in person election results, via the SGA webmaster.
The Supervisor of Elections may extend poll hours for a period not to exceed two (2) hours. 

The Supervisor of Elections shall notify all parties, candidates, and individuals of the extension. 

Polling Rules:
No candidate nor person affiliated with a political party shall serve as an election official. 

When voting on the online poll, the student shall login using their FSU ID and password.

sections.heading: Chapter 713 Conditions For Victory
sections.text:
Votes Required for Victory:
All elected offices will be won by whoever attains a majority of the vote, unless a seat with three (3) or more candidates appear for a seat; then, ranked choice voting will be utilized, should technology permit.
In the event of a tie between two or more candidates, the Supervisor of Elections shall call a Special Election to determine the winner.
Ranked Choice Voting shall be used in any election for a Senate, Congress of Graduate Students, Union Board Campus Recreation Board, and any other ballot-assigned elected position where three (3) or more candidates appear for any individual seat, should technology permit.
Victory by Acclamation:
In the event of candidates or voting blocs running unopposed in any election at the deadline of declaration of candidacy filing, the candidates or voting blocs shall be declared the winner of the election.
