sections.heading: Chapter 714 Winners--Assuming Office
sections.text:
Announcement:

After the results have been verified by the Supervisor of Elections, the Supervisor of Elections shall release the final election results. 

All results and announcements of the unofficial and/or final election results may be challenged to the Elections Commission as specified in Section 703(2) of the Student Body Statutes. 

Certification of Election:

No Certificate of Election shall be issued to a candidate whose election is being contested. 

No candidates shall be installed, given the oath of office or take elective office unless a Certificate of Election has been authorized for that candidate by the Supervisor of Elections. This shall not apply to those candidates appointed to fill vacancies in accordance with the Student Body Constitution and Student Body Statutes. 

Certificates of Election shall be given to a candidate when the Supervisor of Elections certifies the election. Certification of an election shall occur by the Monday following the first meeting of the Elections Commission after the election, provided that the conditions for the Final Election Results are met. Should certification conditions not be met by the deadline, certification shall occur within twenty-four (24) hours of conditions being met.

Installation:

The Supervisor of Elections shall provide for appropriate installation ceremonies for duly elected candidates.

Any duly elected officers that are not in attendance of the formal installation ceremony shall be installed separately by the Student Senate within three (3) Senate meetings after the formal installation ceremonies. No elected official shall be sworn in before the formal ceremony. 

If a duly elected officer misses the formal installation ceremony and is not sworn in by the Student Senate, the duly elected officer shall immediately vacate the office in question. 

Newly elected officers shall assume office immediately upon installation by the Supervisor of Elections.

Installation ceremonies for those elected shall be held between two (2) and five (5) weeks after the conclusion of an election.

Unless there are enough election violations filed to disqualify a candidate or political party, the date and time of Inauguration for the Spring and Fall General Elections shall not be impacted by election violations or appeals.

sections.heading: Chapter 800 Purpose, Scope, And Definitions
sections.text:
The Finance Code defines the standards of financial accountability and fiscal management that the Student Government Association (SGA) has established as objectives of self-governance.

The Finance Code governs the budgeting and expenditure of all of the following:

A&S funds allocated to SGA branches, offices, agencies, institutes, affiliated projects, and Recognized Student Organizations, including those cases where money was distributed through the fund distribution committees.

A&S funds spent directly on student activities and/or events by Student Senate.

All revenue generated through the use of A&S funds, as per Chapter 804 of these Statutes.

Definitions:
Printed Materials: Printed materials shall be defined as flyers, posters, pamphlets, banners, signs, advertisements, T-shirts and any other promotional materials. Web-based material will be subject to the same (applicable) provisions as all other printed material.

Expenditure: The purchase of items or services.

Transfer: A transfer shall be defined as the moving of funds from one budgetary category to another.

Stewards of the Finance Code: 
The Senate Finance Committee is assigned responsibility for oversight, review, and periodic update of the policies expressed in the Finance Code. The Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy is responsible for assuring that the Finance Code is fully implemented. The Student Body Treasurer is responsible for approval or rejection of all expenditures of all A&S recipients (excluding the Union, Campus Recreation, and COGS).

The Student Body Treasurer:
The Student Body Treasurer is responsible for the approval or rejection of all A&S expenditures requested by branches, offices, agencies, institutes, affiliated projects, and Recognized Student Organizations. Graduate RSOs shall have their expenditures approved by the COGS Financial Officer or COGS Speaker in lieu of the Student Body Treasurer.

The Student Body Treasurer may reject expenditures that the Treasurer deems fiscally irresponsible. Reasons for rejection include, but are not limited to:

Any expenditure that is deemed irresponsible, excessive, or unnecessary.

Any expenditure that violates conditions of the Student Body Finance Code.

Any expenditure requested primarily for the purpose of circumventing the RSO Budget Fund process.

Any expenditure rejected by the Student Body Treasurer may be appealed to the Student Body President. Rejected expenditures may also be appealed to the Senate Finance Committee or the Student Senate, either of which may overturn the decision by a two-thirds (2/3) vote. Any expenditure rejected by the COGS Financial Officer or COGS Speaker may be appealed to the COGS General Body. Any expenditure appeal rejected by the COGS General Body may be appealed to the Student Body Treasurer.

In order for the Student Senate to hear the appeal of a rejected expenditure, the item must first be placed on the calendar (under New Business) by the Rules & Calendar Committee. The Senate President must then attempt to notify the Student Body Treasurer and the President of the entity whose expenditure was rejected.

If the appeal of a rejected expenditure is to be heard by the Senate Finance Committee, then the Student Body Treasurer and the President of the entity whose expenditure was rejected must be notified prior to the meeting.

In the event that the Treasurer is not available to approve or reject a requested expenditure within two (2) business days of its submission to the SGA Accounting Office, the Student Body President or Vice President shall have the power to approve or reject the expenditure. If the request is rejected in this manner, the appeal mechanism outlined in Section 800(5)(c) shall still apply.

The director or financial officer of any agency, institute, affiliated project, or funding board must meet with the Student Body Treasurer or a designee, who, is financially certified through the SGA Accounting Office, to address financial concerns, upon request of the Student Body Treasurer.

The Student Body Treasurer shall compile a list of all expenditures that the Student Body Treasurer signs, approve, or rejects. A copy of this list shall be forwarded to the SGA Accounting Office, the Student Senate President, the Senate Finance Committee, and all parties who request a copy from the Student Body Treasurer’s office. This list of expenditures shall be sent to the Student Senate and the Senate Finance Committee by the first of each month.

sections.heading: Chapter 801 Eligibility Requirements For SGA Funding And Spending
sections.text:
Organizations must either be recognized by the University or affiliated with Student Government Association to receive or expend A&S fees.

Student organizations must have both an on-campus mailing address and an account with the SGA Accounting and Advising Office (except RSOs under the Sports Club Council, which must have an account with the Campus Recreation Accounting Office).

The Director/President and Financial Officer/Treasurer of each SGA-funded organization, agency, institute, executive institute and affiliated project, shall be required to complete the online Financial Training Workshop prior to expending funds and receive Financial Certification status from the SGA Accounting Office.

Counter-signing Requirements:
All SGA-funded entities are required to elect, have appointed, or otherwise select a financial officer (who is to be the designated custodian of the account) and a president to counter-sign for all expenditures.

In addition to the organizational co-signatures and the signature of the Student Body Treasurer, all expenditures must have the signature of the Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy, or a designee.

The Statement of Understanding: Each A&S funded entity shall be required to have its President/Director and Treasurer/Financial Officer co-sign this statement of understanding, which will be retained in the SGA Accounting and Advising Office before any expenditures may be made by the entity. The Statement of Understanding shall read:

“The undersigned herein designated as (name of office held or name of organization) fully understands the Student Government Finance Code, which applies to all funds allocated by Student Government. Furthermore, the undersigned agrees to abide by all policies and procedures for expending such funds. Finally, the undersigned understands that any violation of the Finance Code will be prosecuted to the full extent of the law.”

FSU Student Membership Requirements:
For a Recognized Student Organization to be eligible to receive funds, all officers of that organization and a majority of its membership must be A&S Fee paying students at Florida State University.

All RSOs within the FAMU/FSU College of Engineering are exempt from Section 801(6)(a). Each organization which falls under this category must designate a financial officer who is an A&S Fee paying student at Florida State University to serve as custodian of the accounts and to ensure funds received from FSU are only distributed to A&S Fee paying students of Florida State University.

Recognized Student Organizations must keep accurate and complete membership rosters, and provide these records to University officials upon request.
Registered Student Organizations that qualify for COGS funding and receive funds from COGS, or any COGS funding boards, shall only be eligible to receive SGA funding through COGS and COGS funding boards for the remainder of the fiscal year the funding was accepted in. Registered Student Organizations that qualify for COGS funding and receive funds from the Student Senate, or any Senate funding boards, shall only be eligible to receive SGA funding through the Senate and Senate funding boards for the remainder of the fiscal year the funding was accepted in.
“Senate funding boards” include, but are not limited to: the RSO Allocation Committee and the College Leadership Council Funding Board.
“COGS funding boards” include, but are not limited to, LSC and MSC.
Funds received from the Campus Advancement and Development Fund shall not be considered funds of the Senate, for the purposes of this section.

sections.heading: Chapter 802 General Guidelines And Restrictions On Expenditures
sections.text:
The A&S Fee Guidelines were promulgated jointly by the Student Government Association and Florida State University. The allocation and expenditure policies and procedures contained in the A&S Fee Guidelines are obligatory upon Student Government Association.

Activities funded must not conflict with the purpose or regulations of the Florida State University, Board of Trustees policies, or state and federal laws.

No A&S monies shall be dispersed to pay for previous expenditures without prior approval. SGA shall only be obligated to pay where a legitimate purchase order has been properly issued, or other paperwork as designated by the SGA Accounting Office. This clause may be waived by an appeal in the form of a resolution to the Senate Finance Committee. The appeal must include a letter of explanation as to why the expense did not receive pre-approval as well as the financial statement and expense reports from the event. A representative for the organization requesting the appeal must be present. The appeal must pass the Finance Committee by three-fourths (3/4) and receive a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Student Senate. Should either vote fail, SGA shall not be liable for the expense.

SGA shall not fund any item pertaining to an event or travel in the past including, but not limited to: clothing, awards, and promotional items. The selection process for any awards paid for by A&S monies must occur after the initial request presentation, and the recipient must be notified that their award was paid for by SGA.

Accessibility of Meetings & Events: Exempting SGA-sponsored concerts, no FSU student shall be charged admission for any event funded in whole or in part by A&S monies, unless the student is unable or unwilling to provide proof of studentship that shall include, but not be limited to, their valid FSU ID. All SGA-funded events and meetings must also be well publicized and conducted in an environment that is generally accessible to the public.

No event or meeting at which A&S Fees are utilized may be conducted in a private residence. This includes, but is not limited to, apartments, homes, and condominiums. This does not apply to community clubhouses. Exceptions to this rule shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

Evidence of an adequate advertisement plan of A&S Fee utilizing meetings and events must be presented at the time the expenditure is initially presented to the Student Body Treasurer. Failure to properly promote an event is grounds for rejection of all expenditures associated with the event.

SGA-sponsored concerts shall include Headliners concerts, Homecoming Live, and any other concerts that attain the sponsorship of SGA via Senate resolution. Such concerts must have their ticket prices approved by Senate through resolution.

Events should be held on campus if appropriate accommodations on campus are available. Agencies, affiliated projects, and SGA offices must have off-campus events approved via a resolution of the Student Senate. Funding for undergraduate RSOs to host events off campus shall require a majority vote of approval by the RSO Allocation Committee and the Student Senate. Graduate RSOs must have approval as outlined in the COGS Code.

Limitation on Outside (Non-FSU) Benefits:

Funds may not be expended to support a candidate for political office, nor for contribution to political activity directly seeking to affect the passage, defeat, or status of any legislation except as provided by Florida Law. This statute shall by no means be interpreted as restricting the lobbying efforts of the Student Body President, Student Senate, or the Office of Governmental Affairs.

Items/services purchased with A&S money may not be used for the primary benefit of community programs outside of FSU, or for donations to such programs. This provision shall not be construed so as to prevent organizations from receiving funding as outlined in Chapter 810 of the Student Body Statutes.

All events funded in whole or in part with A&S money must provide priority admissions to current Florida State University students.

Student Groups affiliated with national political parties or supporting/advocating a national, state, city, and county political agenda may request money from Student Government Association for awareness of their RSO on campus. RSO events, spreading messages and ideologies of their RSO on campus, and for travel to advance their RSO’s mission at Florida State University. A&S Fees shall not be used to: endorse a political candidate on or off campus or advance political messages and ideologies off-campus.

Religious based student groups may receive funding for awareness/advertising of their RSO on campus, RSO events, and travel that advances their mission at Florida State University. Funding for proselytizing is prohibited. Religious based organizations providing service are exempt from being registered as a service organization. Religious groups can request money for service projects or service travel, but must not proselytize their religion. Religious topics or lectures may be offered during travel or events; however, if requested by a participant, an alternate activity must be arranged.

Acknowledgment of SGA Funding:

All online and printed materials purchased or manufactured with A&S Fees must include the FSU SGA logo, or the logo of the SGA-budgeted entity purchasing the item(s). On printed materials, the SGA logo shall be no less than 1/30 of the size of the area in which the logo is placed on materials not advertising a specific event, the logo may be substituted with the words “Paid for by SGA” or “Paid for by Student Government Association” in clearly visible font. One of the following areas on printed materials must be used to meet the logo requirement:

On the front of posters and flyers

On the front or back cover of pamphlets and other publications

Inside the front cover of publications

On either the front or the back of t-shirts or tank tops.

All audio and video advertising funded by non SGA-budgeted entities in whole or in part with A&S Fees shall publicly acknowledge SGA funding by including the statement “Paid for by FSU SGA” or “Funded in part by FSU SGA”. Classified advertisements must either include the FSU Student Government logo or the words "Paid for by FSU  SGA.”

Any printed materials sponsored by an A&S recipient must include the name of recipient.

All printed materials and broadcasts expressing a political message must also include, with the SGA logo: "The views expressed herein do not necessarily reflect those of the FSU Student Government Association."

No personal gifts may be purchased with A&S money. Items given for recognition may only be funded from the Clothing & Awards Category.

Alcohol may not be purchased with A&S monies, either specifically or as part of a facility rental agreement or any other package.

Disposable plastic water bottles and disposable plastic straws may not be purchased with A&S monies. In lieu of disposable plastic water bottles, RSO may not purchase other environmentally harmful materials such as Styrofoam.

In the case of a natural disaster or any other unforeseen emergency in which sustainable methods of water distribution are hindered, plastic water bottles may be purchased without a vote of the RSOAC or Finance.

This section may additionally be waived by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the RSOAC for RSOs.
SGA entities may seek an exemption from this waiver for specific events or broad operations by notifying the Chair of the Finance Committee, who shall place the request on the agenda and conduct a hearing on the request. All requests must pass by a two-thirds (2/3) vote.

No weapons may be purchased with A&S monies. This includes firearms, destructive devices, or other dangerous articles or substances, including but not limited to, pellet guns, bb guns, paintball markers, slingshots, crossbows, stun guns, Tasers, metallic knuckles, archery equipment, or any dangerous chemical or biological agents. This section shall not apply to the funding of organizations that utilize these items for the purpose of sport under the purview of Campus Recreation, however Campus Recreation must have policies in place around the purchase and use of their firearms and weapons.

Any organization that has property stolen must file a report with the FSU Police Department or Tallahassee Police Department. No transfer or allocation for the purpose of replacing said goods may be passed without such a report.

The Executive Projects Account and the Student Government Association Golden Torch Lecture Series Account may use the lump sum of funds in the expense account for any purpose.

All receipts must be turned in within ten (10) business days to the SGA Accounting Office or the organization’s future requisitions will not be approved until past receipts are turned in.

sections.heading: Chapter 803 SGA Budgetary Categories And Categorical Restrictions
sections.text:
All SGA-funded entities shall be funded in seven (7) budgetary categories. The seven (7) categories shall be: 

Salary, OPS Wages, Contractual Services, Expense, Food, Clothing & Awards, and Other Capital Outlay.

Transfer Requirements:
SGA branches, offices, agencies, institutes, affiliated projects, and recognized student organizations which are allocated A&S monies may only transfer A&S money between budgetary categories through the passage of a resolution. Such transfers shall also require the consent of the Director or chief executive of the entity within which the funds are being transferred.

Fund Distribution Committee Procedures with Regard to Categories: The Student Senate shall appropriate the entirety of all allocations to fund distribution committees in block in the Expense category, from which each fund distribution committee will have the authority to distribute those funds to its constituent RSOs among the Contractual Services, Expense, Food, and Clothing & Awards categories.

These allocations from block Expense to other categories shall not be considered transfers.

No allocation may be made to or by fund distribution committee in the Other Capital Outlay category.

The Salary Category: The Salary category shall be used to fund wages and benefits for staff positions. This category does not cover elected or appointed student positions.

The creation of new Salary positions must be done through the annual budget process.

Salaried positions may only be removed, or decreased in wages/benefits in a manner consistent with federal and state law and university policy.

The OPS Wages Category: The OPS Wages category shall be used to fund wages for elected and appointed student positions. All OPS paid positions shall be held by persons currently enrolled at FSU, unless otherwise specified in these Statutes.

Wages may only be drawn from this account in the manner explicitly stated by the Student Senate in the proviso language of the annual budget. Money may not be redistributed within the category except as stipulated in Section 803(5)(b).

Changes in the manner in which an SGA-funded entity distributes its wages (i.e., creating or removing an OPS paid position, increasing or decreasing the hours/week of a current OPS paid position, or increasing/decreasing the hourly wage of an OPS paid position) must be approved by the Student Senate through resolution. This resolution must first be referred to, and passed by majority vote, the Senate Finance committee.

Cases in which raises in the state or federally mandated minimum wage necessitate the increase of hourly wages may be handled immediately by the SGA Accounting Office, and are not held to the provisions of Section 803(5)(b).

No currently filled OPS paid position may be decreased in paid hours/week or hourly wages without the approval of the individual whose wages are being lowered. This is to protect OPS paid officials from circumvention of the impeachment and executive removal proceedings.

All OPS paid positions must be advertised for a minimum of two (2) weeks prior to being filled. A job description must be put on file with the SGA Administrative Assistant prior to any position drawing OPS wages.

RSOs shall not receive or distribute OPS Wages.

The Contractual Services Category: The Contractual Services category shall be used to pay for services rendered by contractually bound speakers, entertainers, or bands.

Any transfer within an SGA branch, office, agency, institute, or affiliated project from Contractual Services to any other category requires a three-fourth (3/4) vote of Student Senate to pass.

All contractual expenditures in excess of $3,000 require the approval of Senate by resolution. If the contractual expenditure is $10,000 or more, a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate is required for approval of the resolution. If the planned price-per-capita for students is to be one hundred ($100) or more, the Finance Committee must approve the resolution by a three-fourths (3/4) vote prior to Senate approval, where two-thirds (2/3) is needed.

The Food Category: The Food Category shall be used to pay for food for general meetings, presentations, banquets, and other public, publicized, free-admission events sponsored by SGA-funded entities. Such expenditures may include, but are not limited to: groceries, delivered food, and catered buffets.
No SGA branch, office, agency, institute, or affiliated project shall be allocated more than fifteen percent (15%) of its annual budget in the Food category.

No more than fifteen percent (15%) total of the annual RSO Budget Fund bill may be allocated to the Food category.

No Allocation Committee shall allocate more than twenty-five percent (25%) of its budget to the Food category.

Any transfer within an SGA branch, office, agency, institute, or affiliated project to the Food category from any other category shall require a 3/4 vote of Senate to pass.

Any allocation from Senate Projects to the Food category of any entity shall require a 3/4 vote of Senate.

Food may not be purchased for Executive Board meetings, or any meeting or event with an expected attendance of fewer than 15 FSU students.

No A&S monies shall be spent on plated dinners. This rule may be waived by a two third (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

The Clothing & Awards Category: The Clothing & Awards Category shall be used to pay for clothing (t-shirts and polo shirts) for the purpose of promoting an SGA-funded entity or event, and awards (trophies, plaques, and certificates) for the purpose of recognizing an individual or group.

Clothing shall be restricted to T-shirts, tank tops hoodies, sweatshirts, hats, and polo shirts, unless otherwise approved by a three-fourth (3/4) vote of the Senate Finance Committee.

Clothing must be made available free of charge to all FSU members of the entity purchasing them. There shall be no separate Executive Board clothing. Executive Board clothing can be waived in the form of a resolution with approval by a three-fourths (3/4) vote of the Senate Finance Committee and a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.

A proof of the clothing item clearly depicting the front and back of the item and including the acknowledgement of SGA funding (as per Section 802(6)), must be submitted to the Student Body Treasurer at the same time as the expenditure.

No obscene, inappropriate, or offensive images or text may be displayed on any clothing purchased in whole or in part with A&S funds.

Allocation Committees shall not fund more than $10 per clothing item in sizes small through extra-large and $12 per clothing item for sizes extra-extra-large and above. Senate may waive this clause with a two-thirds (2/3) vote on the floor.

Awards shall be restricted to trophies, plaques, and certificates.

The way the recipient of any award was (or will be) decided must be submitted to the Student Body Treasurer at the same time as the expenditure. Under no circumstances may this category be used to purchase personal gifts.

Any single award costing in excess of $75 shall require the approval of the Senate Finance Committee by majority vote.

The Other Capital Outlay (OCO) Category: The OCO Category shall be used to pay for items costing in excess of $5,000 and with a life expectancy of at least a year.

All money budgeted to the OCO category in the annual Budget bill must have attached proviso language explicitly stating the purpose of the funds. All appropriations from Senate Projects into this category must be preceded by a resolution explicitly stating the purpose of the funds.

Inventory of all items purchased from this category must be maintained by both the organization and the SGA Administrative Office.

The Expense Category: The Expense Category shall be used to pay for items, such as office supplies, nametags, printing, postage fees, telephone charges, and facility rentals, which do not fall under any other category. This account also covers all costs associated with student travel. SGA will fund, either directly or through reimbursement, airfare, rental car(s), gas mileage, and lodging. Student organizations shall not be funded for meals or limited incidental expenses.

Guidelines on Items & Purchases:
No gift cards, gift certificates, phone cards, or other transferable purchases may be made with A&S money.

Office supplies purchased from this category must be limited to those with a clear purpose furthering that entity’s operation and function. Decorative or unnecessary office items may not be purchased with A&S money.

No obscene, inappropriate, or offensive images or text may be displayed on any printed material purchased in whole or in part with A&S funds.

Postage must be budgeted by the account needing postal service. Metered mail service may be obtained from the FSU Post Office with an FSU Postal Charge Form. Postage stamps shall not be purchased.

SGA Travel Guidelines:
Travel expenses may only be incurred in the performance of official duties of the Florida State University Student Body.

Only current FSU students and approved organizational advisors may be remitted money for travel.

Travel expenses must be requested and approved via the Travel Authorization Request (TAR) form. All foreseeable expenses must be requested in advance, as any deviation from the initial requests is subject to review and possible rejection by the Student Body Treasurer.

The Student Body Treasurer shall have the authority to only partially fund travel expenses that the Student Body Treasurer deems unreasonable, provided such expenses were not approved prior to the travel. If the Student Body Treasurer is a beneficiary of any travel expense, the Senate Finance Committee shall review the expense before the trip and approve by majority vote the expenditures. By majority vote, the Finance Committee can partially fund as well as reject the travel expenditures in which the Treasurer benefits. An appeal of the Finance Committee’s decision shall be heard by the Student Senate under “New Business” with a majority vote required to overturn the Finance Committee’s decision.

A roster with the names and emergency contact information of all individuals travelling must be provided to the SGA Accounting Office prior to departure.

SGA will fund, either directly or through reimbursement, airfare, rental car(s), gas mileage, lodging, meals, conference fees, and limited incidental expenses.

Airfare must be purchased at the lowest possible price, and must be coach/tourist class seating. The Student Body Treasurer may reject large expenditures for airfare if the tickets were purchased less than two (2) weeks in advance, even if the purchased tickets were the cheapest available at the time of purchase.

Rental cars must be purchased through the University’s contracted rental company. Students may also choose to use their private vehicles and be reimbursed for gas mileage. Mileage will be reimbursed in a manner consistent with federal, state, and university standards. If mileage is to be incurred above the initially requested and approved figure (on the TAR), then all fuel expenses must be documented with receipts.

Lodging accommodations must be made at the lowest possible cost. Groups shall stay four (4) to a room unless prevented from doing so by fire code and/or co-ed issues. Hotel charges shall not exceed $300 per room per night (excluding tax).

Travelers have the option of being reimbursed at the government per diem rate of $80 per day in lieu of claiming lodging and meal expenses. This shall only apply in cases where SGA did not fund any lodging for the organization.

Incidental expenses shall be limited to those absolutely necessary for travel, such as road tolls, parking fees, and other associated costs.

All groups and individuals traveling must retain (until reimbursement) original receipts of all expenses for which they intend to be reimbursed. Travelers will only be reimbursed for expenses incurred and justified with receipts, with the exception of gas (Section 803(10)(b)(6)(B)) and per diem (Section 803(10)(b)(6)(E)).

sections.heading: Chapter 804 Self-Generated Funds
sections.text:
Delineation of Self-Generated vs. A&S Generated Funds: 
Money accrued by SGA-funded entities through such activities as fundraising, the collection of dues, the receipt of outside donations, and profit-generating ventures (e.g., charging event admission to non-FSU students) shall be considered Self-Generated provided that:
The money is not Activities & Services Fees.
The money was not earned at an event or in a manner that utilized any A&S fees.

In the case of non-A&S money generated at an event (or in a manner) utilizing A&S fees, all money yielded, up to the amount of the initial A&S expenditure, must be placed back into the appropriate category (or categories) from which the A&S money was initially expended. These funds shall not be considered self-generated, and shall be held to all the applicable restrictions (both general and category-specific) of A&S fees, including those outlined in this Finance Code.

If funds are generated in excess of the amount of the initial expenditure of A&S money, the excess shall be considered Self-Generated money. In this case, such funds must be kept in the entity’s on-campus account with the SGA Accounting Office.

Decisions over what constitutes money generated “at an event (or in a manner) utilizing A&S fees” shall be made by the Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy, who is encouraged to consult the Senate Finance Committee in ambiguous situations.

Money shall not be considered to have been generated by utilizing A&S funds simply by virtue of being collected in A&S funded reservable space.

Membership dues shall never be considered to have been generated through investment of A&S money, except under exceptional circumstances which must be approved by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate Finance Committee.

Self-Generated money may be kept in the entity’s on-campus account with SGA Accounting Office or off-campus at a private bank or other institution (except as specified in Section 804(1)(b)).

Self-Generated money is not subject to the provisions of the Finance Code, and expenditures from the (on-campus account) Self-Generated category shall not require the approval of the Student Body Treasurer or any other SGA official. While such spending need not be publicly advertised, neither shall there be any guarantee of confidentiality.

Under no circumstances may FSU students be charged admission to any event funded with any A&S money (excluding SGA-sponsored concerts, which are held to the provisions of Section 804(1)(a)). No FSU student may be denied membership to any SGA-funded organization purely because of their inability to pay dues.

sections.heading: Chapter 805 Penalties For Misspent Funds And Violations Of The Finance Code
sections.text:
Purview: All SGA funded entities, excluding the Union, Campus Recreation, the Student Senate, the Executive Branch (excepting all financially distinct offices), the Elections Office, and the Judicial Branch are subject to the provisions and penalties of Chapter 805 of the Finance Code. The aforementioned exempted entities may not be directly sanctioned, but violations and other irresponsible spending may be taken into account in subsequent allocations proceedings, and also may be grounds for impeachment. The Senate Finance Committee shall take the lead for all investigations as well as all mid-year reviews of any A&S Fee recipient (with the Budget Committee assisting for the mid-year reviews).

Causes for Sanction: Entities may be subjected to the sanctions outlined in Section 805(3) for any of the following reasons, with severe and/or repeated incidents being taken into particular consideration:

Violating any condition(s) of the Finance Code.

Expending A&S money in a manner inconsistent with the request presented to and approved by the Student Body Treasurer (or, if initially rejected by the Treasurer, the Student Body President, the Senate, or the Senate Finance Committee).

Expending A&S money on items or services that are irresponsible and/or do not serve the entity’s mission or the Student Body.

Exhibiting a pattern of reckless or irresponsible spending, even if expenditures are deemed suitable on an individual basis, that places the entity in either a deficit or such a precarious budgetary situation that the future fiscal welfare of the entity is placed in jeopardy.

Entering into a preemptive or unauthorized contractual agreement.

Any situation where there is serious and justified concern that the President/Director and/or Treasurer/Financial Officer may be removed from office in the immediate future.

Sanctions:
Freezing of Funds: An entity whose funds are frozen may make no expenditures for the (pre-specified) duration of the freeze, which may not exceed ten (10) business days. Previously approved expenditures will be voided unless (1) the purchase order has already been conferred or (2) the Student Body Treasurer consents to the processing of the expenditure.

Restriction of Funds: An entity may have its future expenditures restricted to only those pre-specified expenses deemed essential to the entity’s operation. This sanction may only take place after an organization’s funds have been frozen, and shall apply for an indefinite period of time (until the sanction is explicitly lifted). Such restrictions must be explicitly stated at the time of restriction, and must be limited to one, or a combination of, the following:

The prohibition of expenditures from a particular category or categories (including, if desired, all categories).

The specific enumeration of allowable expenditures, including ranges for dates of purchase, cost, and descriptions of the items/services to be purchased.

The requirement that the Senate Finance Committee approve all expenditures not specified in Subsection (2) (directly above).

Any entity whose funds are frozen or restricted must have its Treasurer/Financial Officer (or designee) make presentations to the Student Body Treasurer (or designee) and the Senate Finance Committee. These presentations shall be scheduled at the behest of the Treasurer and the Senate Finance Chair, respectively, and neither individual shall mandate more than two presentations per any 30-day period (unless consented to by the entity’s Treasurer/Financial Officer).

Authority to Instate, Appeal, and Repeal Sanctions:
Freezing Funds: Any entity’s funds may be frozen by the Student Senate, the Senate Finance Committee, the Student Body President, or the Student Body Treasurer.

The decision of the Student Body President or Treasurer to freeze funds may be overturned by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

The Senate Finance Committee’s decision, which is made by majority vote, may be overturned by a mutual agreement of the Student Body President and Treasurer or two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

The Senate’s decision, which is made by majority vote, may be overturned by mutual agreement of the Student Body President and Treasurer. It may then be reinstated by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Student Senate.

The party initiating the freeze may rescind it at any time.

Restricting Funds: At the end of the freeze period, if the problems inciting the initial freeze have not been rectified, another freeze period may be initiated by any of the procedures outlined in Section 805(4)(a). Provided the initial freeze period was for at least three (3) business days, SGA may alternatively choose to restrict the entity’s funds indefinitely in the following manner:

A resolution, initiating in the Senate Finance Committee (and passing by majority vote), is passed by the Student Senate, explicitly outlining the terms of the restriction as per Section 805(3)(b). This resolution must pass the Senate with a two-thirds (2/3) vote.

These restrictions may be subsequently amended or repealed by resolution, which must also initiate in the Senate Finance Committee (and pass with majority vote) and pass the Senate with a two-thirds (2/3) vote. This process notwithstanding restrictions of funds shall only expire at the end of the fiscal year when accounts are swept.

sections.heading: Chapter 806 Funding Boards
sections.text:
Title and Purpose:

Title: This act shall be known as the Allocation Committee Act.

Purpose:

An Allocation Committee shall be defined as any Funding Board or Fund Distribution Committee outlined in Section 806(1)(b)(2) and/or (3).

This Act shall apply to the following Funding Boards: the RSO Allocation Committee (RSOAC), Law School Appropriations Council (LSAC), Sports Club Distribution Council (SCDC), and Medical School Council (MSC).

Compliance with the A&S Guidelines:

The Student Body Treasurer and the SGA Advisor shall have the responsibility and oversight of the Allocation Committee for purposes of enforcing the Finance Code and Student Body Statutes.

Procedures and Requirements to Receive Funds:

To receive funds an organization must officially be registered with the Office of Student Organizations and Involvement.

Organizations must become re-registered each academic year to continue eligibility requirements.

The President/Director and Treasurer/Financial Officer of each organization shall be required to be financially certified.

Any registered organization must first approach the appropriate Fund Distribution Committee or Funding Board for each and every funding request.

Use of Funds:

Registered Student Organizations that charge membership fees may not exclude any students from membership solely because of their inability to pay dues.

Registered Student Organizations may not charge admission fees to FSU students for any event subsidized or paid for by student A&S Fees allocated to them.

All monies shall be spent in accordance with the Finance Code and A&S Fee Guidelines.

Allocation Procedures: The following guidelines shall apply to all Allocation Committees:

The registered student organizations requesting funds must submit a request to the Chair of the particular Allocation Committee.

The approval of funds shall be approved by not less than a majority of the Allocation Committee’s membership, where quorum is present.

For any group to apply for funding in front of an Allocation Committee, the student organization must have completed the registration process as outlined by the Office of Student Organizations and Involvement for each academic year.

sections.heading: Chapter 807 Operation Procedures
sections.text:
Allocation Procedures for Funding Boards:

Purpose: The following statutes shall serve as the minimum standard for all Funding Boards to receive allocations in the annual budget. Failure to comply with the guidelines will result in actions in accordance with Chapter 805 of the Finance Code. Chapter 806 will take precedence in the event of any contradiction or discrepancy between Chapter 806 and Chapter 807.

Powers and Duties:

All funding boards shall prepare an annual budget for its respective recognized student organizations (RSOs).

These budgets shall be sent to the Student Body Treasurer, the Senate Finance Committee, and the Senate Budget Committee. The RSO Allocation Committee is exempt from this requirement.

Shall act as the official representative for all member RSOs at all Senate or COGS allocation hearings.

Public allocation hearings shall occur at least once per fiscal year. Hearings shall follow the procedures in Section 807(1)(c) of the Student Body Statutes.

Shall adhere to or exceed all statutory regulations as specified by Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statutes.

Shall be responsible to ensure compliance of all its respective RSOs with Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statutes.

Sports Club Distribution Council shall have the powers to create an “unallocated” account for the purpose of emergency funding hearings. If a Board holds allocations annually, this account may not exceed ten percent (10%) of the total allocated monies each fiscal year. If a Board holds allocation hearings more frequently, the amount unallocated may be no greater than an even distribution between standard allocation periods. This provision may be overridden via resolution of the Student Senate.

Sports Club Distribution Council shall be authorized to create an Administration Expense Account not to exceed 1.5 % of the aggregate funding board budget, which is to be used only for expense items and shall not be subject to transfer from the unallocated account authorized in Section 807(1)(b)(6).

No funding board shall allocate or fund any amount in the OCO category, absent Senate or COGS approval by resolution. This provision shall not be construed so as to prevent the Senate from doing so at any time.

Hearing and Deliberation Procedures:

Hearings shall be conducted to inform the committee of the respective RSOs’ budget requests.

The hearings and deliberations shall be public and advertised to the respective RSOs, the general student body, the Student Senate President, the Student Body Treasurer, and COGS.

The respective RSOs shall request money in the categories as outlined in Section 803(1).

Funding Boards shall design funding guidelines that must be approved by a majority vote of the Funding Board, a majority vote of the Senate Finance Committee, and by resolution of the Student Senate.

LSAC and MSC guidelines shall be approved by a majority vote of COGS.

SCDC funding guidelines must be approved by a majority vote of the Senate Finance Committee, and by resolution of Senate.

The Chair of the Senate Finance Committee shall submit a resolution for the approval of the guidelines to the Student Senate no more than two (2) weeks after the approval in Committee.

The resolution shall be referred to the Finance Committee. The Finance Committee shall ensure the guidelines’ compliance with Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statutes.

A simple majority is required to amend either the resolution or the guidelines in both committee and Senate.

Substantial (not grammatical or timeline) changes must also be approved in the same manner.

Allocations requests shall be submitted before the beginning of hearings. Late allocation requests shall not be accepted without a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the committee. This shall not preclude emergency funding requests.

Deliberations shall consist of the allocation of A&S Fees to RSOs that requested money.

Hearings and deliberations may be conducted as often as any Funding Board sees fit; however, hearings and deliberations must occur at least once per fiscal year to receive any funding.

Each funding board shall report periodically to the Senate Finance Committee and annually to the Senate Budget Committee as to its current fiscal state.

Law School Council and Medical School Council: 
These two funding boards shall adhere to the COGS Guidelines and follow COGS fund allocation process.

Sport Club Distribution Council:

Purpose: The Sport Club Distribution Council (SCDC) shall represent the registered organizations under Campus Recreation, that are designated as "sports" before all budgetary committees of the Student Government Association and shall serve in sub-appropriating funds to the above mentioned registered organizations within SCDC.

Selection: Selection of the SCDC shall be each spring semester as stated below:

The Director of Campus Recreation shall serve as an advisor to the registered organizations within SCDC and shall be an ex-officio non-voting member of SCDC.

Each SCDC member shall serve for one year beginning in the spring semester.

Each registered organization within SCDC shall be entitled to one representative to the Council. The representative shall be the President or the President's designee of the respective sports club and sports organization.

A recreational organization confirming more than one hundred (100) members may exercise the option of electing a second voting representative to serve on SCDC.

The Student Senate President shall appoint an ex-officio member to the SCDC.

The Executive Officers:

The SCDC shall nominate from its membership executive officers to include a Chair and Vice Chair.

Should a vacancy occur in an executive office, the SCDC shall nominate a replacement for the remainder of the term.

Duties of the Executive Officer:

Chair:

Preside over all meetings of the funding board.

Represent the funding board in all official business.

Be responsible for compiling and presenting the budget of that funding board.

Be responsible for all official correspondence.

Be responsible to inform the Senate President, Student Body Treasurer, and Chair of the Senate Budget Committee of the time and place of allocation hearings and deliberations no less than forty-eight (48) hours earlier.

Call special meetings.

Act as a non-voting member, unless in the event of a tie.

Be elected in accordance with the approved guidelines of the funding board.

Be forwarded and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Senate Rules of Procedures, unless they are members of the SGA Union Board. Any Funding Board Chair who is not subject to Senate confirmation shall make a report o the Student Senate no less than once per semester.

Be responsible for timely advertisement of allocation hearings for all respective RSOs.

Shall not serve as a Chair of any other Funding Board or Allocation committee.

Vice Chair:

Assume all duties of the Chair in chair’s absence, as designated by the Chair.

Keep accurate minutes of all meetings, deliberations, and hearings.

Keep records of the fall and spring allocations process.

Ensure all recipients of A&S Fees from their funding board are familiar with the Florida State University SGA Finance Code. Reference Chapter 800-806.

Perform any other duties as designated by the Chair or in the approved guidelines of the funding board.

Be elected in accordance with the approved guidelines of the funding board.

Specific Guidelines:

No allocations shall transpire without the approval of the specific allocations via resolution of the Student Senate.

The Budget Committee shall hear each allocation as presented by the funding board chair. The Budget Committee shall then draft a resolution to recommend approval or disapproval in whole or part.

Each resolution must be drafted in a timely manner, relying upon the funding board.

Each line of a proposed sub-allocation of A&S Fees shall be approved separately. Approval of allocations requires a simple majority vote of the Budget committee. Disapproval of allocations requires a four-fifths (4/5) vote of the committee. Organizations that are not officially recognized by the Student Activities Center cannot be approved.

The resolution may only be open to amendment on the Senate floor following a majority vote of the Student Senate. The motion to amend the resolution must specify which part of the resolution to amend. Each amendment to the resolution shall require a separate majority vote to hear the amendment. Following a majority vote, normal rules and procedures for passing amendments shall apply.

The makeup shall include a Senator appointed by the Student Senate President. This member shall be considered an ex-officio voting member of the committee. The appointed Senator is not required to be a member of the Budget Committee, nor shall their appointment be construed as to consider them a member of the Budget Committee.

Special Budget Requests:

There shall be a separate procedure included in the guidelines specified in Sections 806(6) and 807(1)(c) for special budgetary requests to be used for new organizations that recently met the requirements of Section 806(3)(d) after the annual allocation.

An organization may not request or receive funding from SCDC other than the semi-annual and emergency allocation (not more than once per fiscal year) during the fiscal year, unless otherwise specified in its approved guidelines.

Within five (5) business days from the date an organization's budget is finally approved, the Chair of SCDC shall deliver the budget to the SGA Advisor, Student Senate President, Senate Finance Committee and the Student Body Treasurer.

The Recognized Student Organizations shall use the online budget request form to request funds from SCDC. No Sports Club RSO may request funding from a funding board or fund distribution committee other than via a resolution of Student Senate.

Each Board shall submit its budget request on forms prescribed by the Senate. The Student Senate shall allocate funds to the SCDC as part of its annual budgets. The SCDC shall re-appropriate as necessary, notify their organizations accordingly, and forward the individual organization requests to the Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy for processing to the Vice President for Student Affairs.

SCDC shall have a faculty/staff advisor appointed to advise the members of the Board on precedent and the administration’s opinion. The advisor shall also assist in the organization of the meetings, hearings, and deliberations. A faculty/staff advisor shall be considered an ex-officio member of the committee.

For any expenditure by an RSO in excess of one thousand ($1,000) the signature of the organization advisor shall be required. This signature shall not be construed as an approval or disapproval by the advisor. It shall only serve as confirmation that the advisor has been consulted.

Meetings:

The SCDC shall hold meetings on a monthly basis for all registered recreational organizations and/or such other times as are appropriate.

A special meeting of the SCDC may be called by petition of a majority of the SCDC.

Quorum shall be a majority of the total membership.

sections.heading: Chapter 808 Replacement And Renovation Accounts
sections.text:
The Student Union and Campus Recreation will set aside 0.25 percent (a quarter of one percent) of the cost of the facilities (based on the Markell Chart as provided by the FSU Office of Environmental Health and Safety) for a replacement and renovation (R&R) account to be transferred no later than June 1 of each fiscal year. These funds will be used for depreciation of their respective facilities and budgetary emergencies as well as for repair and replacement of furniture and equipment. There will be two categories of R&R:

Physical Plant (anything with a useful life over five (5) years as defined by the FSU University Controller's Office).

Furniture and Equipment Replacement (anything with a useful life less than or equal to five (5) years as defined by the FSU Controller's Office).

Any expenditure from the R&R account up to $10,000.00 must be approved by the Facility Director and Facility Board with notification given to the Senate President, Student Body President and the Vice President for Student Affairs.

Any expenditures from the R&R account over $10,000.00 must be approved by a majority of the group consisting of the Facility Director, Facility Board, Senate President, Student Body President, and Vice President for Student Affairs. The Facility Board shall have only one (1) vote.

In an emergency, and the absence of other individuals mentioned in Sections 808(2) and 808(3), the Directors of Campus Recreation, and Student Union may expend funds with the approval of the Vice President for Student Affairs.

The required contribution for R&R will have first priority on the self-generated funds for the Student Union and Campus Recreation.

Once a five percent (5%) level of the replacement cost of the facilities (as determined by Markell Charts) has been achieved, the Senate President will create a committee to review these funds. No funds shall be allocated to these accounts beyond the five percent (5) level without Student Senate's permission.

sections.heading: Chapter 809 Activity And Service (A And S) Fee Management And Reserve Account
sections.text:
The Office of the Vice President for Student Affairs (OVPSA), shall maintain an A&S Reserve account that shall be maintained at fifteen (15) percent of the annual A&S budget passed by Student Senate.

All A&S Fees held in excess of the mandatory level at the end of each fiscal year, shall be allocated in the annual A&S budget for the following fiscal year pursuant to Chapter 413.

The OVPSA must receive Senate approval to hold more than more than mandatory level.

The Chair of the Finance Committee, Student Senate President, or Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall present the request in the form of a resolution and shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senate.

The A&S Reserve account will be utilized for cash flow needs, enrollment shortfalls, and budgetary emergencies. Funds released for these purposes shall require authorization via a Senate bill.

The required contribution into the A&S Reserve account to maintain its mandatory level will be the first priority of A&S dollars.

sections.heading: Chapter 811 The Service Funding Act Of 2009
sections.text:
Title and Purpose:

Title: This act shall be known as the Service Funding Act of 2009.

Purpose: The purpose of this act is to explicitly outline the process, rules, and regulations by which organizations whose primary mission is service will receive funds from the Student Government Association.

Service Travel:

Service organizations will only be granted funds for transportation and lodging as it relates to travel. A&S Fees may not be spent for any other purpose related to a service trip.

International travel must be approved by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of any Fund Distribution Committee or Funding Board.

Service organizations may apply for funding to attend relevant service, advocacy conferences.

Equipment, Supplies and Resources:

Any equipment used for service may be purchased by an individual organization, but equipment is the property of the Florida State University Student Government Association.

Any equipment purchased must be reusable and long-lasting.

Equipment purchased with funds granted by the Student Government Association and used for hard labor by service organizations must be permanently stored at the Center for Leadership and Social Change.

Service organizations will be eligible for funds for business and office supplies to be used within the university. Office materials and supplies purchased with A&S monies may not be used to fundraise.

Service organizations will be eligible for funds for registration fees and training workshops costs.

sections.heading: Chapter 812 RSO Allocation Committee (RSOAC)
sections.text:
NOTE: Student Senate Bill #78-043 made revisions to this Chapter which will become effective on December 1, 2026.

Committee Structure
The RSOAC shall be comprised of seventeen (17) voting student members:

The Chair and Vice Chair of the Student Senate Finance Committee;
Two (2) additional Senators appointed by the Student Senate President;
Five (5) students-at-large elected during the Fall SGA elections, pursuant to Section 13 of this Chapter;

Two (2) students-at-large designated by the Student Body President;
Four (4) students-at-large designated by the Student Body Treasurer;
One (1) member-elect of the Campus Recreation Board designated by the outgoing Chair of the Campus Recreation Board;
One (1) member of the Union Board designated by the Chair of the Union Board.

All appointments to the RSOAC shall be financially certified prior to being a voting member of the committee.
Committee appointments should be made and designated by the appropriate entity before the annual Fall SGA Inauguration.

Committee members shall serve a one-year term beginning and ending with the Fall SGA Inauguration.

Committee members must meet the enrollment requirements provided in §100.6.
Committee members are subject to the requirements of Chapter 205, Student Body Statutes (the SGA Code of Ethics) including the requirement to avoid conflicts of interest. As such, committee members are required to abstain from voting on any funding recommendation that would benefit an organization of which they are a member or affiliated within any capacity. 
Following the certification of Fall SGA election results and prior to the Fall Senate organizational meeting, an organizational meeting of the RSO Allocation Committee shall be convened. This meeting shall be scheduled and hosted by outgoing Senate Leadership. During this meeting, the committee shall:
Receive a joint training session conducted by SGA Accounting and the Office of Student Organizations and Involvement, covering financial procedures, RSO eligibility, and committee responsibilities. The outgoing Chair and Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee shall be invited to assist with the training and help transition the new committee; and
Elect a Chair and Vice Chair from all members of the committee.
Review the most recent annual evaluation of the RSOAC program prepared by the Student Body Treasurer, as required by Section 11 of this Chapter, in order to understand past performance, challenges, and recommendations for program improvement.
Leadership
Committee leadership elections shall occur during the organizational meeting held following Fall elections and prior to the Fall SGA Inauguration, as outlined in Section 2(g).
Committee leadership elections shall follow the procedures in §400.7, Student Body Statutes and Rule 5.5 of the Senate Rules of Procedure.
The Chair of the RSOAC may not simultaneously serve as Chair or Vice Chair of another SGA committee or entity.
The Chair or Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee may be removed by either: The Student Senate President, for cause, with written notice to the committee and the Senate President Pro Tempore; or a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the voting members of the RSO Allocation Committee.
Upon removal of the Chair or Vice Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee, or if a vacancy otherwise occurs, the committee shall, at its next regular meeting, elect a replacement from among its members by majority vote, subject to confirmation of eligibility.
The Student Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore shall be notified within two (2) business days of any vacancy or replacement election. 
Duties of the Vice Chair
The Vice Chair shall be responsible for recording and maintaining official minutes of all RSO Allocation Committee meetings.
The Vice Chair shall publish and transmit all minutes to the Student Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Historian and ensure their publication within the timeframe required.
The Vice Chair shall be responsible for the collection and maintenance of scoring materials and administration of the committee’s evaluation rubric during meetings, ensuring that all votes and scores are properly documented and retained.
Duties of the Chair
The Chair shall serve as the chief point of communication between the RSO Allocation Committee, all Registered Student Organizations, and the Student Senate.
The Chair shall coordinate with the SGA Accounting Office and the Office of Student Organizations & Involvement to provide timely notice of funding outcomes and committee decisions to all applicants.
Joint Responsibilities
The Chair and Vice Chair shall be jointly responsible for preparing and publishing the agenda of each RSO Allocation Committee meeting.
The agenda shall include all funding requests scheduled for consideration, relevant documentation, and any items of general business, and must be distributed in accordance with this Chapter and Chapter 203 of the Student Body Statutes.
Committee Operations
Quorum shall consist of at least seven (7) members.
The committee shall establish a regular, weekly meeting schedule and must meet on Thursdays, and shall have a meeting end time of no later than 10:00 PM ET. However, the time of conclusion may be waived by a 2/3 vote of the committee.
Funding requests must be submitted no later than 12:00 PM ET (noon) on the Monday prior to the Thursday meeting at which they will be considered.
Requests submitted after the Monday deadline shall be scheduled for the following week’s meeting unless otherwise approved by the Chair.
All funding requests shall be reviewed by the SGA Accounting Office for authenticity in RSO registration status prior being forwarded to the Chair of the RSOAC. The SGA Accounting Office retains decision making authority in regards to the validity of all requests submitted to the RSOAC.
The agenda for each Thursday meeting shall be distributed to committee members and sponsoring RSOs by Tuesday at 5:00 PM.
The Vice Chair shall maintain an attendance log for all scheduled meetings of the RSOAC. This log shall be transmitted to the Senate President Pro Tempore and posted with the committee minutes.
An absence means failure to attend a noticed meeting of the RSOAC.
An excused absence may be granted by the Chair for circumstances including, but not limited to, academic obligations, documented illness, religious observances, University-sponsored activities, or emergencies. Members shall notify the Chair as soon as practicable and, when feasible, at least twenty-four (24) hours in advance.
Unexcused absence means any absence not excused under 4(g)(2).

Upon a third (3rd) unexcused absence within a member’s one-year term, an elected student-at-large member shall be immediately suspended from the RSOAC and the matter shall be forwarded to the Senate Rules Committee within two (2) business days. The suspended member shall not be counted toward quorum and shall not vote pending disposition.

The Senate Rules Committee shall apply the same process used for Student Senators regarding attendance and fitness to serve. If the Rules Committee finds that the individual cannot continue to serve in their capacity, it shall recommend impeachment to the Senate Judiciary Committee. The Rules Committee may, by majority vote and upon written justification of extraordinary circumstances, grant additional excused absences or a one-time waiver not to exceed two (2) additional absences for the remainder of the term. Any waiver granted shall be reported to the Senate at the next regular meeting.

If any designated representative of an entity accrues more than three (3) unexcused absences within their term, the representative shall be removed from the RSOAC, and the Chair shall request a new designee from the designating authority. The designating authority may, at their discretion, decide to redesignate the same individual. If a replacement is not named within five (5) business days of notice, the seat shall remain vacant until filled and shall not count toward quorum while vacant.
Absences accumulate per term of service (from Fall Inauguration to the subsequent Fall Inauguration) and reset at the start of each term. This section applies Suspended or removed members within this Chapter do not count toward quorum during suspension or after removal.to regularly noticed RSOAC meetings.
Funding Recommendation Process
The Student Senate shall retain final authority over the approval of all RSOAC funding recommendations.
Funding recommendations made by the RSO Allocation Committee shall be transmitted to the Student Senate in the form of an allocation resolution sponsored by the Chair and Vice Chair of the Senate Finance Committee, and co-sponsored by any Senators serving on the RSOAC.
Allocation Resolutions must be submitted by the Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee via the Senate Legislation Submission form no later than 11:59 PM ET (midnight) on the Friday following the Thursday RSOAC meeting, to be included on the next week’s Senate agenda with all other legislation.
Allocation Resolutions shall be placed on the agenda for the following Wednesday Senate meeting. The Senate President shall have the discretion to place these resolutions on either the Consent portion or the Second Reading portion of the agenda.
 Before any allocation resolution may be amended, a motion to open the allocation resolution must be made and agreed to by a simple majority, which shall be followed by an opening and debate. Upon adoption of such motion by a two-thirds (2/3) roll-call vote, individual amendments may then be entertained. Each amendment shall require a separate motion, debate, and two-thirds roll-call vote. However, the Student Senate shall not increase funding for any Registered Student Organization that the RSO Allocation Committee voted to recommend zero funding for.
All adopted amendments must be documented and emailed to the Senate Clerk, Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Historian within one (1) hour of the conclusion of the meeting by the amendment’s sponsor. 
Amendments to Allocation Resolutions may be submitted in advance of the meeting to the Senate President and Senate Clerk to be listed on the agenda.

Eligibility Criteria for Student Organizations

All organizations applying for funding must be currently registered with the Office of Student Organizations & Involvement and in good conduct standing with Florida State University. 
Student organizations may not receive funding from the RSO Allocation Committee if they have also received funds from the College Leadership Council Funding Board, the Sport Club Distribution Council, or line-item funding in the annual SGA budget in the same fiscal year.
Funding Guidelines and Restrictions
All requests must be for eligible uses of Student Activity & Service Fee revenues, as provided in the SGA Financial Manual.
The Student Body Treasurer shall coordinate with the Department of Student Engagement to establish an online system for submitting funding requests.
Funding requests shall generally be required to include a description of the intended use of funds and why the requested funding is needed. Student organizations shall be required to provide an estimate of the number of FSU students that are likely to attend an event or travel opportunity funded by SGA.
Pursuant to §1009.24, Florida Statutes, SGA funding may only be used to benefit the student body in general. As such, funding from the RSO Allocation Committee may not benefit activities for which an admission fee is charged to students. Further, student organizations that charge membership fees may not exclude any student from participation in any events or programs funded by SGA as a result of a student’s inability to pay such fees.
Funds may not be used to cover membership dues or fees associated with a student’s or organization’s national or international affiliations.
The committee shall not recommend funding for events or programs that are likely to have only group members attend and/or have no general benefit to the student body.
The committee shall not recommend funding for events that are exclusive to a club or organization’s executive board. 
Requests for clothing may only be approved once per fiscal year. Any clothing funded by SGA must directly promote the student organization.
Organizations seeking funding for service trips must first demonstrate that they made a good-faith effort to participate in an open or public service opportunity offered by the Center for Leadership and Service, if such an opportunity was available. If participation in such a trip was not feasible due to scheduling, availability, or capacity, the organization may pursue independent service trip funding through the RSO Allocation Committee. In such cases, documentation of the organization’s outreach to CLS and explanation of why participation in a CLS-facilitated trip was not possible must be provided with the funding request.
Student organizations shall submit their request prior to the RSOAC meeting via a recording of their presentation, ideally with a slideshow to assist their request.
The presentation's recording may not be longer than 7 minutes, and must detail the specifics about their request for the full awareness of the SROAC membership.
Time may be designated at the discretion of the Chair of the RSOAC to watch these pre-submitted presentations during the meeting, or members may be required to watch these presentations prior to the meeting.

All video presentations must be submitted alongside the organization's application to the RSOAC. 

A representative of the Student Organization must attend the RSOAC meeting they will be considered in, for the purposes of answering questions about the presentation. 

If there are no representatives from the organization, the request will be tabled.

If, at the next meeting of the RSOAC, there is no attending representative, the request shall be zero funded.
Funding Limits
 Travel
Maximum of $250 per student.
Annual Cap per Organizations
No organization may receive more than 3.5% of the total budget allocated to the RSOAC in the annual budget process during a single fiscal year, regardless of the number of individual requests or categories funded.
For purposes of this section, “total funding” includes all allocations for travel, events, programming, or any other expenditures recommended by the RSO Allocation Committee and approved by the Student Senate.
Single Allocation Rule
An organization may not receive funding for more than one (1) request within the same allocation resolution transmitted to the Student Senate.
The Committee shall have discretion to recommend that the Student Senate exceed the funding limit for Travel or Events/Programming with the usage of Senate Projects funding, said recommendation shall be listed in the scoring rubrics “Evaluator Notes” section.
Funding Allocation Schedule
In order to comply with University purchasing and travel guidelines, of the funding allocated to the RSO Allocation Committee in the annual SGA budget:
5% shall be available for allocation beginning July 1 each year through the end of the Summer semester;
47.5% shall be available for allocation in the Fall semester, in addition to any unexpended funds from earlier in the fiscal year; and
47.5% shall be available in the Spring semester, in addition to any unexpended funds from earlier in the fiscal year.
All final funding allocations must be approved by the Student Senate at least 30 calendar days before the event or travel is to take place.
In addition to the requirement above, funding for events or travel scheduled during the months of May or June must be approved by the Student Senate before the conclusion of the Spring semester. There shall be no exceptions to this requirement, which is needed in order to maintain compliance with the University’s fiscal year-end closeout procedures.
Post-Award Requirements
All events funded by SGA must be publicly advertised on the University-designated student organization management platform in a manner visible to the general student body. This shall serve as the baseline standard for public advertisement. Additional promotion through means such as social media, digital signage, newsletters, or tabling is encouraged but not required.
Any events, programs, travel, or other activities supported by SGA funding must comply with the FSU Student Organization Conduct Code as well as all federal, state, and local laws.
Every organization receiving funding from SGA must submit a post event evaluation form, along with receipts for any purchases made, to the SGA Accounting Office, within ten (10) business days following the event.
If the requirements above are not followed by an organization, they shall be barred from requesting any further funding until their post-award violations are rectified with SGA accounting.

Annual Review Requirement
No later than the end of the Fall semester each year, the Student Body Treasurer shall conduct an evaluation of the RSOAC program. This review shall assess the overall effectiveness of the program and identify any areas for potential improvement.
This evaluation shall include:
The number and nature of instances in which standard funding rules or limits were waived;
An analysis of how such waivers impacted student organizations and the broader student body;
The adequacy of the current funding level for the program;
Recommendations for enhancing the program’s structure, parameters, and allocation limits; and

A breakdown of the number and types of organizations that receive funding, including both organizational status (USSO, ASO, GSO) and programmatic category (e.g. academic, cultural, special interest, political, community service).
Following the evaluation, the Student Body Treasurer shall prepare a report of findings and recommendations. This report shall be submitted to the Student Senate Budget Committee during the annual SGA budget planning cycle.
Policy Implementation: 
The Student Senate shall adopt a policy, pursuant to the requirements of Chapter 416, Student Body Statutes, to govern the operations of the RSO Allocation Committee, to establish procedures governing funding requests, and to establish criteria for the committee to use in evaluating funding requests. At minimum an established policy must create a rubric that the committee shall use for all allocations.

sections.heading: Chapter 813 RSO Development Fund
sections.text:
Purpose: The RSO Development Fund shall be established to provide limited financial support to Registered Student Organizations (RSOs) to assist with basic programming and operational expenses.
Funding Guidelines
Each RSO shall be eligible to receive no more than three hundred dollars ($300) in a single fiscal year.
Each RSO shall be limited to one (1) allocation per fiscal year.
Allocation Process
The Student Body Treasurer shall collaborate with the Department of Student Engagement to develop and maintain an online application for funding requests.
The application shall require the following information:
Name of the RSO;
Name and position of the submitting officer;
The organization’s mission statement;
Number of active members;
Requested funding amount (if less than $300);
Attestation that the RSO does not charge mandatory dues; and
Description of the intended use of funds.

Program Administration

Only the President or Treasurer of the RSO may submit funding applications, this shall be verified upon receipt of the application by the SGA Accounting Office.
The Student Body Treasurer, or their designee, shall review each application to determine eligibility and shall have the authority to approve or reject funding applications.
Approved applications shall be forwarded to the SGA Accounting Office to initiate the transfer of funds.
Reporting Requirements: The Student Body Treasurer shall submit a monthly report to the Student Senate, in the form of a
memorandum included on the Consent Agenda, which shall include:

A list of RSOs that received funding;
The amount and intended purpose of each allocation;
The remaining balance of the RSO Development Fund; and
Any relevant concerns, emerging trends, or recommendations for future consideration.
