Adopted by Bill B77-034 on 8/13/2025

sections.heading: Chapter 900 The Uniform Agency Act Of 2023
sections.text:
Purpose:

Title: This act shall be called the “Student Government Association Executive Agency Act of 2023, hereinafter referred to as the “Executive Agency Act.”

Purpose: This chapter shall create uniform guidelines and operating procedures for Student Government Association sponsored entities known as “Agencies.” The purpose of the Executive Agency Act is to establish a common set of rules for all agencies under the Student Government Association, ensuring a unified approach to serving the diverse student body. Each agency, while maintaining its unique identity and focus, will adhere to these general rules, promoting consistency, fairness, and transparency across all agencies.

Membership: Membership in each agency is open to all members of the Florida State University Student Body. No university student may be denied membership on the basis of race, creed, color, religion, national origin, age, ability, veteran’s or marital status, sexual orientation, gender identity, gender expression, or any other protected group status as established in Chapter 206. Each agency is committed to fostering an inclusive environment that respects and celebrates diversity. All students, regardless of their background or identity, are encouraged to participate in the activities of the agencies, contribute to their objectives, and benefit from their resources.

Scope: The act shall become, upon its enactment, fully binding on all entities defined herein as “Agencies.”

Definitions:
AGENCY: An “Agency” is defined as a programmatic division of the Executive Branch created to provide support for and education on a particular identity group of the Florida State University Student Body.

RECOGNIZED STUDENT ORGANIZATION (RSO): Each Recognized Student Organization is an entity separate and distinct from, but under the authority of the Student Government Association as recognized by The Office of Student Organizations and Involvement. An organization, as distinguished from an Agency, is a group of students organized primarily to advance social, athletic, fraternal, and philanthropic needs.

RULES OF PROCEDURE: Each Agency shall adopt its own internal “Rules of Procedure” in compliance with the Student Body Constitution and Statutes to further enumerate its organization, administration, and general operating procedures. These Rules of Procedure shall be treated as a policy pursuant to Chapter 416, and the adoption or revision of these policies shall not require approval by the Senate.

Creation:
In addition to a bill to create an agency by Senate, or by referendum, the Student Body President may request the creation of an Agency upon identifying a need, pursuant to Section 300(3)(c) and (d), of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes. This request must be submitted in writing to the Student Senate President, and must include the stated purpose of the proposed agency. Upon receipt of this request, the Senate President shall introduce a bill onto the Calendar, within three (3) weeks, which shall propose the creation of the requested Agency.

The proposed Agency will be created upon the enactment of the Bill. The new Agency will be incorporated into the organizational structure of the Student Government Association Executive Branch and shall be immediately subject to all privileges and responsibilities intrinsic to agency status.

If a Recognized Student Organization is converted to an Agency, the Recognized Student Organization will cease to exist, and the Agency shall have no identity separate from the Student Government Association.

Operation:
The supervision and regulation of the agencies is the responsibility of the Student Body Vice President.

Agencies are required to be in compliance with their individual Rules of Procedure, Student Body Statutes, Student Body Constitution, Florida State University regulations and policies, the State of Florida Constitution and Statutes, and the United States Constitution at all times while in operation. Non-compliance with these provisions shall call for remedial action. The Student Body President and Student Senate President shall be authorized to take whatever action is deemed necessary and proper as defined in the Student Body Statutes.

Amendments to an Agency’s Rules of Procedure must be submitted in writing to the Agency Director and voted on at the next Executive Board meeting.

Amendments to an Agency’s Rules of Procedure require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Executive Board to become formally adopted.

Agency Executive Boards: All agencies shall be governed by an Executive Board composed of a majority of student members to oversee their activities. There shall be no fewer than five (5) student members on an agency Executive Board.

Each Agency shall, at minimum, have the following Executive Board members who shall be appointed in the manner specified in Section 304, unless otherwise delineated by the Agency’s Rules of Procedure.

The Director shall: 

Serve as Chair of their Agency’s Executive Board.

Execute decisions on policy, procedure, and activities voted on by the Executive Board.

Establish ad hoc committees as necessary for the express purpose of managing specialized initiatives.

Delegate responsibilities to other Executive Board members within their respective positions that are necessary for the growth of their agency.

Supervise and assist the Agency Treasurer in managing the financial needs of the agency.

Preside over and have the authority to call Executive Board, General Body, and ad hoc committee meetings.

Hold overarching responsibility and maintain accountability for all actions undertaken by the Agency and its board members within the organization.

Nothing in this section shall be construed as to hold the Director personally responsible for any actions taken by the Agency and its board members outside the course and scope of their duties outlined in the Student Body Constitution, Student Body Statutes, & the Agency’s individual Rules of Procedure.

Serve as an ex-officio member of the Office of Governmental Affairs Agency Committee or appoint a designee.

Create additional Executive Board positions deemed necessary and proper that are not otherwise delineated within Statutes in line with the Agency’s respective Rules of Procedure.

Communicate regularly with the Executive Branch and Legislative Branch of the Student Government Association.

The Assistant Director shall:

Support the Director in overseeing the daily operations of the agency.

Exercise the authority and duties of the Director in their absence.

Cosign official documents along with the Director as required in their respective capacity.

Manage affiliate organizations as laid out in Section 900(10) and the Agency’s individual Rules of Procedure.

Perform additional duties related to the administrative aspects of the Agency as assigned by the Director.

The Treasurer shall: 

Record fiscal spending, uphold the integrity of financial records, and oversee the deposit of Agency funds.

Submit all budget requests in a timely manner and promote fiscal accountability.

Properly maintain all records and documentation regarding the financial affairs of the agency.

Develop a report on the financial status of the Agency to the Executive Board upon request.

Communicate regularly with the Student Body Treasurer on the financial needs of the agency.

Perform additional duties related to the administrative aspects of the Agency as assigned by the Director.

The Secretary shall:

Record minutes for all of their respective Agency’s meetings and ensure their Agency maintains compliance with all state regulations regarding public meetings and documents, and Student Body Statutes requirements as laid out in Chapters 203 and 204.

Maintain a contact list of active members and record of the attendance at Agency meetings.

Maintain a membership roster of each affiliate organization.

Execute and be responsible for submitting in a timely manner, forms, documents and reports as required for the operation of the office.

Perform additional duties related to the administrative aspects of the Agency as assigned by the Director.

Agency Meetings:

All meetings of Executive Agencies, and events held thereof, shall be open to all members of the Florida State University Student Body and remain compliant with Chapter 203 of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes.

Executive Board Meetings:

The Executive Board of each Agency shall meet at least once per month. The meetings must be publicized, a quorum must be present to conduct business, and minutes must be taken.

A majority of the Executive Board shall constitute quorum for Agency meetings unless otherwise specified by the Agency’s individual Rules of Procedure.

Executive Board meetings shall be called upon by the Agency’s Director or by written request of a majority of the Agency’s Executive Board.

Notification of all board meetings shall be made at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the designated meeting time.

No official acts may take place unless a quorum is present.

General Body Meetings:

General body meetings shall be held at least once per semester, with the date and time of each meeting advertised to the public at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the designated meeting time.

Removal from Office:

All Agency Directors, Assistant Directors and Board members are subject to impeachment by the Student Senate.

Each Agency’s Board may, by two-thirds (2/3) vote of a quorum of Board members, recommend their Director, Assistant Director, Treasurer, or Secretary for removal to the Student Body President in accordance with Section 304.

All Executive Board members not confirmed by the Student Senate are subject to removal at any time by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Agency’s Executive Board.

Vacancies:

In the event that a Director or Assistant Director of an agency should take temporary leave of two weeks (14 days) or more from the FSU environment, and thus be unable to directly contribute to, or oversee the agency, it shall be their responsibility to notify in writing the Chief of Staff and the Director of Student Affairs no less than two weeks (14 days) prior to such leave.

Said letter must include an officer of the agency appointed by the Director who will serve as chief contact, liaison, and administrator of the Agency, and who is duly authorized to serve in such capacity during such time as the Director/Assistant Director may be absent.
An extension of up to ten (10) school days can be permitted for good cause by proof of extenuating circumstances received by the Chief of Staff including, but not limited to, death of an immediate family member, medical reasons, religious observance, and any other excused absences as provided by the University.

Leaves of absences do not include university recognized holidays including, but not limited to Spring Break or other regularly scheduled campus-wide holidays.

Any Executive Board Members other than the Director who no longer wish to serve on the Executive Board must submit a resignation to the Director at least two (2) weeks in advance, along with any relevant information in the form of a letter.

In the event an Agency Director resigns from office, refer to the procedure described in Section 304 of the Student Body Statutes.

The resigning officer shall submit all documents pertaining to their position and shall facilitate a proper transition for the new officer at least one (1) week prior to the officer’s final day in their position.

Termination:
Agencies will be eligible for termination when it is determined through Student Senate review, that the agency is no longer providing the services for which it was created.

Student Government Association Agencies shall be terminated upon enactment of a bill to delete the agency from the Student Body Statutes, Title X, and Student Government Association Executive Agencies. If an Agency is terminated, its budget shall be allocated via the annual budget process the following fiscal year.

Affiliate Organizations:
Affiliate Membership is available to all Recognized Student Organizations (RSOs) that have an interest in contributing to an Agency’s mission statement.

Qualifications: RSOs seeking Affiliate Membership must submit the following to the Agency Director to initiate the Affiliate Membership process:

Letter of Intent

Copy of organization’s Constitution

Copy of RSO re-recognition process approval

Each Agency’s Rules of Procedure shall govern all additional aspects regarding their Affiliate Membership process including, but not limited to, additional membership qualifications, approval, denial, general meetings, as well as their Affiliate’s roles and responsibilities.

Monetary Allocations:
Pursuant to the A&S Fee Guidelines, the Student Senate shall be the allocation and revisionary authority in all budgetary matters pertaining to agencies.

The Student Body Treasurer shall be responsible for the financial responsibility of Executive Agencies. All expenditures of agencies must be approved and have the signature of Agency’s Director and Treasurer before all purchase requests are submitted to the SGA Accounting Office. After the SGA Accounting Office approves the expenditures, it must be sent to the Student Body Treasurer for approval or rejection.

The Director, Assistant Director, and Treasurer of each Agency must be financially certified through the Student Government Association.

Agencies must notify the SGA Accounting Office and the Student Body Treasurer in writing to request additional funds at any point during the fiscal year from the Student Senate.

Each year the budgets of the agencies shall be zero based and reviewed by the Senate Funding Committees who shall make appropriate recommendations to the Senate Budget Committee.

Publications:
Compliance: All advertisements must comply with the University Posting Policy (http://posting.fsu.edu).

Approval: The Agency Director must approve all publications, shirts, flyers, etc. prior to duplication and distribution.

The Agencies: Presented below is a comprehensive list of all Student Government Association Executive Agencies, each accompanied by its respective mission statement. 

Asian American Student Union (AASU):
The AASU shall represent the Asian American community at the Florida State University and promote the spread of awareness pertaining to Asian American heritage and culture. AASU will serve to encourage and promote for the civic engagement of the Asian and Asian American community, as well as the student body at the Florida State University. It shall function as an educational and cultural learning instrument for the FSU community, by providing cultural programs and materials, which promote awareness of and appreciation for the various and distinct Asian cultures. AASU shall serve as the nucleus of a network to improve the opportunities and living conditions of the Asian community. To this end, AASU shall represent all registered Asian and Asian American student organizations on campus, coordinate available resources, and serve as a catalyst in protecting the rights and representation of the Asian and Asian American student body.

Black Student Union (BSU):
The BSU shall serve primarily to promote and provide for the social welfare of the Black Student Body at the Florida State University. The BSU shall be limited neither to the aforementioned objectives nor to the Florida State University in scope. The BSU shall also strive to provide and promote economic, political and academic enrichment through its activities, and it shall serve as a catalyst to the enlightenment of the Florida State University community to the distinct and proud cultural heritage of Black people in America as well as on the African continent. Finally, it shall be a source of edification of the Black experience at Florida State University.

Hispanic/Latine Student Union (HLSU):
The HLSU shall serve as an institution dedicated to unifying, informing, and serving the Hispanic/Latine community at the Florida State University (FSU) and Tallahassee community. The HLSU will function as an educational and cultural learning instrument for all students, faculty, and staff. It shall provide a centralized coordination of resources and service for Hispanic/Latine community. The HLSU shall serve as a nucleus for a network with other national institutions and organizations to improve the opportunities and living conditions of the Hispanic/Latine community. It shall be open and accessible to everyone thus providing a liaison between FSU and Tallahassee community.

Jewish Student Union (JSU):
The Jewish Student Union (JSU) is a Student Government Agency belonging to Florida State University. The Jewish Student Union at Florida State University is committed to creating an environment for students to learn, embrace, and celebrate Jewish culture. The Jewish Student Union shall serve the Jewish community as a unifying organization through its Advisory Council, which is made up of other Registered Student Organizations. The JSU will represent the Jewish community to the Student Government Association, Administration, and Tallahassee community. We aspire to foster an inclusive community to engage the student body in meaningful programming. Through educational initiatives, cultural celebrations, and social events, the JSU strives to cultivate a vibrant space that empowers individuals to deepen their understanding of Judaism.

Pride Student Union (PSU):
To provide services and programs to address the needs of lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, queer, questioning, asexual, and intersex students and to increase the awareness of issues pertinent to them within the Florida State University community. Further, the Pride Student Union shall endeavor to create a supportive and healthy environment for the welfare of all students regardless of their sexual orientation or gender identity.

Women Student Union (WSU):
The purpose of the Women Student Union (WSU) shall serve to develop a greater awareness in the Florida State University community of women’s rights and issues and their relationship to the economic, social, and political nature of society. The Women Student Union of the Florida State University values struggles of the past, asserts rights in the present, and celebrates aspirations for the future. The Women Student Union fosters the growth of women personally, professionally, and politically. The WSU will celebrate the power existing within every woman to promote self-autonomy, denounce all limitations, educate on systems of oppression and advocate inclusivity within a diverse community. WSU facilitates a network among organizations, departments, and services to embrace, engage and empower. The Women Student Union shall be limited neither to the aforementioned objectives nor to the Florida State University in scope. It shall serve to promote a positive approach towards women’s concerns in the Florida State University community. The Women Student Union will develop programs, services, and activities that will reach out to women and will connect students to administration, faculty, and staff to create a feeling of strength and solidarity within the Florida State University community. It shall empower women in the Florida State University community by actively confronting sexual discrimination, teaching leadership skills, encouraging involvement and promoting advocacy. The agency will function as an educational and cultural learning instrument for students, administration, faculty and staff. It shall serve as a nucleus for a network with other women-centered organizations to improve the opportunities and conditions of women on campus and in the community. The agency shall provide a centralized coordination of resources and services for women. It shall be open and accessible to everyone, and will strengthen the connection between Florida State University and the Tallahassee community.

Veterans Student Union (VSU):
The VSU shall be committed to the collective interests of all student veterans of the armed forces and those who support them. The primary goal of the VSU is to ensure good academic standing and successful employment and/or postgraduate education acceptance for all VSU members. Inherent in this mission is our effort to promote and support the bonding of student veterans so that a spirit of academic and professional accountability is fostered within the ranks of VSU members. The VSU will aid the administration of the Florida State University in the achievement of the goal of becoming “the most veteran friendly public university in the nation.” The VSU shall be limited neither to the aforementioned objectives nor to the Florida State University in scope. The VSU shall also strive to provide and promote economic, political, and academic enrichment through its activities, and promote awareness of and appreciation for those who have served in the armed forces and the military culture.

sections.heading: Chapter 1000 Affiliated Projects Act
sections.text:
Title: This act shall be called the “Student Government Association Affiliated Projects Act of 1994”, (Affiliated Projects Act).

(History: Revised by the 47th Senate Bills 22 and 158. Revised by the 48th Senate Bills 47 and 129. Revised by the 49th Senate Bill 14. Revised by the 56th Senate Bill 83. Revised by the 65th Senate Bill 11. Revised by the 74th Senate Bill 60.)

Creation, Purpose, and Definition:
Purpose: The purpose of this act is to prescribe the policies governing the special projects jointly undertaken by the Executive and Legislative Branches of the Florida State University Student Government Association and other Florida State University departments.

Creation:
In addition to a bill to create an affiliated project by the Student Senate, or by referendum, the Student Body President may request the creation of an affiliated project upon identifying a need, pursuant to Section 300(3)(c) and (d), of the FSU Student Body Statutes. This request must be submitted in writing to the Senate President and must include the stated purpose of the proposed Affiliated Project. Upon receipt of this request, the Senate President shall introduce a bill onto the Calendar, within two (2) weeks, that shall propose the creation of the requested affiliated project.

The proposed affiliated project will be created upon the enactment of the bill. The new affiliated project will be incorporated into the organized structure of Student Government Association and shall be subject immediately to all privileges and responsibilities inherent with affiliated projects status.

Definition: An SGA Affiliated Project is an operation formally adopted by the Student Government Association as a special project; is characterized by its autonomous nature; generates funding when possible, may be housed outside of the Union, deals frequently with the community and provides information, services and unique opportunities for students.

Monetary Allocations:
An affiliated project shall receive a substantial amount of their funding from sources other than Student Government Association. Any money allocated to an affiliated project by Student Government Association shall be line itemized.

Affiliated projects shall be audited by the Auditor annually.

Should fiscal problems arise concerning an affiliated project, the Finance Committee of the Student Senate may place the Affiliated Project on a probationary period.

Affiliated projects are expected to generate funding for programming whenever possible. All funding raised must be marked as self-generated in the yearly budget.

During the budgeting process an affiliated project must prepare a proposal that fully explains any new line item that it is asking to be funded. Substantial increases in lines formerly budgeted must also be explained.

Operations: Affiliated projects may be housed in areas outside of the Union.

Evaluations:
The Student Life Committee shall consider whether each affiliated project should continue in existence and receive funding, and make such recommendations in writing to the Student Senate President. This shall occur no later than the twelfth week of the Fall semester, on a four-year basis.
Affiliated projects shall be reviewed on a four-year staggered basis, starting Fall 2026.

If determined necessary by Senate leadership or the Student Life Chair, a project may be reviewed during any Fall semester. 

New Affiliated projects shall be reviewed twice as often for its review cycle. 

Affiliated projects are to be overseen by the Student Body Treasurer.
The following is a list of Student Government affiliated projects and their corresponding chapter number as they appear in Title X.
Chapter 1001 - Alumni Village Child Development Center

sections.heading: Chapter 1001 Alumni Village Child Development Center
sections.text:
Parent Cooperative Board of Directors (Board):

Composition: There shall be a Parent Cooperative Board of Directors composed of three (3) elected persons: the President, the Treasurer, and the Secretary.

Selection and Term of Office: Members of the Board of Directors are elected by the parent body of Alumni Village Child Development by a majority vote and are required to serve for a minimum of two (2) semesters.

Members: Members of the Board must be students or their spouses and currently have a child enrolled in the Child Development.

Duties and Powers:
The duties of the Board include hiring a Child Development Center Teacher/Director in conjunction cooperatively with the Director of Student Affairs Coordinator.

Further duties of the Board of Directors include assisting in the following areas: (a) business and social correspondence and meetings; (b) preparation of the annual budget; school managements and policies; and (d) tuition collection.

Meetings: The Board shall meet a minimum of once each semester, and the entire parent body shall meet once each semester. A voting quorum consists of two-thirds (2/3) of all parent members.

The Director shall ensure that minutes are taken at all meetings and that a copy of said minutes are sent to the Student Body President. A file containing the minutes of all past meetings shall be maintained.

History: Revised by the 49th Senate Bill 14.

sections.heading: Chapter 1002 Student Alert Force Escort (S.A.F.E.) Connection
sections.text:
Creation and Purpose:

Title: This act shall be called the "S.A.F.E." Act.

Creation: There shall be an Affiliated Project of the Student Government Association and FSU Police Department known as S.A.F.E. Connection.

Purpose: The purpose of S.A.F.E. Connection is to provide a safe mode of transportation for students on campus through an escort service. S.A.F.E. Connection is also to provide a mode of transportation for students under the influence of alcohol. S.A.F.E. Connection is to further promote awareness of the dangers of driving under the influence, and to promote education, activities and programs concerning crime prevention and safety to the students, faculty, staff and visitors of Florida State University.

Services: S.A.F.E. Connection shall operate according to rules and procedures promulgated by the FSU Police Department. It shall serve the students, faculty, staff, and visitors to the university.

Director:

Selection and Term of Office:

The Director shall be chosen in accordance with the S.A.F.E. rules and procedure.

Duties:

The Director shall be responsible for effectively executing all those duties granted them in the rules and procedure.

Assistant Director:

Selection of Term:

The Assistant Director shall be chosen in accordance with S.A.F.E. rules and procedures.

Duties:

There shall be one Assistant Director. The Assistant Director shall be responsible for effectively executing all those duties granted them by S.A.F.E. rules and procedures.

Substantive Changes to the S.A.F.E. Program:

The appropriate authority specified in the S.A.F.E. rules and procedures shall notify the Student Senate and the Student Body President in writing no less than five (5) business days prior to the implementation of substantive changes to the S.A.F.E. Program, which include:

Any purchase which exceeds thirty-thousand dollars ($30,000.00).

Any changes to the S.A.F.E. rules and procedures.

Any other action as may be required by the S.A.F.E. rules of procedure.

Funding:

S.A.F.E. may receive A&S Funds, although the majority of the funding of S.A.F.E. shall be derived from non-A&S Fees.

sections.heading: Chapter 1003 Student Publications Office
sections.text:
Creation and Purpose:

Creation: There shall be an Affiliated Project of the Student Government Association known as the Student Publications Office.

Purpose: This Affiliated Project shall be responsible for coordinating, producing and publishing the publications of the Student Government Association.

Student Publications Supervisor:

The Student Publications Supervisor shall be a salaried, full-time position.

The Supervisor shall represent the staff of the Publications Office at all agency meetings, and other appropriate functions.

The Supervisor shall work with FSU staff, administration, faculty and students to guarantee the successful publication, distribution, and marketing of all office publications.

The Supervisor shall advise and assist the staff.

Publications: 
Purpose: Student Publications shall assist the Student Government Agencies, Institutes, Affiliated Projects, and recognized student organizations in the publications of flyers, pamphlets and other publications as needed on a first come, time available basis.

Staff: In cases of disagreements between the Supervisor and staff on Student Publications decisions, the Supervisor’s decisions shall be final.

sections.heading: Chapter 1004 The Florida State University Medical Response Unit
sections.text:
Title, Creation, and Purpose:

Creation: There shall be an Affiliated Project of the Student Government Association, FSU Police Department, and University Health Services known as the Florida State University Medical Response Unit.

Purpose: The FSU Medical Response Unit is a service of the University Health Services, the Florida State University Police Department, and the Student Government Association that functions as a volunteer medical first responding agency at the Florida State University.

Services:

Operations: The FSU Medical Response Union shall operate according to rules of procedures promulgated by its Board of Directors, which shall be treated as a policy pursuant to Chapter 416. Adoption or revision of this policy shall not require Senate approval. These rules of procedures shall be considered public and available for viewing inspection upon written request. It shall serve the students, faculty, staff and visitors to the university in the following manner.

The FSU Medical Response Unit shall provide basic medical care as outlined by medical protocol manual approved by the Medical Director and Clinical Supervisor to students at scheduled events or as dispatched by FSUPD, Leon County EMS or requested through the FSU Medical Response Unit Supervisors office. Medical care may be provided in the event that the members come upon a need during regular commutes on campus.

Regardless of personal qualifications and certifications, the Medical Response Unit shall perform only those actions and/or procedures approved by the Medical Director and Clinical Supervisor.

Members of the Medical Response Unit - at a minimum - shall be certified as specified by the United States Department of Transportation National Emergency Medical Service (EMS) Education Standards.

The Medical Response Unit shall be considered a Volunteer Medical Response Agency under the Florida State Statutes and shall be subject to appropriate regulation and protocol.

In the event of a major catastrophe the Medical Response Unit may act as directed by Emergency Management Administration protocols.

The Medical Response Unit shall serve as an emergency medical care education program for the FSU student volunteer members of the unit.

Use by Campus Organizations:
Any recognized student organization, academic department, or administrative department of FSU can request the services of the Medical Response Unit.

Campus organizations, academic departments, or administrative departments of FSU may not be charged for the services of the Medical Response Unit during any fiscal year in which A&S Fees have been allocated to the Medical Response Unit. Should cost associated with services exceed A&S Fees, cost recovery may be instituted by fees to campus departments/organizations though not including registered students.

The use of these services will be on a first-come, first-serve basis.

The Board of Directors reserves the right to refuse participation at any campus event.

Organization: The Medical Response Unit shall be governed by an Executive Director, a Director of Operations, an appointee from University Health Services, and a Board of Directors.

Executive Director:

Selection and Term of Office:

The Executive Director shall be chosen by the First Responder Unit Board of Directors. The Executive Director shall also be approved by the Medical Director, the Director of University Health Services and/or a designee, and the FSU Chief of Police and/or a designee.

The Executive Director’s term is one year period ending at the confirmation of the next Executive Director. The Board of Directors is responsible for the evaluation of the Director’s performance.

The Executive Director shall be forwarded to and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Title II of the Student Body Statutes before the spring inauguration.

Duties:

The Executive Director shall be responsible for the efficient and effective operation of the Affiliated Project.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for the management of the Affiliated Project’s budget and overall fundraising.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for the hiring and dismissal of all staff members. The Executive Director shall also be responsible for the comprehensive training set forth by the Board of Directors.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for ensuring that the Affiliated Project is in compliance with all guidelines outlined in Title VIII (Finance Code).

The Executive Director shall be responsible for executing all activities and programs of the Affiliated Project.

Director of Operations:

Selection of Term:

The Director of Operations shall be chosen by the Medical Response Unit Board of Directors. The Director of Operations shall also be approved by the Medical Director, the Director of University Health Services and/or a designee, and the FSU Chief of Police and/or a designee.

The Director of Operations’ term shall end at the appointment of the next Director of Operations.

Duties:

There shall be one Director of Operations. The Director of Operations shall be second in command of the Medical Response Unit.

The Director of Operations shall carry out the duties of the Executive Director in their absence.

The Director of Operations shall be responsible for all policies, procedures, and operations of the Medical Response Unit.

University Health Services Designee:

Duties:

The Instructor/Clinical Supervisor shall be selected by the University Health Services Director and shall ensure that the Medical Response Unit maintains compliance with all applicable local, state, and federal statutes and regulations.

The Instructor/Clinical Supervisor shall also maintain communication with all supporting and parallel agencies to include, but not be limited to Leon County EMS and any applicable state agencies.

The Instructor/Clinical Supervisor shall ensure all training and certification of all Medical Response Unit volunteers is in compliance with all applicable local, state, and federal statutes and regulations.

sections.heading: Chapter 1005 WVFS Radio Station
sections.text:
Purpose:

To provide diverse entertainment and information to the students of Florida State University and members of the surrounding community in a manner consistent with the college radio format.

To provide experience and training opportunities for students and members of the surrounding community in radio station operations.

To promote university and community activities in a manner consistent with station programming goals and Federal Communication Commission rules and regulations.

Campus Board of Directors:

Purpose: There shall be a campus-wide Board of Directors, hereinafter referred to as the Board of Directors, which shall serve as the liaison between station leadership and the Office of Student Affairs, the Student Government Association, and the affiliated school or college. The Board of Directors will establish its own criteria for meetings and its own rules of procedure. These rules of procedure shall be a policy pursuant to Chapter 416 and adoption or revision of this policy shall not require Senate approval

Powers and Duties: The Board of Directors shall have the responsibility of insuring that all station operating procedures meet Federal Communication Commission rules and regulations; shall handle appeals made by station personnel against decisions made by the state Executive Board consistent with the station bylaws; shall approve bylaws and amendments to bylaws recommended by the Executive Board, shall have final approval over paid/OPS recommendations from the Station Executive Board; and shall make suggestions for new projects and programming.

Composition:

The Board of Directors shall consist of seven members (7), four (4) of whom will be students at Florida State University and three members of the FSU faculty/staff.

The student members shall consist of the Student Body President or a designee, the Student Senate President or a designee, the station Program Director and an elected member of the station Executive Board.

The three faculty/staff members shall include the Dean of the affiliated school or college and a designee, the Advisor appointed by the affiliated school or college, and the Vice President for Student Affairs or a designee.

Term of Office:

The Student Body President and the Student Senate President or their designees shall serve on the board during their terms of elected office.

The Program Director shall serve on the Board during the program director’s tenure of office.

The elected member of the radio station Executive Board shall serve for a period of one (1) year from the time of the election. If the individual is unable to complete their term the Executive Board shall select a replacement no less than two (2) weeks from the announcement of the resignation or removal of the sitting member.

Minutes: 
All Board of Director meetings minutes shall be taken by an appointed member of the Board in accordance with the Board’s rules of procedure. Copies of the minutes will be provided to the membership no later than two (2) weeks after each meeting. A copy of each meeting’s minutes shall be submitted to the Office of Student Governance and Advocacy for public inspection and shall be placed in the WVFS public file as mandated by the FCC.

Advisor:

Adoption: There shall be a faculty/staff advisor appointed by the affiliated school or college who shall serve at the discretion of the leadership of the college, school or department from which the advisor is appointed.

Powers and Duties:

To ensure that all federal, state and local laws and guidelines are followed in all station operations and to report on any and all FCC issues to the Vice President for Student Affairs.

To design and administer any and all academic programs associated with the station.

To represent the interests of the affiliated college or school to the station Executive Board.

To perform any additional functions, powers, and duties outlined in the station bylaws and policy manual.

To suggest and assist in implementing any new areas of programming that the Executive Board has approved.

Station Executive Board:

Purpose: There shall be a Station Executive Board, hereinafter referred to as the Executive Board, which shall be responsible for determining rules and policies to meet radio programming needs, daily operation requirements, staff management and making recommendation to the Board of Directors for the filling of all paid OPS positions. The Executive Board shall create all of the internal bylaws and policies for the station and make these recommendations to the Board of Directors for final approval. The Executive Board shall decide on and implement any changes or additions to radio station programming and shall work with the Advisor to implement the academic programs and ensure FCC compliance requirements.

Composition:

The Executive Board shall consist of the following members: the station Program Director, the Advisor, and the heads of all the station departments established in the station bylaws.

The Student Body President or a designee and the Student Senate President or a designee shall serve as non-voting ex-officio members of the Executive Board.

Operations:

Station Policy: Station policy shall be established by the respective department heads of each station department and approved by the Executive Board. Station policy will be recorded in the station policy manual and station bylaws.

Operations: Station operations will be conducted by student and community volunteers trained in the proper procedures and supervised by the heads of each department, the Executive Board, the Advisor, and the Board of Directors.

Facilities: he station will operate in the space provided and maintained by the Florida State University.

sections.heading: Chapter 1006 The Campus Recreation Board
sections.text:
All rules and policies pertaining to the Campus Recreation Board must be consistent with pertinent State law, University policies and procedures, and with A&S Fee Guidelines.

This act shall be called the "Campus Recreation Board Act of 1995," hereinafter referred to as the "Campus Recreation Board Act."

Establishment of the Campus Recreation Board: The Campus Recreation Board, hereinafter referred to as the Recreation Board, provide students, faculty, and staff with activities and programs and services to be offered through the Bobby E. Leach Recreation Center and other campus recreation facilities. The Recreation Board shall represent the University community and assure that facilities, services, and amenities shall be offered as necessary or convenient in order to meet the needs and interests of the University community.

Election of the Campus Recreation Board:
The Recreation Board shall consist of twelve (12) members, eight (8) of whom shall be students elected by the Student Body. Four (4) members shall be appointed by the University President. The Recreation Board shall elect by a majority vote a Chair and Vice Chair.  The Chair shall be a student member of the Recreation Board. The Chair shall vote only in the case of a tie. Employees of the Campus Recreation Department may serve as non-voting, ex-officio members of the Recreation Board and the Selection Commission.

All interested students will be able to apply for a position on the ballot following the attendance of a mandatory candidate meeting. All applications are to be reviewed and verified by the Supervisor of Elections for eligibility pursuant to this chapter. All confirmed candidates will be put on the ballot.
Candidacy for Campus Recreation Board Membership

The Campus Recreation Board shall publicly advertise openings for student members of the Campus Recreation Board for the fall elections. This shall be done a minimum of ten (10) business days preceding the fall elections.
The Campus Recreation Board shall coordinate interest meetings for all interested applicants to learn about the responsibilities of the Campus Recreation Board. All applicants must attend an interest meeting in order to qualify for candidacy.
The Chair of the Campus Recreation Board shall forward a list of those who attended the interest meeting to the Supervisor of Elections two (2) business days before the filing deadline.
All candidates who file with the Supervisor of Elections for the Campus Recreation Board, must attend an orientation meeting pursuant to 704.2.

Terms of Office: The terms of office for the student members of the Recreation Board shall be for one (1) year or until their successors are elected and confirmed, except in the case of an appointment to fill a vacancy, in which case the appointment shall be for the unexpired term.

Student members of the Recreation Board may be removed for cause at any time in accordance with the provisions of Student Body Statutes, Section 405(1).

The Chair and Vice Chair of the Recreation Board:
The election for Chair and Vice Chair shall be conducted during each Fall semester. The Chair and Vice Chair of the Recreation Board may be removed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Recreation Board.

The Chair shall call and preside over all meetings and general business of the Recreation Board and shall act as the Recreation Board spokesperson. The Chair shall appoint all committees of the Recreation Board. The Chair shall attend all staff meetings of the Campus Recreation Board.

The Vice Chair shall perform the duties of the Chair in the Chair's absence and perform other duties delegated by the Chair of the Recreation Board.

Members of the Recreation Board shall receive no compensation from the Campus Recreation Department or from A&S Fees for the performance of their duties as members of the Recreation Board.

In the case of a vacancy on the Campus Recreation Board, the Chair will publish the vacancy and application window, and hold one interest meeting, while the window is open. The application window must be open for ten (10) business days, and must be opened within one (1) business day of the Campus Recreation Board being notified of the vacancy.  

The Campus Recreation Board shall conduct interviews with all those who applied. At least three (3) Campus Recreation Board members must be present during all interviews. Interviews must be conducted within five (5) business days of closing the application window.  

The Campus Recreation Board will then meet within seven (7) days and choose a new member at the discretion of the Board to be sworn in at their next meeting.

Organization of the Recreation Board:
The Recreation Board shall adopt bylaws for its organization, administration, and procedures.

Ex-Officio Members:

The Student Body President or a designee, the Student Senate President or a designee, and the Recreation Director shall be ex-officio, non-voting members of the Recreation Board. The Recreation Board may appoint additional ex-officio, non-voting members to the Recreation Board as deemed necessary.

The Recreation Board shall meet no less than once each month. Meetings of the Recreation Board shall be publicly advertised at least twenty-four (24) hours prior to the meeting. No meeting may be held with less than a quorum present.

Powers and Duties of the Recreation Board:

The Recreation Board is primarily responsible for the establishing and developing of rules and policies which will ensure the operation and maintenance of the Campus Recreation facilities and programs in a coordinated, efficient, and effective manner.

The Campus Recreation Board shall:

Review individual departments and organization budgets.

Assess the effectiveness of programs, services, and activities.

Upon allocation by the Student Senate of A&S request, the Recreation Board shall authorize the A&S funds to the appropriate Campus Recreation budgets and any amendments.

Approve all non-student use of the Bobby E. Leach Student Recreation Center.

Serve in an advisory capacity to all program heads.

sections.heading: Chapter 1007 Office Of Inter-Residence Hall Councils
sections.text:
Creation, Purpose and Mission:

Creation: This act shall create an affiliated project of the Student Government Association known as the "Inter-Residence Hall Councils."

Purpose: The purpose of the Inter-Residence Hall Council is to coordinate programs and activities for the enhancement of student life in the residence halls, to represent the views of residents, and to enhance communication between residence halls. This is achieved through campus-wide programming and the creation and governance of Hall Councils, individual leadership boards of elected students with each residence hall complex.

The mission of the Inter-Residence Hall Council is to engage students in the on-campus living experience through leadership development, community involvement, and peer advocacy.

Membership:

Any student of a Florida State University residence hall is eligible to be a member-at-large of IRHC.

Executive Officers: Any member elected in the Spring by the individual Board of Director members and/or a designee.

Board of Directors: The vice presidents of each Hall Council that serve as representatives.

If there is no current hall government vice president available to represent their hall, the Hall Council President will serve as a temporary board member until the Vice President position is filled.

Hall Councils: Any member elected in the fall by each individual residence hall complex population. Elections are run by the Executive Officers.

Board of Directors:

Composition of the Board:

The Vice President(s) of each Residence Hall shall serve on the Board.

The President of the National Residence Hall Honorary will also be a non-voting member of the Board.

The Sustainable Campus liaison for the Inter-Residence Hall Council will also be a non-voting member of the Board.

Any student who is an officer of the Florida Association of Residence Halls (FARH), the South Atlantic Affiliate of College and University Residence Halls (SAACURH), or the National Association of College and University Residence Halls (NACURH) shall be an ex-officio non-voting member of the Board.

The IRHC Advisor(s) or a designee shall be an ex-officio non-voting member of the Board. That individual shall be appointed by the Associate Director for Residence Life.

The following shall be the Executive Officers of IRHC:

Director

Associate Director

National Communication Coordinator

Assistant Director of Finance

Assistant Director of Operations

Assistant Director of Marketing and Outreach

During the summer semester, only the Executive officers will act as a voting members of IRHC.

During the summer semester, in lieu of Board members’ absence, a majority vote of all Board members present is necessary to approve all expenditures provided the expenditures are also approved by the advisor.

Powers and Duties of the Board:

Executive Officers shall:

Chair standing committees in accordance with the IRHC By-Laws.

By majority vote, call emergency meetings or cancel a scheduled meeting (with at least twenty-four (24) hours’ notice).

Serve a one-year term. Any Executive Officers may be re-nominated at the end of office and may be re-elected for additional terms of office.

Be responsible for all duties outlined in the Inter-Residence Hall Council bylaws.

Board members shall:

Have the authority to pass any rules or regulations which is deemed necessary and proper for the efficient operation of the IRHC and which are in accordance with the SGA Constitution, IRHC By-Laws, and the Student Body Statutes.

Have the power to amend the IRHC By-Laws by a majority vote.

Have the power to remove any Board member(s) in accordance with the SGA Constitution and IRHC By-Laws.

All powers not explicitly enumerated to the executive officers shall be reserved by the Board of Directors as a whole.

Unless specifically mentioned otherwise, the executive officers will have the ability to vote as a member of the Board of Directors on all matters presented before the Board.

Meeting:

The Board shall meet at least once a week except during the summer semester.

Meetings may be called by the Director or at the request of a majority of the Board.

Board members shall be notified of all meetings at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance of the designated meeting time.

No official action may be taken unless at least a quorum and the advisor are present.

The Assistant Director of Operations shall ensure that minutes are taken of all meetings. A file containing the minutes of all past meetings shall be maintained.

The Executive Board:

Selection and Term of Office:

Voting on the Executive Board shall be done by the Board of Directors. All IRHC members are eligible and election of the Executive Board shall take place no later than the first week of April.

The Executive Board shall serve a one year term. Any Executive Board member may be re-nominated at the end of the term of office and may be re-elected for a second term of office.
The Director of the Inter-Residence Hall Councils shall be appointed by the Student Body President in consultation with the entities’ preference and confirmed by the Student Senate.

 Powers and Duties: The Director shall:
Chair the Board and preside over all IRHC meetings and be entitled to vote only in the case of a tie.

Be responsible for the efficient organization of the office.

Make and execute decisions on policy, programs, and activities of IRHC with the advice of the Board.

Officially act for and represent IRHC.

Be responsible for requests and expenditures of Student Activity and Service Fee allocations.

Call meetings of IRHC at least forty-eight (48) hours in advance.

Have the authority to establish ad hoc committees and select a chair for said committees.

Be an ex-officio member for all standing committees.

Have the authority to appoint all staff members.

Adopt rules of procedure for IRHC meetings. These rules of procedure shall be considered a policy pursuant to Chapter 421 and adoption or revision of this policy shall not require Senate approval.

Be confirmed by the Student Body President and Senate.

Removal from Office:

Board of Directors: All Board members and Executive Officers, with the exception of the Director are subject to impeachment at any time by the Board of Directors in accordance with the SGA Constitution and IRHC By-Laws.

Director: The Board may, by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of its members, recommend the removal of the Director.

Staff: The Director shall have the authority to dismiss staff members at their discretion.

Vacancies:

Board of Directors: If a position of the Board is vacated less than four (4) weeks before elections of officers, the Director shall appoint a replacement to serve until the elections. The appointment is subject to the approval of the Board by a majority vote. If a position on the Board is vacated more than four (4) weeks before elections of officers, a new election shall be held.

Director: If the Office of Director is vacated, the Associate Director shall assume the office.

If the Associate Director is unable to permanently assume the position of the Director, the vacancy can be held, subject to the provisions in Section 1007(7)(a).
Compensation and Conflict of Interest Restrictions
Any member of the IRHC Executive Board who receives any form of financial subsidy, remuneration, or compensation from University Housing shall be ineligible to hold any position that receives OPS wages from the Student Government Association.
No member of the IRHC Executive Board who concurrently serves as a Student Senator or holds any other Major Office within the Student Government Association, as defined in Chapter 100.5(C) of the Student Body Statutes, may vote on or otherwise participate in official action on any matter directly related to the Inter-Residence Hall Council.
Violations of this section shall constitute a conflict of interest under Chapter 205, “Code of Ethics,” and shall be subject to penalties prescribed therein.

sections.heading: Chapter 1008 Student Union Board
sections.text:
All rules and policies pertaining to the Student Union Board must be consistent with pertinent state law, university policies and procedures, and the A&S Guidelines.

This act shall be called the "Student Union Board Reform Act of 2006."

Establishment of the Union Board: The Union Board, hereinafter referred to as the Union Board, is established to provide students, faculty, and staff with activities, programs, and services to be offered through the Student Union Complex. The Union Board shall represent the University community to ensure that the facilities, services, and amenities offered by the Student Union Complex meet the needs and interests of their constituents.

Union Board Membership:
The Union Board shall consist of seventeen (17) voting members.

Twelve (12) voting members shall be students approved by the Union Board Selection Commission according to Section 1008(4) and elected by the student body in the Spring Student Government Elections.

The remaining five (5) voting members shall be appointed by the University President or designee.

Ex-Officio Members:
The Student Body President or a designee, the Student Senate President or a designee, and the Director of the Student Union shall be ex-officio, non-voting members of the Union Board. The Union Board may appoint additional ex-officio, non-voting members to the Board as deemed necessary.

Terms of Office:
The terms of office for the student members of the Union Board shall be for one year or until their successors are elected and confirmed except in the case of an appointment to fill a vacancy, in which case the appointment shall be for the remainder of the unexpired term.

The terms of office for voting members appointed by the University President shall be established in the Union Board bylaws.

Ex-officio, non-voting members, appointed by the Board, may serve on the Union Board for as long as the Board shall see fit.

Student members of the Union Board may be removed for cause at any time in accordance with the provisions of Student Body Statutes Section 405(3).

Candidacy for Union Board Membership:
The Union Board shall publicly advertise openings for student members of the Union Board for the spring elections. This shall be done a minimum of ten (10) business days preceding the spring elections.

The Union Board shall coordinate interest meetings for all interested applicants to learn about the responsibilities of the Union Board. All applicants must attend an interest meeting in order to qualify for candidacy.

The Chair of the Union Board shall forward a list of those who attended the interest meeting to the Supervisor of Elections two (2) business days before the filing deadline.

All candidates who file with the Supervisor of Elections for the Union Board, must attend an orientation meeting pursuant to Section 704(2).

Election of Student Union Board Members:
The names of the forwarded candidates shall be placed on the ballot pending an official declaration of candidacy. This provision may be altered pending conditions pursuant to Section 1008(4)(d).

Organization of the Union Board:
The Union Board shall adopt bylaws and rules for its organization, administration and procedures.

Election of Union Board Leadership:

The Union Board shall elect a Chair and a Vice Chair, both being a student member of the Board.

The election for Chair and Vice Chair of the Union Board shall be conducted at the beginning of each new session after the Spring election and upon the departure of the existing chair and vice chair.

The election method and guidelines shall be established within the Union Board Policy Manual.

Duties of the Union Board Leadership:

The Union Board Chair shall:

Call and preside over all meeting and general business of the Union Board.

Act as the spokesperson for the Union Board policies and interests.

Appoint all members of the Union Board committees.

Appoint all liaison positions to the Student Union complex’s departments and subsidiaries.

Attend all Student Union complex staff meetings.

The Chair may only vote on general Union Board business in the case of a tie.

The Chair shall also perform any other duties delegated by a majority vote of the Union Board, which do not violate any standing Student Government or Union Board policies and/or Statutes.

The Vice Chair shall:

Perform the duties of the Chair in the Chair’s absence.

Perform other duties delegated by the Chair of the Union Board and/or according to the Union Board bylaws.

Committees of the Union Board:
The Union Board may establish committees.
The Union Board Chair shall appoint all committee members. Members of such committees may include ex-officio, non-voting individuals who are not members of the Union Board.

The Chair and Vice Chair of the Union Board may be removed by a two-thirds vote of the Board.

The Union Board shall meet not less than once each month. Meetings of the Board shall be publicly advertised at least twenty four hours (24) prior to each meeting. Meetings held without quorum cannot feature votes.

The Powers and Duties of the Union Board:
Determine policies, program services, activities, amenities, and facilities to be offered by the Student Union Board and throughout the Student Union Complex.

Participate in the budgetary process for all Union departments such as:

Review individual department and subsidiary budgets.

Assess the effectiveness of program services, activities, and amenities and facilities.

Present a budget request and justification for all Union departments and subsidiaries to the Student Senate each fiscal year as well as any supplemental requests.

Upon allocation by the Senate of the A&S Fee request, the Union Board shall authorize the A&S Fee funds, in addition to self-generated revenues to the appropriate Union budget and any amendments.

Allocate all space in the Student Union complex in accordance with Union Board and University Policy.

Serve in an advisory capacity to all departments and subsidiaries within the Student Union Complex.

Vacancy in Union Board Membership:
In the case of a vacancy on the Union Board, the Union Board Chair will publish the vacancy and application window, and hold one interest meeting, while the window is open.  The application window must be open for ten (10) business days and must be opened within one (1) business day of the Union Board being notified of the vacancy.

The Union Board shall conduct interviews with all those who applied. At least three (3) Union Board members must be present during all interviews. Interviews must be conducted within five (5) business days of closing the application window.

The Union Board will then meet within seven (7) days and vote on each candidate in a manner set in the Union Board Policy Manual. The selected member will be sworn in at the next scheduled meeting of the Union Board.

sections.heading: Chapter 1009 Office Of The Student Council For Undergraduate Research And Creativity
sections.text:
Creation and Purpose:

Creation: This act shall create a council under the Student Government Association known as the Student Council for Undergraduate Research and Creativity (SCURC).

Purpose:

SCURC shall implement and oversee the Florida State University Undergraduate Research Journal, The Owl, as a means to engage the student body and highlight student research.

SCURC shall strive to increase the number of students engaged in research projects at Florida State University.

SCURC shall serve as a resource for undergraduate students to request funding to attend or present at academic conferences related to their intended research area or creative pursuit.

Membership: Participation is open to students at the Florida State University.

Board of Directors:

Purpose: There shall be an executive board of SCURC to advise the Director on ways to enhance the operation and effectiveness of the Bureau.

Membership:

The Board of Directors shall consist of seven (7) members all of whom shall be students at the Florida State University.

The voting members will consist of the Executive Director, the Deputy Director, four (4) Branch Directors, and the Treasurer.

Composition: The Board of Directors shall meet no less than once a month. The Board of Directors shall be composed of the following members:

Executive Director of SCURC
Deputy Director of SCURC

Director of Scholarship and Grants

Director of Advising

Director of Publications

Director of Outreach
Treasurer
Powers and Duties: The Board shall:

Advertise the funding opportunity for presentations and attendance at academic conferences.

Serve as the decision-making board for SCURC.

Plan and execute general body meetings for SCURC members.

Ensure the success of SCURC and its publications.

Meetings:

The Board of Directors members shall hold a minimum of one (1) meeting per month during the academic year.

Additional meetings shall be scheduled as needed.

Those Board members directly responsible for outreach shall hold a minimum of one (1) meeting at the start of the Fall and Spring semesters.

Direct and frequent communications with the directors shall be maintained by these Board members throughout the semester to ensure efficiency and accountability.

Executive Director:

Selection and Term of Office:
The Director’s position shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Section 202(1)(a).

The Director’s term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties:
The Executive Director shall conduct Board of Directors meetings on a regular basis.

The Executive Director shall serve as a liaison between SGA and SCURC.

The Executive Director shall oversee the application process for the Board of Directors, Publication Staff, and Committee Members, and delegate their tasks and duties.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for the overall efficiency, effectiveness, and operations of SCURC.
Deputy Director

Selection and Term of Office

The position of Deputy Director shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Chapter 202.1 A.

The Deputy Director's term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties
In the absence or resignation of the Executive Director, the Deputy Director shall assume all duties and responsibilities of the Executive Director. In such cases, the Deputy Director shall be given priority in filling the Director’s position. During the absence or removal of the Executive Director, the Deputy Director shall serve as Acting Executive Director until a new director is appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Section 202(1)(a).
The Deputy Director shall be responsible for taking minutes at all official meetings and ensuring they are accurately recorded and distributed in a timely manner.
The Deputy Director shall manage and maintain records of all SCURC activities, ensuring proper documentation and archiving of important documents.
The Deputy Director shall serve as a liaison between SCURC and other student organizations, fostering partnerships and collaborative initiatives.
Director of Scholarship and Grants

Selection and Term of Office
The position of Director of Scholarship and Grants shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Chapter 202.1 A.
The Director of Scholarship and Grants’ term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties
Lead the Scholarships and Grants Branch, ensuring all activities align with the mission and goals of SCURC.
Ensure that the review and selection of recipients are completed within four (4) weeks of submission.
Monitor the use of awarded funds to ensure they are utilized appropriately and effectively.
Lead and manage committee members, assigning tasks related to reviewing applications, developing criteria, and managing communication.
Complete two publicly posted office hours per week to assist applicants and recipients and address any inquiries.
Regularly report to the SCURC Board of Directors on the status of the scholarship and grant programs.
Director of Advising

Selection and Term of Office
The position of Director of Advising shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Chapter 202.1 A.
The Director of Advising’s term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties
Lead the Advising Branch, coordinating all advising activities to ensure quality support for student researchers.
Develop and implement strategies to improve the advising services provided to students.
Organize workshops on research methodology, writing, presentation skills, and navigating professional research relationships.
Lead and manage committee members, assigning tasks related to advising sessions, workshops, and resource development.
Complete two publicly posted office hours per week to assist students and address any inquiries.
Regularly report to the SCURC Board of Directors on the status of the advising programs and services.

Director of Publications

Selection and Term of Office
The position of Director of Publications shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Chapter 202.1 A.
The Director of Publications’ term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties

Lead the Publications Branch, overseeing all activities and ensuring alignment with SCURC’s mission and goals.
Manage the publications of the branch.
Work directly with Editors-in-Chief (EICs) to solicit, review, and select research articles and other content for publication.
Lead and manage committee members, assigning tasks related to editing, reviewing, and contributing to publications.
Complete two publicly posted office hours per week to assist authors and address any inquiries related to publications.
Coordinate with Managing Editors (MEs) to ensure all content meets publication standards and deadlines.
Regularly report to the SCURC Board of Directors on the status of the publications and any issues that arise.
Director of Outreach

Selection and Term of Office
The position of Director of Outreach shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Chapter 202.1 A.
The Director of Outreach’s term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties
Lead the Outreach Branch, developing and implementing outreach plans to increase awareness of SCURC and its resources.
Organize events and campaigns to engage with the student body and promote research opportunities.
Coordinate logistics for events, including scheduling, promotion, and participant engagement.
Collaborate with other organizations and departments to extend SCURC’s reach and enhance outreach efforts.
Lead and manage committee members, assigning tasks related to planning and executing outreach activities.
Complete two publicly posted office hours per week to assist students and address any inquiries related to outreach.
Develop and implement strategies to increase awareness of SCURC and its resources through social media, newsletters, and other communication channels.
Regularly report to the SCURC Board of Directors on the status of outreach activities and any issues that arise.

Treasurer:

Selection:

The treasurer’s position shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Section 202(1)(a).

The treasurer’s term shall end at the end of the Spring semester.

Power and Duties: 
The treasurer shall:

Be financially certified with the Student Government Association Accounting Office.

Formulate, organize and effectively communicate a budget for SCURC through the Student Government Association.

Review all undergraduate funding applications for conferences and grant approval upon qualification and availability of funds.

Work with the advisor to approve or deny applications based on the qualification requirements, available funds, and adhere to the Finance Code.

Be responsible for turning in all receipts and documentation to the SGA Accounting Offices within the time restraints.

Work with the advisor to ensure fiscal responsibility with granting funds.

Grant funds based on a first come, first serve basis.

Make sure all funding adheres to the Finance Code.

The Undergraduate Academic Conference funding applications shall adhere to the following qualifications and guidelines:

Completed applications must be turned in at least thirty (30) business days before the conference; must include FSUID and be registered as a FSU undergraduate student at the time of the conference; provide verification of any additional financial support and a breakdown of anticipated expenses.

For a conference presentation grant, the student must be a primary presenter and provide proof of acceptance to the conference and a faculty signature endorsing attendance at the conference.

For a conference attendance grant, the student must provide a faculty signature endorsing attendance at the conference.

Funding applications shall be distributed by reimbursement processes; all receipts must be turned in within thirty (30) days of the conference; and failure to do so will cause your grant to be cancelled.

Funding applications shall be available online. Applications shall adhere to the applications instructions for guidance on submission.

Academic conference funding shall be divided into two (2) periods per fiscal year.

Applicants shall be notified in a timely manner of their status of funding and will be recorded for the University’s records, in order to promote Florida State University’s academic accomplishments.
Branches

Scholarship and Grants Branch

Structure

Director of Scholarship and Grants

Leads the branch, oversees all activities, and ensures alignment with SCURC's mission and goals.

Must complete two weekly publicly posted office hours per week.

Committee Members (4)

The Executive Director shall recommend four (4) committee members to the Student Body President for appointment.
Assist the Director in reviewing applications, developing criteria, and managing communication with applicants and recipients.
Committee Meetings
The branch must meet wholly once per month to review progress, discuss new applications, and address any issues related to scholarships and grants.

Responsibilities
Administer and oversee the awarding of scholarships and grants to student researchers.
Develop criteria and application processes for scholarships and grants. Current criteria used for all application processes must be posted on the University-designated student organization management platform.
Review and select recipients for funding opportunities. Reviews of grants must be completed within four (4) weeks of submission. Disbursement must be submitted by that time.
Ensure proper use and reporting of funds by recipients.

Advising Branch

Structure

Director of Grants
Leads the branch, coordinates advising activities, and ensures students receive quality support.
Must complete two publicly posted office hours per week.
Committee Members (4)
The Executive Director shall recommend four (4) committee members to the Student Body President for appointment.
Consist of experienced researchers and faculty who provide advising and support to students.
Committee Meetings
The branch must meet wholly once per month to review progress, discuss new applications, and address any issues related to advising.
Responsibilities
Provide guidance and support to student researchers throughout their research projects or their entry into undergraduate research.
Offer one-on-one advising sessions, workshops, and resources for research methodology, writing, presentation skills, and navigating professional research relationships.
Help students identify research opportunities and navigate the research process, including intern/externships, publication pathways, and more.

Publications Branch
Structure
Director of Publications
Leads the branch, oversees the editorial process, and ensures timely publication of journals.
Must complete two publicly posted office hours per week.
Editor-in-Chiefs (EIC)
There shall be one (1) EIC per journal published by the SCURC. They will work directly under the Director of Publications.
Managing Editor (ME)
There shall be one (1) ME per journal published by the SCURC.
Responsible for managing content editors and acting as quality assurance for each respective journal.
Works directly under their respective Editor-in-Chief.
Committee Members (4)
The Executive Director shall recommend four (4) committee members to the Student Body President for appointment.
Serve as editors, reviewers, and contributors for the publications.
Committee Meetings
The branch must meet wholly once per month to review progress, discuss new applications, and
address any issues related to publications.
Responsibilities
Solicit, review, and select research articles and other content for publication.
Maintain contact with authors and coauthors, including notification based on review.
Establish clear criteria for all public posting.
Ensure the quality and academic integrity of all published materials.

Outreach Branch

Structure

Director of Outreach

Leads the branch, develops outreach plans, and oversees execution.
Must complete two publicly posted office hours per week.
Committee Members (4)
The Executive Director shall recommend four (4) committee members to the Student Body President for appointment.
Assist in planning and executing outreach activities, managing social media, and engaging with the community.
Committee Meetings
The branch must meet wholly once per month to review progress, discuss new applications, and address any issues related to outreach.
Responsibilities
Develop and implement strategies to increase awareness of SCURC and its resources.
Organize events and campaigns to engage with the student body and promote research opportunities.
Collaborate with other organizations and departments to extend SCURC’s reach.

Removal from Office: The Board may recommend removal of any of its members or directors by a two-thirds (2/3) vote. Removal of any bureau officer must comply with relevant Student Body Statutes or by impeachment from the Student Senate.

Vacancies: Vacancies shall be filled by the original process, and the person filling the vacancy shall serve the remainder of the term of office.
