sections.heading: Chapter 1010 Office Of The Mental Health Council
sections.text:
Creation and Purpose:
Creation: This act shall be called the Student Government Association Mental Health Council (MHC).

Purpose:

The purpose of the MHC is to increase dialogue about mental health issues through education and awareness initiatives.

The vision of the MHC is to advocate for the Florida State University’s student body access to mental health resources.

The MHC will work with Florida State University’s Counseling Center to create programming and provide resources that prioritize mental health issues and promote open positive dialogue in an effort to encourage outlets of support.

Mission: The mission of the mental health council is to empower students with mental health resources through de-stigmatization, community involvement, and advocacy.

Powers and Duties

The MHC shall be authorized to create policies and/or procedures, subject to review and approval by the Student Senate, to facilitate the implementation of its services and programs.

Mental Health and Safety Manual:

The MHC shall be required to produce a Mental Health and Safety Manual for the purpose of acquainting students with the wellness resources available on campus.

MHC shall be authorized to produce additional print and/or digital materials to promote and ensure the accessibility of the Mental Health and Safety Manual throughout the campus community. 

MHC shall regularly update the Mental Health and Safety Manual to ensure the accuracy of the information provided therein.

MHC shall make a presentation to the Student Senate and invite the Congress of Graduate Students  once per semester to raise awareness of the Mental Health and Safety Manual and to report on any recent updates thereto.

Optional Mental Health Certification:

MHC is authorized to create an optional certification program to indicate a students’ awareness of wellness resources on campus.

Any certification program created and offered under this Section shall be made accessible to all students via Canvas or any similar online learning management system utilized by the University .

Nothing in this Section shall be construed to indicate or imply that a student is considered a mental health professional, or is otherwise qualified to provide mental health services, by virtue of their participation in any Mental Health Certification program as described herein.

Membership:

Participation is open to all students, faculty, and staff at Florida State University.

Board of Directors:

Purpose: There shall be a Board of Directors, hereinafter referred to as the Board, which shall be responsible for determining policies dealing with the programming and activities of the Mental Health Council in conjunction with the MHC advisor.

The MHC will work with the University Counseling Center and will not provide medical advice or portray themselves as licensed clinical professionals.

Membership of the Board: The members will consist of the seven (7) Executive Board members, limited to: the Executive Director, the Deputy Executive Director, the Director of Outreach, the Director of Programming, the Secretary, the Director of Finance, and the Director of Marketing.

Powers and Duties of the Board:

The Board will work to survey a diverse population of students to gain insight on concerns and opinions relevant to the mission of the office.

The Board will plan, coordinate, and execute programs and campaigns that provide education, resources, and a comfortable environment for students in conjunction with Florida State University’s Counseling Center.

The Board will work with other members of the Student Government Association in ways to advocate for the mental health of students within Florida State’s Student Body.

Mental Health Certification Requirement for Board Members: upon such time as the MHC may implement a mental health certification program as authorized by §915.2(c), all Board members shall be required to pass the mental health certification exam within thirty (30) days of their confirmation.

Meetings:

The Board shall meet at least twice a month. A report of this meeting shall be issued to the Executive and Legislative branches of the SGA. This report shall be given during the messages portion of the Senate Calendar.

All Board members shall be notified 48 hours in advance of any meeting.

The Director or Deputy Executive Director shall be in attendance at all meetings of the Board.

Executive Director:

Selection and Term of Office:

The Director will select seven (7) Board of Directors. Positions for the Board of Directors must be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before filled.

The Executive Director term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties:

The Executive Director of the MHC shall be responsible for conducting a formal interview process for a Deputy Executive Director, and a Director of Outreach, and Director of Finance and forwarding candidates to the Student Body President for appointment.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for the effective operations of the MHC. This shall include the supervision of the Board, planning of annual campaign strategies for further student involvement, and providing direct service to the student body in conjunction with the University Counseling Center/Department of Health and Wellness.

The Executive Director shall have the authority to form committees in support of the completion of specific tasks related to the operations of the MHC.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for the management of the council’s budget with approval of the MHC Board of Directors.

The Executive Director shall be responsible for seeing that the affiliate is in compliance with all guidelines outlined in Title VIII (Finance Code).

The Executive Director shall meet twice a month with the MHC Advisor to coordinate future programming for the MHC.

Deputy Executive Director:

Selection and Term of Office:

The position of Deputy Executive Director shall be advertised for at least two (2)	weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Section 202(1)(a).

The Deputy Executive Director term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties:

The Deputy Executive Director shall be responsible for aiding the Director and shall fulfill the duties of the Director in the Director’s absence.

Deputy Executive Director should oversee internal operations of MHC such as supervising the board of directors.

Director of Outreach:

Selection:

Forwarding of candidates for the Director of Outreach (DO) position shall be in compliance with Student Body Statutes Sections 202(1), 304(2), and 304(3).

The Director of Outreach will serve as a direct liaison between the Executive Branch and the Legislative Branch of SGA. The Director of Outreach will recommend legislation on behalf of the Executive Branch and work with Student Senators to give Executive insight to mental health initiatives.

The Director of Outreach will focus on the on-campus initiatives of the MHC, as well as the training and placement of students interested in mental health advocacy.

The Director of Outreach term shall end at the close of the Spring semester.

Powers and Duties: The Director of Outreach and the Deputy Executive Director shall assist the Executive Director in the effective operation of the MHC.

Director of Finance:

Selection and Term of Office:

The Director of Finance position shall be advertised for at least two (2) weeks before interviews may be conducted. The applicants shall be interviewed and then appointed by the Student Body President and confirmed by the Student Senate in accordance with Section 202(1).

The Director of Finance term shall end at the end of the Spring semester.

Power and Duties:

The Director of Finance shall:

Be financially certified with the Student Government Association Accounting Office.

Formulate, organize and effectively communicate a budget for MHC through the Student Government Association.

Work with the advisor to approve or deny applications based on the qualification requirements, available funds, and adhere to the Finance Code.

Be responsible for turning in all receipts and documentation to the SGA Accounting Offices within the time restraints.

Work with the advisor to ensure fiscal responsibility with granting funds.

Grant funds based on a first come, first serve basis.

Advisor: The Director of the Florida State University’s Counseling Center will serve as the advisor for the affiliate.

Removal from Office: The Board may recommend removal of any of its members or the Executive Director by a two-thirds (2/3) vote. Removal of any affiliate officer shall occur only in accordance with Chapter 405 of the Student Body Statutes or by impeachment from the Student Senate.

Vacancies: Vacancies shall be filled by the original process, and the person filling the vacancy shall serve the remainder of the term of office.

NOTE: Student Senate Bill #77-029 renumbered former Chapter 915, Student Body Statutes ("The Office of the Mental Health Council") to a new Chapter 1114. However, Chapter 1114 had already been created by Bill #77-028; accordingly, the chapter titled "The Office of the Mental Health Council" is numbered as Chapter 1117.

sections.heading: Chapter 1011 The SGA Cooperative Collection At FSU Libraries
sections.text:
Purpose:
The SGA Cooperative Collection at FSU Libraries shall ensure student access to resources, materials, and equipment which promote academic success, student well-being, campus engagement, and recreation. This affiliated project is a partnership between the Student Government Association and the Florida State University Libraries.
Structure
The SGA Cooperative Collection at FSU Libraries will function as an ongoing collection development partnership aimed at supplementing FSU Libraries’ Collection Development Policy to better support the acquision and circulation of non-traditional library materials for several key collections.
Collections may include, but are not limited to:
Permanent Course Reserves Collection (e.g. textbooks and test prep materials)
Scholar Support Collection (office supplies, whiteboard markers, headphones, phone chargers, etc.)
Circulating Technology Collection (laptops, calculators, DSLR cameras, etc.)
The Leisure Library (see 1011.6)
Other collections as established in partnership with University Libraries and approved by the Student Senate and SGA leadership. All items purchased with SGA funds will be branded as such.
Oversight and Operations:
The SGA Cooperative Collection at FSU Libraries shall be jointly overseen by the Student Government Association and University Libraries.
The Student Senate shall designate one (1) Liaison to the Cooperative Collection who shall:
Act as the primary SGA point of contact.
Submit at least one (1) report per semester to the Student Senate on usage, student feedback, and expansion opportunities.
Collaborate with University Libraries and SGA leadership to sustain and improve operations.
Circulation, lending, and item management shall be conducted by University Libraries staff under standard library procedures.
Rental Process:
University Libraries shall manage general lending procedures (checkout durations, penalties, replacement fees).
Collection-specific rules and sub-regulations may be established through Senate Resolution, jointly developed with University Libraries, with affirmative signature of the Head of Access Services & Delivery at FSU Libraries, or equivalent position.
Funding and Fiscal Responsibility:
The SGA Cooperative Collection at FSU Libraries shall have a dedicated annual budget category within the SGA budget.
Within this category, there shall be line items for each collection (e.g., Permanent Course Reserves Collection, Scholar Support Collection, Circulating Technology Collection, The Leisure Library).
Funding sources include SGA allocations, grants, University contributions, external partnerships, and self-generated revenues.
Fiscal oversight shall be provided by the Office of the Student Body Treasurer and Student Senate Finance Committee with annual review by the Student Senate Budget Committee.
Evaluation and Annual Review:
The SGA Cooperative Collection at FSU Libraries shall undergo an annual review conducted by a Review Board which shall meet prior to the annual budget process each year to prepare a request to the Student Senate Budget Committee.
The Review Board shall be composed of:
FSU Libraries’ Head of Access Services & Delivery, or an appropriate designee;
FSU Libraries’ Access Services Librarian, or an appropriate designee;
Program Director of Student Governance and Advocacy, or an appropriate designee; 
FSU-SGA Secretary of Academic Affairs, or an appropriate designee from the Department of Academic Affairs;
Student Senate President;
Student Senate President Pro Tempore;
Chair of the Senate Internal Affairs Committee;
Chair of the Senate Student Life Committee;
Chair of the Senate Finance Committee;
Senate Liaison to FSU Libraries;
Deputy Student Body Treasurer, as Vice Chair;
Student Body Treasurer, as Chair.
The Review Board shall evaluate utilization, student satisfaction, rental process effectiveness, and fiscal health.
Such meetings of the Review Board shall be considered public meetings and shall be noticed as such in compliant with all FSU-SGA Statutes.
A written summary of findings shall be presented to the Student Life Committee and the Student Senate no later than the seventh week of the Spring semester.
The Leisure Library:
The Leisure Library shall enhance student well-being and community connection by providing non-academic items that promote creativity, recreation, and holistic wellness.
Items available for student checkout may include, but are not limited to: lawn games, board games, arts and crafts kits, casual reading materials, and wellness tools.
The Leisure Library shall be funded through its own line item within the Cooperative Collection budget category in the annual FSU-SGA budget.
HISTORY

Amended by Bill B78-032 on 7/22/2026

sections.heading: SENATE RULES OF PROCEDURE
sections.text:
THE FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY

STUDENT SENATE RULES OF PROCEDURE

sections.heading: RULE ONE - Election, Vacancies, And Removal Of The Office Of Student Senate President And Student Senate President Pro Tempore
sections.text:
Pursuant to Article II, Section 4 of the Student Body Constitution and §400.8, Student Body Statutes, the Organizational Session shall be convened between certification of the Fall general election and prior to inauguration for the purpose of electing the Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore. During the first meeting following the Organizational Session, the Senate Rules of Procedure from the previous Senate session shall be adopted in order to conduct business. 
The Organizational Session shall be presided over by the outgoing Senate President. In the event that the outgoing Senate President is unable to preside, the order of succession for presiding shall be as follows: Outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore, the Judiciary Committee Chair, the Internal Affairs Chair, the Finance Chair, and then the Student Life Chair. 
In the event that no Senator listed in the order of succession is able to preside, the most senior member of the Senate shall preside. 

If the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore is unable to preside, the order of succession for their tasks will be the same as listed in subsection (a). In the event that no Senator listed in this order of succession is able to preside, the most senior member of the Senate will assume the Senate President Pro Tempore's duties. 

The Organizational Session shall follow the order of business listed below and no other business shall be considered. 
Call to Order by the presiding officer.
Pledge of Allegiance. 
Moment of Silent Reflection. 
Reading of the Indigenous Land Acknowledgement. 
Roll Call and Verification of Quorum by the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore or designated Senator. 
Public Comment from students, Registered Student Organizations (RSOs), and members of the campus community. Each speaker shall have a maximum of two (2) minutes. 
Opening Address by the presiding officer, explaining the purpose of the session, the applicable Sunshine and open-meeting requirements, and the standards of decorum to be maintained throughout the proceedings.
Explanation of Procedure. The presiding officer shall briefly explain the rules governing nominations, candidate presentations, debate, and voting for the election of the Senate President and Senate President Pro Tempore.
Nominations for Senate President. 
Candidate Presentations, Questioning, and Debate.
Voting for Senate President. 
Election of Senate President Pro Tempore. Upon certification of the Senate President’s election, the presiding officer shall continue to preside over nominations, presentations, and voting for the Senate President Pro Tempore following the same process outlined in subsections (i) through (k). 
Administration of Oaths of Office. 
Announcements. The presiding officer may invite brief announcements from the newly elected officers or from outgoing Senate officers related to transition and preparation for the next session. 
Adjournment. The presiding officer shall entertain a motion to adjourn. Upon adjournment, the session shall stand concluded, and the results shall be certified pursuant to §400.8 of the Student Body Statutes. 
No motions other than those related to nominations, debate procedure, or adjournment shall be in order during the Organizational Session.

Following the close of public comment, no individual who is not a duly certified Senator or Senator-elect shall be recognized to speak or be motioned to speak for the remainder of the session.

A quorum of two-thirds (2/3) of the membership of the upcoming Senate (continuing Spring Senators + newly elected Fall Senators) is required to conduct the Organizational Session. While the outgoing Senate President or designated Senator presides, elections shall be administered by the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore or designated Senator via secret ballot and require a majority (>50%) to elect, pursuant to §400.8(d).
Runoff Elections for Student Senate President and Student Senate President Pro Tempore:
If no candidate attains a majority, the candidate with the fewest votes is eliminated and another round of balloting is held; this successive elimination continues until two candidates remain, after which majority is required to elect.

Ties for fewest vote total shall be decided by the presiding officer.

Ballots shall be tallied by the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore or designated Senator under the supervision of the presiding officer.

The Chairperson shall have the right to cast a vote for election of the Student Senate President or Student Senate President Pro Tempore in such cases where their vote would be decisive to break a tie by lot.

Nominations shall be taken from the floor and require a second from Senators other than the nominator. Only members of the upcoming Senate may be nominated.

Candidates shall be recognized in alphabetical order by last name and allotted five (5) minutes to give a presentation to the Senate. After each presentation, the Senate shall conduct six (6) questions to that candidate. Each Senator may ask only one question total per candidate. Following questions, the Senate shall enter a debate period not exceeding ten (10) minutes for each candidate, conducted in accordance with the rules governing debate on a pending motion as set forth in Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised. These debate periods shall not be modified, and any motion to extend debate shall not be in order, along with that any motion to exit or modify the prescribed debate shall not be in order. Candidates not presenting shall be requested to exit the Chamber during presentations, questioning, and debate. 

Individual Senators recognized by the Chair shall be limited to one speech on this pending motion, limited to one (1) minute of debate time and a total of two times being recognized. The Chair will look favorably on a Senator who has yet to be recognized in the totality of the Organizational Session.

Upon election, the officers-elect shall take the oaths prescribed in 202.9 and 202.10, administered by the outgoing Senate President Pro Tempore or designated Senator, and the Clerk shall record the oaths in the Senate Journal. Assumption of office and ratification shall follow §400.8(f)–(g), Student Body Statutes. 

In the event of permanent vacancy in the office of Student Senate President, the Student Senate President Pro Tempore, at the next scheduled Senate meeting, shall assume the chair and immediately call for election of a new Student Senate President following the same procedure above. If the current Student Senate President Pro Tempore is nominated for the office of Student Senate President, or the positions of Student Senate President and Student Senate President Pro Tempore are vacant simultaneously, the following shall be the order of succession: Chairperson of Judiciary, Chairperson of Internal Affairs, Chairperson of Finance, and Chairperson of Student Life. Any person in this line of succession who shall become acting Student Senate President shall have only the authority to sign bills waiting to go to the Student Body President, call the next immediate meeting of the Student Senate and conduct the election for the new Student Senate President. In the case where the President Pro Tempore and all Committee Chairpersons are nominated or unable to Chair, then the most senior Senator present shall immediately assume the chair for the purposes of conducting the election. The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall reserve the right to retain their position as Student Senate President Pro Tempore if they are nominated and do not win. 

Any member may, at any time, make a motion of no-confidence in the Student Senate President or the Student Senate President Pro Tempore. This action must be seconded and include a reason for the motion being made. The officer shall temporarily vacate their position which shall be filled pursuant to the order of succession listed in Rule 1.7. The Senator who made the motion shall present their motion pursuant to the structure of debate described in Rule Eleven. For the motion to pass, a majority of the members of the Senate being present shall be required. Following passage of a motion of no confidence, the officer in question shall permanently vacate their position and the presiding officer shall immediately call for the election of the recently vacated position following the same procedure above. 

Motions of no-confidence may only be used against one Senate Leader at a time, and may not be abused for purposes that would result in violations of the Senate Conduct Code, most notably those of obstruction, delays, or other interferences with Senate business for partisan reasons.

sections.heading: RULE TWO - Student Senate President: Duties And Powers
sections.text:
The Student Senate President shall be the chief legislative officer of the Student Body and shall perform duties as provided by the Student Body Statutes, Constitution of the Student Body, and these Senate Rules of Procedure. 

The President shall be the presiding officer of the Student Senate except when they choose to temporarily relinquish the chair. In such cases, the Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall assume the chair, unless the President appoints another senator to temporarily preside over the Senate.

The President shall not designate a senator as temporary chair if said senator has participated in the debate of a question or measure still before the body. The President, once they have relinquished the chair to debate, shall not resume the chair until the question before the body has been resolved.

When not holding the chair or presiding over the Senate, the President shall retain all the rights, privileges, and responsibilities of any other Senator.

Other than the Student Senate Pro Tempore and cases arising out of Rule 1.7, any Senator who temporarily assumes the chair shall only have the authority to preside over meetings.

The Student Senate President shall preserve order and decorum in the Senate Chambers and, in the case of disturbance or disorderly conduct, may have members or guests of the Senate removed. 

The Student Senate President shall have the authority to appoint the members of all Senate committees. 

The Student Senate President may compel any committee of the Senate to meet at a specific time with at least a 24 hour notice to the appropriate Chair and committee members. 

The Student Senate President shall have the sole authority to appoint, subject to Senate confirmation, the Senate Parliamentarian, Public Affairs Officer, Senate Clerk, Senate Historian, and other officers as needed.

The Student Senate President shall, within eight (8) school days, sign all documents which require the signature of the Student Senate President. The Student Senate President shall decide all points of order, subject to an appeal by any member. The President may require the member raising a point of order to cite the rule or other authority in support of the question. Unless otherwise specified in these Rules, any motion to appeal the decision of the Chair shall require a majority vote of the Senate to pass.

Subject to order and decorum, the President shall provide reasonable access to members of the public, and press, including at least one representative from each of the print, radio, and television news media. If anyone wishes to video record or voice record the Senate Proceedings, the individual or group shall simply inform the President, who shall then inform the Senate of such occurrence. This provision is not to restrict the recording of Senate, but is a sign of courtesy to inform the Senate that their likeness or voice will be recorded by an individual or group. 

The Student Senate President shall have the authority to assign Senators to serve as liaisons to campus entities. 

During the 2nd Senate after Fall inauguration the Student Senate President shall announce open liaison and designee positions. 

During the 3rd Senate after Fall inauguration the Student Senate President shall assign Senate liaisons to campus entities. Liaisons can be replaced, or added at any time through the authority of the Senate President. 

The list of all Senators who serve as liaisons shall be published on the SGA website. 

The Student Senate President shall, at minimum, assign a liaison to the Executive Branch, the Union Board, the Campus Recreation Board, the Congress of Graduate Students, the Class Councils, SGA Elections, SGA Agencies, SGA Departments, SGA Affiliated Projects, SGA-funded Student Leadership Councils, PC-SGC, the Childcare Center, CARE, Sustainable Campus, the Facilities Department, Transportation and Parking Services, the FSU Police Department, the Governing Greek Councils, the Office of Fraternity and Sorority Life, and the FSU Food for Thought Pantry. They may also assign a liaison to any other on-campus entities, at their discretion.
The following Standing Committee Chairs shall serve as the designated liaisons to the corresponding Executive Branch Departments:
The Chair of the Judiciary Committee shall serve as the liaison to the Office of the Attorney General.

The Chair of Internal Affairs shall serve as the liaison to Administrative Affairs. 

The Chair of the Finance Committee shall serve as liaison to the Office of the Treasury.

The Chair of the Student Life Committee shall serve as liaison to Campus Life and Programming.

The Student Senate president shall retain the authority to appoint Senators to serve as liaisons to all other Executive Branch departments, including but not limited to Diversity, Equity, and Inclusion (DEI), Athletics, Sustainability, Academic Affairs, and Health, Wellness, and Safety.

No Senator shall serve as a liaison to more than four (4) entities at a time. 

At a minimum of once per month, all liaisons must file a report regarding their specific campus entity with the Senate during the Report of the Liaisons. 

The Student Senate President shall also have the authority to assign Senators to serve as designees to campus entities. Designee shall be defined as positions where the Student Senate President has voting power or is an ex-officio member. Designee shall be held to the same rules as liaisons. 

The Senate President can resume their role as an ex-officio or voting member as they see fit.
In the event that any required campus entity does not have an assigned liaison, the Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall act as the point of contact until a permanent liaison is assigned

The Student Senate President and Public Affairs Officer shall be the administrator of any official social media account(s) of the Legislative Branch and can appoint this power to any designee. All social media page must be kept on the lowest privacy levels and must be open for all to view. The Senate President or designee shall be responsible for creating a Monthly Newsletter including events funded by Student Senate.

sections.heading: RULE THREE - Student Senate President Pro Tempore: Duties And Powers
sections.text:
The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall assist the President and perform duties as provided by the Student Body Statutes, Constitution of the Student Body, and these Senate Rules of Procedure.
In the event of the Student Senate President's absence or temporary vacancy the Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall act as Student Senate President during the Student Senate President's absence.
The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall administer the oath of office to all persons confirmed by the Senate. In the absence of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore this duty shall be vested in the officer presiding over the Senate at the time of confirmation.
The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall be the Chair of the Senate Rules Committee.
As Chair of the Rules Committee, the Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall oversee all Senate committee administrative operations, ensuring proper coordination, communication, and compliance among all standing committees of the Student Senate. 
The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall administer and oversee the operations of the College Delegation Program, including ensuring that all Delegations function in accordance with Rule Sixteen of these Rules of Procedure. 
The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall be responsible for enforcing compliance with Delegation duties and requirements through the Rules Committee and shall ensure that Delegation Chairs complete their required meetings, outreach, and constituency reports. 
The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall draft all charges of impeachment that arise from proceedings within the Rules Committee.

sections.heading: RULE FOUR - Legislative Officers
sections.text:
The Student Senate President shall be responsible for the duties of all vacant Senate Officers. 

The Parliamentarian shall advise the Senate on matters of procedure and pertinent laws, statutes, and constitutional provisions and enforce the rules relating to procedure. The Parliamentarian shall maintain order in the Senate Chambers under the direction of the President or other presiding officer(s). The Parliamentarian shall strictly enforce the rules relating to conduct within the Senate Chambers. The Parliamentarian shall perform any other duties that the President shall determine to be necessary. 

The Public Affairs Officer shall be responsible for maintaining the Senate social media presence and outreach. The Public Affairs Officer shall work with committee chairs to help inform the student body on committee meeting information. The Public Affairs Officer shall also perform any other duties that the Student Senate President or President Pro-Tempore shall determine to be necessary for these purposes.  

The Public Affairs Officer shall be in contact with the SGA Webmaster to ensure that postings are within the Florida State University communications guidelines. 

The Public Affairs Officer shall post on the Student Senate Instagram account at the beginning of the fall and spring semesters when PAC, RTAC, and all relevant funding board requests open. This post should include a brief description of the funding boards, links to the funding board pages on the SGA website, and links to the applications. The Student Senate Press Secretary shall also contact the Executive Branch when the post is up, so a post can be made on the SGA Instagram account.

The Senate Clerk shall be responsible for tracking and distributing legislation and other literature to Senators. The Clerk shall also work in collaboration with the Historian to create and maintain the weekly Senate agenda. The Clerk shall be responsible for managing the CivicPlus application during sessions of the Senate. The Clerk shall also perform any other duties that the Senate President or President Pro-Tempore shall determine to be necessary. 

The Senate Historian shall be responsible for taking minutes in the Senate Chamber. The Historian shall also work in collaboration with the Clerk to create and maintain the weekly Senate agenda. The Historian shall also perform any other duties that the Senate President or President Pro-Tempore shall determine to be necessary.

The Parliamentarian, Public Affairs Officer, Historian, Clerk, and any additional appointed legislative officers shall be appointed by the President from outside the membership of the Senate and shall be subject to confirmation from the Senate.

sections.heading: RULE FIVE - Committees
sections.text:
Committee Appointments: The Student Senate President shall appoint all committees of the Student Senate. The Senate body may order the Student Senate President to redo committee assignments a two-thirds (2/3) vote.
Standing Committees shall consist of no less than five voting members.
Ex Officio Members: The Student Senate President and the Student Senate Pro Tempore shall serve as ex-officio voting members of all Senate committees. An ex-officio voting member shall count towards quorum but not against it.

The Student Senate President may appoint a maximum of two senators to each Senate committee as non-voting members. Non-voting members shall not be considered for the purpose of determining quorum.
Election and Removal of Standing Committee Chair and Vice Chair:
Committee elections shall occur immediately after the publication of committee assignments following fall and spring inaugurations. Senate shall move to enter committee caucus for the purpose of electing Committee Chairs and Vice-Chairs.
The overseer of the nominations, speeches, debates, and vote for the Chair position of each of the standing committees shall be a member of the Office of the Senate President, as designated by the Student Senate President. In the event that one or more of these overseers are absent, the Student Senate President shall designate any additional overseers as they see fit.
Nominations for Committee Chair and Committee Vice-Chair shall be taken from the committee members and shall require a second. The nominee must accept the nomination. Each candidate shall be allowed, in alphabetical order, to address the standing committee for no more than five (5) minutes in the form of a speech.
The overseer shall allow no more than two (2) committee members to speak in general, untimed questioning. 

Following questioning, the overseer will move the committee into a period of debate not exceeding 5 minutes for each nominee, conducted in accordance with the rules governing debate on a pending motion as set forth in Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised. The period will start with 3 minutes of debate and can be extended by 2 minutes by a 2/3 vote of the committee. Individual Senators in the committee shall be limited to one speech on the nominee, limited to one (1) minute of debate time. All nominees not addressing the standing committee shall be requested to leave the immediate area when not speaking, including during all debate on the candidates.
Chairs shall be determined by a majority vote of the committee, including the nominees. If no candidate receives a majority, a runoff election will be held between the two candidates who received the most votes in the first round. In the event of a tie in the final round, the Student Senate President shall cast the tie breaking vote.
Following the conclusion of Chair elections, the overseer shall relinquish the floor to the new Chair, who shall conduct the Vice-Chair elections. The process for the nominations, speeches, and debate for the Vice-Chair shall be the same as that for Chair. The Chair shall cast a vote in the event of a tie.
When a Senator vacates a Chair position, an election shall be held to fill the vacancy prior to the resumption of that committee’s business. When a Senator vacates a Vice Chair position, the Chair may appoint an interim Vice Chair for the remainder of the meeting or immediately hold elections for the Vice Chair position. If an interim Vice Chair is appointed, an election for the Vice Chair position must be held at the end of the meeting where the vacancy occurred.
In the event that the positions of Chair and Vice Chair are concurrently vacated, or the Vice Chair wishes to be a candidate for the position. The Student Senate President, or member of the Office of the Student Senate President as designated by the Student Senate President shall preside over replacement elections, unless they wish to be a candidate for Chair, in which case the responsibility shall fall to the next most senior member.
A Chair or Vice-Chair may be removed by a majority vote of the committee they serve on. Only those who have served on the committee for a minimum of one (1) calendar month shall be eligible to vote on this motion. At least five (5) committee members eligible to vote on the matter must be present for the vote to be held.
The Vice Chair shall preside over the motion and vote to remove the Chair. In the case that the Vice Chair is unavailable, or the committee is voting to remove both the Chair and Vice Chair, the most senior member of the committee shall preside.
In the event that the Chair or Vice Chair should take temporary leave, as in the case of a summer leave of absence, the new officer’s tenure shall last only until the return of their predecessor, upon which time they shall relinquish the title, duties and responsibilities of that office.
Standing Committee Chairs: The Chair of a standing committee shall be a voting member of the committee. However, they shall only vote when their vote is decisive in breaking a tie, in accordance with Robert’s Rule of Order. They shall set the calendar, and they shall preside and keep order and decorum of the meetings.
The Chair of a standing committee shall review and sign all committee reports and shall present them to the Senate. The Chair shall sign such other documents as may be required.
The Chair of a standing committee shall be responsible for establishing the meeting time and place of the committee and shall have the authority to call a meeting of the committee with a 24 hour notice to committee members, the Senate Advisor and the Senate President by phone and/or e-mail.
The Chair of a standing committee is authorized to invite any individual to appear before the committee for the purpose of submitting information.
If the Chair wishes to debate a motion, they will do so in accordance with Robert’s Rules of Order by relinquishing the chair to a member who has not debated on the current motion. The Chair shall not resume the chair until after the question has been decided.
The Chair shall, upon request by a primary sponsor of an item or the inability of a primary sponsor to attend a meeting in which the item they are sponsoring is being heard, be empowered to table the item until the committee’s next meeting without a motion.
Standing Committee Vice-Chairs: In the event of the absence of the Chair from any standing committee meeting, the Vice-Chair shall assume the duties of the Chair, and the Chair shall receive one (1) full absence unless excused.
The Vice-Chair shall act as the recording secretary of all standing committee meetings and shall be responsible for keeping the minutes of the meeting and submitting the minutes to the Chair of the standing committee the Vice-Chair is a member of. The Vice-Chair shall also keep an active contact list of all committee members.
Standing Committee Business: No standing committee may do business without the presence of a quorum of the committee. A quorum shall be defined as more than half of the voting members of the committee. Committees shall create and publish their own rules on the SGA website, as long as those rules do not violate any rules in these Rules of Procedure, SGA Statutes, or the Student Body Constitution. The Committee Chair shall be responsible for the safekeeping of such rules. Committee rules of procedure must pass by a simple majority vote.
Committee Referral: The Student Senate President shall refer all bills and constitutional amendments to the appropriate standing committee for consideration and action, and the Student Senate President may refer any proclamation or resolution to committee or directly to the calendar for second reading. In the case of legislation being referred to multiple committees, the committee assignments shall not be bound by a specific sequential order. The legislation must receive approval from all relevant committees, regardless of the order, to be placed on Second Reading. Each committee shall hear the most recently passed version of the legislation. A piece of legislation passing an individual committee shall proceed with any amendments to the next committee for consideration. Failure of legislation by any assigned committee shall result in the defeat of the legislation and it shall be removed from the Calendar.
Any senator can move to appeal a referral by the President and motion for a different or additional committee to hear the legislation or that, in the case of multiple committee assignments, the legislation may not be referred to a specific committee. Such motions require a majority vote to pass. This provision shall not be interpreted as limiting the Student Senate President's discretion to refer any measure to any other committees.
A senator may also move that legislation on first reading be read in its entirety by the presiding officer and moved to second reading the same session it is introduced. This motion requires approval by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Senators present.
The Student Senate President may refer any resolution to committee(s) or directly to the calendar for second reading, except for changes to the Rules of Procedure or resolutions commending or condemning a specific person or group, which must go to the Rules and Calendar Committee.
If a piece of legislation is unanimously approved by all of its assigned committees, not including abstentions, the Student Senate President shall have the discretion to place the legislation on the Consent Calendar. Constitutional amendments and Major Legislation may not be placed on the Consent Calendar.
Transfer Bills cannot be considered on the Consent Calendar.
Committee Meetings: No committee shall take formal action upon measures except at public meetings, notice of which has been published or announced to the Senate session. Each committee member shall be contacted by phone or electronic mail by the Chair at least twenty-four hours prior to the call to order of said committee meeting.
The date, time and location of any and all committee meetings shall be determined by the Chair or acting Chair of the committee. Standing committees shall meet at least once weekly unless otherwise determined by the Student Senate President.
All committee meetings must conclude three hours after the meeting’s Call to Order. This rule may be waived by a 2/3 vote of the committee, but no meeting shall last later than 11:30 PM.

All meetings of committees shall be open to the public at all times, subject to the presiding officer's right to maintain order and decorum. Only members of the committee may speak on measures before the committee unless the committee waives the rules to allow a non-member to offer additional information to the discussion. A non-committee member shall not be allowed to participate in debate on any measure unless permitted by the Chair. Committee meetings shall be held in an on-campus location at the discretion of the committee.
Only those measures of which notice of introduction has been given and/or measures which have originated in committee may be acted upon at a committee meeting.
Committee Minutes: Each committee shall compile and publish Committee minutes following each meeting. Committee minutes must be filed with the Senate Advisor and Webmaster no later than noon of the day of the next Senate meeting. Such minutes shall include:
Member attendance list.
Amendments to measures before the committee and votes on those amendments including voting position by member.
Final votes on measures.
Pertinent discussion the committee feels should be brought to the attention of the Senate.
The date and time of the meeting and the date and time of the next meeting.
It shall be the responsibility of each committee to report back to the Senate on all measures referred to the committee. The Chair of a committee or their designee shall present the committee report on the Senate floor. Any member of a committee may also give an additional report on the committee's actions.
The President shall have the power to create ad hoc committees and appoint their members and Chairs. Non-Senators may participate as voting members of ad hoc committees; this does not allow for Senate Officers to take part, besides the Senate Parliamentarian if deemed needed.. Under no circumstances shall an ad hoc committee prevent any measure from reaching the floor of the full Senate.
An ad hoc committee may also be created by a motion made during New Business. The motion shall be debatable and only pass with a two-thirds (2/3) vote. The Student Senate President shall have the power to appoint the members and Chairs of ad hoc committees created by motion.
The Budget Committee shall not be considered an ad hoc committee under this Rule, but a special committee convened annually for the purposes of the Annual Budget as defined in Chapter 416.

The Student Senate President may establish subcommittees of standing committees and shall appoint their members and Chairs. The Student Senate President shall consult with the Chair of the parent committee regarding appointment of subcommittees.
In the event that the Student Senate President refers any piece of legislation, in accordance with Rule 5.07 to a committee, failure to call a meeting will result in an absence for the committee Chair and Vice Chair with the exclusion of breaks and holidays in accordance with the Florida State University Academic Calendar unless excused by the Student Senate President.

sections.heading: RULE SIX - Standing Committees: Duties And Responsibilities
sections.text:
The Senate Finance Committee shall: 	

Exercise jurisdiction over all fiscal matters of the Student, including but not limited to transfers, allocations, proviso revisions, and other appropriations of Activity & Service Fee funds.
Debate, amend, reject, or recommend the passage of any measure pertaining to financial policy, appropriations, or Chapter 800 of the Student Body Statutes.
Conduct reviews and provide legislative oversight of all A&S fee recipients, accounts, and expenditures, and may require reports or testimony as deemed necessary by the Committee or by the Student Senate President in consultation with the Chair.
Review Chapter 800, the Finance Code, and suggest amendments or revisions to improve financial accountability, efficiency, and transparency.
Forward or deny all nominations for agency, department, and affiliated project financial officers, including the Office of the Student Body Treasurer.
Serve as the primary fiscal oversight body of the Senate outside of the Annual Budget process, ensuring that expenditures and appropriations comply with law, policy, and Student Body Statutes.
All fiscal matters not directly related to the Annual Budget shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Finance Committee. The Annual Budget Bill shall fall under the jurisdiction of the Budget Committee.

The Senate Judiciary Committee shall: 

Debate, amend, reject, or recommend for passage measures pertaining to the Student Body Constitution or Statutes. 

Review the Student Body Constitution and Statutes and suggest possible amendments to these documents. 

Forward or deny nominations to the Student Government Supreme Court and Attorney General’s Office, pending the confirmation by the full Senate. 

Review, consider, and if necessary, initiate impeachment proceedings against any officer of the Student Body, as mandated in the Student Body Constitution and Statutes. 

The Senate Internal Affairs Committee shall: 

Forward or deny all nominations to offices in Student Government by the Student Body President not including those approved by any other Senate Committees, pending confirmation by the full Senate. 

Members of this committee must be present for a nominee’s interview, in its entirety, to be allowed to vote. 

Review and propose any changes deemed necessary to the format or content of Student Government applications. Changes must pass the committee as well as the Senate by a two-thirds (2/3) vote in order to be formally adopted. Any changes to the form shall be in compliance with Chapter 202 of the Student Body Statutes. 

Create surveys for the senate and committees to determine satisfaction and provide recommendations to the President. 

Review departments funded by Student Government to determine their compliance with the Student Body Statutes.

Conduct oversight of the appointment process to ensure that all statutes in relation to the candidate search and selection process are being followed.

Review and propose any changes to the appointment process to ensure a fair consideration of all applicants in line with Chapter 304 of the Student Body Statutes.

The committee shall be responsible for maintaining a list of suggested interview questions to be asked during the confirmation process. The Vice-Chair shall ensure that this list of interview questions is made available on the SGA website. 

The Senate Student Life Committee shall: 

Review issues pertaining to the student body and inform the Senate as to any pertinent action. 

Hear resolutions relating to student life and the Tallahassee community.

Coordinate with the Senate Public Affairs Officer to conduct forums for students to express their concerns. The committee is encouraged to work with the Executive Branch on such forums. 

Review Senate Projects Account requests.
Be in charge of organizing the Student Senate’s weekly participation in Market Wednesday and other public tabling opportunities.
Student Life Committee members are not bound to attend themselves, but are highly encouraged to participate to ensure the Student Senate is actively engaging with the Student Body in-person and weekly.
Senators may earn 1 additional mental health day for every 4 hours of tabling, in addition to the allowance provided in Rule 13.9(e). Such tabling opportunities should include, but not be limited to, Market Wednesday and the Involvement Fair. The Student Senate President Pro Tempore, in collaboration with the Chair of the Student Life Committee, shall determine and approve which tabling opportunities satisfy this provision. This provision may be exercised up to 4 times within a semester.
The amount of mental health days awarded through this provision are limited to 5 per term.
Review current Affiliated Projects and decide on whether they shall remain an Affiliated Project and continue to receive funding from the Student Government Association.
The Student Life Committee is encouraged to visit Affiliated Projects, it possible, in the beginning of the Fall Semester to be able to see their performance and effects in person. Members of the Senate also interested in serving the Budget Committee for the Spring Semester are also highly encouraged to participate in these visits. 
The recommendations of these deliberations shall be submitted to the Student Senate President no later than the twelfth week of the Fall semester via resolution. 
This process is to be conducted on a four-year basis, beginning on the Fall semester of 2026, and repeating henceforth. 
Each year 2-3 projects shall be reviewed by the Student Life Committee, and each project shall be reviewed once every four years unless otherwise determined by Senate Leadership of the Chair of Student Life.
Upon the introduction of a new Affiliated Project, it shall be reviewed twice in the four-year cycle to ensure performance and efficiency.
One review shall be done in the time it would follow for the four-year cycle, and a second for the halfway mark of this four-year count.

sections.heading: RULE SEVEN - The Rules Committee
sections.text:
Composition: The Student Senate President, Student Senate Pro Tempore, the Chairs of each of the standing committees outlined in Rules Six, and the chairs of the Senate Funds Distribution Committees outlined in Rule 5. The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall serve as the Chair of this committee.

In the event a Chair of the standing committee is unable to attend a Rules committee meeting due to an excused reason, they may designate their vice chair to serve in their place for that meeting upon submitting a written declaration to the Student Senate President Pro Tempore. 

In the event a Chair and vice chair of a standing committee is unable to attend a Rules meeting due to excused reasons, the Chair may designate another member of that committee to serve in their place for that meeting upon submitting a written declaration to the Student Senate President Pro Tempore. 

The Student Senate President may temporarily preside over the Rules committee in the absence or request of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore.

The Rules Committee shall: 

Debate, amend, reject, or recommend passage of any amendments to the Senate Rules of Procedure. 

Review and suspend Senators for excessive absences as provided for in these Rules. 

Approve or disapprove of the nominations of appointed Senators, pending the approval of the full Senate. 

Facilitate communication between the officers of the Senate and ensure that a contact list of all Senators is made and distributed to Senators. 

Review the Calendar for the Senate.
The Vice Chairs of each standing committee outlined in Rule Six shall serve as ex-officio voting members of the Rules Committee for all matters, except as provided below.
Vice Chairs shall not have voting rights on matters involving the suspension or unsuspension of Senators.
Vice Chairs shall not have voting rights on any resolutions of condemnation.
Vice Chairs shall not count toward quorum during the consideration of the matters outlined above and shall not be permitted to vote on them. They may remain present during such deliberations only at the discretion of the Chair. It shall be the responsibility of the Chair of the Rules Committee to clearly announce when a restricted item is under consideration and to ensure these voting limitations are observed.
The Senate Historian shall serve as the Vice Chair of the Rules Committee, unless otherwise assigned by the Chair of the Rules Committee.

sections.heading: RULE EIGHT - Senate Business
sections.text:
When in session, the Senate shall meet weekly on Wednesdays. The meeting shall be called to order at 7:30 p.m. All regularly scheduled meetings of the Student Senate shall be publicly posted or advertised on the Student Government website. Any such advertisement shall include the time and place of the Senate meeting. 

The Senate shall stand adjourned at 11:00 pm.

Any outstanding business shall be tabled at 10:50 p.m. and heard during “Unfinished Business” in the following Senate meeting. The Senate shall then immediately move into statements of dissent, advisor announcements, and final roll call, without deviating from this order.
During summer sessions of the Senate, the Student Senate President may be empowered to call meetings on a biweekly basis.

The Student Senate President shall call a special session of the Senate at their discretion or if requested by a majority vote of the Senate in the form of a petition. All Senators shall be notified of this special session by the Senate Advisor at least 24 hours prior to the special session being held, and shall follow the calendar as listed this rule.

A petition to call a special session shall include Senators’ names, seats, and FSU IDs.

The Calendar shall govern the order of consideration of measures by the Student Senate and shall be as follows: 

Call to Order 

Pledge of Allegiance 

Moment of Silent Reflection 

Reading of the Indigenous Land Acknowledgement

Roll Call and Verification of Quorum
Presentations and Awards

Public Comments from Students, RSOs, and Members of the Campus Community

Messages from SGA Entities

Report of Senate Officers

Report of the Senate Liaisons 

Senate Confirmations 

Consent Calendar
Corrections and Approval of Senate and Committee Follow-up Memos

Report of Remaining Fund Balances
Items Pulled from the Consent Calendar
Constitutional Amendments

Legislation on First Reading

Legislation on Second Reading

Unfinished Business 

New Business 

Closing Announcements 

Advisor Announcements

Final Roll Call and Adjournment 

The Calendar cannot be changed on the Senate floor of a Senate meeting without a motion to Unlock the Calendar If objected to, a two-thirds vote is required for the motion to pass. To return to the normal agenda, any Senator may move to return to the orders of the day. If objected to, a two-thirds vote is required to overturn the motion.

Any legislation to be included on the calendar of a Senate meeting, must be submitted to the Senate Advisor, Senate President, Senate President Pro Tempore, and Senate Clerk no later than midnight on the Friday before the Senate meeting. 

If a Senator wishes to introduce any legislation for First Reading after the submission deadline, it shall require a three-fourths (3/4) vote to be introduced during that Senate meeting. This Senator must provide a copy of the item to all senators prior to the meeting for the motion to be considered. 

The Senate Clerk shall publish the calendar. In their absence, the Senate Advisor shall perform this duty.

The Senate Historian shall record the Journal of the official proceedings of the Senate. In the Historian’s absence, the Senate President shall have the power to assign this duty.

Either the Senate Historian or Advisor shall publish the Senate Journal each week no later than forty-eight hours prior to a regular session of the Senate. Journal entries shall include, but not be limited to:

Times of convening and adjournment. 

A List of Senators present and absent for first roll call. 

Name of presiding officer(s). 

Any messages to the Senate from the public or other SGA and university entities.

A description of all measures introduced and date of entry. 

A summary of all committee reports. 

“Upcoming events” cards. 

A list of all legislation that has been signed by the Student Senate President and transmitted to the proper respondent(s) since the previous Senate meeting. 

Description of any floor amendments or committee amendments offered and their disposition. 

Any material votes required by the Student Body Constitution, Statutes, or these rules. 

Any submitted Statements of Dissent. 

All roll call votes. 

A list of Senators present and absent for the final roll call. 

A copy of each piece of legislation shall be provided electronically to each Senator prior to and available at each meeting at which it will be considered: 

The management of electronic document distribution shall be assigned to the duties of the SGA Staff. 

It shall be the responsibility of the Student Senate President Pro Tempore to display Senate documents during Senate meetings.

A limited amount of printed copies will continue to be made available for guests in the Senate, the number of which shall be at the discretion of SGA Staff. 

At their discretion, the Student Senate President may request that students wishing to speak during the Student and RSO Comments section of the agenda fill out a “Request to Address” card. 

The Special Introductions portion of Senate meetings shall be reserved time where guests invited at the discretion of the Student Senate President may address the Senate. Any Senator may move for other speakers to be permitted, subject to a majority vote. This motion shall be debatable.

The presiding officer may call for the Senate to recess for a specified amount of time. This action shall require a majority vote if objected to by any senator. Any Senator may also make a non-debatable motion to recess, which shall require a second, and a majority vote for passage if objected to. The presiding officer shall call the meeting to order at the expiration of the time specified in such a motion.

Upon the completion of all items on the Senate’s Calendar, the presiding officer shall entertain a motion to adjourn the meeting, which shall require a second and a majority vote for passage if objected to.

Consent Calendar: The presiding officer shall individually read the description of, and entertain individual motions to approve, each item placed on the Consent Calendar. Any Senator may object to any legislation being considered on the Consent Calendar without the need the need for a vote, at which point the legislation shall be considered pulled from the Consent Calendar.  

Any legislation pulled from the Consent Calendar shall be considered in normal order during Second Reading.  

If a piece of legislation requires a compulsory recorded vote, or is otherwise unable to be passed by consent, the Senate shall take a recorded vote after a motion to approve is made by any Senator, if it is not pulled.

sections.heading: RULE NINE - Outlined Vote Thresholds And Governing Authority
sections.text:
1. The rules contained in the current edition of Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised shall govern the Senate in all cases to which they are applicable and in which they are not inconsistent with the Student Body Constitution, Statutes, or these Senate Rules of Procedure. 

2. Any Senator may raise a point of order to request that the presiding officer enforce the rules. The decision of the chair may be appealed by a majority vote. 

3. The operations and proceedings of the Florida State University Student Government Association and the Student Senate shall be governed in accordance with the following hierarchical order of authority, which shall be controlling in the event of any conflict: 

a. The Constitution and laws of the United States, the Constitution and laws of the State of Florida, applicable municipal ordinances, and duly promulgated University regulations and procedures; 
b. The Student Body Constitution; 
c. The Student Body Statutes; 
d. The Senate Rules of Procedure; and, 
e. Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised. 

4. The outlined voting thresholds and procedures shall not conflict at any point in time with Statutes or the Constitution of the Student Body and shall be updated to reflect the proper vote totals in totality at the convenience of the Student Senate. 
5. A table shall be created to define voting thresholds, the title shall have the following Headers in order “Vote Description, Vote Type, Statute Reference”, and shall be designated as having been one full title or row in the table by the separating semi-colon in the text.

a. Vote Descriptions: These shall at any point in time be reasonably construed to provide a short description of what the point or intent of the vote threshold is or the vote attached to the threshold. 
b. Vote Type: The following “Vote Types” shall be allowed, “Majority, Two-Thirds, Three-Fourths, Unanimous Consent, Other.”

sections.heading: RULE TEN - Submission And Consideration Of Measures
sections.text:
Definitions: 

A "Constitutional Amendment" shall be any measure proposing a change, deletion or addition to the Student Body Constitution. 

A "Bill" shall be any measure proposing an amendment to the Student Body Statutes or any measure appropriating money. 

A "Resolution" shall be defined as a formal statement/amendment of Senate policy or intent. 

An "Allocation Resolution" shall be defined as a resolution approving, and allocating funding recommendations originating from Student Government Association funding boards or committees established in Student Body Statutes or allocating or transferring Student Government funds to student organizations through processes expressly authorized by statute.  
A "Proclamation" shall be defined as a formal public declaration or official announcement issued by the Senate to recognize a specific individual, group, event, or cause. 

An "Amendment" shall be efined as a written document proposing a change to a pending measure, including a Bill, Resolution, Proclamation, or Constitutional Amendment. Amendments mist be submitted via the designated Amendment Form.
A "Friendly Amendment" shall be defined as a proposed amendment that is accepted by the primary sponsor of the measure and receives no objections from the Senate allowing for its immediate adoption without debate.
A "Nomination" shall be the name of any person who has been forwarded to fill a vacant position in Student Government that requires confirmation by the Senate. 

“Confirmation” shall be defined as the approval of a nomination by the Senate, in which case the nominee shall then immediately assume office. 

“Statement of Dissent” shall be defined as a written explanation expressing disagreement with any motion, action, or measure made the Senate. 

Any bill, resolution, or proclamation filed on time shall be drawn up by the Senate Staff and distributed to members of the Senate via CivicPlus.
Any bills affecting Student Government funds which are restrictive shall state all restrictions, earmarks, stipulations and provisions as part of the proviso of the bill. 
All appropriations bills must be accompanied by an information form detailing the need for the money, the specific uses for the money, and alternative methods of funding which have been investigated. 

All legislation shall include a cover sheet with the legislation's purpose. No legislation shall be placed on second reading without a cover sheet. 

All legislation shall be submitted on the appropriate forms as designated by the Student Senate President. 

Any measure being brought before the Senate for the first time shall be placed on first reading, unless otherwise moved.

Any measure reported out of committee(s) shall be placed on second reading to be heard by the full Senate at the next meeting.

All nominees to Student Government offices requiring Senate confirmation shall have their completed applications forwarded to the appropriate Senate committee for consideration. The committee shall interview and question the nominee and then vote on whether to forward or deny them. Following the vote of the committee, all nominees forwarded by the committee shall be called to the floor of the Senate at its next meeting. The structure of debate for Senate confirmations shall be as follows:

Nominees shall be allowed to give an opening statement lasting no longer than five (5) minutes, with their remaining time being allocated to their closing. 

Nominees may be questioned by any Senator on matters of their experience, qualifications, and goals for the respective position. 

Upon passage of a motion to enter debate by majority vote, Senators may speak freely as to the qualifications of any candidate. Nominees shall be permitted to remain in the Senate Chamber during debate if they so choose.

Upon the passage of a motion to call the question on a candidate for confirmation, each nominee shall have the time remaining from their opening statement to give a closing statement as to why they should be confirmed. 

The primary sponsor of any piece of legislation may withdraw consideration of the document from the Calendar of the Senate at any time without the need for a formal motion.
In the event one or both primary sponsors are unable to present legislation due to extenuating circumstances, a present cosponsor may be delegated to present subject to the opinion of the presiding officer. 

Any amendment to a measure must be submitted via the amendment form hosted by the SGA Webmaster and must contain the exact language of the proposed amendment including that which shall be inserted and/or deleted. A direct copy of each submission shall be sent to the Student Senate President, Student Senate President Pro Tempore, Student Senate Clerk, Student Senate Historian, Student Senate Parliamentarian, any relevant Standing Committee emails, Senate Program Advisor, and the Program director of Student Governance and Advocacy. Additionally, a copy of the submission shall be sent back to the sponsor (submitter).

Motions to amend may be made during any round of debate and shall require a second. If the proposed amendment is germane and receives no objections, the presiding officer shall ask the primary sponsor if the amendment is favorable. If the sponsor finds the amendment favorable, the original measure shall be amended, and debate shall proceed on the measure as amended.
A motion to amend made on the Senate floor must still be submitted to the amendment form before the adjournment of the meeting, 

If the motion to amend is objected to or the sponsor does not find the amendment favorable, debate on the primary measure shall halt and the Senate shall consider the amendment as a stand-alone measure. The Senator who made the motion to amend shall be considered the sponsor for purposes of debate. 

Debate on the amendment shall not address the merits of the original measure, unless it is pertinent to the merits of the amendment. Additionally, questions and points of information should only inquire on the facts of the amendment itself. 

Unless otherwise specified by the Student Body Constitution or Student Body Statutes, a motion to amend shall require a majority vote to pass. 
All amendments that appropriate or transfer funds to organizations that are not part of the originally submitted bill or allocation resolution must be individually debated on the Senate floor, regardless if the sponsor accepts them as friendly or unfriendly. 

The Senate may, at any time following the proper motion, move to committee caucus for the purpose of expediting the consideration of any measure. A motion to move to committee caucus shall require a two-thirds vote of the Senate. The Student Senate President, or other presiding officer, shall reconvene the Senate at the end of the caucus. 

Any Senator may, at any time, move to meet as a committee of the whole for the purpose of discussing any Senate business. A motion to convene as a committee of the whole may pass by consent or, if objected to, shall require a two-thirds vote of the Senate. A motion to adjourn such a committee meeting and return to a regular Senate meeting shall require a majority vote.

The Student Senate President shall preside over a committee of the whole, unless they choose to relinquish the Chair. 

The Student Senate President Pro Tempore shall act as the Vice Chair of a committee of the whole, unless they choose to relinquish their position. 

When the Senate reconvenes, any senator may move to accept the decision of the committee as the decision of the whole.

Should the Senate enter a committee of the whole, only members of the original committee who were on the prevailing side of a motion may move for a reconsideration of the vote on the said motion. 

Any senator may, during New Business, move to add a Statement of Dissent into the record. 

The statement must solely address a singular action, motion, or measure made during that meeting.

There may only be one statement submitted per any action, motion, or measure per Senator.

Senators who did not make the action, motion, or measure on the floor may cosign the Statement with the consent of the Senator who made the action, motion, or measure.

The statement must be submitted to Senate Staff within two (2) school days following the meeting of the senate when the action, motion, or measure was made.

A proclamation recognizing all Florida State University students that have deceased shall be heard on the floor of the Senate during the meeting prior to the last Senate meeting of the session, or “Sine Die.” 

The list of students will be provided by the SGA Director.

This proclamation shall be proposed and advertised one (1) week prior to it being heard. 

This proclamation shall be referred to the Student Life Committee after its first reading and shall be reported out of the committee in one (1) week.

sections.heading: RULE ELEVEN - Debate And Voting
sections.text:
No person who is not a Student Senator, Senate officer, or SGA Staff member shall be recognized to speak before the Senate unless a motion is made and seconded to allow such a speaker. Senators may make a debatable objection to the motion in which case a majority vote will be necessary to allow such a speaker. 

Only Student Senators, Senate officers, and SGA Staff members shall be allowed on the floor of the Student Senate while the Senate is meeting, except for SGA staff.

Rules 11.1 and 11.2 shall not apply to individuals invited to address the Student Senate whose name or purpose of address appears on the Senate Calendar.

A Senator who wishes to gain the floor shall raise their hand and wait to be recognized by the presiding officer.

Any Senator recognized by the presiding officer shall rise to address the Senate. 

When a measure or motion comes before the Senate for consideration, the structure of debate shall be as follows: 

Opening statement by the sponsor(s) of no more than five (5) minutes. No motions may be made during this round. 

Questions pertaining to the measure or motion, which shall be directed to the sponsor(s). The presiding officer shall have the discretion to direct questions to individuals other than the sponsor(s), and may determine the number of questions that shall be asked.

A period of open debate, with a length determined by the Senate that shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes. Senators who speak in open debate must specify their stance on the agenda item prior to further elaboration. Questions relating to the agenda item must be made in the form of a point of information directed to the presiding officer. 
The Senate may motion to add additional time to the period of open debate, as long as the total time of debate does not exceed thirty (30) minutes.

Any statement in open debate that exceeds the thirty (30) minute maximum, or that exceeds the allotted time stated by the presiding officer, shall be considered a filibuster, and the presiding officer may end the debate. This can be overridden by a simple majority vote of the Senate.

If the Senate votes to override the decision to end debate, the Senator previously recognized shall be allowed to finish their statement. Once they have completed their statement, debate shall end. 

Once recognized, a Senator shall have three (3) minutes to make a statement. This time may be increased by the presiding officer as deemed fit, but shall never be less than three (3) minutes.

If the Senator recognized does not use their entire allotted time, they may yield the remaining time to the sponsor or candidate being discussed so they may comment on the Senator's statement. 

Closing statement by the original sponsor. The length of this statement shall be whatever remaining time the sponsor yielded after their opening. No motions may be made during this round.

No Senator who has already been recognized to speak once may be recognized to speak again during general questioning or open debate unless all other Senators who haven't spoken and wish to be recognized have been recognized, as per Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised.

These speaking limitations shall not be applied to raising motions or points. 

Points and motions do not count against time during any timed round. The remaining time of debate shall be returned to upon completion of any motion or matter that arises, including amendments deemed unfriendly. 

Any Senator may yield their remaining time to any other Senator except on closing debate. If no other Senator wishes to speak when called on by the presiding officer, the current round shall be extinguished. 

A motion to move into open debate shall be undebatable. If objected, the motion will automatically move to a vote that passes by simple majority, as per Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised. 
Open debate shall end:  

If the allotted time for open debate expires and the time is not extended by motion or is in excess of thirty (30) minutes. 

In this case, the debate will immediately move to the agenda item's closing, if they have time remaining from their opening, and voting.
If a motion is made to call the question.
If an objection is made to this motion, the motion to call the question shall immediately be voted on and passed by a two-thirds (2/3) majority, per Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised. 
If a motion is made to table the agenda item.

If an objection is made to this motion, the motion shall immediately be voted on and passed by simple majority, per Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised.

If not prescribed in statutes or these rules, the presiding officer shall determine the manner in which the vote is taken, however a senator may move for a vote by electronic device, hand count, or roll call. 

In cases of roll call votes, the Student Senate President Pro-Tempore shall call the roll of the Senate, in alphabetical order, recording the vote of each Senator. 

Before the result of a roll call vote has been announced, the presiding officer shall ask if any Senator wishes to cast or change their vote. 

In no case shall a Senator cast a vote in place of another Senator. No person who is not a Senator shall vote. Violations of this provision shall be punished as the Senate deems proper. 

Any Senator may raise a point at any time unless denoted otherwise in these Rules. 

Types of points used within Senate include but are not limited to: 

Point of Personal Privilege:

To register a complaint about the environment of the meeting or make a personal request. 

Point of Information:

To request information of the presiding officer who may direct the point to any person who is present at the meeting.

Point of Clarification:

To make a germane factual statement.

Point of Order:

To enforce the rule(s). 

Point of Parliamentary Inquiry:

To ask a question regarding the rule(s).
