sections.heading: RULE TWELVE - Student Senate Conduct Code
sections.text:
All individuals in attendance of a Senate meeting shall demonstrate the proper respect for the business and procedures of the Student Senate and all other individuals in attendance. 

All individuals shall refrain from creating disturbances, especially loud conversation and noise, during official Senate proceedings. 

All Senators shall wear appropriate business or business casual attire while in the Senate chambers. Failure to act in accordance with the said rule shall result in the dismissal of the individual from Senate chambers at the discretion of the presiding officer. 

The presiding officer shall ensure that no Senator refers to or personally attacks another Senator or speaker by name or gesture during debate. This rule shall exclude pertinent debate during elections and confirmation hearings related to character and suitability for office.

The presiding officer shall ensure that no on-campus political party is advertised in the Senate Chambers or committee meetings. Such advertising shall consist of, but is not limited to, t-shirts, stickers and buttons that advertise party names. No International Federal, State, or Local candidate or political party shall be advertised in the Senate Chambers. This shall not limit a person in announcing a statement of fact, such as they, or another person are running for office.

A member of the Senate shall accept nothing which reasonably may be construed to improperly influence their official act, decision or vote.

sections.heading: RULE THIRTEEN - Senate Attendance
sections.text:
Attendance at the following meetings shall be considered mandatory for all Senators and Senate Officers. A roll call will be conducted at the beginning and end of each meeting for the purpose of determining quorum and attendance: 

Regularly scheduled meetings of the Student Senate as a whole. 

All standing committees, sub committees, and ad hoc committees on which a Senator or Senate Officer serves. 

Any properly called special session of the Senate. 

If a special session is called by the Student Senate President, an excused absence shall not negatively affect a Senator’s attendance record.

Any other meeting, upon concurrence of the Student Senate President and Student Senate President Pro Tempore, with at least twenty-four (24) hour notice to all the members required to attend. 

The Senate may overturn this provision at any time before or after the meeting with a two-thirds (2/3) vote. 

When roll is called at any meeting and a Senator is absent or tardy, the presiding officer must publicly state if the absence or tardy is excused or unexcused.

A Senator shall be considered as having no absences at the beginning of their term in office. Absences will accumulate over their term in office and will be counted against the Senator regardless of any change in the academic semester, or any intervening election in which their seat is not up for consideration. 

If an absence is considered unexcused, the failure to attend any meeting in its entirety shall constitute one full absence. If an absence is considered excused pursuant to Rule 13.9, the failure to attend any meeting in its entirety shall constitute one-half absence. There shall be a maximum of three (3) excused absences allowed to be used per term, any other absences shall be considered unexcused.
If a Senator has an excused absence in accordance with Rule 13.9(b)(4), this shall not constitute a one-half absence.

Failure to be present for any one roll call that determines attendance or quorum shall count as one-half absence. 

Senators who are not present during the initial roll call are tardy and must check in with the presiding officer upon entry into the meeting. 

If a tardy Senator does not check in with the presiding officer, they will accrue one-full absence in circumstances where a previous roll call is accepted as final roll call. 

Quorum shall be defined as more than half of the voting members of the body that is meeting.

At any time, any Senator may move for a roll call to determine quorum. 

Before a quorum call is conducted, the presiding officer shall call a three-minute recess to allow Senators to return to the chamber. 

In cases where quorum is not achieved and business must end, that quorum call shall be considered the final roll call of that meeting. 

Under no circumstance shall any Senator receive more than one full absence during any one meeting, even if multiple quorum or roll calls are conducted. 

Senators shall notify the appropriate presiding officer of a planned absence or tardy in writing prior to any missed Committee Meeting or Senate Meeting. 

If prior notice is not possible, any Senator who receives an absence or tardy shall be required to provide a written excuse to the presiding officer of the missed meeting within six (6) school days of the meeting. Failure to submit a written excuse within this period will result in the absence or tardy being declared unexcused. 

With proper documentation, the following shall be considered excused in addition to excuses listed in the university policy on attendance: 

Documented illness. 

Documented attendance of a class or class-related activity. 

Study session(s) or studying for a documented exam on the day following the absence. 

Religious holy days.

Calls to active military duty or jury duty.

Deaths in the family.

Official University activities.

In any other circumstance, the presiding officer shall have the discretion to determine if an absence or tardy is excused or unexcused, subject to appeal by the absent Senator before the Rules Committee. 

The decision of the presiding officer shall be presented to the absent Senator in writing and a copy shall be furnished to the Student Senate President Pro Tempore. 

The presiding officer shall be required to report all absences and tardies to the Student Senate President Pro Tempore within twenty-four (24) hours after the meeting and shall state whether or not the absence or tardy is excused or unexcused. 

Senators shall be allowed to be absent for one full meeting during each term. These shall be deemed a “Mental Health Day” and shall not count towards the total number of absences accumulated by each senator. Senators must notify the Senate President Pro-Tempore at least one day prior to the day of the excused meeting.

Penalties: for Absences and Tardies:

If a Senator is absent for two (2) committee meetings, they shall be required to meet with their Chair to determine whether or not they should be reassigned. If a decision is not reached in that meeting, the committee may, by a majority vote, expel a member who has received two (2) absences. If expelled from a standing committee, an expelled member must be reassigned to a different standing committee by the Student Senate President. 
If a Senator knows that they will not be able to attend the regularly scheduled meetings of a committee, it is their responsibility to meet with the Student Senate President regarding a reassignment prior to absences being accrued. 

Any Senator who accumulates any combination of three (3) absences through excused (0.5) and unexcused (1) absences, as described in Rule 13.4, shall be automatically suspended and forwarded to the Rules Committee for review over the Senator’s absences. Suspended senators shall not be considered in determining quorum, nor shall they be entitled to any rights or privileges of a Senator, except for those related to due process of potential impeachment proceedings. 

Taking the number of both excused and unexcused absences into consideration, the Rules Committee shall decide if the Senator is capable of continuing their work as a Senator in good faith. 

If the Rules Committee finds that the Senator is no longer capable of consistent attendance, they shall then forward the Senator to the Judiciary Committee for impeachment proceedings and the Judiciary Committee shall conduct those meetings according to all of the laws and rules related to impeachment contained in these rules, Statutes, and the Constitution. 

If the Rules Committee finds that the Senator is capable of continuing their work as a Senator in good faith, they shall unsuspend the Senator, then propose and vote on any number of additional absences that the Senator may accumulate before being suspended and subject to review by the Rules Committee again.

If the Judiciary Committee finds that the Senator is capable of continuing their work as a Senator in good faith, the Senator shall be remanded to the Rules Committee. After the Judiciary Committee meeting in which the Senator is remanded, the Rules Committee shall propose and vote on any number of additional absences the Senator may accumulate before being re-suspended. If the Senator is remanded to the Rules Committee, the committee by a two-thirds majority vote may forward the Senator directly to the Senate floor.

If the Senate, via the impeachment process, finds that the Senator is capable of continuing their work as a Senator in good faith, the Senator shall be unsuspended. The Senate shall enter debate to propose and vote on any number of additional absences the Senator may accumulate before being re-suspended.
Disability-related exceptions may be approved by the Student Senate President, Student Senate Pro-Tempore, and/or the Rules Committee.

All Senators shall be permitted to take a leave of absence during the summer session by informing the SGA Advisor in writing at least 2 weeks before the last Senate meeting in the Spring Semester. Any Senate seats temporarily vacated in this manner shall be advertised and filled in the same manner as other vacant Senate seats. Any Senator who takes this leave of absence shall resume office at the first Senate meeting of the fall semester.
All Senators shall be permitted to request a temporary leave of absence during their term for serious health conditions, family emergencies, or other significant circumstances that would reasonably prevent consistent attendance or participation in Senate duties. Such requests must be submitted in writing to the Student Senate President and the Student Senate President Pro Tempore and must specify the anticipated duration of the leave. The Rules Committee shall review the request and determine whether the leave shall be granted and under what conditions the Senator may return to active service. During an approved leave of absence, the Senator shall not accrue absences or be counted toward quorum.

sections.heading: RULE FOURTEEN - Discipline
sections.text:
If a Senator violates a provision of the Constitution, Statutes, or these Rules of Procedure, engages in disorderly conduct, or takes any other action(s) unbecoming of a Student Senator, the Senate may discipline the said Senator through a censure.

A censure shall:

Be a formal reprimand of a Senator’s action(s),

Be moved and seconded by four (4) senators, after which the question on the censure shall be put without intervening debate,

In the motion, the Senator making the motion must concisely state the reason for the censure.

Require a two-thirds (2/3) vote to pass,

If passed, be referred to the Rules Committee, which shall determine the level of punishment for the censure. Punishments for censure include:

A verbal or written warning,

Suspension from committee assignment(s) for no longer than four (4) meetings,

Suspension from all Senate business for no longer than three (3) weeks,

This action shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Rules Committee.

Forwarding to the Judiciary Committee to commence impeachment proceedings.

This action shall require a two-thirds (2/3rds) vote of the Rules Committee.

If moved in a committee, be voted on by the full Senate at the next Regular Meeting as a part of the committee’s report to the Senate.

Nothing in these Rules shall be construed as to prohibit the independent initiation of impeachment proceedings against the accused Senator by the Judiciary Committee in the manner prescribed by the Student Body Constitution and Student Body Statutes.

Failure of a Standing Committee Chair to give twenty-four (24) hour notice of a committee meeting shall constitute a one-half unexcused absence against the Chair.

Failure of a Vice Chair to prepare and submit a committee report in accordance with these rules shall constitute a one-half unexcused absence against the Vice Chair.

sections.heading: RULE SIXTEEN - College Delegations
sections.text:
RULE SIXTEEN – College Delegations 

A College Delegation shall consist of all Senators elected from the same academic college or unit as defined by Student Body Statutes and Senate apportionment. 
Each Delegation shall be recognized as a formal body within the Student Senate for purposes of coordination, representation, and constituency outreach. 
Meetings of College Delegations shall be required to be compliant with Chapter 203 and Chapter 210. 
Each College Delegation is required to meet at least once per semester. 
Absences to College Delegation meetings shall be recorded according to Rule 13.
Elections of College Delegation Leadership: 
After the ratification of the Senate President and Senate President Pro-Tempore, College Delegations shall convene to elect from among its members a Delegation Chair pursuant to Standing Committee elections in Rule 5.5. 
Election shall be by simple majority of the Delegation members present. 
Standing Committee Chairs shall be ineligible to serve as Delegation Chairs. 
This clause shall not be in effect if a Standing Committee Chair is a Senator within a college of two Senators or less. 
When a college is apportioned only one Senate seat, the senator shall be required to submit at least one instance of correspondence with their college’s administration to the Student Senate President and Student Senate President Pro-Tempore. 
They are not subject to fulfill the duties outlined in Rule 16.3 or Rule 16.5. 
In colleges apportioned two Senate seats, the most senior senator shall automatically serve as Delegation Chair unless they submit via email their intent to abdicate the role of Delegation Chair to the Student Senate President and Student Senate President Pro-Tempore. 
In college apportioned two Senate seats, and both senators have the same amount of tenure, then the Student Senate President has the right to appoint one of the two senators as College Delegation Chair. 
The other senator shall serve as the College Delegation Vice-Chair. 
The term of office for a Delegation Chair shall run concurrent with Standing Committee elections and shall be performed during the same meeting of the Senate.
Elections shall take place following Standing Committee elections and shall be performed during the same meeting of the Senate. 

Delegation shall elect a Vice Chair to assist the Chair and serve in their absence. 
In colleges apportioned two Senate seats, the most Junior Senator shall automatically serve as Delegation Vice Chair, unless the most senior senator abdicates Delegation Chair to the most Junior Senator. In this instance, a College Delegation Vice-Chair shall not be required. 
The Student Senate President or a designee from the Office of the Student Senate President or the Student Governance & Advocacy Office shall have the authority to preside over Delegation Chair and Vice Chair elections. 
The Delegation Chair shall perform the following duties: 
Represent the interests and concerns of their College Delegation before the Student Senate as a whole. 
Preside over College Delegation meetings. 
Serve as the official liaison between the Student Senate and their academic college’s Student Leadership Council, if such a body exists. 
If the Student Leadership Council does not exist, the College Delegation shall serve as the official liaison to their College’s administration. 
Organize and oversee the Delegation’s outreach initiatives to students in their college, including (but not limited to): tabling events and email correspondence. 
In the absence of the Chair, the Vice Chair shall assume all of the above duties. 
The Delegation Vice Chair shall perform the following duties: 
Take minutes at College Delegation meetings. 
The deadline to submit minutes shall be pursuant to Rule 5.11. 
Preside over Delegation meetings in the absence of the Delegation Chair. 
Ensure that all members of the Delegation are notified of scheduled meetings and shall monitor attendance of Delegation members. 
Assist the Delegation Chair in coordinating outreach initiatives and constituency concerns as directed. 
In the absence of the Vice Chair, the Chair shall assume all of the above duties. 
Each College Delegation is encouraged to organize itself to address the needs of its constituency and to coordinate the legislative agenda of its members. 
Constituency Reports shall provide a comprehensive summary of Delegation activities, including but not limited to: 
An overview of business addressed at College Delegation meetings. 
An overview of business addressed with the College Delegation’s respective college’s administration and/or Student Leadership Council (if such exists). 
An overview of concerns accumulated via outreach from the College Delegation’s constituency. 
Overview can include (but is not limited to) surveys, tabling events, and social media engagement. 
An overview of a comprehensive action plan of how the College Delegation plans to address the concerns of their constituency through legislation or other efforts through the Student Senate. 
College Delegation Oversight: 
The Senate President Pro-Tempore shall be responsible for: 
Hosting at least one (1) workshop per academic year to train Delegation Chairs and Vice Chairs on effective constituent outreach, reporting procedures, and time management strategies.
The facilitation of College Delegation Constituency Reports and are subject to provide feedback. 
Placing College Delegation Constituency Reports on the Student Senate Agenda under “Report of Senate Liaisons.” 
Ensure that the list of all recognized Delegations and their membership is maintained and updated at all times in accordance with the SG & A Webmaster. 
This includes the list of recognized College Delegations and their leadership. 
Conduct an annual review of College Delegations in accordance with the Executive Branch Department of Academic Affairs.

sections.heading: POLICY 2025-01: RSO ALLOCATIONS COMMITTEE

sections.heading: Section 1: Legislative Intent
sections.text:
Annually as part of the budget process, the Student Government Association may establish an allocation for the RSO Allocation Committee.
This program is designed to assist RSOs in carrying out their missions and enhancing campus life through student-led programming, events, travel opportunities, and other initiatives.
All funding allocated via this program is designated one-time, one-use funding.

sections.heading: Section 2: Committee Meetings
sections.text:
The Chair of the RSO Allocation Committee shall establish a regular, weekly meeting schedule. The committee must meet on Thursdays.
Committee meetings must be held once per week beginning the second week of each semester unless no funding requests are received.
All meetings of the committee are subject to the requirements of Chapter 203, Student Body Statutes, “The SGA Sunshine Act.”
In addition to the public notice requirements under the SGA Sunshine Act, the Chair shall send a notice of the meeting time and location to any RSOs scheduled to present at least 24 hours before the meeting.
By Tuesday at 5:00 PM prior to each meeting, the Chair of the committee shall distribute a meeting agenda to all committee members as well as an agenda packet including each funding request to be considered during the meeting and a draft Senate resolution with the committee’s funding recommendations.
At the request of any committee member, or by action of the Chair, a funding request on the agenda of the committee may be tabled until the next meeting of the committee, or until a date certain.
The Chair shall endeavor to schedule meetings and such that no more than eight (8) funding requests are heard per week. The Chair may, however, at their discretion, schedule additional requests as needed, with no more than fifteen (15) funding requests heard per week.
The order in which requests are heard shall be based primarily on the chronological order in which funding requests are received. The Chair may adjust the order to prioritize requests based on the scheduled date of the associated event or trip.
All committee meetings must conclude by 10:00 PM. However, this rule may be waived by a 2/3 vote of the committee, but shall go no later than 11:30 PM.
Official attendance at committee meetings shall be kept by the Vice Chair. Attendance at meetings is mandatory and all rules regarding attendance for the purposes of this committee shall match and reflect those found in Rule #13 of the Student Senate Rules of Procedure, “Senate Attendance.”
When a funding request comes before the committee, there shall be a period of consideration. A period of consideration shall last no longer than thirty (30) minutes on a funding request and will occur as follows:

A presentation by the representative(s) of no more than five (5) minutes. No motions may be made during this round.
The opening statement shall be followed by a period of general questioning. The presiding officer shall recognize each member on the committee wishing to ask a question. Questions shall be technical and non-debatable, which shall consist of factual inquiries directed toward the RSO representative(s), these questions shall only consist of the approved question list. Only the Chair or Vice Chair retain the authority to ask or approve clarifying questions outside of the approved question list under extraordinary circumstances. 
The Presiding officer shall ask for a motion to enter roundtable discussion. If there is an objection, the motion fails and questioning continues.
In roundtable discussion, the presiding officer shall open the floor for members to speak freely. Discussion may include clarifying questions for the Chair, Vice Chair or other committee members or further limited technical non-debatable questions to the organization.
Following the period of roundtable discussion, the presiding officer shall enter the period of scoring for committee members. The committee shall have up to five (5) minutes to complete scoring for the organization, after which all scores shall be submitted to the Vice Chair. Once all scores have been received, a motion to lock the scores shall be entertained, requiring a majority vote. Upon adoption, all submitted scores shall be considered final. At no point during the scoring period shall there be debate, private communication, or internal discussion among committee members, except that the Chair and Vice Chair may provide clarifying information to ensure members understand the rubric and scoring process.
Committee members must confine their remarks in roundtable discussion to the pending funding request. Personal remarks must not enter into discussion. All remarks must be addressed to the Chair. Any member violating these rules may, at the discretion of the Chair, lose the floor.
Committee members may ask follow-up questions that can probe for clarification but should avoid leading or subjective phrasing. The Chair shall be responsible for ensuring no questions fall outside of this standard.
All votes must be recorded by the Vice Chair in the minutes.
Representatives may yield their time to the Chair. Follow-up questions do not require reservations and may be asked freely.
The Chair shall not vote except in cases of a tie.

sections.heading: Section 3: Requirements For Funding Requests
sections.text:
All funding requests must include three (3) supporting/competitive quotes for each category in which the RSO is requesting funds. If less than three quotes were submitted with the application, the Chair can accept these quotes at the meeting. If an RSO fails to provide these three quotes, they must submit another application.
All requests must be of a line-item nature with quotes (clothing costs, performer costs, reservation costs, equipment rental, facility rental, airline ticket quotes, rental car quotes, hotel quotes, etc.), and an explanation of need and of benefits to the student body.
All final funding allocations of the committee must be approved by the Student Senate at least 30 calendar days before the event or travel is to take place. Accordingly, the committee should consider requests and make funding recommendations to the Student Senate no later than five to six weeks prior to the event or travel date. 
All other guidelines and restrictions regarding funding requests to the RSO Allocation Committee are prescribed in Chapter 816, Student Body Statutes.

sections.heading: Section 4: Criteria For Evaluation Of Funding Requests
sections.text:
All funding applications submitted to the committee shall be reviewed and scored by each voting member using the scoring rubric and criteria provided in Table #1 below. The rubric assigns a numerical value to clearly defined criteria, with a maximum possible score determined in advance.
At the conclusion of each committee meeting, the Vice Chair shall compile and average the scores submitted by each voting member for every application considered. The starting value of each funding request shall be the total amount of valid expenditures included in the application, as determined by eligibility under applicable funding categories. Items that do not qualify as allowable expenditures within the specific funding type, such as non-programming items within a programming request or ineligible travel costs within a travel request, shall not be included in the total amount to be scored. The Chair shall be responsible for reviewing each request prior to scoring to ensure that only valid and eligible expenditures are considered in the total amount used for evaluation.

The committee’s funding recommendation for each application shall be directly proportional to the average points received out of the maximum of one hundred (100) points. For example, if an application receives an average score equal to ninety (90) of the total one hundred (100) possible points, the committee shall recommend awarding 90% of the amount requested. This proportional funding model is intended to ensure consistency, fairness, and transparency in the allocation of limited resources. Final funding allocations shall be subject to approval by the Student Senate.
Each subsection of the rubric should have at least three targeted questions asked consistently across applicants.
For each completed and compiled rubric, the Vice Chair shall maintain a final scored rubric summary for every organization considered. This summary shall include the average score from all committee members, as well as an “Evaluator Notes” column.
The “Evaluator Notes” column shall be used to document key answers, quotes, or clarifying information provided by the organization during questioning that the Chair or Vice Chair determine were central to the committee’s deliberation or final scoring outcome. These notes are intended to enable the Student Senate to understand the substantive basis for the committee’s recommendations.
The allocation resolution transmitted to the Student Senate shall include, for every organization reviewed by the RSO Allocation Committee, the following materials:
The individual scores submitted by each voting committee member;
The overall averaged score for the organization, as compiled by the Vice Chair;
The corresponding Evaluator Notes section documenting key responses, quotes, or clarifications that informed the committee’s decision;
The attendance record for the meeting, identifying which members were present for each organization’s presentation and scoring;
The original Qualtrics funding request submission, including all attached documentation;
All supporting quotes, invoices, or pricing materials reviewed by the committee; and
Any presentation materials submitted by the organization ahead of the committee meeting.
These materials shall be attached in full to the allocation resolution and made available to the Student Senate and the public as part of the legislative record, regardless of whether an organization received full, partial, or zero funding.
Under no circumstances may the RSO Allocation Committee allocate or recommend any funding to a Registered Student Organization outside of the approved rubric and scoring process established in this policy. Any recommendation not derived from rubric-based evaluation shall be deemed invalid and returned to the committee for proper consideration

Table #1: RSO Allocation Committee Full Evaluation Rubric:

Subsection / Criteria	Descriptor	Max Pts	 	 	 	 	 
1. Purpose, Impact & FSU Benefit	To assess how clearly and effectively the proposed program advances the missions of both Florida State University and the Student Government Association, and how strongly it contributes to the educational, cultural, and reputational benefit of the student body.	35	Outstanding 	Excellent	Standard	Developing	Unsatisfactory
1A. Clarity of Purpose & Alignment	

How clearly the proposal states a single, focused purpose; the measurable outcomes tied to that purpose; and an explicit, credible link to FSU/SGA mission areas in the context of an event or student travel (learning, leadership, public service, research/scholarship, representation/advocacy, diversity & inclusion, civic engagement, cross-campus collaboration).    

Evidence required in the application (must be present to score above “Developing”):

- A one-sentence purpose statement + a short paragraph of context.
- At least one measurable outcome (what changes/outputs will occur).
- Mission alignment statement naming the relevant mission area(s) and how this activity advances them.
- If travel: the role/participation (presenting? competing? serving?), plus a specific campus-return deliverable with audience and date window.

	10	The proposal presents a crystal-clear, mission-driven purpose with measurable outcomes and direct institutional benefit to FSU students.
- Purpose is singular and specific; no scope creep.
- Lists 1–3 explicit, measurable outcomes (e.g., “deliver X open workshop(s) serving ≥N students within 30 days; submit public recap w/ materials”).
- Direct, named mission linkage to at least one area (learning/leadership/service/etc.) and explains mechanism of impact (how the activity advances that area).
- If travel: applicants are active contributors
(presenting/competing/serving), and commit to a campus-return deliverable with date, format, target audience, and dissemination plan (University-designated student organization management platform/event listing, open attendance, posted slides/resources).
- Outcomes include a verification method (sign-ins, artifact links, media, post-event survey plan).	The proposal offers a strong and focused purpose with clear alignment to FSU and SGA missions, though less comprehensive in outcomes or follow-up.
- Purpose is clear and focused.
- States measurable outcomes, though fewer details on verification or thresholds.
- Named mission area(s) with a credible explanation of alignment.
- If travel: active participation or official representation is documented; campus-return deliverable is specified but with lighter detail (e.g., timeframe but no comms plan).	The proposal communicates a
general purpose that loosely aligns with FSU and SGA goals but lacks measurable outcomes or detailed impact explanation.

- Purpose understandable but partly broad or mixed aims.
- Outcomes are present but partly qualitative (hard to verify) or stated as activities instead of results.
- Mission linkage is general (“supports learning/diversity”) without the how.
- If travel: states benefit to participants; mentions sharing back but lacks a concrete deliverable or audience.	

The proposal’s purpose is vague or incomplete, showing minimal evidence of measurable outcomes or meaningful mission alignment.

- Purpose is vague/compound; unclear what success looks like.
- Outcomes missing or non-measurable (“raise awareness” with no
indicator).
- Mission linkage implied, not stated; reads as a club goal vs. FSU/SGA
mission advancement.
- If travel: primarily passive attendance; no campus-return plan.

	

The proposal lacks a defined purpose or any credible link to FSU or SGA missions and presents no measurable benefit to students.

- No clear purpose/outcomes.
- No articulated mission link.
- If travel: recreational/social focus; no broader student benefit; no campus-return deliverable.

1B. Student Benefit & Reach	

The extent to which the proposed activity produces clear, equitable, and measurable benefits for FSU students. This includes (a) the scale of participation, (b) the diversity and accessibility of the audience or participants, and (c) the depth of educational, cultural, or developmental value delivered.
   

Required evidence (must be present to score above “Developing”):

- Estimated number of students directly served and indirectly
impacted.
- Description of how the event or trip is accessible to all students (e.g., open attendance, low/no cost, marketing plan).
- Explanation of what benefit participants will gain (skills, experience, service, cultural enrichment, advocacy, etc.).
- If travel: explanation of how outcomes will be shared back to campus (e.g., panel, presentation, mentoring session).

	10	The proposal provides broad, inclusive, and measurable benefits that significantly enhance the student experience across multiple communities.
- Clearly defines target audiences (by size and diversity) and shows how students across majors, backgrounds, or identities can access or participate.
- Lists specific measurable outcomes (attendance numbers, engagement metrics, or follow-up deliverables).
- If travel: includes verifiable plan for post-trip engagement that reaches
  50+ students or multiple RSOs/departments.
- Emphasizes equity of access (low cost, ADA compliance, open promotion).
- Provides credible evidence that the activity enhances student learning, leadership, public service, or cultural understanding.	The proposal demonstrates
meaningful student benefit and engagement, serving diverse students through
clear, well-defined outreach.

- Identifies clear audience(s) and expected participation figures.
- Shows reasonable accessibility and effort to engage diverse students.
- Explains learning or developmental outcomes (skills, awareness,
  leadership, etc.).
- If travel: includes a defined, though smaller-scale, campus-return event (e.g., workshop, social media resource series).	The proposal shows a reasonable but limited student benefit, primarily serving a single community or
demographic with minimal inclusivity detail.

- Benefits are clear but focused on one community or major demographic.
- Accessibility efforts mentioned but not detailed.
- Learning/developmental impact is general (“participants will learn about…”).
- If travel: campus-return deliverable mentioned but without detail on format, audience, or timeline.	

The proposal provides unclear or narrow student benefit, focusing mostly on internal membership without measurable outreach or accessibility.

- Primarily serves RSO members with minimal outreach.
- Little or no data on participant numbers or accessibility.
-Learning/developmental impact implied but not articulated.
- If travel: benefit restricted to attendees; no campus-sharing plan.

	

The proposal shows no tangible student benefit or engagement beyond a few participants and lacks any demonstration of inclusivity.

- Event or trip primarily benefits a few individuals; no demonstration of broader student engagement or measurable outcome.
- No mention of accessibility, inclusion, or campus return.

1C. Enhancement of SGA/FSU Image & Recognition	

How the proposed program, project, or travel activity enhances FSU’s reputation for excellence, leadership, innovation, diversity, and service, both on and off campus. Evaluators are determining whether the proposal provides public-facing, verifiable presentation of Florida State University or creates lasting positive visibility for FSU students, organizations, or programs.
   
Required Evidence (must be present to score above “Developing”):

- Description of the audience (campus, local community, regional, national, or international).
- How FSU is represented or promoted: use of logos, affiliation, or official participation.
- Expected outcome: recognition, media coverage, awards, publication, conference presentation, or event visibility metrics.
- If travel: verification that students are actively presenting, competing, serving, or representing FSU, and plan to publicly report back or share results on campus (through event, media, or official channels).

	10	The proposal clearly and credibly elevates FSU’s visibility or reputation through public engagement, achievement, or service.
  
- Specifies the audience and scale of recognition (campuswide, statewide, national, or international).
- Defines tangible, measurable outcomes, such as media coverage, published materials, awards, competition results, or formal university acknowledgment.
- If travel: participants are official representatives of FSU (presenters, competitors, performers, or delegates) and have a plan to share outcomes broadly with the FSU community through open reporting or events.
- Explicitly references FSU’s values of academic excellence, diversity, and public service in context of the activity.	Demonstrates clear, credible
enhancement of FSU’s image through representation or outreach.
    
- Defines scope of recognition (university, community, or regional).
- Specifies deliverables or visibility outcomes (public event, digital publication,
or official acknowledgment).
- If travel: FSU representation is verified but campus-return plan has limited detail.
- Reflects university professionalism and positive visibility.	Provides moderate FSU representation but with limited scope or detail.
  
- Mentions FSU branding or affiliation but without measurable or external
outcomes.
- Event is primarily campus-based and open to FSU students but lacks external exposure.
- If travel: mentions FSU participation but no documentation of how visibility will be created or reported back.	

Shows weak or unclear connection to FSU’s image or visibility.

- References FSU only generally (“FSU students attending”) without
explaining representation.
- No measurable or visible outcomes identified.
- If travel: attendees are passive participants; no evidence of official
representation or follow-up plan.

	No discernible enhancement of FSU’s image or recognition.

- Activity does not involve representation, visibility, or measurable contribution to FSU’s standing.
- May be personal, social, or purely internal with no campus or public relevance.
1D. Contribution to Campus Culture / Tradition	How intentionally and effectively the proposed activity strengthens the FSU community, fosters collaboration among student organizations, and contributes to campus unity, pride, and continuity of tradition. Evaluators should determine whether the activity builds lasting engagement or creates opportunities for new traditions consistent with the values of the FSU Student Body.
   
Required Evidence (must be present to score above “Developing”):

- Description of how the activity promotes connection, belonging, or community engagement among students.
- List of collaborating RSOs, departments, or community partners, if applicable.
- Explanation of how the program contributes to an existing or new FSU tradition, initiative, or annual event cycle.
- Plan for sustainability or recurrence (whether the event can become ongoing or institutionalized).
- Indication that the activity reinforces FSU’s identity, inclusivity, and spirit in line with SGA’s constitutional goals.	5	The proposal clearly and intentionally strengthens FSU’s campus culture and fosters enduring community connections.
    
- Brings together multiple RSOs, colleges, or departments under a common purpose that reflects FSU’s values of diversity, collaboration, and service.
- Demonstrates potential to become or sustain an identifiable FSU tradition (annual event, recognized initiative, or long-standing collaborative effort).
- Defines measurable outcomes such as cross-organization participation numbers, volunteer hours, or recurrence plans.
- Explicitly references SGA’s mission of representation, engagement, and unity.	Promotes strong community
engagement and contributes meaningfully to student unity.

- Includes clear collaboration among at least one other RSO or campus unit.
- Shows evidence of recurrence or intent to integrate into ongoing university programming.
- Aligns with FSU’s commitment to diversity and inclusion.	Demonstrates moderate contribution to campus culture or student engagement.
    
- Connects to the campus community through open participation or spirit promotion.
- Primarily a single-organization effort with limited collaboration.
- Tradition potential mentioned but not developed.	Shows limited or unclear contribution to campus culture.

- Event or trip primarily benefits internal membership; no concrete
collaboration or long-term impact described.
- Tradition or community aspects implied but unsupported.	No evident connection to campus culture or community unity.

- Isolated activity with no engagement beyond participants; lacks inclusivity or FSU-specific identity.
2. Student Engagement, Inclusion & Community Reach	To assess the extent to which the proposed activity actively engages students across diverse identities, organizations, and disciplines, fosters inclusion, and expands involvement beyond the proposing RSO’s core membership. This section measures both depth (quality of engagement) and breadth (diversity and reach) of participation, ensuring that SGA-funded initiatives reflect the diversity and unity of the FSU community.	15	Outstanding 	Excellent	Standard	Developing	Unsatisfactory
2A. Depth of Student Engagement	The quality and intentionality of student involvement during the activity. This includes how interactive, developmental, and participatory the experience is, beyond mere attendance or observation.
   
Evaluators should determine whether the proposal:
- Clearly defines how students will be engaged (learning, leadership, service, creation, collaboration).
- Identifies specific engagement methods (workshops, mentorship, service projects, peer dialogue, competitions, panels, creative production, etc.).
- Demonstrates active participation rather than passive observation.
- Connects engagement activities to measurable outcomes or skill development.
 
Required Evidence (to score above ‘Developing’):
- A description of student roles (e.g., participants, leaders, presenters, organizers).
- Explanation of what students will do during the event (activities, discussions, projects, competitions, service, etc.).
- Learning or skill outcomes tied to engagement (what knowledge, ability, or experience students gain).
- (If travel) Evidence that participants are actively presenting, performing, serving, or competing, and not only attending.	5	The proposal provides clear, intentional, and measurable forms of student engagement.
    
- Students are active participants, not just attendees, directly involved through collaboration, dialogue, performance, service, or leadership.
- Engagement plan identifies specific activities, timelines, and participant roles.
- Outcomes are quantifiable and skill-based (e.g., communication, teamwork, leadership, civic understanding).
- Engagement model aligns with FSU’s educational and service mission, emphasizing depth and reflection.
- If travel: participants play central, contributory roles and have an identifiable plan to extend engagement upon return (e.g., training peers, leading workshops).

	Demonstrates well-developed
opportunities for meaningful interaction and learning.
   
- Participants have active roles; some details provided about structure and
expected outcomes.
- Engagement methods are interactive (discussion, group work, competition, service).
- If travel: participants contribute substantively, though reflection or campus follow-up is less detailed.	Provides moderate engagement
that primarily involves attendance or observation with limited interactive
elements.

- Some opportunity for feedback, Q&A, or discussion, but engagement is
not the event’s core design.
- Outcomes are described broadly (“students will learn about…”).
- If travel: engagement is passive, but participants are expected to share
experiences informally.	Demonstrates minimal or unclear student engagement.

- Participation described vaguely (“students will attend”).
- No clear engagement activity or learning outcome.
- If travel: attendees observe without formal roles or contribution.	No engagement plan or evidence of active participation.

- Students are passive audience members or recipients with no measurable outcome.
- No linkage to learning, leadership, or service.
2B. Inclusion & Accessibility Efforts	

How purposefully and effectively the proposed activity incorporates inclusion, and accessibility principles in both planning and execution.

This includes:
- Ensuring that participation is open, affordable, and accessible to all students.
- Representing diverse perspectives, identities, and disciplines in content and leadership.
