sections.heading: JUDICIARY: RULE 1 - Authority And Changes To Committee Rules
sections.text:
The Judiciary Committee shall be governed by, in order of precedence, the Constitution of the Student Body, the Statutes of the Student Body, the Rules of Procedure of the Student Senate, these Judiciary Rules of Procedure, and the latest version of Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised.
Changes to these Rules of Procedure shall require a majority vote of the committee.
HISTORY
Adopted by Res. R78-030 on 6/17/2026

sections.heading: JUDICIARY: RULE 2 - Agenda And Business
sections.text:
Meetings of the committee may be called by the Chair as deemed necessary, providing that hours’ notice of the date, time, and place of the meeting is provided via the SGA website or other form of public announcement, per Chapter 203 of Student Statutes.  

The Chair of the committee shall be responsible for setting the agenda and docket for each meeting. In the absence of the Chair, the Vice Chair shall assume all official duties of the Chair. In the absence of the Vice Chair, the most senior member of the committee shall assume all official duties of the Chair.  

The Chair, or presiding officer, shall call each meeting to order, which shall immediately be followed by a roll call of attendance and verification of quorum by the Vice-Chair or presiding officer.
The Chair, or presiding officer, may set requirements for attendance as needed to ensure engagement. 
The committee shall reserve the right to table legislation by majority vote, unlock the calendar by majority vote, and wield all other procedural and legislative powers given to the committee in the Senate Rules and Procedures, Student Body Statutes, and Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised.  

In the event of the Chair or Vice Chair being a sponsor of legislation up for debate in the committee, the Chair or Vice Chair shall temporarily step down from their position and follow the procedure as outlined in Part 1, Rule One, Section 1.1.  

All other procedures related to the agenda and business shall be derived from the Senate Rules of Procedures. 
HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-030 on 6/17/2026

sections.heading: JUDICIARY: RULE 3 - Debate Procedure
sections.text:
For the purposes of debate, the Chair shall preside over all discussions and be responsible for yielding time to committee members to speak.
For the purposes of hearing assigned legislation, the Chair shall afford the sponsors 3 minutes for their opening statements.
Following opening statements, the committee may move to enter either round table discussion or pro-con debate. In the event neither motion is made, the chair may compel a motion to enter round table discussion.
Following the cessation of round table, pro-con debate, or both, the committee may move to call the question and afford the sponsors of the legislation the time remaining from their opening for their closing.
Non-Senators may be eligible to speak, however, a motion must be made to allow a non-senator to speak, per Rule 5.10(c) of Senate Rules of Procedure.
All other procedures related to debate shall be derived from the Senate Rules and Procedures and Robert's Rules of Order Newly Revised.

HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-030 on 6/17/2026

sections.heading: JUDICIARY: RULE 4 - Hearings Procedure
sections.text:
A hearing shall be defined as an opportunity for any organization, student, or SGA entity to speak to the Judiciary Committee to inform the committee on a specific topic or give the opportunity for the committee to ask questions in a formal setting.
If a hearing is scheduled for the committee, it shall take place following the completion of all legislative work for that day.
The Chair shall yield an amount of time to be determined at their discretion but no shorter than five (5) minutes to the group testifying before the committee for an opening statement.
Following the opening statement, each member of the committee shall be given 3 minutes individually to ask questions or make statements.
When all committee members have been given the opportunity to speak, the group testifying shall have 3 minutes for a closing statement 

HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-030 on 6/17/2026

sections.heading: JUDICIARY: RULE 5 - Interview Procedure
sections.text:
Candidates being interviewed for confirmation shall be allowed to make an opening statement for up to, but not exceeding, five (5) minutes. Any remaining time shall be allotted to a closing statement.
The committee shall enter a round of questioning after the candidate has concluded their opening statement. Questions may relate to, but are not limited to, the candidate's desired position, experience, character or future goals. 
The committee shall enter a round of deliberation lasting a total of fifteen (15) minutes. This round may be extended by motion from a member of the committee. 
After a motion is made to call the question, the candidate shall be allowed to make a closing statement for up to, but not exceeding, any time remaining for their closing statement. 
The committee shall conduct a vote, administered by the Vice-Chair or presiding officer, on whether the candidate shall be approved by the committee and forwarded to the full Senate for consideration. 
HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-030 on 6/17/2026

sections.heading: JUDICIARY: RULE 6 - Impeachment Hearing Procedure
sections.text:
Per Statute 206.2(d) and Sections 405.3 and 405.4, the Judiciary Committee may initiate impeachment proceedings against any Student Government officers, members, or employees of the entity found in violation of Section 206(1).
Upon receiving formal charges of the impeachment from the Senate Program Assistant, the Judiciary Committee shall vote on whether these charges shall be considered by majority vote. 
If the motion to consider passes, the Committee shall notify the accused officer via their official FSU email, at least one week before the impeachment hearing, including the time, date, and place of the meeting. The accused officer shall retain the right to speak in their defense, refuse to appear, remain silent, and refer to counsel at any time.
The officer considered for impeachment shall have five (5) minutes total to speak in their defense. This can be split between their opening and closing statements. 
Following their opening statement, the Committee shall enter a period of deliberation and questioning until a motion is made to call the question. 
After the motion to call the question has passed, the accused officer may present their closing statement if time has been yielded from their opening. 
Impeachment of the accused officer shall require a majority vote, made by open ballot. 
HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-030 on 6/17/2026

sections.heading: IA: RULE 1 - Authority And Changes To Committee Rules
sections.text:
The Internal Affairs Committee shall be governed by, in order of precedence, the Constitution of the Student Body, the Statutes of the Student Body, the Rules of Procedure of the Student Senate, these Internal Affairs Rules of Procedure, and the latest version of Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised.
Changes to these Rules of Procedure shall require a majority vote of the committee.

sections.heading: IA: RULE 2 - Meetings Of The Committee
sections.text:
Meetings of the committee may be called by the Chair as deemed necessary providing that 24 hours’ notice of the date, time, and place of the meeting are given via the SGA website or other form of public announcement.
Unless a different date and time are set by the Chair pursuant to section (A) of this rule, committee meetings shall be held at 6:30 p.m. Eastern Time on Mondays during the regular session of the Student Senate. This shall be considered the regular meeting time at which committee business will be completed.
The Chair, or presiding officer, shall call each meeting to order, which shall immediately be followed by a roll call of attendance and verification of quorum by the Vice-Chair.
Committee members, either by motion or petitioning the Chair to take action, may request a bill, matter, or nomination on the agenda of the committee be held over until the next meeting of the committee.
Only members of the committee are permitted to speak on any measure being considered by the committee. This rule may be waived via motion to allow a non-member to speak.
All meetings are to be made open and available to the public. This is to ensure correct adherence to Chapter 203 of the Student Body Statutes.
The chair or the presiding officer over the committee shall read the Land Acknowledgement at the start of the meeting or designate another member to do so.

sections.heading: IA: RULE 3 - Interview Procedure
sections.text:
The committee must abide by any additional time constraints and requirements as outlined in the Student Body Constitution or Student Body Statutes.
The following procedure shall take place for all candidate confirmation hearings conducted by the committee
The candidate shall be allowed to make an opening statement for up to, but not exceeding, three (3) minutes. Any remaining time shall be allotted to a closing statement.
The committee shall enter a round of questioning. Questions may relate to, but are not limited to, the candidate’s desired position, experience, character or future goals.
Any Senator(s) present who are not committee members may ask any additional questions not previously directed to the candidate by the committee.
The committee shall enter a round of deliberation that shall not exceed fifteen (15) minutes. 5. After a motion is made to call the question, the candidate shall be allowed to make a closing statement for up to, but not exceeding, any time remaining from their opening statement.
The committee shall conduct a vote, administered by the Vice-Chair on whether the candidate shall be forwarded to the full Senate for consideration.

sections.heading: IA: RULE 4 - Bills And Resolutions Procedure
sections.text:
The following procedure shall take place for all bills and resolutions considered by the committee
The sponsor(s) shall be allowed to make an opening statement for up to, but not exceeding, five (5) minutes. Any remaining time shall be allotted to a closing statement.
The Chair shall entertain any questions from committee members.
The committee shall enter a round of deliberation that shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes.
The sponsor(s) shall be allowed to make a closing statement for up to, but not exceeding, any time remaining from their opening statement.
The committee shall conduct a vote, the administration of which shall be at the discretion of the Chair, on whether the legislation shall be forwarded to the full Senate for consideration.

sections.heading: IA: RULE 5 - Department Review
sections.text:
In accordance with Chapter 900.5 of the Student Body Statutes, the following procedure shall be followed when conducting the annual review of SGA Departments.

Timeframe
At least two (2) weeks prior to the first day of presentations, the Chair must contact the Departments with the time, location, and guidelines for the content of the presentations.
Department Presentations 
The Chair shall request that Department leaders provide the following information:
The names and contact information of the current leadership.
All relevant financial information and documentation.
A list of previous and upcoming events (Including figures on turnout).
A description of how the Department is fulfilling their mission statement and the mission of Student Government as a whole.
Any other information as determined by the committee.
An overview of their selection and forwarding process for executive board members to be appointed by the Student Body President.
A report of their satisfaction with their governing statutes.
Committee Questioning
Following a Department's presentation, the committee shall question the presenters using the following procedure:
The committee shall enter a round of general questioning from committee members.
Any Senator(s) present who are not committee members may ask any additional questions not previously directed to the presenters by the committee.
Any member of the public present may ask any additional questions not previously directed to the presenters by Senators.
The presenters may ask any questions of the committee.
Deliberation
In the committee meeting immediately following the conclusion of all presentations and questioning, the committee shall enter deliberation via a motion.
The order in which the Departments will be considered for deliberation shall be determined by the committee.
During deliberation, the committee shall not compare Departments with one another based on their presentations, proposals, or deliberations relating to another Department.
Following deliberation on a Bureau, a vote shall be held to determine whether the committee recommends the Bureau remains established.
Once the vote has concluded, the committee shall then further deliberate to provide some short reasoning behind the recommendation and shall provide any guidance and feedback for the Bureau.
Department Review Resolutions
Following the completion of deliberations, the committee shall draft separate resolutions for each bureau that shall be introduced at the next possible Senate meeting.
Each resolution shall explain the following pertaining to each Department:
A summary of their presentation to the committee
Analysis of the criteria enumerated in Chapter 301 of Student Body Statutes.
The result of the committee’s vote on recommending the retention or dissolution of the Department.
The committee’s reasoning for their decision and vote.
Proposed next steps and recommendations for the future of the Department.

HISTORY
Amended by Res. R77-064 on 10/8/2025

sections.heading: IA: RULE 6 - Quorum
sections.text: Quorum shall be defined as more than half of the total number of committee members present, for the purpose of discussing and transacting business, pursuant to Chapter 400.4 of Student Body Statutes.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 1 - Authorities And Changes To Committee Rules
sections.text:
The Chair of the Committee shall be responsible for setting the agenda and docket for each meeting. In the absence of the Chair, the Vice Chair shall assume all official duties of the Chair. In the absence of the Vice Chair, the most senior member of the Committee shall assume all official duties of the Chair.
Changes to these Rules of Procedure shall require a majority vote of the Committee, changes shall be submitted through a Senate Resolution.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 2 - Meetings Of The Committee
sections.text:
Meetings of the Committee may by the Chair as they deem necessary with a three (3) day public notice of the date, time, place, and subject matter of the meeting, in adherence with the Rules of Procedure of the Student Senate and the Florida Sunshine Law.
Unless a different date and time are set by the Chair pursuant to one (1) of this section, Committee meetings shall be held at 5:00 p.m. on Tuesdays during the regular session of the Student Senate. By majority vote of the Committee the time may be changed for the following meeting.
By majority vote of the Committee or by action of the Chair, a bill, matter, or nomination on the agenda of the Committee may be tabled until the next meeting of the Committee.
The Vice-Chair shall submit a Report after every meeting to the SG&A Webmaster within twenty-four (24) hours after the meeting. The Report shall include:
Call to Order
Verification of Quorum
Land Acknowledgement
Announcements
Old Business
New Business
Unfinished Business
Closing Announcements
Date and Time of Next Meeting
Adjournment
The Presiding officer shall call each meeting to order, and immediately after the ViceChair shall verify quorum by a roll call vote.
Participation in debate on measures before the Committee is restricted to Committee members. However, the Committee may, at its discretion, waive this rule to permit a non-member to speak.
A Committee member may propose a motion to allow a non-senator to address the Committee. This motion, if passed, grants speaking privileges to the non-senator for a specified duration or topic, as determined by the Committee.
All meetings are public, and space shall be made available in the meeting room for members of the public to sit and listen. This rule is to ensure proper adherence with the Statutes of the Student Body and the Florida Sunshine Law.
The Chair shall go through the Report format laid out above from the top down and shall begin debate on business by stating the question before the Committee. When a Bill or Resolution comes before the Committee the rules outlined in Rule 5 shall apply.
No Senator may make any statement without first being recognized by the Chair.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 3 - Quorum And Ex-Officio Member Status
sections.text:
A quorum for the purpose of discussing business shall be constituted by a majority of the Members of the Committee present, including the Chair of the Committee who is a non-voting member but shall count towards the quorum. No bill or matter shall be ordered or reported from the Committee unless a majority of the Committee is present. 
The Student Senate President and the Student Senate President Pro-Tempore are ex-officio members of the Committee and shall vote, if necessary, in adherence with the Student Senate Rules of Procedure.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 4 - Attendance
sections.text:
Official attendance at all Committee meetings shall be kept by the Vice-Chair and transmitted weekly to the Student Senate President Pro-Tempore.
Attendance at meetings is mandatory and all rules regarding Attendance for the purposes of this Committee shall match and reflect those found in the Rules of Procedure of the Student Senate.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 5 - Bills And Resolutions
sections.text:
The following procedure shall take place for the hearing of all Bills and Resolutions before the Committee
The sponsor(s) shall be allowed to make an opening statement of no more than five (5) minutes. Any time remaining from the opening shall be reserved for the closing statement. No motions may be made during this round.
The opening statement shall be followed by technical non-debatable questions. The Chair shall recognize each Senator wishing to speak in the order in which they raise their hand. Motions to amend may not be made during this round.
The sponsor(s) answer shall remain within the bounds of the question being addressed to them. The Chair reserves the right to take back the floor if the sponsor(s) answer is not germane.
Technical non-debatable questioning shall be followed by general questioning. The Chair shall recognize each Senator wishing to speak in the order in which they raise their hand. Motions to amend may be made during this round.
The sponsor(s) answer shall remain within the bounds of the question being addressed to them. The Chair reserves the right to take back the floor if the sponsor(s) answer is not germane.
Immediately following general questioning, the Chair shall announce any Senators may propose amendments. Each amendment must be submitted either in writing or verbally to the Chair.
The Senator proposing the amendment will be granted two (2) minutes to explain it. A brief discussion, not exceeding five (5) minutes, will follow. The Committee shall then vote on each amendment, requiring a simple majority for adoption.
If there are no remaining amendments, general questioning shall be followed by one round of roundtable debate. The Chair shall ask for a motion to open the floor to roundtable debate. The sponsor(s) may not participate in this round, even if they are a member of the Committee.
Senators must confine their remarks in debate to the pending question. Personal remarks must not enter debate. All remarks must be addressed to the Chair. Any Senator violating these rules may, at the discretion of the Chair, lose the floor.
Each Senator is limited to three (3) minutes for their statements. The total duration for this phase shall not exceed thirty (30) minutes, unless extended by a majority Committee vote.
After the conclusion of remarks by all Committee members, the Chair will entertain a motion to call the question on the Bill or Resolution. A roll call vote shall then be administered by the Vice-Chair. The Chair shall not vote, except to break a tie.
If the Chair does not want to break the tie, the matter shall be tabled for reconsideration at the next meeting, ensuring decisions are made with a clear majority.
In instances where the Chair or Vice Chair is a sponsor of the legislation under discussion, they must temporarily step down from their official role for the duration of the discussion and voting on that specific legislation.
If it is only the Chair, the Vice Chair shall temporarily preside over the proceedings related to that legislation.  i. If both the Chair and Vice Chair are unable to preside a temporary Chair shall be elected by a simple majority vote of the Committee members present to preside over the proceedings related to that legislation.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 6 - Activity And Service Fee Budget Allocation
sections.text:
In adherence with Chapter 416 of the Statutes of the Student Body, the annual Activity and Service Fee (A&S) Budget of the Student Senate shall be deliberated and approved in whole by the Budget Committee. The following procedures shall take place for the consideration of the Budget:
The Chair shall meet with the Senate Advisor to designate the period in which Budget requests will be open and the dates and times hearings and deliberations will take place. At this time, the Chair shall also acquire the estimated amount to be allocated in the Budget from the Senate Advisor.
During the Activity and Service Fee Budget Allocation process, the Budget Committee shall be additionally composed of the following ex-officio members:

One (1) representative from the Campus Recreation Board

One (1) representative from the Union Board

One (1) representative from the Executive Branch

Two (2) representatives from the Congress of Graduate Students

The Student Body Treasurer, or designee

An estimated amount of the Budget shall be submitted to the Student Senate President by the Chair in the form of a bill. This bill will then be amended in Committee to include the finalized A&S Fee Budget Allocations and the accompanying proviso language
The Chair shall send official communication to all budgeted organizations in the form of an email with the dates the Budget request period will be open and the process for which they can submit their request and schedule a hearing time with the Committee. This email shall be sent out on the day the request period opens, at the latest.
Members of the Budget Committee must recuse themselves from voting on any budget allocation involving an agency or organization with which they have a direct association. This includes holding a position within, having immediate family involvement, or possessing a financial interest in the agency or organization. Members are responsible for declaring any such conflicts and recusing themselves prior to discussions on the relevant budget item.
If a member fails to recuse themselves and a potential conflict of interest is identified, the Chair is to be notified. The Chair will then assess the situation and, if necessary, enforce the recusal to uphold ethical standards and maintain the integrity of the Committee’s decisions.
Hearings shall be held by the Committee during which budget requests are defended. Each requesting organization shall have a separate hearing. The requesting organization shall have twenty (20) minutes to present and defend their request, with ten (10) minutes of questions by the Committee afterwards. The Chair shall extend these time limits at their discretion. 
Quorum for a budget hearing constitutes a minimum of three (3) Senators.
At the conclusion of hearings, the Committee shall deliberate on the allocation of the Budget to requesting and non-requesting budgeted organizations. The following motions are required to successfully allocate money to organizations in deliberation
Motion to Unlock the Line for X Organization
Motion to Allocate X amount in X Category
Motion to Lock the Line for X Organization
Motion to Call the Question on Budget Allocations for the Budget Bill of the XXXX-XXXX Fiscal Year
After all allocations have been completed and agreed upon by the Committee, proviso language shall be drafted to outline stipulations to the monies allocated, in adherence with Statues of the Student Body and precedence. The following motion is required to successfully approve the proviso language in deliberation
Motion to Call the Question on the Proviso for the Budget Bill of the XXXX-XXXX Fiscal Year
A roll call vote shall be conducted by the Chair upon the calling of the question. A simple majority is required.
After the conclusion of deliberations and the majority approval of the Committee of both the Budget Allocations and the accompanying proviso, the following motion is required to successfully approve the Budget Bill:
Motion to Call the Question on the Budget Bill of the XXXX-XXXX Fiscal Year
A roll call vote shall be conducted by the Chair upon calling of the question. A simple majority is required.
When the Budget has been deliberated and approved in whole by the Budget Committee it will be heard on Second Reading. The Chair shall submit the finalized Bill to the Student Senate President and the SGA Webmaster at the end of deliberations. The Chair shall ensure the Budget and proviso are properly advertised on the Student Government website while on Second Reading.
The Chair shall make a good-faith effort to complete the Budget no later than March 1st of each year.
Hearings, deliberations, and meetings of the Budget Committee are public and shall be publicly advertised. The Chair shall not exclude any student from witnessing the hearings or deliberations in adherence with the Statues of the Student Body and the Florida Sunshine Law.

sections.heading: BUDGET: RULE 7 - Budget And The Senate
sections.text: Any and all procedures, guidelines, concerns, or rules not addressed in these rules and procedures may be derived from the senate rules and procedures and Roberts Rules of Order.

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 1 - Meetings Of The Committee
sections.text:
Meetings of the Committee may be called by the Chair as they may deem necessary on three days’ notice of the date, time, place and subject matter of the meeting, or pursuant to the provision of the Standing Rules of the Senate, as amended.
At the request of any member, or by action of the Chair, a bill, matter, or nomination on the agenda of the Committee may be held over until the next meeting of the Committee. Senators may object to the request or action, in which case a majority vote will be necessary hold the bill, matter, or nomination.
The Committee shall provide a public announcement of the date, time, place and subject matter of any hearing to be conducted by the Committee at least 3 calendar days prior to the commencement of that hearing, unless the Chair determines that good cause exists to begin such hearing at an earlier date.
The Chair shall set an Agenda for every meeting and distribute said Agenda to all members of the committee at least 6 hours before the next meeting. The Agenda shall at least include:
Call to Order
Verification of Quorum
Land Acknowledgement
Approval of the last meetings minutes
Announcements
Unfinished Business
New Business
Closing Announcements
Adjournment
The Presiding officer shall call each meeting to order, and immediately after verify quorum by a roll call vote.
No person who is not a Student Senator, Senate officer, or an SGA Advisor, shall be recognized to speak before the committee unless a motion is made and seconded to allow such a speaker. Senators may object to the motion in which case a majority vote will be necessary to allow such a speaker.
All meetings are public, and space shall be made available in the meeting room for members of the general public to sit and listen. This rule is to ensure proper adherence to chapter 203 of the SGA Student Body Statutes.
The Presiding officer shall go through the Agenda from the top down and shall begin debate on business by stating the question before the committee, unless otherwise requested.
No Senator may make any statement without first being recognized by the Presiding Officer. 

HISTORY
Revised by Res. R78-025 on 6/3/2026

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 2 - Bills And Resolutions
sections.text:
When a bill or resolution comes before the committee there shall be debate. Debate on a bill or resolution will begin with structured debate. Structured debate for a main motion consists of the following:
An Opening statement by the sponsor(s) of no more than five (5) minutes. No motions may be made during this round. All time yielded during the opening statement shall be given back to the sponsor for a closing statement pursuant to Rule 2.1.d
The opening statement shall be followed by a questioning period. The presiding officer shall recognize each Senator who raises their hand to be recognized. In the event that multiple Senators raise their hand, priority will come first by the alphabetical order of the Senator's last name. Once a Senator is recognized they shall have five (5) minutes for their questions. Questions shall be related to the sponsor's knowledge on the current topic under consideration. Once all Senators who wish to be recognized are recognized at least once, the Presiding officer shall ask for a motion to call to question. If there is an objection to approving the motion, then debate shall be undertaken pursuant to Rule 2.1.c.
There shall be two (2) rounds of roundtable following questioning only if there is an objection. In the first round of debate, the presiding officer shall recognize each Senator who raises their hand, priority will come first by alphabetical order of the Senator's last name. Once a Senator is recognized they shall have five (5) minutes to speak, which they may use to ask any questions or speak on the matter at hand. Should all Senators have spoken who wish to speak, and a Senator wishes to be recognized for a second time, then the committee shall move into the second round of debate at the discretion of the presiding officer. Any motion can be made if a motion to amend is made, Rules 2.3 and 2.4 shall be used. 

After either all Senators who wish to speak have spoken, or if all Senators have spoken twice, the presiding officer shall automatically move to call the question. Once the question has been called by motion or automatically, the Sponsor shall give a closing statement equal to the amount of time that they yielded to the presiding officer. All remaining time at the end of this closing statement shall be absorbed by the presiding officer. 

Senators must confine their remarks in debate to the pending bill or resolution. Personal remarks must not enter into debate. All remarks must be addressed to the presiding officer. Any senator violating these rules may, at the discretion of the presiding officer, lose the floor. 

A primary amendment is a change or addition to the main motion under discussion. A secondary amendment is a change or addition to a primary amendment. The sponsor of the matter under consideration must state whether they find the amendment friendly or unfriendly. If the sponsor finds the amendment friendly, and no Senators object to its adoption, the amendment is automatically adopted. Amendments shall be heard using the Structured debate on an amendment procedure, only if the sponsor of the matter under consideration finds the amendment unfriendly. All amendments must be recorded by the vice-chair in the minutes.
Structured debate on an amendment consists of the following:
An opening statement by the amendment's sponsor(s) of no more than five (5) minutes. All time yielded during the opening statement shall be given back to the Sponsor for a closing statement pursuant to Rule 2.4.7.
Following the opening statement there shall be a period of questioning. The Presiding Officer shall recognize each Senator on the committee who raises their hand to be recognized. In the event that multiple Senators raise their hand, priority will come first by the alphabetical order of the Senator's last name. Once a Senator is recognized they shall have two (2) minutes for their questions. Questions shall be related to the sponsor's knowledge on the current topic under consideration.
Following the questioning period there shall be one (1), five (5) minute round of debate. Any Senator may be recognized by the presiding officer. At the discretion of the presiding officer, the time for debate can be extended by up to an additional five (5) minutes.
If a motion to have a secondary amendment is made the sponsor of the primary amendment shall state whether it is found friendly or unfriendly, and the Presiding Officer shall stop the timer until consideration of the secondary amendment is done.
If a secondary amendment is found friendly it shall be adopted. If a secondary amendment is found unfriendly the sponsor shall have two (2) minutes for an opening statement. The Presiding Officer shall immediately call the question.
A secondary motion need only pass by a simple majority.
Once time expires, the primary amendment shall be called to question. Prior to the vote on the question, the Sponsor shall give a closing statement equal to the amount of time that they yielded to the presiding officer. All remaining time at the end of this closing statement shall be absorbed by the presiding officer.
A primary amendment need only pass by a simple majority.

A Senator may yield his or her time to the Presiding Officer. No yielding of time to other Senators is permitted. 
A speech interrupted for a Point of Order or Point of Privilege will be charged against the speaker only if the interruption was caused by the speaker's misconduct or violation of the rules.
After time has elapsed, the Presiding Officer will entertain a motion for the main motion to be called to question.
When a motion is made to call the main motion to question the Presiding Officer shall conduct a roll call vote. All standing rules, and statutes will be observed to determine the success of a main motion.
The Presiding Officer shall not vote except in cases of a tie.

HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-025 on 6/3/2026

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 3 - Consent Resolutions
sections.text:
When a Allocation Resolution is brought to the committee, the Presiding Officer shall seek a motion to forward such a Resolution after its presentation by the Sponsor and a round of questioning.
A Consent Resolution shall only be debated if there is an objection to the motion for its forwarding to the Senate.
If objected to, debate shall be conducted by means of Structured Debate outline in Committee Rule 2
Primary amendments to a Consent Resolution must only pass if there is a two thirds (2/3) vote of the Committee.
Following structured debate, the Consent Resolution shall then be forwarded to the Senate by a simple majority).

HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-025 on 6/3/2026

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 4 - Nominations
sections.text:
When a nomination comes before the committee the same rules of debate in rule 2 shall be followed, with the nominee taking the role of the Sponsor and no amendments being allowed during the time of nomination. 
HISTORY
Revised by Res. R78-025 on 6/3/2026

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 5 - Quorums
sections.text:
Half the Members of the Committee, present either in person or via video call, shall constitute a quorum for the purpose of discussing business, and transacting business. No bill, matter, or nomination shall be ordered reported from the Committee, however, unless a majority of the Committee is actually present at the time such action is taken and a majority of those present support the action taken.

HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-025 on 6/3/2026

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 6 - Attendance Rules
sections.text:
Official attendance at all Committee business meetings of the Committee shall be kept by the Vice Chair.
Attendance at meetings is mandatory and all rules regarding attendance for the purposes of this committee shall match and reflect those found in the Student Senate Rules of Procedure.

sections.heading: FINANCE: RULE 7 - Decorum
sections.text:
During presentations, committee members are expected to give their undivided attention to the speaker.
Committee members shall be expected to wear business casual to all committee meetings unless unable to due to work or academic commitments. 

Committee members attending via video call are expected to keep their camera on at all times, unless they have been given exemption by the Chair for technical or practical reasons. Any individual who does not have their camera on at all times, unless they have been given exemption by the Chair for technical or practical reasons. Any individual who does not have their camera on shall not be considered "present" for a given matter. 
HISTORY
Amended by Res. R78-025 on 6/3/2026

sections.heading: SL: RULE 1 - Authority And Changes To The Committee Rules
sections.text:
The Student Life Committee shall be governed by, in order of precedence, the  Constitution of the Student Body, the Statutes of the Student Body, the Rules of Procedure of the Student Senate, these Student Life Committee Rules of  Procedure, and the latest version of Robert’s Rules of Order Newly Revised.
Changes to these Rules of Procedure shall require a majority vote of the committee.

sections.heading: SL: RULE 2 - Meetings Of The Committee
sections.text:
Meetings of the Committee may be called by the Chair as they may deem necessary on 24 hours’ notice of the date, time, place, and subject of the meeting, or pursuant to the provision of the Standing Rules of the Senate, as amended.
Unless a different date and time are set by the Chair pursuant to (A) of this section, Committee meetings shall be held beginning at 3:30pm on Tuesdays during the regular session of the Student Senate, which shall be the regular meeting day for the transaction of business.
At the request of any member, or by action of the Chair, a bill, matter, or nomination on the agenda of the Committee may be held over until the next meeting of the Committee.
The Committee shall provide a public announcement of the date, time, place, and subject of any hearing to be conducted by the Committee at least 24 hours prior to the commencement of that hearing, unless the Chair determines that good cause exists to begin such hearing at an earlier date.
The Presiding officer shall call each meeting to order and immediately after, the Vice-Chair shall verify quorum by a call of the roll.
Only members of the committee may speak on measures before the committee unless the committee waives the rules to allow a non-member to offer additional information to the discussion. A non-committee member shall not be allowed to participate in debate on any measure.
All meetings are public, and space shall be made available in the meeting room for members of the general public to sit and listen. This rule is to ensure proper adherence to chapter 203 of the SGA Student Body Statutes.
No Senator may make any statement without first being recognized by the Presiding Officer.

sections.heading: SL: RULE 3 - Procedures For Hearings Bills And Resolutions
sections.text:
Opening statement by the sponsor(s) of no more than five (5) minutes. No motions may be made during this round.
Technical, non-debatable questions, which shall consist of factual inquiries directed toward the sponsor(s). The number of questions asked shall be at the discretion of the presiding officer. No motions or points of information shall be made during this time.
Round Table Discussion, the committee shall discuss how to move forward, and during this stage the presiding officer will accept motions to amend the legislation being heard.
Closing statement by the original sponsor. The length of this statement shall be whatever remaining time the sponsor yielded after their opening. No motions may be made during this round.
Vote, done by roll call.

sections.heading: SL: RULE 4 - Quorum
sections.text: Half the Members of the Committee, actually present, shall constitute a quorum for the purpose of discussing business, and transacting business. No bill, matter, or resolution shall be ordered reported from the Committee, however, unless a majority of the Committee is actually present at the time such action is taken and a majority of those present support the action taken. The Chair of the committee may, at their discretion, upgrade the Senate President and/or the Senate President Pro-Tempore from their status as ex-officio members, to voting members.

title: Congress of Graduate Students: Cogs Administrative Code

sections.heading: COGS Administrative Code
sections.text:
ADMINISTRATIVE CODE

CONGRESS OF GRADUATE STUDENTS

FLORIDA STATE UNIVERSITY

HISTORY
Adopted by Bill B16-022 on 9/8/2008

sections.heading: 100.1 Purpose
sections.text: This chapter shall outline the system of the Congress of Graduate Students Administrative Code, hereafter referred to as “this code” or “Code,” observed by the Congress of Graduate Students, hereafter referred to as “COGS,” in enacting and adopting measures, as well as provide definitions and interpretations, in the construction of, and in compliance with, this code.

sections.heading: 100.2 Jurisdiction Of Code
sections.text: All provisions of this code are fully applicable to all entities, organizations, and individuals within the jurisdiction of COGS. Any and all funding derivative from COGS is contingent upon the recipient’s compliance with this code.

sections.heading: 100.3 Intellectual Property Of Code
sections.text: This code shall be considered the copyrighted intellectual property of the Florida State University Student Government Association; however, this code may be reproduced or adopted by any entity for non-commercial purposes, so long as such entity attributes the origination of the work to “The Florida State University Student Government Association."

sections.heading: 100.4 Code To Be Split Into Titles
sections.text:
There shall be four titles within this code, each containing related or similar topics, and each composed of numerically ordered chapters and sections as follows:

(a) Title I: (100–199) Construction of Code

(b) Title II: (200–299) The Congress of Graduate Students

(c) Title III: (300–399) Finance Provisions

(d) Title IV: (400–499) Specific Provisions for Select Graduate Entities and COGS Funding Boards

sections.heading: 100.5 Severability Of Code
sections.text: All provisions of this code are fully severable. If any word, clause, or provision of this code is found to be in violation of federal law, the laws of the State of Florida, or the Florida State University Student Body Statutes or Constitution, it will in no way affect the validity or applicability of the remainder of this code.

sections.heading: 100.6 Succession Of Named Entities
sections.text: In the event that an entity referred to within this code should lawfully become identified by another name, or have its responsibilities divested to another entity, the COGS Advisor shall have the authority and responsibility, independent of any action of the Assembly, to replace the inaccurate name in the text of this code to reflect reality.

sections.heading: 100.7 Definitions
sections.text:
In construing these statutes and each and every word, phrase, or part hereof, where the context will permit:

(a) The singular indicates the plural and vice versa.

(b) The terms “Congress of Graduate Students,” “COGS,” and “the Assembly” may be used interchangeably throughout this code and are intended to identify the entity empowered by Article IX of the Student Body Constitution.

(c) The term “student” shall be defined as any individual enrolled in a postbaccalaureate, special, master’s, professional, specialist, or doctoral program.

(1) Within this code, the terms “student” and “graduate student” may be used interchangeably and shall only refer to the aforementioned individuals.

(d) The term “presentation” shall be defined as anything relating to the applicant’s course of study augmenting professional development and stature in the field. Presentations may include, but are not limited to, papers, speeches, demonstrations, art, photography, competition performance, and conferences.

(e) The following shall constitute the standards for voting within the Assembly:

(1) The term “majority” shall refer to a simple majority unless otherwise specified, which shall be defined as greater than half of the votes cast when an item is under consideration.

(2) The term “two-thirds (2/3) majority” shall be defined as greater than two-thirds (2/3) of the votes cast when an item is under consideration.

(3) The term “majority of the entire membership” shall be defined as greater than half (1/2) of all Representatives, whether present or not, except those Representatives on Leave of Absence.

(f) The term “Speaker” shall be defined as the Speaker of COGS.

(g) The term “Executive Committee” shall be defined as the entity composed of the elected officers of COGS, as listed in s. 204.1, COGS Code, and may be used interchangeably with “Executive Board.”

(h) The term “A&S Funds” shall be defined as the funds appropriated to COGS under the Florida State Student Body Constitution from Activities and Service Fees, restricted in use by the Florida State Student Body Constitution, Statutes, and Policies and state and federal laws.

(1) The term “A&S Fees” may be used interchangeably with “A&S Funds.”

(2) The term “COGS Funds” will encompass “A&S Funds” and any other funds COGS received.

sections.heading: 100.8 Abbreviations
sections.text:
The following shall serve as accepted abbreviations throughout this code and in COGS records and papers:

(a) A&S: Activity & Service.

(b) COGS: Congress of Graduate Students.

(c) DSE: Department of Student Engagement.

(d) IROP: COGS Internal Rules of Procedure.

(e) LSC: Law School Council.

(f) MSC: Medical Student Council.

(g) OPS: Other Personnel Services.

(h) RSO: Recognized Student Organization.

(i) SGA: Student Government Association.

sections.heading: Chapter 200 Purpose Of The Congress Of Graduate Students
sections.text:
Purpose - The Congress of Graduate Students, in accordance with Article IX of the Florida State University Student Body Constitution shall:
Defend the interests of graduate, special, master, specialist, professional, doctoral, and post-baccalaureate students in graduate student life, services, and academics.
Manage the funds within its purview in a fiscally responsible manner.
Work to ensure the greatest participation by graduate students in the immediate governance of, and policy development for, the Florida State University.
Provide an official voice through which the opinions of the Graduate Student Body may be expressed.

sections.heading: Chapter 201 Membership
sections.text:
Elected Congress.- The Congress shall be an elected body of graduate and professional students, with vacancies to be filled by petition. The procedure for the election of Representatives shall be defined in Chapter 205 of the Code.
Seats.- The Congress shall be composed of forty-three (43) Representatives with the following allocation:
Thirty (30) seats for the members of each college/academic unit, except for the College of Applied Studies and Special Students, apportioned annually through the D’Hondt Method, based on the most recent annual population data for each college, as provided by the University.
By the second COGS Assembly meeting of the Fall Semester, the SGA Supervisor of Elections shall provide the Assembly, by memo and personal appearance at the meeting, with a list detailing the number of seats apportioned to each college/academic unit, as well as an accounting of the calculations used to determine the apportionment. Should the list not be provided by this deadline, the COGS Executive Board shall be empowered to facilitate the apportionment in the Supervisor’s place.
Should there be a discrepancy that results in the erroneous allocation of seats, the Assembly may move to reject the apportionment and request that the Supervisor (or COGS Executive Board, if providing the list under paragraph (1)) provide a corrected apportionment to the Assembly at their next meeting. Such motion requires a two-thirds (2/3) vote to pass and is debatable.
If no motion to reject is passed, the apportionment shall become official upon adjournment of the Assembly meeting in which it is presented.
Six (6) advocate seats under the following titles: Graduate Student Housing Advocate, International Student Advocate, LGBTQ+ Student Advocate, Minority Student Advocate, Veteran’s Advocate, and Student with Disabilities Advocate. Any graduate student, regardless of college, may serve as an Advocate.
Six (6) At-Large seats, which may be filled by any graduate student, regardless of college.
One (1) seat for the combined grouping of Special Students, the College of Applied Studies, and the Panama City Campus. Should this seat be filled, attendance by the representative will count towards quorum, but failure to attend will not count against quorum.
Leaves of Absence- A "leave of absence” shall be understood as creating a temporary vacancy in the seat of, and for a period of time requested by, the Representative requesting the leave.
The Representative’s seat may be temporarily filled through petition by another student with similar qualifications; the Representative on a leave of absence shall resume his or her seat upon the end of the leave.
The student temporarily filling the vacant seat shall be informed, prior to accepting the position, of the length of his or her seat. Such a temporary Representative may petition the Congress to fill another vacant term (for which he or she is qualified), either temporary or permanent, without submitting an additional petition form, if the new term would be effective not more than one (1) regular meeting after the old term.
No leave of absence shall become effective unless a written or electronic letter requesting a leave of absence has been communicated to the COGS Advisor and Speaker or acting Speaker. Such letter must contain the individual’s name, position, duration of leave of absence (including effective dates of initiation and termination of leave), and reason for the request.
A representative’s requested leave of absence will not be granted unless one of the following conditions is met:
The representative will not be enrolled in graduate credit hours; or
The representative will be out of town for academic opportunities, such as study abroad, or field research, and will be missing at least three regular meetings; or
The representative is a member of the U.S. military and is called to Active Duty; or
Any other reason, if request is approved by the Internal Affairs Committee.
A leave of absence may not be granted if the Representative will not return before the end of the Congress.
Resignation.- No resignation shall become effective unless a written or electronic letter of resignation has been communicated to the COGS Advisor and Speaker or acting Speaker. Such letter must contain the individual’s name, position, and effective date of resignation. Such letter should be signed by the individual resigning and submitted in person or by e-mail. No letter may have an effective date more than thirty (30) calendar days from submission of the letter.
In the event of resignation of the Speaker or any Deputy Speaker, the Advisor shall notify the Assembly within two (2) school days (forty-eight [48] hours) from the receipt of resignation.
In the event of resignation of the Chair or Vice Chair of any committee, the individual resigning shall notify the committee within two (2) school days (forty-eight [48] hours) of resignation.
Impeachment.- COGS Representatives, members of the Law School Council, and members of the Medical Student Council may be removed from office by impeachment. The provisions of this section, as it applies to COGS Representatives, is merely an additional method of recommending impeachment to the Student Senate and does not create additional requirements for impeachment over those set out in the Student Body Constitution or Statutes.
The scope of impeachable charges shall be limited to misfeasance, malfeasance, or nonfeasance of the following: the COGS Code, the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, Constitution, and Conduct Code, or state or federal law.
This provision shall not interfere with legislative immunity enjoyed by Representatives on the floor of the Assembly.
The following procedures shall be used for the initiation of impeachment proceedings against an officer covered by this section:
The Internal Affairs Committee, by a majority vote, shall be responsible for initiating impeachment proceedings against any officer, only after formal charges have been presented to the Chair of the Committee by the COGS Advisor, or upon vote of the Committee to recommend impeachment pursuant to § 203.3.
Charges must be filed within fifteen (15) business days of the alleged offense. This section shall not apply to impeachment proceedings occurring as a result of action under § 203.3.
The formal charges must include the name of the student lodging the charge, the name of the officer who committed the alleged offense, the provision of the regulation which the officer has allegedly violated, as well as the date, time, and location where the offense was alleged to occur.
The charge may include multiple offenses.
The charge must be signed by the student lodging the complaint. If the charge is truancy, pursuant to § 203.3, the charge shall be signed by the Speaker or their designee.
Any member of the Student Body may file a charge with the COGS Advisor, so long as the charge is consistent with this chapter.
Once formal charges have been filed, the Speaker of COGS shall request that the Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court designate a law student to be assigned as counsel to the accused officer. The officer charged may also retain outside counsel at their expense if they so choose.
The Internal Affairs Committee must meet within fifteen (15) business days after said charges have been filed and decide whether to recommend impeachment to the Congress. The fifteen-day rule shall not apply to impeachment proceedings occurring as a result of action under § 203.3.
The Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee shall notify the accused officer of the date, time, and location of any hearing to consider the impeachment, no less than twenty-four (24) hours before the hearing. At the hearing, the accused shall have the right to speak in his/her defense, refuse to appear, remain silent, or refer to counsel at any time. At the conclusion of the hearing, the Committee shall openly deliberate, and then vote by secret ballot on whether or not to recommend impeachment to the full Assembly.
The student lodging the complaint is encouraged, but not required to appear before the Internal Affairs Committee and testify.
The Committee, through its Chair, shall have the power to subpoena witnesses to testify before it during the course of the proceedings. Such witnesses must be given no less than a twenty-four (24) hours’ notice. Non-compliance with a subpoena without good cause shall be considered nonfeasance.
If the Committee does not vote to recommend impeachment, the charges shall be dismissed, and no appeal to the Assembly shall be available.
This shall not prejudice the ability of individuals to initiate impeachment proceedings with the Student Senate after the fact.
If the Committee does recommend impeachment, by majority vote, impeachment proceedings for the officer in question will be added to the agenda of the next regularly scheduled session of the Assembly.
Should the Internal Affairs Committee recommend impeachment, the Assembly shall follow the following procedures:
The rules governing impeachment proceedings within the Assembly may be laid down in the COGS Internal Rules of Procedure, but in the absence of such provisions, the Speaker shall determine through memorandum what rules shall be followed. In either event, the proceedings shall conclude with a roll-call vote as to whether or not the officer should be impeached. Impeachment shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly; abstentions shall not be entertained.
The Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs shall preside over the Assembly during the consideration of any impeachments.
The Assembly, through the Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs, shall have the power, by the majority vote, to subpoena witnesses to testify before it during the hearing. Such witnesses shall be notified no less than twenty-four (24) hours in advance of the hearing. Non-compliance with a subpoena without good cause shall be considered nonfeasance.
If the impeachment vote is unsuccessful, the charges will be dismissed.
This shall not prejudice the ability of individuals to initiate impeachment proceedings with the Student Senate after the fact.
If the Assembly Impeaches:
The Speaker shall immediately transmit a report of the proceedings to the Student Senate President and Chair of the Senate Judiciary Committee explaining the proceedings and identifying the officer who was impeached.
The officer shall be immediately suspended from their position, and shall lose all rights and privileges of office.
If after the impeachment report has been lodged with the Senate, the Senate declines to initiate impeachment proceedings, the officer will be immediately reinstated with all rights and privileges of office thereto appertaining.
If after the impeachment report has been lodged with the Senate and the Senate should sustain it, then provisions for the removal of the officer will proceed in accordance with § 405.5 of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes.
Both plaintiff and defendant have the right to appeal the decision of the Student Supreme Court to the Vice President of Student Affairs. Appeals must be submitted within three (3) business days of the decision of the Supreme Court.
For members of the Law School Council and Medical Student Council, the provisions of subsections (f) and (g) shall not apply and the impeachment charges approved by the Assembly shall be filed with the Supreme Court for trial.
The Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs shall serve as the lead impeachment manager on behalf of the Congress and may appoint any other graduate students, as necessary, to assist in prosecuting the impeachment.
The impeached officer shall have the right to be represented by student counsel. The Chief Justice of the Student Supreme Court may appoint a law student as student counsel for the officer if requested.
The Student Supreme Court shall set the procedures for impeachment trials, except that the officer shall be removed by majority vote of the justices participating in the case and shall have the right to appeal their removal to the Vice President for Student Affairs.
Vacancies. - Vacancies in the Congress may be filled by petition of a student qualified to hold the vacant seat.
The Deputy Speaker for Communication shall advertise vacancies on a regular basis.
A graduate student may fill a vacant seat with the signature of twenty (20) enrolled students within their college, or 10% of the graduate student body of that college, whichever is less. Petitioners must file their petitions with the Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs and shall be heard at the next Assemble meeting after their eligibility to serve is certified by the COGS Advisor. All petitioners must be accepted by a majority vote of COGS members present at an official meeting.
In cases where two (2) or more petitions are received for the same seat, COGS shall fill the seat by a majority vote after deliberation, as per the COGS Internal Rules of Procedure.
If two (2) or more petitions are received for the same seat and an at-large seat is vacant, the Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs may redesignate the petitioner that was not selected for the seat originally petitioned for by COGS to be a petition for the vacant at-large seat, so long as the petition has twenty (20) signatures.

sections.heading: Chapter 202 Organization Of The Congress
sections.text:
Quorum.- A quorum is required to conduct business in the Assembly, or any committee thereof.
A quorum exists if both of the following conditions are met:
The Speaker (in the Assembly), the Chair or Vice Chair (in a committee), or a presiding officer designated by § 204.4 is present, and
A majority of Representatives, or a majority of the committee’s members in committee, is present at a meeting called in accordance with the FSU Sunshine Act, COGS Code, and IROP.
In the absence of a quorum, the Assembly, or any committee thereof, may not take any formal action, except to make a call of the house or adjourn, and may only:
Take roll calls;
Take public comment;
Hear reports and announcements; and
Discuss matters not before the body for final decision.
Adoption of Internal Rules of Procedure.- COGS, as per Article IX of the Florida State University Student Body Constitution, shall have the authority to adopt its own internal rules of procedure by a two-thirds (2/3) vote. A resolution adopting the Assembly’s IROP shall be considered and adopted by the second meeting of each Congress.
Meetings of the Congress.-The Assembly shall meet on the first and third Monday of each month during the fall, spring, and summer academic semesters.
If a regularly scheduled meeting of the Assembly would fall within any of the following occurrences, then such meeting shall be considered waived:
Within seven (7) days prior to the official Florida State diploma date;
During Spring Break; or
During observed University holidays.
If an emergency situation should arise during any of the times identified in subsection (a), the Speaker, upon the concurrence of the COGS Advisor, shall be empowered to call a special session of the Assembly. At such special session, no other business than that which is on the agenda at the beginning of the meeting shall be entertained.

sections.heading: Chapter 203 Membership Requirements
sections.text:
Definitions.- For the purpose of this chapter:
The term “excused absence” shall be defined as an absence for which either:
Advanced notice was provided to the Speaker (or Chair for a committee meeting) at least one (1) hour prior to the start of an Assembly (or committee) meeting, and:
Is defined as an excused absence under the University’s Attendance policy; or
Is otherwise deemed a valid reason by the Speaker (or Chair for a committee meeting).
The absence is declared “excused” by a majority of the Executive Committee.
The term “unexcused absence” shall be defined as an absence that is not excused.
The term “unexcused late” shall be defined as an occurrence where a Representative arrives at least five (5) minutes after a meeting is called to order, and the Representative does not provide notice to the Speaker (or Chair for a committee meeting) prior to the start of the meeting.
Attendance Requirement.- A Representative and their seat shall be up for review when a Representative has accumulated four (4) total absences from Assembly and committee meetings within the same Congress, unless a leave of absence is granted.
For the purpose of this section, the total number of absences is calculated as follows:
Unexcused late: 0.5 absence;
Excused absence: 0.5 absence; and
Unexcused absence: 1.0 absence.
Attendance Enforcement.- The Deputy Speaker for Communication shall keep track of all absences and inform the Speaker, Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs, and Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee when a member reaches the threshold set in § 203.2.
When a Representative meets the threshold in section (2) of this Chapter, they shall appear before the next meeting of the Internal Affairs Committee, who shall decide, by majority vote, whether to provide a certain number of additional absences or to recommend the Representative for impeachment, pursuant to § 201.5. The Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs shall provide notice to the Representative at least forty-eight (48) hours prior to the committee meeting.
If the member is recommended for impeachment, they shall be suspended from COGS pending final disposition of the impeachment proceedings. If final disposition results in action other than the removal of the member, the Internal Affairs Committee shall grant, by majority vote, a specified number of additional absences to the member, which shall be at least one.
Financial Certification Requirement.- All Representatives must become financially certified, as defined by SG&A Accounting, by their second Assembly meeting. Upon the start of a new fiscal year, Representatives must be re-certified by the second Assembly meeting after the start of the new fiscal year.
The Representative shall inform the Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs upon becoming financially certified. The Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs shall maintain a record of all Representatives and whether they are financially certified.
Failure to be certified within the period set by this section shall make the Representative ineligible to vote on any matters involving the allocation or transfer of A&S Funds and they should be recorded as abstaining on the matter.
Exceptions.- Exceptions to sections (2) and (4) of this Chapter may be granted upon unanimous recommendation of the Executive Committee and ratification by a majority of the entire membership of the Assembly.

sections.heading: Chapter 204 Officers
sections.text:
Creation - The Congress shall have five (5) officers which shall be the Speaker, Deputy Speaker for Finance, Deputy Speaker for Communication, Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs, and Deputy Speaker for Advocacy. Together, the officers are referred to as the “Executive Board” or “Executive Committee.”
Election of Officers at the Start of each Congress - Elections of the officers for COGS shall take place at an organizational session in which all COGS members elected at the fall election may vote. Officers elected at the organizational session shall assume office upon being sworn in at fall inauguration.
Procedures for Organizational Session - The organizational session shall be held at least one week prior to Fall Inauguration and shall be called by the Speaker, within twenty-four (24) hours of the announcement of COGS election results, by memorandum to the elected members and published electronically to the public. The organizational session must occur at least two weeks after the announcement of election results.
Upon calling the organizational session, the Speaker shall provide all elected members with a form for the declaration of candidacy to the office of Speaker. Candidates for speaker must complete the form and return the form to the speaker no later than forty-eight (48) hours prior to the start of the organizational session. The form shall be created by the speaker and shall include:
The title “Declaration of Candidacy for Office of Speaker”;
The statement " I, [NAME OF REPRESENTATIVE], do hereby declare my candidacy for the office of speaker of the Congress of Graduate students. I affirm, on penalty of impeachment, that I am duly qualified to hold office under the Student Body constitution, that I will not graduate during the term I am seeking election for, and that I intend to serve the entire one-year term.";
A signature and date line for the candidate to sign and date;
A signature, print name, and date line, entitled "Nominator", for the representative that intends to nominate the candidate;
A signature, print name, and date line, entitled "Seconder", for the representative that intends to second the nomination of the candidate.
No later than twenty-four (24) hours prior to the organizational session, the Speaker shall publish  the names of all candidates for Speaker to the elected members.
The Speaker shall serve as Chair for the organizational session.
Should the Chair be a candidate, in the election of a COGS officer, the chair shall be assumed by the next eligible person in the chapter 117 line of succession for the purpose of that election. 
The Speaker shall begin tabling the certificates of election of COGS Representatives. The speaker shall then call the roll of Representatives-elect to determine whether a quorum is present. Should a quorum be present, the speaker shall immediately proceed to the election of a speaker for the next Congress. Upon the election of a speaker, the chair shall move the elections of the Deputy Speakers for Finance, Communications, Judicial Affairs, and Advocacy, Respectively.
If a quorum is not present, the Congress shall recess for fifteen (15) minutes and, upon reconvening, call the roll of Representatives-elect again. If a quorum is still not present, the speaker shall adjourn the meeting and call another organizational session to convene no later than seventy-two (72) hours after the noticed meeting time of the original organizational session.
A Speaker and two other members of the COGS Executive Committee must be elected before the organizational meeting adjourns.
The chair shall then move to a period of closing announcements, followed by the adjournment of the meeting, upon the election of all members of the Executive Committee of upon a two-thirds majority vote of the members-elect to adjourn after the requirements of paragraph (e) are met.
Procedure of Officer Elections - COGS officer election procedures shall be the following: 
Members of the COGS Executive Committee shall be elected from among the membership of COGS. Election shall be by secret ballot and shall require a majority vote in order to elect a candidate. Quorum of the Congress must be present for the election of each member of the COGS Executive Committee.
Nominations for officers shall be taken from the floor and shall require a second. Each candidate may accept or decline the nomination. After receipt of nominees, the Chair shall close the floor for nominations, only after ensuring that no other nominations are to be made. If only one candidate is nominated, that candidate shall be declared to be elected by acclimation. The elected officer shall then be allowed to make a brief statement to the congress. 
At the organizational session, called pursuant to section (3). Only those candidates for Speaker who have returned a completed form, as specified in section (3), to the chair are eligible for nomination, unless no candidate returns such form. The chair shall call upon the nominate and second the candidate. If the nominator or seconder is not present, the Chair may take the nomination or second from any other member-elect. 

Nominees for Deputy Speaker for Finance, prior to accepting the nomination, must affirm the Congress that they are willing and able to serve the remainder of the term that are being elected for. 

If there are two or more candidates who accepted their nomination, each shall be allowed, in alphabetical order, to address the Congress for no more than two (2) minutes. The chair shall allow three (3) minutes of questions per candidate. No "con" debate shall be permitted during the election process. All nominees not addressing or taking questions from the Congress shall remain outside the COGS Chambers. Candidates shall not be present during debate on the candidates. Debate on the candidates shall take no more than five (5) minutes. Motions to extend time for opening addresses, questions and discussions of the candidates may be made by Representatives in the Champers and pass by majority vote of the representatives in the Chambers. Once the question has successfully been called to vote on the position, all nominees may enter the Chambers and cast their own secret ballots with the rest of the Congress. 

Oath - COGS Officers shall take the following oath prior to assuming office: "I, [NAME], do swear that I will support, protect, and defend the constitution and laws of the United States, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body; that I shall serve and protect the rights and interests of graduate and professional students; and that I shall carry out my duties, in the role of [POSITION] of the Congress of Graduate Students, to the best of my abilities; so help me God."

Officers are entitled to request that the following alternate oath be administered: "I, [NAME], affirm, on pain of impeachment, that I will support, protect, and defend the constitution and laws of the United States, the State of Florida, and the Florida State University Student Body; that I shall serve and protect the rights and interests of graduate and professional students; and that I shall carry out my duties, in the role of [POSITION] of the Congress of Graduate Students, to the best of my abilities."
Resignation - Officers may resign by submitting written or electronic notice to the Speaker, except that the Speaker shall tender resignation to the COGS Advisor and Student Body President.
The Speaker, or the COGS Advisor in case that the Speaker resigns, shall inform the Congress of the officer’s resignation within twenty-four (24) hours of receiving the resignation, except that weekends and university holidays shall not count towards the time limit. 
The resignation of an officer may take effect upon the election of the successor but shall not take effect no later then thirty (30) days after the resignation is tendered.

Upon receipt of any officer's resignation that takes effect at any time after the next scheduled Assembly meeting, the Speaker or acting Speaker under §  204.4 is authorized to hold an election under section (4) of this Chapter, with the elected Representative taking office upon the resigning officer's effective date.

Removal- Any officer of the Congress may be removed through the procedure of the section.
A representative seeking the removal of an officer shall file, with the COGS Advisor, written charges shall include:
The name of the officer being charged.

A plain statement of the facts at issue, 

The charges upon which the Representative seeks removal of an officer, which shall only be on ground of malfeasance, misfeasance, or nonfeasance, and

The name of the representative bringing the charges.

Upon receipt of the charges, the COGS Advisor shall determine, without consideration of the merits of the charges, whether the charges meet the  requirements of subsection (a). If the charges meet the requirements of subsection (a), the COGS Advisor shall provide the charges to the Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee.
The Chair of the Internal Affairs Committee, upon receipt of the charges, shall inform the charged officers of the charges, inform the charged officer of the next Internal Affairs Committee meeting that is at least seven (7) days after the information is given, and request that the charged officer provide a written defense shall not prevent the Chair from continuing removal proceedings. 

At the first Internal Affairs Committee meeting after the seven (7) days in subsection (c) elapsed, the committee shall hold a hearing on the charges,

The Representative making the charges, and the charged officer, shall have the right to address the committee.
The Committee shall be able to take additional evidence and shall deliberate on the charges.

The committee shall vote on whether to adopt the charge individually, The charged officer and the charging Representative shall not vote if they sit on the committee. Adopted charges shall be accompanied by a recommended punishment, adopted by majority of the committee, as to each charge.

If the committee, by a majority vote, agrees to adopt any charges, the adopted charges shall be placed before the Assembly at its next meeting. Charges not adopted shall be dismissed. 

At the next Assembly meeting, all charges adopted by the committee shall be heard. The assembly shall follow the same procedures as the committee, except that two-thirds vote is required to find the charged officer guilty of a charge. 

Should the Assembly find the officer guilty of any charge, a Representative may move to punish the officer. The punishment shall include public censure, suspension from their role as an officer for a period not to exceed one (1) month, or removal. Suspension or removal shall require a two-thirds vote.

An officer suspended or removed from their role as an officer shall have the right to appeal their suspension or removal to the Vice President for Student Affairs, or person designated by the University to hear such appeals.
Line of Succession to Speaker - In the event of a vacancy in the Office of the Speaker for reason(s) of resignation, incapacitation, ineligibility under the Florida State Student Body Constitution, or any other lawful reason, the Deputy Speaker for Finance shall act as Speaker until the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Assembly. At this time, a new Speaker shall be elected to serve until the expiration of the Congress in which the vacancy occurred. If the Assembly does not elect a new Speaker, the acting Speaker will continue until the Speaker returns or a new Speaker is elected.
 If the Deputy Speaker for Finance is unavailable, then the order of succession, in descending order, shall be:
Deputy Speaker for Communication

Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs

Deputy Speaker for Advocacy

Chair of Internal Affairs

Chair of Outreach

Chair of Advocacy 

The most senior member of COGS.

The most senior member of COGS shall be defined based on the date of swearing in (ties broken by alphabetical order of the last name). The Temporary Chair shall have the right to cast a vote for election of the Speaker in such cases where his/her vote would be decisive.

The COGS Advisor shall, with the assistance of the Deputy Speaker for Communications, maintain a list noting the order of seniority among members of COGS. 
If the current acting Speaker is nominated for office of Speaker, the next officer willing, able, and eligible to serve as identified in subsection (a), in descending order shall immediately assume the Chair for the purpose of conducting the election. If no officer is willing and able, the most senior member of COGS (as defined in 204.7(a)(7), who is willing and able, shall immediately assume the Chair for the purposed of conducting the election. 
Permanent vacancies of deputy speakers- Upon a permanent vacancy in the Office of any Deputy Speaker, the Speaker, on advice of the Executive Committee and in a published written memorandum, shall appoint an Acting Deputy Speaker, who shall serve until the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Assembly. At this time, a new Deputy Speaker may be elected to serve until the expiration of Congress in which the vacancy occurred. If the Assembly does not elect a new Deputy Speaker, the acting Deputy Speaker will continue until a new Deputy Speaker is elected. 
Vacancies of Deputy Speakers Created by Leave of Absence - Upon a vacancy in the Office of any Deputy Speaker created by the officer taking a leave of absence, the Speaker, on advice of the Executive Committee and in a published written memorandum, shall appoint and Acting Deputy Speaker, who shall only serve until the next regularly scheduled meeting of the Assembly.
