At this time, a new Deputy Speaker may be elected to serve until the original Deputy Speaker's leave of absence expires. 
Vacancy in All Officers and Chairs - In the event that the position of Speaker, Deputy Speaker for Finance and all positions identified in 204.4 (a)(1)-(6) are vacant simultaneously after the first meeting of the Congress, the most senior member of COGS, as defined in 204.7(a)(7) shall be requested to temporarily chair an emergency meeting of the Congress until a Representative is elected to the Office of the Speaker. The COGS Advisor shall notify all COGS Representatives and call an emergency meeting of COGS no later than one (1) week from when the concurrent vacancies were discovered. Quorum shall not be required for such a meeting. In such a meeting the only business conducted shall be the election of a Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Finance who shall serve until the expiration of the Congress in which the vacancies occurred. 
Duties - The duties of each officer shall be:

The Speaker shall:
 Preside over all COGS functions
Represent the COGS and the Graduate Student Body to the University and the public
Create and oversee the implementation of COGS functions
Appoint Representatives to committees
Take care that the COGS Code, Budget, and the Florida State University Student Body Statutes are faithfully executed
Chair the Executive Committee and serve as a member of the Internal Affairs Committee
Perform all other duties and responsibilities as may be required by law and the Florida State University Student Body Statutes and Constitution.
The Deputy Speaker for Judicial Affairs shall: 

Audit the COGS Code and bylaws to ensure continued compliance with the Florida State University Body Constitution and Statutes.
Preside over the impeachment process
Swear in new members of the Assembly and inform them of their responsibilities prior to their petition hearing before the Assembly.
Conduct an audit of COGS financial records no less than once per fiscal year, or upon request of the Speaker
Assemble and disseminate to the members of the Assembly an extensive list of pertinent questions to be asked in consideration of petitions of new members 

Serve as a member of the Internal Affairs Committee

Assist the Speaker as needed with the administration of COGS

The Deputy Speaker for Communication shall:

Inform all members of meeting dates and happenings.
Create and supervise COGS announcements and bulletins
Act as the public relations liasion between COGS, Florida State University, and public press domains
Record minutes of all Executive Committee meetings
Work with SGA Student Publications to maintain a website
Disseminate information concerning vacant seats in the Assembly to Florida State University students.
Serve as a member of the Outreach Committee and assist the Committee with its mission.
Assist the Speaker as needed with the administration of COGS.
The Deputy Speaker for Finance shall:
Oversee the expenditure of the Annual Budget.
Prepare budget request guidelines for the upcoming fiscal year for ratification by the Budget Committee
Issue reports on the balance and expenditures of COGS accounts.
Oversee Conference Grant disbursement.

Serve as a member of the Internal Affairs Committee.

Assist the Speaker as needed with the administration of COGS.

The Deputy Speaker for Advocacy shall: 
 Oversee the advocacy work of COGS,
Serve as a member of the Advocacy Committee 
Work with the Advocacy Committee to implement the advocacy goals of COGS
Serve on the Strategic Planning Committee, as set out in Chapter 209,
Act as a liaison between COGS and Graduate Assistants United,

Assist the Speaker as needed with the administration of COGS.

sections.heading: Chapter 205 Elections
sections.text:
Adoption of SGA election code with exceptions- Pursuant to Student Body Statutes, the Congress adopts the SGA Election Code, as laid out in Student Body Statutes Title VII, as the governing instrument for COGS elections, except that the procedures of this Chapter shall control for COGS elections, notwithstanding conflicting provisions of the Election Code.
Supervisor of elections to conduct elections- The SGA Supervisor of Elections shall be responsible for conducting elections for the Congress of Graduate Students.
Non-partisan Elections- COGS elections shall be non-partisan.
Candidates to not attend seminar- Candidates for COGS do not need to attend the Candidate Seminars.
Combined financial statements for COGS candidates- Candidates for COGS shall file a combined Campaign Finance Statement by the Final Expense Statement deadline, as set out in Title VII, which shall include:
An itemized list of all campaign contributions and expenditures; or
A statement, under penalty of disqualification, that the candidate received no contributions, nor made any expenditures.
Breaking of ties- Any ties in a COGS election shall be resolved by a vote of COGS immediately upon the convening of the new Congress, taken by secret ballot, with the tied candidates being on the secret ballot.
Judicial branch to resolve disputed elections- Election appeals shall be made to the Student Government Elections Commission, as specified by Title VII. Appeals from the Elections Commission shall be to the Florida State University Student Supreme Court.
Elections to be held during fall SGA elections- Elections will be held in conjunction with the regular fall semester Student Government elections.
Franchise- All enrolled graduate and professional students are eligible to vote in COGS elections, provided that college-specific seats shall only be voted on by students of the said college.
Notice of elections- The Supervisor of Elections shall advertise the seat allocation information at least twenty-four (24) hours before the first day of the Declaration of Candidacy date, as specified by the Student Government Election Code. The Deputy Speaker for Communications shall also advertise the seats up for election on the Congress’s social media pages.
Certification of elections- No more than two weeks after election day, the Supervisor of Elections shall certify, in writing to the Speaker, the election of all COGS representatives whose elections are not under active appeal. This certification shall include, at minimum:
The date of the Supervisor’s certification;
The name of each Representative certified as elected and their seat;
A statement of certification under the Elections Code and COGS Code;
The signature of the Supervisor and a witness, whose name shall be listed in print as well as the signature; and
The SGA seal.

sections.heading: Chapter 206 Committees
sections.text:
Establishment of standing committees- There shall be three standing committees of COGS:
The Outreach Committee
The Advocacy Committee
The Internal Affairs Committee
Establishment of select committees-There shall be select committees of the Congress, including:
The Budget Committee
The Strategic Planning Committee
Any select committee formed under the following procedure:
All select committees shall be formed upon:
Request of any member of COGS that is ratified by a majority vote of the Assembly; or
Recommendation of the Speaker that is approved by a majority vote of the Executive Committee.
The individual initiating the request for formation of the select committee shall describe the purpose, intent, timeframe, and scope of the committee.
Committee assignments-The Executive Committee, by majority vote, shall appoint Representatives to the standing committees no later than each Representative’s second meeting of the Congress.
All members of the Assembly shall be a member of one (1) a standing committee. If for a legitimate reason a member is unable to serve on a standing committee, waiver of this provision may be granted at the discretion of the Speaker. Appeals of the Speaker's decision shall be made to the Assembly which shall ultimately approve or deny the request for waiver.
Any member of the Assembly receiving a waiver under the provisions of subsection (a) will be assigned associate membership of a standing committee. Such associate members may participate in their assigned committee, with all voting privileges, and will count towards quorum when present, but shall never count against quorum, nor be assessed as absent, when not present.
After initial assignments are made, transfers to a specific committee shall only be made if both the Speaker and the representative to be transferred give consent. Any representative shall be transferred out of a committee to an undesignated committee upon request. 
If the membership of any standing committee should fall below five (5) members, the consent requirement in subsection (b) shall be waived and it shall be the duty of the Speaker to reassign a sufficient number of Representatives so that no committee has less than five (5) members. Deference should be given where possible to the desire of representatives to be transferred. 
Deferral of committee assignment-Upon joining the Congress, a Representative may elect to defer their committee assignment until after the Representative attends a meeting of each standing committee. Should the representative defer their assignment, the Representative shall attend one meeting of each standing committee, and, upon attending all standing committees, provide the Speaker with their preference for assignment. Such preference is not binding, and the decision of the Executive Committee may not be appealed to the Assembly. 
Committees to be led by chair and vice chair-Each committee shall be led by a Chair and Vice Chair. Unless otherwise indicated by Code, the chair and vice chair of each committee shall be elected by a majority of the committee's members.
The Chair shall preside over all meetings of the committee, decide points of order, recognize members, set the agenda for meetings, and ensure that all committee meetings are properly noticed. The chair shall meet with the speaker on a regular basis to discuss the committee's business and discuss future opportunities for the committee.
The Vice Chair shall preside over the committee in the absence of the Chair, shall take minutes of all committee meetings, and ensure that all meeting minutes are posted.
Removal of Chair and Vice Chair: Except when the chair or vice chair of a committee is prescribed by Code, a chair or vice chair may be removed by either:
A two-thirds (2/3) vote of the committee; or
A majority vote of the Executive Committee sitting with the Chairs of all standing committees.
Committees to Report to Assembly: At each meeting of the Assembly, each standing committee will be required to inform the Assembly of its activities. This shall be the responsibility of either the Chair, or a committee member designated by the Chair. The budget Committee and Strategic Planning Committee shall only be required to report when the committees are sitting.
Committees to Meet Regularly: Standing committees shall meet no less than once every two (2) months. The Chair will have the authority to set the meeting time and location on campus (or by teleconference) in consultation with the committee, 
Referral of Business to Committees: The Speaker shall be entitled to refer any measure for consideration by the Assembly to an appropriate committee before a floor vote. This decision may only be overturned by a majority vote of members present at a COGS meeting. The Assembly may also refer a measure to an appropriate committee by majority vote.
Committees Authorized to Propose Matters to Assembly: Each committee shall be empowered to propose any measure it feels appropriate to the Assembly.
Charges of Standing Committees: The standing committees are charged with the following competences
Internal Affairs Committee shall focus on the following areas:
Prepare and distribute the monthly COGS newsletter
Keep website information updated
Relations between COGS, and the SGA, MSC, and LSC
Oversight all COGS funding expenditure, 
Train new COGS members,
Make/propose amendments to the COGS Code
Hear cases of impeachment and removal prior to the full assembly, 
Maintain attendance records, initiate removal proceedings for members who are no longer in compliance with attendance requirements, 
Implementing the Aspects of the Strategic Plan within the Committee's jurisdiction, and
All other areas in which the Chair and Speaker agree the Committee should focus.

The Outreach Committee shall focus on the following areas:
Social and community planning
Recruiting New Members to COGS 
Connecting RSOs across programs and colleges
Planning and executing events under the COGS banner,
Relations with Graduate Assistants United (GAU),
Managing responsibilities for orientation, 
Implement the Aspects of the Strategic Plan within the committee's jurisdiction, and
All other areas in which the Chair and the Speaker agree the committee should focus. 
The Student Advocacy Committee shall focus on the following areas:
Graduate student pay and funding, in conjunction with GAU
Childcare
Diversity on campus
Health insurance
Academics and Honor Policy
Parking and transportation
Housing and dining
Library
Health and wellness
Implement Strategic Plan components within the committee's jurisdiction
All other areas in which the Chair and the Speaker agree the committee should focus.
Charges of Select Committees: The select committees shall be charged with specific competences as determined by memorandum of the Speaker (which shall, if the standing committee was created by motion of the Assembly, include the scope set by the motion), but the following select committees shall at least have the following competences.
The budget committee shall draft the Annual Budget, as prescribed by Chapter 208, review and recommend changes to the conference grant amounts outlines in § 307.9, and discuss any other matters agreed upon by the Chair and the Speaker.

The Strategic Planning Select Committee shall focus in the preparation and updating of the Congress of Graduate Students Strategic Plan, associated metrics, and accountability mechanisms as described in Chapter 209.

sections.heading: Chapter 207 Proceedings
sections.text:
Construction-The provisions of this Chapter shall be read in conjunction with IROP. But in case of conflict, the provisions of this Chapter shall preempt IROP.
Ratification of actions of officers-Ratification of actions shall be conducted by motion and shall follow the Internal Rules of Procedure. A confirmation or ratification vote shall require a two-thirds (2/3) majority, except as otherwise required by this code.
Bills- Bills shall be used to amend COGS Code, Annual Budget, and Annual Budget proviso. Amendments to the COGS Code shall require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of COGS.
Bills shall include a title which summarizes the bill, a short title for the bill, and shall include the enacting clause “Be it Enacted by the [Number of Congress] Congress of Graduate Students that:”

Bills may include proviso language to take ancillary actions, including, but not limited to:
Setting an effective date later than upon becoming law.
Issuing waivers under COGS Code (unless Code requires the waiver to be made by resolution).
Providing limitations on funds allocated by COGS.
Providing approval for COGS to enter into written agreements related to the bill.

Bills amending COGS Code shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Assembly:
The Speaker, who signs in a ministerial capacity to signify the Assembly’s approval of the bill.
The COGS Advisor, who shall sign, in a ministerial capacity, within two (2) school days of receipt to signify receipt by the SGA Advising Staff.
The Vice President for Student Affairs, who has ten (10) school days from being presented with the bill to sign or veto the bill. Should the bill not be acted upon within the aforementioned time limit, the bill shall be deemed as approved and enrolled.

Bills amending the Annual Budget or its Proviso shall be signed in the following order after approval by the Assembly:
The Speaker, who signs in a ministerial capacity to signify the Assembly’s approval of the bill.
The Deputy Speaker for Finance, who signs in a ministerial capacity to acknowledge the amendment to COGS finances.
The COGS Advisor, who shall sign, in a ministerial capacity, within two (2) school days of receipt to signify receipt by the SGA Advising Staff.
The University President or their designee, who has ten (10) school days from being presented with the bill to sign or veto the bill. Should the bill not be acted upon within the aforementioned time limit, the bill shall be deemed as approved and enrolled
Resolutions- Resolutions shall be used to convey the opinion of the Congress, amend the Internal Rules of Procedure, and issue waivers (as required by Code). Resolutions shall be signed by the Speaker, acting in a ministerial capacity, to signify the Assembly’s approval of the resolution.
Resolutions shall include the following resolved clause: “Be it Resolved by the [Number of Congress] Congress of Graduate Students:”

The Congress may not enter into written agreements unless approved by resolution, except for those agreements allowed for in bill proviso.

Investigative rights of the Congress- COGS, and its committees, shall be vested with the necessary powers to investigate acts of students, RSOs, and other entities or officers who are associated with COGS. This shall include, but not be limited to, subpoenaing witnesses, hearing testimony, and reviewing documents. The exercise of this power shall be delineated in the COGS Internal Rules of Procedure, or in the absence of such provisions, at the discretion of the Speaker.

sections.heading: Chapter 208 Budget
sections.text:
Short title- This chapter may be referred to as “The Annual Budget Procedures Act of 2012."
Purpose- This chapter establishes the procedure by which the COGS Annual Budget is produced and passed.
Budget to be completed by start of fiscal year- The Annual Budget shall be approved by COGS before the beginning of the fiscal year that it affects.

Source of funds- The Annual Budget shall derive its funds from those appropriated under the Florida State University Student Body Constitution and any other  source.

Proposed budget to be drafted by Budget Committee- The Annual Budget shall be prepared and proposed by the Budget Committee.

The membership of the committee shall be appointed by the Speaker and confirmed by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly. The committee shall include at least four (4) COGS members and the Deputy Speaker for Finance, who shall serve as Chair of the Budget Committee.
Hearings, deliberations, and meetings of the Budget Committee shall be properly noticed to the public.
Hearings, deliberations, and meetings of the Budget Committee are public and shall be advertised in the Congress. The Chairperson of the Budget Committee shall not exclude any student from witnessing the hearings or deliberations in accordance with the FSU SGA Sunshine Act. 
The Budget Committee through its chair and vice chair, shall provide proper notice at the beginning of the budget drafting process, including:
Notifying graduate RSOs of the budget process fifteen (15) school days before the deadline to submit budget request; and
With the COGS Advisor, notifying the graduate RSOs at Florida State University by email letter educating them of their opportunity to receive annual funding during the budget process

Each organization receiving money from the Annual Budget shall make a budget request.
A budget request shall consist of questions pertaining to the organization's activities in a form designed by the Deputy Speaker for Finance and approved by the Budget Committee
All RSOs that are eligible to receive COGS fundings, and are not funded by MSC and LSC, are eligible to submit a budget request.
The Budget Committee is authorized to fund more than the amount requested.
The Budget Committee shall hold hearings during which budget requests are defended. Each budget request shall have a separate hearing. The Procedures shall be set by the Chair of the Budget Committee prior to the start of the hearings
At the conclusion of all hearings, the Budget Committee shall openly deliberate on the budget and create a proposed Annual Budget bill, including any proviso language. The bill shall be officially proposed upon a two-thirds (2/3) vote on the Budget Committee. The Chair of the Budget Committee shall have the authority to make technical and formatting changed prior to presenting the proposed Annual Budget bill.

Proposed budget to be noticed- The proposed Annual budget shall be noticed as follows:
Upon completion of technical and formatting changes to the Proposed Annual Budget Bill, the Chair of the budget Committee shall present the bill to the Congress, either in person or via email, at least ten (10) school days prior to the floor vote. 
The Chair of the Budget Committee shall provide an electronic copy of the proposed Annual Budget, as presented to the Assembly, to the COGS Advisor.

The proposed Annual Budget and proviso language must be advertised on the COGS website by the Chair at least five (5) days before it is considered in a meeting of the Assembly. Such publication must include the date, time, and location of the COGS meeting where the proposed Annual Budget is to be debated, along with the phrase "public comment is welcome."
Budget to be approved by Assembly- The Annual Budget shall be approved by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly.
Amendments to the Proposed Annual budget must follow a majority vote to unlock a specific line item and category of the proposed Annual Budget or a line of the proviso language. Any Amendment which affects the allocation amount in any line of any recipient require a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Congress.
The Annual Budget and proviso language cannot be approved separately.
The final vote on the Proposed Annual Budget shall be by roll-call vote.
If COGS fails to pass the proposed Annual Budget, the Budget Committee shall propose a new Annual Budget with substantial changes within three (3) weeks of the prior proposed Annual Budget's failure in the Congress.
Budget to be reviewed by university- Once approved by COGS, the Annual Budget shall be presented to the University President or their designee for signature. If the University President, or their designee, should veto the Annual Budget, it shall be returned to COGs for revision. If the University President, or their designee, does not sign or veto the Annual Budget within fifteen (15 school days of receipt, the Annual Budget will be considered approved.
Amendments to budget- After the budget has been approved, amendments to the budget, as well as Budget proviso, may be made by bill. 
Monies may be moved within a line item between the categories of Salary, OPS Wages, Contractual Services, Expense, or OCO upon request of any COGS-funded entity by a majority vote of the Assembly. Such transfers of $500 or less shall be deemed approved when, during New Business, the Deputy Speaker for Finance Presents en bloc all pending transfers of $500 or less and no Representative objects. If there is an objection, each bill shall be debated as normal. 
Any amendment to the Annual Budget, or its proviso, shall require the signature of the University President or his/her designee.
Student organizations held harmless- If this chapter is violated by COGS with respect to any RSO, no prejudice shall be held against the RSO for failure to appear or failure to comply with the process before the RSO learned of the meeting or process.
Authority to create reserves- The Budget Committee and Assembly shall have the option to set aside funding to the "COGS Reserves" account. Requests to allocate COGS Reserves funds to other accounts shall be proposed as a COGs Funding Bill and, just be approved by a majority of the COGS General Assembly. The organizations, and internal COGS accounts, throughout the fiscal year, may request transfers from reserves through a form promulgated by the Executive Committee
Authority to designate funding as discretionary- Within the COGS Budget Bull, the Budget Committee and Assembly shall have the option to set aside "Discretionary Funding" for organizations requesting COGS funding for each budget category. Discretionary Funding may be utilized for approved purchases within the allocated budget category not defined in organizations' annual budget requests.

sections.heading: Chapter 209 Strategic Planning
sections.text:
Creation- There is created a Congress of Graduate Students Strategic Plan.
Purpose- The Strategic Plan shall provide for an organized document to identify the long-term growth and sustainability of COGS. The Strategic Plan shall serve as a guiding document to improve cohesion between sessions and provide for a reference point to improve the identified goals of graduate students in student governance.
Strategic plan requirements- The COGS Strategic Plan shall:
Provide Mission and Vision Statements for COGS.
The Mission Statement shall be a succinct summary of what COGS is and provide an easily identifiable foundation for developing name and identity recognition for the body.
The Mission Statement must align with the mission statement identified in the Florida State University strategic plan.
The Vision Statement shall provide the long-term goals and aspirations for which COGS seeks to achieve.
The Vision Statement must complement the mission and vision statement identified in the Florida State University strategic plan.
Identify goals in advocacy, community building, and internal operations to support the achievement of the Mission and Vision Statements.
Provide measurable goals to monitor attainment, where applicable.
Adhere to all applicable laws of the State of Florida, Board of Governors regulations, and regulations of the Florida State University Board of Trustees.
Strategic planning committee-There shall be a Strategic Planning Committee, which shall be a select committee of the Congress.
The committee shall consist of at least five members, as well as the Deputy Speaker for Advocacy (who shall be Chair). Members shall be appointed by the Speaker and confirmed by a majority vote of the Assembly no later than the final Assembly meeting of the Fall semester. The Vice Chair shall be elected by the committee.
For the 33rd Congress, the Chair of the Strategic Planning Committee shall be appointed by the Speaker and confirmed by majority vote of the Congress.
Timeline-The committee shall run in a 12-week period to commence no later than the second full week of classes in the spring term following the commencement of a new session of COGS.
At the conclusion of the 12-week period, the Strategic Planning Select Committee shall approve a strategic plan to forward to the Congress of Graduate Students for consideration and approval.
During the 12-week regular session, there shall be two sessions: a steering session and a plan development session.
The first six weeks shall be the steering session. During this portion, the Committee shall hear presentations and updates on COGS and graduate student governance from the Speaker and stakeholders within the university community. The Committee shall consider the presentations against the mission and vision statements and identify portions of the strategic plan that need updating.
The second six weeks shall be the plan development session. During this portion, the Committee shall conduct the necessary drafting and editing process to update the Strategic Plan.
Special meetings prior to the 12-week period may be requested as needed by the Speaker or by simple majority vote of the Congress. Such special meetings must have a specifically identified topic for discussion.
The committee shall meet, at minimum, during the COGS session in which the expiration of the plan falls. The Speaker retains the right to call the Committee more frequently. The committee shall not have more than one 12-week period per session of COGS.
Adoption of strategic plan- The Strategic Planning Select Committee shall develop the mission and vision statement, associated goals and metrics, and strategic plan narrative. The Committee shall approve the Strategic Plan by majority vote. Upon committee approval, the Chair and Vice Chair shall present the Strategic Plan to the Assembly, who shall adopt it by majority vote.
Duration of strategic plan-The Strategic Plan shall be valid for the three subsequent academic years after approval.
Amendments to strategic plan- Amendments to the mission and vision statement prior to the expiration of the Strategic Plan shall require a two-thirds (2/3) majority vote of COGS.

sections.heading: Chapter 210 Ethics
sections.text:
Short Title-This chapter may be referred to as the “Ethics Code.”
Ethics and professional conduct rules- The following shall constitute the individual rules governing the ethical and professional conduct of COGS Representatives and members of funding boards:
Representative office in COGS is a trust to be performed with integrity in the public interest. By personal example and by admonition to colleagues whose behavior may threaten the honor of the Congress, they  shall watchfully guard the responsibility of their office and the responsibilities and duties placed upon them by the Congress.
A member shall respect and comply with the law and shall conduct themselves at all times in a manner that promotes public confidence in the integrity and independence of the Congress. Each member shall conduct themselves in a manner that promotes a professional environment, free from discrimination. 
A member shall accept nothing which reasonably may be construed to improperly influence their official act, decision, or vote.
A member shall scrupulously comply with the requirements of all laws related to the ethics of public officers.
No member shall knowingly make or issue false or malicious statements about other Representatives or officers of the Student Body.
With the exception of the Annual Budget, no member shall vote on any measure which will personally and directly impact them financially. With the exception of the Annual Budget, or sub-allocation budgets from MSC or LSC, no member shall vote on any measure which will directly impact any organization of which that member is a member of their executive board. The Speaker or Chair may, upon personal knowledge or a point of order, require that a member abstain from a vote implicating this subsection. This decision is appealable and may be overturned by a majority vote of the Assembly. Voting incompatible with this subsection is an actionable violation of the Ethics Code.
Enforcement-Violations of the Ethics Code shall be filed in writing with the COGS Advisor and COGS Speaker. Allegations of violations of this chapter shall be referred to the Internal Affairs Committee within ten (10) school days of receipt, of the charges, who shall investigate the allegations. Should the committee determine, by majority vote, that a violation occurred, it may;
Initiate impeachment proceedings under § 201.5;
Present a resolution of censure to the Assembly, which shall only be adopted by a two-thirds (2/3) vote of the Assembly;
Suspend the Representative or funding board member for a period of no more than fourteen (14) calendar days; or
Any combination thereof.
Non-exclusivity- Punitive action under this chapter shall in no way affect liability for violation of the Florida State University Student Code of Conduct, Student Body Statutes, or any other lawful procedure.

sections.heading: Chapter 211 Awards
sections.text:
Laura Vaughn representative of the year award- Each Congress, at the last or second-to-last meeting of that Congress, shall determine which Representative will be named as the Laura Vaughn Representative of the Year.
The award shall go to the Representative who, in the opinion of the Congress, has best served the Congress, the Graduate Student Body, and the University over the course of the Congress.
The sitting officers of the Congress shall not be eligible to receive the award.
The Speaker shall take nominations for the award from the floor. No debate shall be allowed. The Speaker shall provide the Congress with a secret ballot by which Representatives may rank the nominees in order of preference.
Should no Representative receive a majority of first-preference votes, the Representative with the least number of first-preference votes shall be removed from contention and their votes shall be redistributed based on the next preference of each vote. Should no Representative have a majority of votes after this redistribution, the Representative with the least number of votes shall be eliminated and votes distributed in accordance with each vote’s next preference. This shall continue until a Representative has a majority of votes.
The award shall be presented to the winner by the outgoing Speaker at Fall Inauguration.
A list of the names of the Representatives who were named Laura Vaughn Representative of the Year shall be maintained on the COGS website.
Laura Vaughn shall be listed as the Laura Vaughn Representative of the Year for the Thirty-Second Congress.

sections.heading: Chapter 300 Requirements For Student Organizations To Receive Funding
sections.text:
Organization recognized by university for four weeks - All student organizations must be recognized by the Division of Student Affairs for a minimum of four (4) weeks in order to receive COGS Funds.
Organization officers financially certified - The President and Treasurer of an Recognized Student Organization (RSO) must be financially certified by COGS in order to receive COGS Funds.
Elected president and financial officer - RSOs are required to elect a Financial Officer to oversee budgetary accounts and a President to countersign for expenditures. To be eligible for COGS Funds, the President and Treasurer must be A&S fee-paying graduate or professional students at Florida State University.
Majority graduate student membership - To be eligible for COGS Funds, a majority of the organization’s members must be A&S fee-paying graduate students at Florida State University.
Second signer for expenditures - All expenditures of COGS Funds by said organizations will require a signature from the Financial Officer and President, or other financially certified officer. 
Abiding by organizational constitution - No RSO which receives funding from COGS, or any of its sub-allocation authorities, may violate the provisions of its individual RSO constitution. Failure of an RSO to abide by, or secure any right granted under its constitution, shall make the organization subject to the measures outlined in Chapter 308 of this Code.

The Speaker shall enforce this provision upon application from any student, or upon being made aware of an ongoing violation of an RSO’s constitution
The Florida State University Student Supreme Court shall have concurrent jurisdiction to enforce the provision of this section through appropriate writs. In the event of a conflict between the Speaker and the Student Supreme Court, the determination and orders of the Student Supreme Court shall prevail.
The copy of an RSO’s constitution filed with the University during the annual RSO recognition process shall be considered authoritative.
Mandatory dues prohibited- RSOs within the jurisdiction of COGS may only collect voluntary dues. This provision shall not require RSOs to pay state or national membership dues on behalf of members.
Compliance does not guarantee funding - No provision of this chapter shall guarantee an RSO to receive COGS Funds from the SGA Accounting Office.

sections.heading: Chapter 301 General Restrictions On Spending
sections.text:
Purpose of receipt of COGS funds - All funds allocated by COGS or its sub-allocation authorities such as graduate funding boards, shall be offered in an effort to nurture the highest levels of scholarship, research, creativity, and social activities necessary to support a comprehensive graduate research university. 
Compliance with applicable policies - Activities funded must not conflict with the purpose and regulations of this Code, the Florida State University Student Body Constitution, Statutes, and Board of Trustees’ policies, or with state or federal laws.

Anti-discrimination policy - No RSO which receives funding from COGS will practice de facto or de jure discrimination against discrimination or differential treatment in membership or otherwise on the basis of race, creed, nationality, alienage, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, family status, or socio-economic status.
Events to be open and available - All events funded in whole or in part by COGS Funds or derivative resources must be equally accessible to all enrolled graduate students at Florida State University, or serve a legitimate academic purpose.
All purchases for events held off the Florida State University campus require approval of the Assembly by majority vote, unless approved by proviso to a funding bill.
The Medical Student Council (MSC) and Law School Council (LSC) are authorized to waive this section for events funded by the respective councils by motion approved by two-thirds (2/3) vote.
Events to be free to students - RSOs within the jurisdiction of COGS may not charge Florida State University students admission fees for any event subsidized or paid for by COGS Funds.
No RSO receiving funding from COGS may charge Florida State University students for food purchased with COGS Funds.
Prohibition on use of funds to support political parties or campaigns - Funds may not be expended to support, in whole or in part, a candidate for political office, nor for contribution to a political party. This provision shall also apply to on-campus SGA political parties and campaigns. 
Prohibition on use of funds for alcohol - COGS Funds cannot be used to purchase alcoholic beverages.
Limits on per person expenditures for food - No RSO shall incur more than twenty dollars ($20) per person, per meal, when using COGS Funds.
This section can be overridden by a two-thirds (2/3) majority vote of the Assembly.
Limits on expenditures for gratuity on food - RSOs may request, receive, and expend a reasonable amount not to exceed twenty percent (20%) as gratuity, for food purchases for events. Reimbursement shall not be granted on meals for individuals receiving a per diem in conjunction with travel. The gratuity must be recorded on the receipt and should reflected in the total cost.

sections.heading: Chapter 302 Funding Of OPS Positions
sections.text:
OPS positions to be held by enrolled students - Elected and non-elected OPS positions shall be held by persons currently enrolled at Florida State University unless otherwise specified in this Code, the Internal Rules of Procedure, or the Student Body Constitution and Statutes.
Advertisement of non-elective OPS positions - All OPS non-elected positions under COGS, or its organizations, shall be advertised in a widely publicized campus forum for a minimum of two (2) weeks.

sections.heading: Chapter 303 Self-Generated Funds
sections.text:
Definitions - The term “self-generated funds” shall be defined as funds earned or obtained without the expenditure of COGS Funds or COGS-fund derivative resources.
Deposit of self generated funds - Self-generated funds may be housed within the organization’s current Department of Student Engagement (DSE) or Florida State University Foundation account. A copy of all deposit transmittals of Self-Generated Funds must be submitted to the DSE Accounting Office in accordance with DSE procedures.
Prohibition - COGS funding may not be used solely for fund generation.
Reimbursement of COGS funds when used in part to generate funds - If funds are generated from an event paid in whole or in part by COGS Funds, the funds generated will be used to offset the cost of the event.

sections.heading: Chapter 304 Purchase Request Procedures
sections.text:
Requirements of purchase requests - All requests for expenditures shall:
Be submitted to NoleCentral, or a successor platform;
Be submitted at least ten (10) business days in advance;
Include estimates of all materials to be produced or purchased; and
Include a justification identifying benefit(s) of the expense to all students at Florida State University.
Mandatory denial of purchase requests - Any request shall be denied by the Speaker, Deputy Speaker for Finance, or SG&A Accounting for:
Failure to meet any requirement of section (1), or
Violations of Code or any other applicable law.
Discretionary denial of purchase requests - The Speaker and Deputy Speaker for Finance shall reject requests for expenditures that they deem fiscally irresponsible and/or excessive. Reasons for rejection include, but are not limited to, any request deemed excessive or irresponsible.
Denials on discretionary grounds may be appealed by writ of injunction to the Student Supreme Court, which shall issue if clear error is shown.
Submission does not guarantee receipt - The initiation of a request in no way guarantees the receipt of funds.

sections.heading: Chapter 305 Printed Materials
sections.text:
Acknowledgement of COGS funding - All printed materials for any and all advertisements, services, activities, programs, or events sponsored by a recipient of COGS Funds must be adequately display the COGS logo or the phrase “Paid for by COGS.”
Disclaimer of COGS neutrality - All printed materials of a COGS-fund recipient that contain a political or controversial message shall carry the phrase: “The views expressed herein do not necessarily reflect those of COGS or SGA.”
Inclusion of organizational branding - Printed materials paid for, or in part by, COGS Funds, must display the organization's name or logo.

sections.heading: Chapter 306 General Travel Policies
sections.text:
Application of chapter - This chapter applies to students whose travel and/or accommodations are being funded by COGS Funds.
Types of funded travel - All funded individual travel must be:
In the performance of official duties on behalf of COGS;
By a student making a presentation at an academic conference;
By a student attending an academic conference;
Part of an honorarium given for services to the Student Body; or
For persons contracted to provide a service to the Student Body.
Paperwork - All required paperwork must be completed in accordance with the requirements of the Florida State University Travel Office and the Department of Student Engagement (DSE) Accounting Office.
Per diem - All per diem shall be funded at the state rate. No per diem shall be authorized for any purpose other than food. This provision shall include, but is not limited to, entertainment and alcoholic beverage expenses.

5. Group travel policy -  As a general policy, COGS does not fund travel for RSOs.

       (a) COGS shall not fund RSO travel for career development and conference travel.

      (b) RSO group travel is limited to travel that serves the promotion of the mission and goal of the RSO as well as to the betterment of the FSU student body.

     (c) Group travel may only be approved by bill proviso or resolution of the Assembly, passed by a two-thirds (2/3), however no such funding may exceed $1,500 except by unanimous vote of the Congress.

sections.heading: Chapter 307 Conference Grants
sections.text:
Creation - There shall be a system of individual conference grants by which the Congress supports graduate and professional students to attend conferences that further their academic or professional endeavors.
Administration - The conference grants system shall be administered by the Deputy Speaker for Finance, in coordination with the COGS Advisor and any other persons designated by the Speaker, and shall be administered on a first-come, first-served basis.

General restrictions for conference grants - No student shall:
Receive more than two (2) grants per fiscal year. Any student receiving a Combined grant shall be considered to have received two grants.
Receive more than seven hundred dollars ($700) in total grants per fiscal year.
Receive more than one (1) grant per conference attended.
Types of conference grants - There shall be four (4) types of conference grants:
Attendance grants
Domestic presentation grants
International presentation grants, and
Combined grants
Budgeting of funds for conference grants - The Annual Budget shall allocate funds for conference grants, with funding split between attendance grants and presentation grants. Combined grants, domestic presentation grants, and international presentation grants shall be considered “presentation grants” for the purpose of this section.
Distribution of funds into three periods - Annual COGS Conference Grant allocations shall be equally distributed into at least three grant funding periods, each lasting four (4) months, as defined in the Annual Budget’s proviso language.
 One month following the close of a conference grant funding period, remaining funds shall be moved forward to the current funding period.
General eligibility for conference grants - Enrolled and A&S fee-paying graduate and professional students at Florida State University are eligible to be awarded conference grants so long as they:
Complete an application promulgated by the Deputy Speaker for Finance and posted on the COGS website;
Submit the application no fewer than fifteen (15) calendar days prior to the conference;
Provide proof of registration for the conference, and.
Proof of attendance shall require one or more of the following (at the discretion of the Deputy Speaker for Finance): conference registration receipt, conference materials, or a conference program.
Are not, individually or as a member of an RSO, receiving any other SGA funds for their conference travel.

Are attending a conference more than one hundred fifty (150) miles away from Tallahassee.
Students may apply for a grant for a virtual conference but may only be reimbursed for the cost of conference registration, and such reimbursement shall not exceed the amount of an Attendance grant.
Specific eligibility for conference grants - The following grants shall have the following specific eligibility requirements:
Domestic presentation grants:
The student shall provide proof of that they have been accepted to present at the conference the grant is for. Presentations may include, but is not limited to, being a solo presenter, serving on a discussion or presentation panel, or giving a poster presentation.
The conference must be within the United States.
International presentation grants:
The student shall provide proof that they have been accepted to present at the conference the grant is for. Presentations may include, but is not limited to, being a solo presenter, serving on a discussion or presentation panel, or giving a poster presentation.
The conference must be outside the United States.
The student shall provide proof of approval by the University for international travel.
Combined grants:
The student shall provide proof that they have been accepted to present at the conference the grant is for. Presentations may include, but is not limited to, being a solo presenter, serving on a discussion or presentation panel, or giving a poster presentation.
The student must not have received any grants for the current fiscal year.
The student shall make an acknowledgment that receiving the Combined grant makes them ineligible for any further grants in that fiscal year.
Amounts of conference grants  - The amount of each grant shall be as follows:
Attendance grants: $200.
Domestic presentation grants: $350.
International presentation grants: $700.
Combined grants: $525.
Reimbursement of funds - Conference grants shall be awarded as a reimbursement of funds spent, pursuant to requirements set by SG&A Accounting.
Interpretation of chapter - The Deputy Speaker for Finance, in consultation with the Speaker and COGS Advisor, is authorized to interpret the provisions of this Chapter. Such interpretations shall be binding unless invalidated by the Student Supreme Court.

sections.heading: Chapter 308 Compliance And Enforcement Mechanisms
sections.text:
Definitions - For the purpose of this chapter:
The term “applicable rules” shall be defined as the provisions of the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, as well as  the provisions of this Code.
The term “violation” shall be defined as misfeasance, nonfeasance, or malfeasance of any responsibility under the applicable rules, or as conduct which is a violation prohibition contained within any of the rules or as fraud or misrepresentation in interactions with COGS or SGA. 
Methods of enforcement - To enforce the provisions of this Title, the Congress may freeze accounts, restrict accounts, or publicly censure non-compliant entities and organizations.
Public censure - COGS may issue a public censure for RSOs or officers who engage in conduct that is either dishonest, unethical conduct, or a violation of this Code, if the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker for Finance concur. 
The censure shall include the reason for issuance, as well as the name of the officer or RSO responsible for the action.
The original censure will be retained by the COGS Advisor. A copy of the censure will be sent to the officer or RSO, and to any funding board that administers the RSO.
A censure may only be revoked only by the Speaker or by an affirmative vote of the Congress.
Any censure shall be included read aloud in the Assembly and included, in its totality, in the minutes of the next Assembly meeting. 
Purpose of freezing accounts - The purpose of freezing funds is to prohibit the RSO from spending funds, to give the RSO the opportunity to correct the problem(s),  and to deter future actions that are inconsistent with the applicable rules. 
Effect of freezing accounts - Upon a freeze being places on an organization's account, no purchase requests, allocations, or transfers involving the frozen account shall be approved or processed. 
Freezing of accounts - Upon concurrence of the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker for Finance, a freeze may be placed upon the account of any RSO within the jurisdiction of COGS for violations of applicable rules. The duration of the freeze is not to exceed fifteen (15) school days.
Purpose of restricting accounts - Restriction of accounts should be reserved for:
The most egregious violations of applicable rules;
Organizations who have failed to comply with applicable rules after a freeze.
Organizations who have violated applicable rules multiple times, or 
Organizations that have demonstrated a lack of institutional or financial control.
Restrictions of accounts - Upon concurrence of two-thirds (2/3) of the Representatives in regular Assembly, restrictions in the form of a bill, may be placed upon the account of any RSO within the jurisdiction of COGS for violations of applicable rules.
The duration of the restrictions are not to exceed the remainder of the fiscal year in force at the time the bill is enacted.
The bill shall make legislative findings as to the grounds for issuing the restrictions.
The bill shall detail the restrictions placed on the RSO's accounts . Restrictions may include but are not limited to:
A ban on specific expenditures from the RSOs accounts, 
Requiring pre-authorization from the Internal Affairs Committee prior to approval of an expenditure, or 
A complete ban on the use of funds in any or all funding categories.
Due to the emergency nature of the placement of restrictions and notwithstanding  S. 203.3(c), COGS Code, the effect of a bill placing restrictions shall go into effect immediately upon passage by the Assembly. Should the bill be vetoed by the Vice President of Student Affairs, the restrictions shall be void. 
Written notice of freeze or restriction - When the Speaker or Deputy Speaker for Finance initiates a freeze or the Assembly imposes restrictions, the cause and duration of the freeze/restrictions shall be identified in a written memorandum from the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker for Finance to the frozen/restricted organization, with copies to the Student Body Treasurer, Business Manager, and COGS advisor. In the case of restrictions, the memorandum should include the restrictions placed by the bill.
Frozen or restricted entity to present to Assembly - Any entity whose accounts are frozen/restricted must have its Treasurer/Financial Officer (or designee) make a presentation to the COGS Assembly. This presentation shall be scheduled at the behest of the COGS speaker and the Deputy Speaker of Finance.
Voluntary removal of freeze or restrictions - A freeze initiated by the Speaker and Deputy Speaker may be rescinded at any time by the Speaker by written notification to those required in section (9). A freeze may also be removed by majority vote of the Assembly. Restrictions may only be removed by majority vote of the Assembly in the form of a bill.
Appeal of freeze or restrictions - The decision to freeze/restrict funds may be appealed to the Student Senate Finance Committee, Student Body Treasurer, or any other officer authorized in the Student Body Statutes. An order by any such entity to lift the freeze. restrictions shall be directly and immediately applicable.
Non-exclusivity of chapter - This chapter shall not prejudice the rights of any Student Body officers under the Florida State University Student Body Constitution or Statutes to impose sanctions on RSOs without the authorization of COGS.
LSC and MSC to have authority to freeze accounts under jurisdiction - LSC and MSC shall have the authority to freeze the accounts of any organization under the jurisdiction of each council.
Each council shall follow the procedures of this chapter when issuing freezes, substituting:
The Assembly with the council; and
The Speaker and Deputy Speaker for Finance with the Chair and Vice Chair of the council, respectively.
Copies of the memoranda issued under subsection (9) shall also be provided to the Speaker and Deputy Speaker for Finance.
In addition to the persons listed in subsection (12), the Speaker and the Deputy Speaker for Finance shall have the authority to issue an order to lift the freeze.

sections.heading: Chapter 400 Law School Council
sections.text:
Creation - There is created a Law School Council (LSC). LSC shall be organized and administered by COGS, and housed under the Student Bar Association as a funding board within its jurisdiction in accordance with the Florida State University Student Body Statutes. 
Purpose - The purpose of LSC is to represent Law School RSOs before all budgetary committees of SGA and COGS, to sub-allocate funds to Law School RSOs, and to monitor and coordinate the budget activities of the various Law School RSOs. 
Council composition - LSC shall be composed of law students with the following composition:
Three (3) members being appointed from the membership of the Student Bar Association through procedures set by the Student Bar Association, provided that the President, Vice President, Secretary, and Treasurer of the SBA shall not serve as a member of the LSC and that the elections occur no later than the final day of February in each year, 

The COGS Representatives for the College of Law, serving as ex officio members,

 Five (5) members being students elected at-large from the student body of the College of Law, and 

A Chair elected by the student body of the College of Law.
Election of at-large members - At-Large Elections shall take place in the Spring SBA Elections, shall be non-partisan, and shall take place under the same procedures used by SBA to elect their executive board. 
Candidates for the at-large positions shall declare their candidacy by the candidate declaration deadline, in accordance with SBA procedures. 

The at-large members shall be the five candidates who receive the most votes. .
The at-large candidate who receives the most votes at the Spring election shall become the Vice Chair of the LSC. The at-large candidate  who receives the second-most votes at the Spring election shall become  the Treasurer of the LSC. 

If there are not more candidates for the at-large seats than open seats at the Spring election, the Vice Chair and Treasurer of the LSC shall be elected from the at-large members at the first meeting of the new LSC board.

LSC board members shall train the Members Elect. At-Large Members’ terms will end at the conclusion of the final board meeting of March, at which time At-Large Members Elect and SBA representatives shall take office

Election of chair- The Chair shall be elected in the same manner as the at-large members, with the candidate receiving the most votes being the winner. Candidates must have previously served on the LSC in some capacity prior to declaring their candidacy for Chair, unless no candidates with such service have declared. 
Advisor to council - An administrative or faculty representative shall serve as an advisor to the LSC Board. This representative shall assist the Board in ensuring that LSC is compliant with the COGS Code, the Florida State University Student Body Statutes, Law School Policy, and Florida State University Policies and Procedures.
Vacancies- Vacancies of the LSC Board shall be filled by appointment. Vacancies in the at-large positions shall be filled through two-thirds (2/3) vote of the remaining LSC members after a publicly noticed application and interview period. Vacancies in the seats representing the SBA shall be filled by the procedures set by SBA
Vacancies of officers - Should the Chair become permanently vacant, the Vice Chair shall become the Chair. If there is no Vice Chair when the Chair becomes permanently vacant, the Treasurer shall become Chair. If there is no Vice Chair and no Treasurer when the Chair becomes permanently Vacant, the LSC shall elect a Chair for the remainder of their term from the remaining at-large members by majority vote of the LSC members. Vacancies in the Vice Chair or Treasurer shall be filled by the Chair appointing an at-large member to said position, subject to confirmation of a majority of the LSC members.
Duties of officers - The officers of LSC shall have the following duties:
The chair shall

Preside over all LSC meetings.
Represent LSC in all official business and budget matters before COGS or the Student Senate.
Have the authority to call special meetings of LSC. 
Be responsible for all official correspondence of LSC.
Perform any other duties as assigned by LSC or this Code.
Act as liaison between Law School student organizations and SGA Accounting.
Not vote on any matter before the LSC, except to break a tie vote. 
The Vice Chair Shall
Keep accurate minutes of all LSC meetings.
Email minutes to the Chair at the conclusion of each LSC meeting.
Keep apprised of any changes in SGA Statutes and COGS Code that may affect the bylaws of the LSC and recommend changes to the Council if needed to comply with SGA Statutes and COGS Code.

Serve as presiding officer of the LSC in the absence of the Chair, during which time the Vice Chair shall not vote, except as to break tie votes.

Perform any other duties as assigned by the LSC Chair or this Code. 

The Treasurer shall:
Keep an accurate and up-to-date budget.
Perform any other duties as assigned by the LSC Chair or this code. 
Attend any budgetary meetings as an LSC representative. 
Work with the Deputy Speaker of Finance in order to perform any requested external audits in compliance with this Code. 
Be listed as an officer of each member RSO in NoleCentral, or its successor platform, to maintain oversight of member RSO accounts.
 Compliance with applicable rules - LSC shall sub-allocate its ordained funds to its member RSOs consistent with the Florida State University Student Body Constitution, Statutes, and A&S Fee Guidelines, as well as this code and any other applicable rules and regulations. LSC shall only sub-allocate funds to law school organizations which have been registered, in accordance with COGS and SGA guidelines.
Appropriation of budgeted funds - LSC shall allocate funds granted to it by COGS to Law School RSOs in a fiscally responsible manner, providing activities and services for the benefit of the maximum number of students.
LSC shall submit a proposed semesterly budget on behalf of all Law School RSOs to COGS in compliance with all requirements of the Annual Budget process. COGS shall make all budget allocations to the LSC in the Expense category.

The LSC Chair and Treasurer shall be responsible for ensuring that members and member RSOs are properly informed about the budgetary process, its timelines, and the total budget allocated to the LSC by COGS. 

The LSC Chair, at the above-mentioned meeting and through email to the members and member RSOs, shall announce the dates that:

The Budget Request Form opens,
The Budget Request Form closes,

The LSC will hold hearings on budget requests,

The LSC will deliberate on the final LSC budget.

The Budget Request Form shall be created by the Treasurer, in consultation with the Chair, the LSC, and SG&A Accounting. If at all possible, the Form need not be overhauled every year.

The procedures for budgetary hearings and deliberations shall be determined under the LSC bylaws.
Any member representing the SBA who sits on their executive board shall abstain from voting or debating on the SBA line item, as required by Student Body Statutes. Likewise, any LSC member who sits on an RSO executive board shall abstain from voting or debating on their RSO's line item.

The LSC Chair may also determine whether a member has a conflict of interest and may bar them from voting or debating on the conflicted line item.

Any such determination by the Chair may be appealed to the Board and overturned by majority vote.

The LSC Budget shall contain and "Unallocated" line item, which shall be used to fund requests by RSOs made outside the annual semesterly budget cycle. it shall also contain an "LSC Expense" line item, which may be drawn upon by the Chair, with the agreement of the Treasurer in support of the mission of the LSC

The Chair shall make every effort to complete the budgetary process prior to the start of the semester that the budget is being made for.

A two thirds (2/3) majority of the LSC is required for final passage of the budget. 

Upon passage of the budget by LSC, the allocations shall be submitted to the COGS Assembly, in the form of a bill, for final approval. 
Emergency allocations and transfers - All LSC allocations and transfers made outside of the semesterly budget shall require the signature of either the Speaker of COGS, or the Deputy Speaker for Finance. The Speaker or Deputy Speaker may deny any allocation or amendment deemed excessive or irresponsible. If an allocation or transfer is denied, the LSC Chair may, within seventy-two (72) hours of being notified of the denial, appeal the denial to the Congress, where it shall be debated and voted on during the “Funding Requests”  agenda item. A two-thirds (2/3) vote of COGS members present and voting is required to approve the allocation or denial, notwithstanding the Speaker or Deputy Speaker’s denial.
Funds not to be expended until annual budget signed - The allocation to LSC shall not be obligated or expended until the COGS annual Budget has been approved by the COGS Speaker and the Deputy Speaker for Finance, and the University President, or their designee
Further duties of the council - LSC shall have the following powers and duties under this code and shall be subject to all other applicable Florida State University Student Body Statutes in the exercise of its powers and duties:

LSC shall hold budgetary hearings at which member RSOs present their requests. In the event that a member of an RSO that submitted a request is unable to attend, the LSC Chair may present the RSO’s request on their behalf.
LSC shall then represent its member RSOs at all budgetary hearings and procedures of COGS.
LSC shall report to the Internal Affairs Committee of COGS as requested by the Internal Affairs Committee, with a minimum fifteen (15) school days’ notice.
LSC may pass Resolutions on behalf of the Law School Student Body.
LSC may remove any non-ex officio council member for nonfeasance by an affirmative, majority vote of all those board members not being considered for removal in the instant controversy.
LSC may, by a majority vote, recommend any member for  impeachment for misfeasance or malfeasance in accordance with Chapter 114 of this Code
LSC shall adopt bylaws at the second meeting of the LSC following the annual installation of new at-large board members by a majority vote of the total membership of the LSC.

Meetings of council - LSC shall hold open meetings in compliance with Chapter 203, Student Body Statutes, on a twice-monthly basis and shall send copies of the minutes of such meetings to all Law School RSOs and COGS.
A special meeting of LSC may be called by the LSC Chair or by petition of two-thirds (2/3) majority of Presidents of the Law School RSOs.
Quorum shall be a majority of total membership of LSC. A quorum must be present for LSC to conduct business,
All LSC action must be approved by a majority vote of those LSC members present and voting.
LSC shall announce and provide notice of its meetings and procedures to Law School RSOs. It shall provide notice at least five (5) school days before any forms, requests, or petitions are due for the meeting.
Attendance at monthly meetings is mandatory for all LSC board members; adequate notice is required for absences. If a member must be absent from a monthly meeting, they must provide adequate notice to the LSC Chair. If a member is absent from more than two monthly meetings, that member will be considered for removal by members of the board. All board members, except for the member at issue, will vote on the removal of the board member. A majority vote will effectively remove the member from the board. The vacancy will then be filed in accordance to the procedures outlined above. 
Within three (3) business days of any LSC meeting, minutes must be submitted to the COGS Speaker for review before allocations are formally authorized.

sections.heading: Chapter 401 Medical Student Council (MSC)
sections.text:
Creation - There shall be created a Medical Student Council (MSC).
Purpose - The purpose of the Medical Student Council is to represent Medical School RSOs before all budgetary committees of COGS; to sub-appropriate funds to MSC RSOs; enhance medical education at Florida State University by promoting a variety of speakers, conferences, and academic projects; express the will of the Medical School Student Body through resolutions; and to monitor and coordinate the budget activities of Medical School RSOs.
Composition - MSC shall be composed of an Executive Board and a General Board.
The MSC Executive Board shall be composed of a President, Vice President, Treasurer, Secretary, and a representative from each degree program track in the College of Medicine hereafter referred to as “program representatives”. Two additional members of the board shall be the MSC Representatives to COGS. Elections shall take place every Fall semester. Members’ terms will end on the last day of the Fall semester, at which time Members-Elect shall take office.
The MSC General Board shall be composed of the President from each of the MSC RSO and one representative for all regional campuses.
Advisor to the council - An Administrative Representative appointed by the Dean of the College of Medicine shall be an advisory member to the MSC Board. This Representative shall assist the Board in ensuring that the MSC follows the guidelines established but this code and the Student Government Finance Code. 
Vacancies - Vacancies of the MSC Executive Board shall be filled in accordance with the procedures outlined in the MSC constitution and Bylaws. Vacancies of the MSC General Board shall be filled pursuant to the RSO's constitution.
Duties of executive board members  - The members of the Executive Board shall have the following duties: 
The MSC President Shall:

Preside over all meetings of the board according to Robert’s Rules of Order.
Act as spokesperson for the Board.
Chair the Executive Committee on all administrative matters.
Determine the MSC General and Executive Meeting schedule.
Act in accordance with the Treasurer of MSC and the finance rules of the Student Government on all financial matters.
Have the power to appoint Ad-hoc committees and their chairmen as deemed necessary with approval from the MSC General Board.
The MSC Vice President shall:

Assume the duties of President when necessary.
Coordinate all public relations efforts of the board.
Coordinate a monthly calendar of events.
Work with student organizations and review all constitutions to insure compliance with student body law.
Chair the Executive Committee for financial special requests.
The MSC Treasurer shall:

Chair the Executive Committee on all financial matters, excluding special requests.
Coordinate all financial matters of the MSC.
Keep an accurate record of the MSC budget.
Request and compile budget proposals from all MSC RSOs before budgetary hearings every fiscal school year.
Submit the MSC Executive meeting minutes to the COGS Speaker within three (3) business days of any Executive Board meeting before the allocations are formally authorized.
The MSC Secretary shall:

Keep accurate minutes of all meetings. 
Keep voting records of all meetings. 
Keep accurate records of attendance and report any violation(s) of the attendance policy.
Attend to all correspondence of the board
Maintain a current list of all MSC RSOs, boards, and organizational boards, and organizational constitutions on file. 
The Program Representatives shall:

Represent the needs of Students in their respective degree programs.
Act as liaisons between the Students in their respective degree programs and the MSC.
The MSC Representatives to SGA and COGS shall:

Keep the MSC Board updated on all events pertaining to SGA and COGS. 
Keep SGA and COGS updated on the activities of the MSC.
Represent the MSC in front of all Student Government entities when the MSC president is not present. 
Coordinate with the MSC President and formulate a long-term political strategy for the MSC and its role within Student Government. 
Present requests, information, bills, and other necessary items to the Student Government on behalf of the MSC.
Fulfill any obligations as required by Florida State Student Government Association or the Congress of Graduate Students.
Powers and duties of the council - The MSC shall have the following powers and duties under this code and shall also be subject to all other applicable Florida State University Student Body Statutes:
The MSC shall represent member RSOs at all the budgetary hearings and Procedures of COGS.
The MSC shall allocate its obtained funds to member RSOs consistent with this code, the Florida State University Student Body Constitution, Statutes, and A&S Fee guidelines, as well as any other applicable rules and regulations. 
MSC shall only allocate funds to recognize medical school organizations in accordance with FSU student affairs guidelines, for a minimum of eight weeks, and which have a minimum of 10 student members. 
The allocation to MSC shall not be obligated to expended until the budget has been approved by the Vice President for Student Affairs. MSC may set up an MSC unallocated account. 
The MSC shall monitor the expenditures of sub-allocated funds to ensure that they are spent as budgeted and in accordance with this code, the Florida State University Student Body Constitution, Statutes, and A&S Fee Guidelines, as well as any other applicable rules and regulations. 
MSC shall report to the Internal Affairs Committee, at a committee meeting as requested by the Committee with a minimum of fifteen (15) school days' notice.
MSC RSOs shall process budget revisions and transfers on the forms prescribed by the appropriate authority with all the requisite approvals prior to implementation. 
After-the-fact amendments to allocations which are greater than $100 shall require majority approval of the MSC Board approval prior to being sent to COGS leadership for signature.
MSC shall promulgate such other rules as deemed appropriate, which shall be kept on file for public record in the DSE Accounting Office, the Office of Information Services, and the College of Medicine Student Organization Office.
The MSC shall pass Resolutions on behalf of the College of Medicine Student Body. 
Meetings of the executive board - The MSC shall hold an Executive Board meeting on at least a monthly basis and post an electronic copy of the minutes on CivicPlus, or its successor platform.
The MSC Executive Board shall also make recommendations at this meeting for all new business, which shall be discussed at the General Meeting. 
Quorum shall be a majority of Executive Board members of the MSC. A quorum is necessary for business to be conducted at the MSC Executive Board Meeting.
Meetings of the general board - The MSC shall hold a General Meeting, composed of both the MSC Executive Board and the MSC General Board, on a monthly basis and shall post an electronic copy of the minutes on CivicPlus, or its successor platform.
The MSC President shall determine the agenda of the General meeting and shall present its recommendations to the MSC General Board.
The MSC General Board shall pass any recommended proposals, pass new proposals, or alter the agenda by a majority vote of those present and voting. In the event of a tie, the MSC President will cast the deciding vote. 
Quorum shall be a majority of the RSO representatives. A quorum is necessary for business to be conducted at the MSC General meeting.
